  • mcp_permission_review_present: MCP capabilities, trust level, data boundary, side effects and approval policy are documented.
  • hook_activation_approval_present: hook event, matcher, command, trust decision and failure behavior are documented and approved.
  • automation_manual_stability_present: automation has manual test evidence, durable prompt, cadence, environment, owner, verification and disable path.
  • model_reasoning_policy_present: durable roles/workflows have default model/reasoning, escalation/downgrade and budget.
  • memory_policy_present: memory is recall only; mandatory rules and secrets policy live in checked-in docs.
  • agent_eval_workflow_present: agent behavior changes have baseline, eval cases, threshold, rerun command and failure labels.
  • agentic_evidence_before_completion: completion/readiness claim cites current evidence or explicit gap.

docs.title: Candidate eval fields
docs.text:
• Agentic scope and runtime surface are classified.
  • Source-of-truth artifacts exist and chat is not the only durable state.
  • Read-only discovery inspected docs, files, commands and sandbox/approval constraints.
  • Approval boundary exists for MCP, hooks, CI, release, external writes and production data.
  • Subagent packet includes sources, assumptions, owned files, forbidden files, expected evidence and stop condition.
  • Parallel work has non-overlapping ownership or sequential fallback.
  • Skill promotion has manual success evidence, trigger, inputs, outputs, verification and failure modes.
  • Plugin boundary includes manifest, bundled capabilities, permissions, eval cases and owner/update loop.
  • Automation has manual stability evidence, durable prompt, owner, cadence, verification and disable path.
  • Completion claim cites current evidence or explicit gap.

docs.title: Tooling candidates
docs.text: Tooling area Candidate Notes Durable rules AGENTS.md Project rules, commands, source policy and done criteria. Control plane REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md Long-running product work state and evidence. Codex runtime config config.toml Model, reasoning and runtime defaults when project-owned. Handoff agent-task-packet.md, handoff-contract.md Fresh-context subagent work and expected evidence. Skills SKILL.md Repeatable workflow packaging after manual success. Plugins .codex-plugin/plugin.json Bundle skills, MCP, hooks, apps/assets and permission expectations. MCP review mcp-permission-review.md Tool/resource/prompt trust, side effects, secrets and approvals. Hooks hooks.json, hook-activation-record.md Event/matcher/command, trust decision and disable path. Automations automation.toml, automation-candidate.md Stable recurring workflow candidate and manual review evidence. Agent workflow readiness agentic-workflow-readiness.md Combined gate packet before promotion or orchestration.

docs.title: Проверки
docs.text:
• Workflow starts from classified use-case archetype and selected runtime.
  • Source-of-truth artifacts are present and current.
  • Read-only discovery inspected project docs, target files, commands and sandbox/approval context.
  • Subagent work has task packet, ownership, forbidden files, output schema and stop conditions.
  • Parallel work has explicit ownership or uses sequential fallback.
  • Skill promotion is backed by manual evidence and failure modes.
  • Plugin packaging includes manifest, bundled components, permissions, eval cases and owner/update loop.
  • MCP and hooks have capability/trust/approval review before side effects or activation.
  • Automation remains candidate-only until manual stability evidence exists.
  • Model/reasoning policy is explicit for durable agents/workflows.
  • Memory is not used as source of mandatory project truth.
  • Final claims cite current evidence.

docs.title: Типовые сбои
docs.text:
• Chat contains real requirements while project artifacts stay stale.
  • AGENTS.md becomes vague, obsolete or filled with one-off instructions.
  • Subagents edit overlapping files without ownership.
  • Handoffs omit source constraints, assumptions, evidence or stop conditions.
  • Skills are created from ideas without successful manual workflow evidence.
  • Plugins are packaged before permissions, evals and owner/update loop exist.
  • MCP tools are treated as safe even when they expose side effects.
  • Hooks are enabled without trust review or failure-mode documentation.
  • Automations are scheduled before prompt/tools are stable.
  • Memory stores context that should be checked into docs, or contains private/secrets material.
  • Completion is claimed from inspection-only evidence.
  • Agents SDK concepts are copied into Codex runtime docs without distinguishing runtime layers.

docs.title: Unsupported claims not adopted
docs.text:
• "Memory is project source of truth." Memory is recall only; durable rules and evidence belong in files.
  • "Subagents are automatically faster." They help only when work is independent and ownership is clear.
  • "MCP tools are safe because they are tools." MCP can expose data and side effects and needs trust review.
  • "Hooks are just convenience scripts." Hooks are executable policy and need approval, failure behavior and disable path.
  • "A repeated workflow should become automation immediately." Automation follows manual stability and first-run review.
  • "Agents SDK and Codex runtime are the same layer." Agents SDK is for code-owned agent apps; Codex App/CLI/IDE is the engineering runtime.

docs.title: Open questions for future implementation
docs.text:
• Which maturity labels should Product-Agent OS use: manual, repeatable, skill, plugin, automation, managed?
  • Should runtime routing be a single decision matrix or split by use-case archetype?
  • Which subagent tasks require worktrees by default?
  • Should MCP permission review be generated for every MCP config change or only side-effecting capabilities?
  • How should skill trigger tests and negative trigger tests be stored?
  • Which agent eval cases are enough before promoting a workflow to plugin or automation?

docs.title: Database & Data
docs.text:
Source status: official + expert reference + vendor documentation + local implementation evidence + tool-assisted

Источники: PostgreSQL Transaction Isolation, PostgreSQL Backup and Restore, PostgreSQL Constraints, PostgreSQL Indexes, PostgreSQL EXPLAIN, Liquibase core concepts, Liquibase rollback, Flyway migrations, dbt data tests, dbt model contracts, Great Expectations, OpenLineage, NIST Privacy Framework, Evolutionary Database Design, Prisma expand/contract pattern, Context7 research, research dossier.

docs.title: Deep research цель
docs.text:
Database & Data слой описывает schema ownership, migrations, constraints, indexes, transactions, backfills, data quality, privacy classification, retention, lineage, backup/restore and production data access.

Главный принцип: data change нельзя считать завершенным, если понятен SQL или ORM diff, но не понятны production impact, rollback/compensation, backup/restore path, data quality checks, privacy boundary and performance evidence.

docs.title: Поддержанные факты
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL transaction isolation documentation describes Read Committed, Repeatable Read and Serializable behavior, including serialization failure retry requirements for stronger isolation levels.
  • PostgreSQL constraints documentation defines integrity mechanisms such as check, not-null, unique, primary key, foreign key and exclusion constraints.
  • PostgreSQL indexes and EXPLAIN documentation support performance review through index design and query-plan evidence. EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the statement, so write statements require transaction/rollback care.
  • PostgreSQL backup and restore documentation separates SQL dump and file-system-level backup approaches; production database work needs restore evidence, not only "backups exist".
  • Liquibase documents changelogs as ordered changesets tracked in DATABASECHANGELOG, and supports rollback definitions, preconditions, contexts and labels.
  • Flyway documents version-controlled migrations, versioned and repeatable migration concepts, dry-run/deployment reports and schema history.
  • dbt data tests are SQL assertions that return failing rows; zero failing rows means the assertion passes. dbt model contracts define and enforce model column names and data types.
  • Great Expectations defines executable Expectations for completeness, schema, uniqueness, validity, volume and custom SQL checks.
  • OpenLineage defines an open standard around dataset, job and run entities for data lineage.
  • NIST Privacy Framework supports privacy requirements, profiles, SDLC alignment and data-processing ecosystem risk management.
  • Evolutionary Database Design describes small version-controlled migration scripts, application changes in CI/deployment pipelines and transition phases for destructive changes.
  • Expand/contract migration introduces new structures in parallel, updates writes, backfills, validates, switches reads/writes and removes old structures after compatibility.

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• Product-Agent OS should not mandate PostgreSQL, Liquibase, Flyway, dbt, Great Expectations or OpenLineage. These provide vocabulary and candidate artifacts; actual tools come from project inventory.
  • Data work is risky when it touches production data, destructive changes, sensitive fields, external consumers, analytics, AI/RAG sources, public APIs or high-volume backfills.
  • Migration rollback can be reversible, compensating or irreversible. It is unsafe to call a destructive migration rollback-safe without evidence.
  • Manual SQL can be operational evidence, but it cannot be the only durable record for schema/data changes.
  • Production data must not appear in docs, prompts, examples, fixtures or templates.
  • Data quality checks must be repeatable. Ad hoc SQL in a chat thread is not enough for a long-lived project gate.

docs.title: Инструкции применения на проекте
docs.text:
1. Классифицируйте работу: schema change, data migration, backfill, retention/deletion, data quality, query/index performance, analytics model, lineage, backup/restore or production data access.
  2. Назовите database engine, environment, owner, data domain and schema/migration source of truth.
  3. Зафиксируйте, затрагивает ли change production data, PII/sensitive fields, external consumers, analytics, AI/RAG sources or public APIs.
  4. Для любого schema/backfill/retention change создайте database-migration-plan.md before implementation.
  5. Держите migrations small, ordered, version-controlled and repeatable; manual production SQL не должен быть единственным record.
  6. Для live/shared systems применяйте expand/contract или другой compatibility-preserving rollout before destructive changes.
  7. Для multi-step writes/backfills опишите transaction boundary, isolation assumptions, lock impact, retry behavior and idempotency.
  8. Для constraints and indexes опишите invariant/query, deployment impact and verification evidence.
  9. Для performance-sensitive changes приложите query plan evidence and expected runtime/lock budget.
  10. Для backfills опишите batch size, resume key, throttling, validation counts, observability and abort behavior.
  11. Классифицируйте rollback как reversible, compensating or irreversible. Irreversible change требует owner acceptance.
  12. Для production data заранее подтвердите backup/restore path and restore evidence.
  13. Классифицируйте PII/sensitive fields до docs, prompts, fixtures and examples. Production data cannot be copied into examples.
  14. Добавьте executable data quality checks для primary keys, nullability, relationships, accepted values, counts and critical business assertions.
  15. Для analytics or AI/RAG pipelines опишите data contracts and lineage или explicit gap.
  16. Для production data access требуйте approval, least privilege, audit trail and no-secrets/no-customer-data evidence.

docs.title: Применяемые методологии разработки
docs.text: Методология Когда применять Как выглядит в проекте Evolutionary Database Design Product schema evolves continuously Small versioned migrations, application changes and tests move together through CI/CD. Migration-first planning Schema, backfill or retention change database-migration-plan.md exists before execution. Expand/contract migration Live systems, shared DB, public consumers, destructive changes Add new structure, dual-write/backfill, switch reads/writes, remove old structure after compatibility window. Database DevOps / migrations-as-code Team-owned DB changes Migrations are versioned, reviewed, repeatable and automated. Data integrity by constraint Relational correctness matters Constraints, keys and indexes are explicit design artifacts. Transaction and concurrency design Multi-step writes, financial/accounting/state workflows Isolation level, locks, retries and idempotency are documented. Data quality gates Critical product, analytics or AI/RAG data Executable assertions validate keys, nulls, relationships, counts, drift and business rules. Data contracts Data model has consumers Columns, types, semantics, compatibility and owner are explicit. Privacy-by-design PII/sensitive/regulated data Classification, minimization, retention, deletion and access boundary are captured early. Backup/restore-first change management Production or irreversible data work Restore path and restore drill evidence exist before risky execution. Lineage-aware data operations Analytics, reporting, ML/RAG, cross-system movement Dataset/job/run lineage is captured or marked as a gap. Performance-by-design Indexes, heavy queries, high-volume backfills Query plan, lock/runtime budget and index impact are reviewed. Production data access control Agent/developer touches prod data Approval, least privilege, audit trail and no-secrets/no-customer-data policy are enforced.

docs.title: Инструменты, артефакты и стандарты документирования
docs.text: Артефакт Зачем нужен Практический формат database-inventory.md Databases, owners, environments, engines, connection boundaries and data domains. Product-Agent OS template. database-dictionary.md Tables/collections, fields, types, business meaning, owner, sensitivity and retention. DBML, dbdocs, SchemaSpy, Markdown. Schema source of truth Machine-readable schema or migration history used for review. Migrations, DBML, ORM schema, SQL DDL. database-migration-plan.md Change intent, ordered steps, dry-run, validation, rollout, rollback/compensation and approvals. Migration plan. database-expand-contract-record.md Parallel structures, dual-write/read switch, cleanup and compatibility window. ADR or migration record. database-backfill-runbook.md Batching, idempotency, resume, throttling, progress, validation and abort behavior. Runbook. database-rollback-feasibility.md Reversible, compensating or irreversible classification with owner acceptance. Rollback record. database-backup-restore-evidence.md Backup source, restore drill, restore target, RPO/RTO and verification result. DB/platform docs and runbook. database-data-classification-matrix.md PII/sensitive fields, legal basis, access boundary, retention and deletion behavior. NIST Privacy Framework profile. database-data-quality-checks.md Executable checks for keys, nulls, relationships, accepted values, counts and drift. dbt tests, Great Expectations, SQL checks. database-data-contract.md Consumer-facing data model columns, types, meaning, compatibility and owner. dbt model contracts or Markdown. database-lineage-map.md Datasets, jobs, runs, sources, sinks and owners. OpenLineage or data catalog. database-query-performance-review.md Query plan, index choices, cardinality, lock impact and expected runtime. PostgreSQL EXPLAIN, stack-native tooling. database-retention-deletion-policy.md What is retained, where, how long, deletion path and audit evidence. Privacy profile / compliance policy. database-synthetic-fixtures-policy.md Safe fixture generation, anonymization limits and prohibition on production secrets/data. docs.title: Product-Agent OS routing
docs.text:
• data_migration usage mode routes schema/data changes to migration planning before implementation.
  • workspace-discovery-auditor detects migrations, ORM schemas, SQL, dbt/GX/OpenLineage signals and production-data risk.
  • requirements-author records data ownership, consumer impact, privacy constraints and accepted gaps.
  • implementation-planner blocks risky data work when migration plan, rollback classification, backup/restore or validation evidence is missing.
  • test-eval-designer selects migration dry-run, integration tests, data quality checks, query-plan checks and fixture safety checks.
  • risk-reviewer handles PII/sensitive fields, destructive migration, production access, irreversible change and performance risk.
  • pr-release-operator includes migration notes, restore/rollback guidance, data quality evidence and operational runbook impact.

docs.title: Candidate readiness gates
docs.text:
• database_schema_source_present: schema/migration source of truth is named.
  • database_migration_plan_present: ordered steps, validation, rollout and owner are documented.
  • database_expand_contract_reviewed: live/shared/destructive change has compatibility plan and cleanup window.
  • database_transaction_boundary_present: isolation, locks, retry and idempotency are documented for multi-step writes.
  • database_backup_restore_evidence_present: production/high-risk change has backup/restore path and restore evidence.
  • database_rollback_feasibility_present: reversible/compensating/irreversible classification exists.
  • database_data_classification_present: PII/sensitive fields have classification, retention and access boundary.
  • database_data_quality_contract_present: executable quality checks or explicit gap exists.
  • database_performance_review_present: query/index/backfill changes include plan, lock and runtime evidence.
  • database_lineage_present: analytics or AI/RAG data movement has sources, jobs, sinks and owners.
  • database_production_access_approval_present: production data access is approval-bound and auditable.
  • database_synthetic_fixture_policy_present: examples/fixtures are synthetic and secret-free.

docs.title: Candidate eval fields
docs.text:
• Database engine, owner and environment are named.
  • Schema/migration source of truth is linked.
  • Migration plan has ordered steps, dry-run and validation commands.
  • Backfill plan includes batching, idempotency, resume and progress evidence.
  • Rollback feasibility is classified as reversible, compensating or irreversible.
  • Backup/restore evidence exists for production or high-risk changes.
  • PII/sensitive fields are classified and examples are synthetic.
  • Data quality checks are executable or the tooling gap is explicit.
  • Query/index changes include plan evidence and lock/runtime notes.
  • Data lineage is documented for analytics or AI/RAG data movement.
  • Production data access is approval-bound and auditable.

docs.title: Tooling candidates
docs.text: Tooling area Candidate Notes Relational source reference PostgreSQL docs Useful for transaction, constraint, index, query-plan and backup vocabulary. Migration management Liquibase Changelog/changeset model, rollback, preconditions, contexts and labels. Migration management Flyway Versioned/repeatable migrations, schema history, dry-run reports and validation. Stack-native migration signals alembic.ini, schema.prisma, Rails/Django migrations Discovery signals; tool choice follows project inventory. Schema documentation DBML, dbdocs, SchemaSpy Useful for dictionaries and relationship maps; requires secret-safe generation. Data tests/contracts dbt Strong fit for warehouse/analytics models, data tests and model contracts. Data quality Great Expectations Executable Expectations for data quality and multi-source comparisons. Data lineage OpenLineage Open standard model for dataset/job/run lineage. Privacy governance NIST Privacy Framework Useful vocabulary for privacy profiles, SDLC alignment and data-processing ecosystem roles. Query performance EXPLAIN, DB-native tooling Attach evidence; avoid side-effecting analysis without transaction safety.

docs.title: Проверки
docs.text:
• Migration plan exists before schema/data execution.
  • Dry-run or staging migration command is named with expected output.
  • Validation checks include counts and semantic business assertions.
  • Backfill has batching, idempotency, resume and progress evidence.
  • Rollback feasibility is explicit; irreversible risk is accepted by owner.
  • Backup/restore evidence exists for production data work.
  • Sensitive fields are classified and examples are synthetic.
  • Query/index changes have query-plan and lock/runtime review.
  • Data quality checks are executable or tooling gap is recorded.
  • Production data access has approval and audit evidence.

docs.title: Типовые сбои
docs.text:
• Manual production SQL is the only record of a change.
  • ORM schema and real database constraints drift silently.
  • Index is added without lock/write-impact and query-plan review.
  • Column is dropped or renamed before consumers move.
  • Migration is called rollback-safe despite data loss.
  • Backfill has no batching, idempotency or resume key.
  • Validation checks count rows but miss semantic equivalence.
  • EXPLAIN ANALYZE is run on writes without transaction/rollback control.
  • Production data leaks into fixtures, prompts, examples or docs.
  • Backup exists but restore was never tested.
  • Data quality checks are ad hoc queries, not repeatable gates.
  • Analytics or AI/RAG lineage is unknown after an incident.
  • Agent receives broad production database access instead of scoped approval.

docs.title: Unsupported claims not adopted
docs.text:
• "ORM schema is the database source of truth." It can be one source, but real constraints, migrations and database state must not drift silently.
  • "Migration applied means migration safe." Safety requires dry-run/staging, validation, rollback/compensation and owner review.
  • "Rollback is just down migration." Destructive data changes may require compensation or explicit irreversible acceptance.
  • "Backups exist, so restore is safe." Restore path needs evidence, not assumption.
  • "Data quality can be checked manually." Long-lived product data needs repeatable checks or explicit tooling gap.
  • "Anonymized production data is safe by default." Synthetic fixtures are safer; anonymization needs privacy review.
  • "Analytics/RAG data lineage can be reconstructed later." Lineage gaps become expensive during incidents and deletion requests.

docs.title: Open questions for future implementation
docs.text:
• Which migration tool defaults should Product-Agent OS recommend by stack: Alembic, Prisma Migrate, Rails migrations, Django migrations, Liquibase, Flyway or framework-neutral?
  • Should database readiness gates live only under data methodology, or also gate backend/API/LLM workflows when data changes are detected?
  • Which schema-diff tools are mature enough to recommend without encouraging unsafe auto-migration behavior?
  • How should Product-Agent OS detect destructive migrations from SQL/ORM diffs?
  • Should the plugin ship default data-quality templates for dbt/GX, or only generic SQL checks?
  • How should RAG ingestion lineage and data retention connect to database methodology and LLM methodology?

docs.title: Delivery, Release & Operations
docs.text:
Source status: official + verified methodology + vendor documentation + tool-assisted + experiment

Источники: DORA software delivery performance metrics, Google SRE SLO chapter, Google SRE Release Engineering, Google SRE Postmortem Culture, OpenTelemetry documentation, Twelve-Factor App, GitHub Actions workflows, GitHub deployments and environments, GitHub Releases, Keep a Changelog, Semantic Versioning, Conventional Commits, CNCF GitOps, Argo Rollouts, OpenFeature, Codex verified operations, Context7 research, research dossier.

docs.title: Deep research цель
docs.text:
Delivery, Release & Operations слой описывает how the system ships, runs, recovers and learns. Для большого проекта release readiness не равен passing tests: нужны scope, owner, version impact, artifacts, rollout, rollback, observability, approvals, incident path and post-release learning.

Главный принцип: release/deploy/publish work сначала собирает auditable evidence packet, потом делает external action. Нельзя tag, publish, create release, upload artifact, deploy, mutate package registry, open PR, push branch, submit to marketplace/store or activate automation без explicit approval and rollback/recovery path.

docs.title: Поддержанные факты
docs.text:
• DORA metrics define delivery performance through change lead time, deployment frequency, failed deployment recovery time, change fail rate and deployment rework rate.
  • Google SRE guidance treats SLOs as user-relevant reliability targets and release engineering as a discipline for repeatable, auditable releases.
  • OpenTelemetry provides cross-stack vocabulary for traces, metrics and logs as runtime release evidence.
  • GitHub Actions workflows, environments and deployments define release controls such as triggers, permissions, required reviewers, wait timers, branch/tag restrictions and environment secrets.
  • Keep a Changelog, Semantic Versioning and Conventional Commits provide compatible but different release communication and versioning practices.
  • CNCF GitOps and Argo Rollouts support desired-state operations and progressive delivery concepts such as canary, blue-green, promotion and rollback.
  • OpenFeature gives a feature-flag vocabulary for runtime rollout, targeting and kill-switch behavior.
  • Codex verified operations supports approval-bound, auditable operational workflows before external actions.

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• Release readiness is broader than tests passing; it includes scope, owner, version impact, artifacts, rollout, rollback, observability, approvals and post-release learning.
  • External release actions should be staged or draft-first until approval boundary and rollback path are explicit.
  • DORA metrics are for process learning, not individual quotas.
  • Feature flags and progressive delivery reduce blast radius only when owner, cleanup, observability and abort criteria exist.
  • Automation promotion is unsafe without manual success evidence, stable inputs/outputs, owner, verification and disable path.

docs.title: Инструкции применения на проекте
docs.text:
1. Классифицировать release work до реализации. Triggers: publish, deploy, tag, GitHub Release, artifact upload, package registry, marketplace, app store, installer, SDK, plugin, public API, migration release, CI workflow mutation, production config, automation promotion.
  2. Держать external release actions read-only/staged, пока release scope, owner, target, approval boundary, version impact, evidence, rollback and residual risk не стали explicit.
  3. Определить release type: internal deploy, public package, SDK, plugin, app, desktop installer, mobile build, docs release, model/prompt release, database migration, infrastructure change or automation candidate.
  4. Для public API/package/plugin/SDK/app release фиксировать SemVer impact или explicit non-SemVer policy.
  5. Держать changelog и release notes раздельно, если это помогает: changelog фиксирует notable changes, release notes объясняют user impact, migration, compatibility and known issues.
  6. Не заявлять release readiness from inspection-only evidence. Нужны current build/test/docs/eval/runtime/artifact evidence или explicit gap.
  7. Для artifacts фиксировать filenames, versions, creation command, storage location, retention and integrity notes where applicable.
  8. Для deployable services разделять build, release and run stages, либо явно фиксировать accepted platform exception.
  9. Для production services определить SLIs/SLOs или explicit accepted gap.
  10. Для runtime release определить observability evidence: logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, alert owner, redaction and expected post-release signals.
  11. Определить rollout strategy: immediate release, release train, staged rollout, feature flag, canary, blue-green, shadow traffic or manual promotion.
  12. Определить stop criteria and rollback/recovery path before release: revert, redeploy previous artifact, disable flag, unpublish, restore backup, compensate data or incident mitigation.
  13. Для GitHub Actions/CI/CD changes фиксировать triggers, permissions, environments, required reviewers, branch/tag rules, secrets, artifacts, concurrency and external action pinning.
  14. Для GitHub deployment environments считать required reviewers, wait timers, branch/tag restrictions, custom protection rules and environment secrets release controls.
  15. Для GitOps-style workflows фиксировать desired state source, reconciliation controller, drift behavior, approval path and rollback/revert behavior.
  16. Для progressive delivery фиксировать cohorts, traffic weights, health checks, analysis metrics, manual judgement, promotion/abort rules and blast radius.
  17. Для feature flags фиксировать default value, owner, targeting rules, cleanup date, observability, kill-switch behavior and failure mode.
  18. Для incidents и failed releases создавать incident record and postmortem, когда impact criteria выполнены; не скрывать failed deploys из learning loop.
  19. Для DORA metrics фиксировать definitions and measurement source. Использовать trends for process improvement, not individual performance.
  20. Promote recurring release/ops workflows only after manual success evidence, stable inputs/outputs, owner, approval requirements, verification and rollback/disable path exist.

docs.title: Применяемые методологии разработки
docs.text: Методология Когда применять Как выглядит в проекте Release engineering Packages, apps, services, plugins, SDKs, installers, docs releases Release scope, reproducible build, artifacts, version impact, owner, approvals and release process. Continuous delivery discipline Frequent changes, shared branches, deployment pipeline Small batches, automated checks, release candidates, environment promotion, rollback/recovery path. DORA measurement Team wants delivery performance trend Change lead time, deployment frequency, failed deployment recovery time, change fail rate, deployment rework rate. SRE / SLO-driven operations Runtime service has availability, latency or support expectations SLIs/SLOs, error-budget thinking, alerts, runbooks and incident response. Observability-driven release Runtime behavior must be diagnosable OpenTelemetry-style traces, metrics, logs, dashboards, alert owners and redaction policy. Progressive delivery Release blast radius must be controlled Feature flags, staged rollout, canary, blue-green, traffic shifting, manual judgement and automated rollback. GitOps / desired-state operations Declarative infra/app state is managed via source control Desired state, reconciliation mechanism, drift handling, approval and rollback are documented. CI/CD governance Workflow can publish, deploy, access secrets or mutate environments Triggers, permissions, environments, reviewers, branch/tag rules, artifacts and external action policy. Versioning and changelog discipline Public API, package, SDK, plugin, app or docs release SemVer impact, compatibility/deprecation notes, changelog categories and user-facing release notes. Incident response and postmortem learning Production incident, failed deployment, user-impacting regression Incident record, timeline, mitigation, root causes, action items, owner and follow-up review. Automation promotion Repeated operations may become automation Manual success evidence, stable inputs/outputs, owner, verification, approval and rollback/disable path.

docs.title: Инструменты, артефакты и стандарты документирования
docs.text:
• release-readiness.md: scope, owner, version, SemVer impact, evidence, artifacts, approval, rollback, residual risk.
  • release-packet.md: PR/release summary, user impact, checks, risks, docs changes, finish options.
  • deployment-plan.md: target environment, release candidate, deploy command, approval, rollout window, stop criteria.
  • rollout-plan.md: feature flag, canary, blue-green, staged percentage, cohort, traffic split, promotion/abort rules.
  • rollback-recovery-plan.md: revert, disable flag, rollback deployment, unpublish, restore, data compensation, mitigation.
  • environment-matrix.md: dev/stage/prod/local/mobile/store/registry targets, secrets, branch/tag rules, owner.
  • ci-cd-workflow-inventory.md: jobs, triggers, permissions, secrets, artifacts, caches, concurrency, external actions.
  • versioning-policy.md: SemVer, calendar versioning, prerelease, deprecation, compatibility, support window.
  • CHANGELOG.md: Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security sections.
  • release-notes.md: user impact, migration steps, compatibility, known issues, support contact.
  • release-artifact-manifest.md: build outputs, hashes/signatures, SBOM/provenance notes, storage, retention.
  • observability-map.md: dashboards, traces, logs, metrics, alert owners, redaction, sampling notes.
  • slo-spec.md: user journey, SLI, SLO, measurement source, alert policy, accepted gap.
  • operations-runbook.md: deploy, rollback, first response, escalation, common failures, diagnostics.
  • incident-record.md: timeline, impact, mitigation, communications, owner, follow-up tasks.
  • postmortem.md: impact, detection, root causes, contributing factors, action items, review status.
  • automation-candidate.md: manual stability evidence, trigger/cadence, write policy, verification, disable path.
  • post-release-review.md: actual metrics, defects, support signals, latency/cost, feedback, next decision.

docs.title: Что еще включить в deep research
docs.text:
• Maturity levels: baseline, team, production, regulated.
  • Release types: docs-only, internal app, production service, public package, plugin, SDK, desktop installer, mobile app, AI model/prompt release, infrastructure release, data migration.
  • Release train vs continuous deployment vs manual approval policy.
  • Feature flag lifecycle: owner, default, cohort, cleanup, kill switch, observability, debt removal.
  • Progressive delivery decision policy: when simple release is enough and when canary/blue-green/manual promotion is required.
  • GitHub environments policy: required reviewers, wait timers, branch/tag restrictions, secrets, custom protection rules.
  • Artifact integrity policy: checksums, signatures, SBOM/provenance, storage and retention by release type.
  • Incident severity and postmortem triggers: user-visible degradation, data loss, rollback, manual intervention, monitoring failure.
  • DORA measurement design: source of data, team scope, anti-Goodhart warning, interpretation cadence.
  • Automation promotion path: manual thread -> playbook -> skill -> plugin -> automation, with disable/rollback path.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS routing
docs.text:
• workspace-discovery-auditor detects release packaging signals: package metadata, versions, changelog, build evidence, test evidence, docs evidence, security/license notes, artifacts, rollback, owner review and publish approval.
  • requirements-author records release target, user impact, compatibility, operational constraints, approval boundary and post-release measurement.
  • implementation-planner blocks plan-ready status when release scope, version impact, evidence, rollout, rollback, environment approval or ownership is missing.
  • test-eval-designer defines release evidence: build/test/docs/eval/runtime checks, artifact verification, smoke checks, rollback verification and post-release monitoring.
  • risk-reviewer checks release risk, unsupported readiness claims, external action approvals, migration/security/data impacts and residual risk.
  • pr-release-operator prepares release packet, changelog/release notes, finish options and staged external action plan.
  • learning-loop-maintainer records release outcomes, failures, DORA/post-release signals and postmortem follow-ups.
  • automation-promoter can only create candidate-only automation after manual release/ops workflow stability is evidenced.

docs.title: Candidate readiness gates
docs.text:
• release_scope_present: release type, target, owner and external boundary are explicit.
  • release_evidence_present: current build, test, docs, eval, runtime or artifact evidence exists.
  • version_impact_present: SemVer/non-SemVer policy, compatibility impact and deprecation notes are documented.
  • changelog_release_notes_present: changelog/release notes include user impact, migration, compatibility and known issues where applicable.
  • artifact_manifest_present: artifact names, versions, creation command, storage and integrity notes are present.
  • rollout_strategy_present: strategy, cohorts/traffic, promotion, abort criteria and blast radius are explicit.
  • rollback_recovery_present: revert, redeploy, flag disable, unpublish, restore, compensation or mitigation path is executable.
  • environment_approval_boundary_present: approval, branch/tag rule, secret boundary and external-write policy are explicit.
  • ci_cd_governance_present: triggers, permissions, secrets, artifacts, caches, concurrency and external action policy are reviewed.
  • observability_release_evidence_present: logs, metrics, traces, dashboard, alert owner and redaction notes exist where applicable.
  • slo_or_operational_gap_present: SLIs/SLOs or explicit accepted gap exists for production service.
  • operations_runbook_present: deploy, rollback, first response, escalation and diagnostics are documented.
  • incident_response_path_present: incident criteria, owner, communication path and postmortem trigger are present.
  • post_release_measurement_present: metrics, support signals, defects, latency/cost or review date are defined.
  • external_release_approval_present: tag, publish, release creation, artifact upload, deployment, PR, push, package registry, marketplace or store action has explicit approval and rollback/unpublish path.
  • automation_manual_stability_present: manual success evidence, stable inputs/outputs, owner, verification and disable path exist before automation.
  • release_evidence_before_completion: any release-ready/works/deployed/published claim cites current evidence or explicit gap.

docs.title: Candidate eval fields
docs.text:
• Release scope, target, owner and external boundary are present.
  • Current build/test/docs/eval/runtime/artifact evidence is linked.
  • Version impact and compatibility/deprecation notes are documented.
  • Changelog and release notes include user impact and migration guidance where applicable.
  • Artifact manifest includes names, versions, creation command, storage and integrity notes.
  • Rollout strategy includes cohorts/traffic, promotion, abort criteria and blast radius.
  • Rollback/recovery path is executable for this release type.
  • CI/CD governance includes triggers, permissions, secrets, artifacts, caches, concurrency and approvals.
  • Observability evidence includes logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, alert owner and redaction notes.
  • External release action has explicit approval and rollback/unpublish path.

docs.title: Tooling candidates
docs.text: Tooling area Candidate Notes Delivery metrics DORA Trend-level process improvement; avoid individual performance use. Reliability target SLO/SLI sheet User journey, measurement source, alerting and accepted gap. CI/CD governance GitHub Actions environments Required reviewers, wait timers, branch/tag restrictions, environment secrets. Release communication Keep a Changelog, SemVer, Conventional Commits Use each for its appropriate layer: change categories, version impact, commit signal. GitOps Desired-state source + reconciliation controller Requires drift, approval and rollback model. Progressive delivery Argo Rollouts or platform equivalent Canary, blue-green, analysis, promotion and abort behavior. Feature flags OpenFeature or platform equivalent Owner, targeting, cleanup, kill switch and observability. Operations docs runbook.md, slo.md, release-readiness.md Common local filenames and templates for release evidence. Package signals package.json, pyproject.toml, go.mod, mkdocs.yml Discovery signals for versioning/build/release impact. Verified operations Codex verified operations Approval-bound, auditable external actions and retries.

docs.title: Проверки
docs.text:
• Release scope, target, owner and external boundary are explicit.
  • Release readiness cites current build/test/docs/eval/runtime/artifact evidence or explicit gaps.
  • Version impact and compatibility/deprecation notes are documented.
  • Changelog/release notes are user-facing and not only commit summaries.
  • Artifact manifest includes version, location, creation command and integrity notes where relevant.
  • Rollout strategy includes promotion, abort and blast-radius control.
  • Rollback/recovery path is executable for this release type.
  • GitHub Actions/CI/CD changes include triggers, permissions, secrets, environments, approvals and artifacts.
  • Observability evidence includes traces, metrics, logs, dashboards, alert owner and redaction notes where applicable.
  • SLO or operational gap is explicit for production services.
  • Incident and postmortem criteria are defined for runtime releases.
  • Post-release measurement links actual signals back to product/reliability hypothesis.
  • External publish/tag/deploy/upload/PR/push/store actions remain approval-bound.
  • Automation candidate remains candidate-only until manual stability evidence exists.

docs.title: Типовые сбои
docs.text:
• Release readiness is claimed from code inspection or passing local tests only.
  • Release notes summarize commits but omit user impact and migration guidance.
  • SemVer bump ignores public API, generated client, plugin or data compatibility.
  • Rollback is named but cannot recover the actual release target.
  • Package publish, tag, release creation, artifact upload, deployment or store submission happens without explicit approval.
  • CI workflow change silently expands permissions, secrets access or deployment triggers.
  • Feature flag ships without owner, cleanup date or kill-switch behavior.
  • Progressive delivery relies on health checks that do not represent user/business outcomes.
  • Observability is added after release, so no runtime evidence exists during incident response.
  • DORA metrics become quotas or individual performance metrics.
  • Postmortem is skipped because the release was rolled back quickly.
  • Automation is activated before manual workflow stability is proven.

docs.title: Unsupported claims not adopted
docs.text:
• "Tests passed, so release is ready." Release readiness also requires artifact, rollout, rollback, observability and approval evidence.
  • "Rollback is just revert." Some releases need unpublish, redeploy, flag disable, restore or compensation.
  • "Feature flags remove release risk." They need owner, kill switch, observability and cleanup.
  • "DORA metrics prove individual performance." They are process metrics and should not be used as personal quotas.
  • "Automation is safer because it is repeatable." Repeatability without approvals and disable path can repeat damage.

docs.title: Open questions for future implementation
docs.text:
• Which release maturity labels should Product-Agent OS use: baseline, team, production, regulated?
  • Which release types need separate templates: docs-only, package, plugin, SDK, desktop/mobile, AI prompt/model, infrastructure or data migration?
  • When should progressive delivery be required instead of simple release?
  • Which artifact integrity evidence should be default: checksums, signatures, SBOM, provenance or none for docs-only releases?
  • How should incident severity and postmortem triggers be encoded for small projects?
  • Should DORA measurement live in delivery docs, metrics docs or both?

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
Source status: official + verified methodology + tool-assisted + experiment

Источники: Feature-Sliced Design, FSD Public API, Storybook Autodocs, Storybook interaction tests, Storybook visual tests, Storybook accessibility testing, Playwright visual comparisons, Playwright Trace Viewer, WCAG 2.2, WAI-ARIA APG, Testing Library guiding principles, MDN accessible HTML, MDN media queries, web.dev Web Vitals, web.dev INP, Context7 research, research dossier.

docs.title: Deep research цель
docs.text:
Frontend слой фиксирует, как строить UI behavior, route/page flows, component boundaries, design-system usage, accessibility, responsive states, visual verification, browser/runtime evidence и performance так, чтобы UI changes были понятны людям и проверяемы агентами.

Главный принцип: frontend-изменение нельзя считать завершенным после code inspection. Для UI нужны user-flow acceptance, documented states, responsive/accessibility coverage и текущие browser/runtime evidence или явно записанный verification gap.

docs.title: Поддержанные факты
docs.text:
• Feature-Sliced Design defines layers and public API boundaries for frontend structure when feature/business slicing reduces coupling.
  • Storybook Autodocs, interaction tests, visual tests and accessibility testing can serve as component documentation and verification surfaces.
  • Playwright supports screenshots, visual comparisons and Trace Viewer for browser runtime evidence.
  • WCAG 2.2, WAI-ARIA APG, semantic HTML guidance and Testing Library principles support user-observable accessibility and interaction checks.
  • Web Vitals and Interaction to Next Paint (INP) give frontend performance vocabulary for user-facing and interaction-heavy routes.
  • Frontend evidence must include visible states, responsive states, keyboard/focus behavior, console/runtime status and privacy-safe screenshots where applicable.

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• Product-Agent OS will not require one frontend framework. React/Next.js, Vue/Nuxt, Svelte/SvelteKit, Angular and framework-neutral HTML/CSS/JS need the same behavior-level contract with stack-specific commands.
  • Storybook is a strong component documentation and verification surface, but it should be conditional: required for design systems and reusable components, optional for small one-off UI.
  • Feature-Sliced Design is useful when layer/slice boundaries reduce coupling; it is not a default folder template for every MVP.
  • Automated accessibility checks are necessary but incomplete. Keyboard flow, focus behavior, accessible names, semantic controls and error announcements still need user-observable evidence.
  • Visual evidence must be privacy-safe. Screenshots, stories and mock data must not include secrets, private customer data or raw private payloads.

docs.title: Инструкции применения на проекте
docs.text:
1. Классифицировать работу: route/page, component, design-system primitive, layout, interaction, state, data-fetching UI, accessibility fix или performance fix.
  2. Начинать с user flow: цель пользователя, экран/route, acceptance scenario и видимые state transitions.
  3. До реализации назвать UI states: default, loading, skeleton, empty, error, validation error, success, disabled, permission denied, offline/stale, long content и responsive states.
  4. Если UI зависит от API/data, связать каждый видимый state с contract examples, auth/permission, error shape, pagination/cache/stale behavior.
  5. Сначала использовать существующий design system. Новый primitive, token или variant требует объяснения, почему текущих элементов недостаточно.
  6. Feature-Sliced Design применять условно: когда UI растет по features/business entities и слои реально снижают coupling. Не создавать пустые слои для маленького MVP.
  7. Если FSD применяется, фиксировать layer/slice, public API и допустимое направление imports.
  8. Storybook использовать как docs and verification surface для reusable components и design system: stories должны покрывать не только happy path, но loading, empty, error, disabled, focus и long-content states.
  9. Accessibility считать поведением продукта: keyboard path, focus visibility, accessible names, semantic controls, labels, error announcements и contrast проверяются или явно помечаются как gap.
  10. Для layout/visual work заранее задать responsive matrix: минимум узкий mobile viewport и desktop viewport; по риску добавить tablet, orientation, reduced motion, dark/theme variants.
  11. Для visual changes сохранять evidence через Playwright screenshots, Storybook visual tests или manual screenshots с browser/viewport notes.
  12. Для interaction changes предпочитать user-observable tests: role/name queries, keyboard input, click/tap, form submit, async state assertions.
  13. Для user-facing routes задавать Core Web Vitals budget или explicit non-applicability. Interaction-heavy screens отдельно проверять INP risk.
  14. Не помещать secrets, tokens, private customer data и реальные private payloads в UI examples, stories, screenshots, fixtures или mocks.
  15. Completion требует current runtime evidence: browser/dev-server check, console status, screenshots, Storybook build/test, Playwright trace или explicit verification gap.

docs.title: Применяемые методологии разработки
docs.text: Методология Когда применять Как выглядит в проекте User-flow-first UI development Любое user-visible UI изменение Экран, user goal, acceptance scenario и state paths заданы до component work. Component-driven development Reusable components, design system, repeated UI patterns Stories фиксируют props, variants, states, events, accessibility и examples. Design-system-driven development Есть tokens, shared components или brand rules Новая UI работа использует существующие primitives; extensions документируются. Conditional Feature-Sliced Design Frontend растет по features/business entities Layers/slices/public API/import rules применяются там, где уменьшают coupling. Accessibility-first / inclusive design Interactive, public, regulated, form-heavy или high-use UI WCAG/APG-oriented checks, keyboard/focus/labels/errors как acceptance criteria. Responsive/adaptive design UI работает в разных viewport/input contexts Viewport matrix, wrapping/truncation, touch/mouse/keyboard assumptions. Interaction-first testing Поведение зависит от user actions Тестируется observable behavior, а не component internals. Visual regression testing Layout/style может сломаться без unit failure Playwright/Storybook screenshots и stable baselines. Performance-by-design User-facing, high-traffic или interaction-heavy routes LCP/INP/CLS budget или явный gap; evidence собирается до release. API-contract-aware frontend development UI зависит от backend/API/feature flags/async data UI states привязаны к OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/Pact/examples/errors/cache behavior. State ownership design Form, cache, global или persistent state становится нетривиальным Local, route, server-cache, global и persisted state boundaries названы. Content and i18n-ready UI Long text, localization, user-generated content Проверены wrapping, truncation, pluralization, empty copy, RTL/locales where applicable. Evidence-before-completion Любая заявка “UI готов” Есть current browser/runtime/visual evidence или explicit verification gap.

docs.title: Инструменты, артефакты и стандарты документирования
docs.text:
• ui-flow-spec.md: user goal, route/screen, acceptance scenario, state paths.
  • route-page-inventory.md: routes, params, data dependencies, auth/permission, SEO/meta notes.
  • component-card.md: purpose, props, events, states, accessibility, linked API, owner.
  • component-state-matrix.md: default/loading/empty/error/success/disabled/focus/responsive/long-text states.
  • storybook-story-map.md: stories, variants, state coverage, Autodocs/MDX links.
  • design-system-inventory.md: tokens, components, variants, icons, typography, spacing, themes.
  • frontend-boundary-map.md / fsd-boundary-record.md: page/widget/feature/entity/shared boundary, public API, import constraints.
  • frontend-api-dependency-map.md: endpoint/query/mutation/event, contract examples, auth, errors, cache behavior.
  • responsive-viewport-matrix.md: desktop/tablet/mobile, orientation, input modality, reduced motion, theme.
  • accessibility-review.md: WCAG target or gap, semantic HTML, keyboard, focus, labels, names, errors, contrast.
  • keyboard-focus-map.md: tab order, trap/release, modal/menu/listbox/dialog behavior, visible focus.
  • visual-evidence-packet.md: screenshots, viewport list, browser/OS, console status, baseline reference.
  • frontend-interaction-test-matrix.md: user actions, expected state, accessible queries, async behavior.
  • frontend-performance-budget.md: LCP/INP/CLS target or non-applicability, measurement path, risk.
  • frontend-browser-support-matrix.md: supported browsers/devices, Playwright projects, known gaps.
  • frontend-content-i18n-record.md: long strings, localization, empty copy, pluralization, RTL, truncation.

docs.title: Что еще включить в deep research
docs.text:
• Stack-specific templates: React/Next.js, Vue/Nuxt, Svelte/SvelteKit, Angular, framework-neutral HTML/CSS/JS.
  • Design system governance: token owner, variant policy, icon policy, breaking component API changes.
  • Storybook adoption policy: when required, when optional, when too heavy for a small project.
  • Visual QA thresholds: what evidence is enough for tiny UI change, page redesign, design-system primitive and public route.
  • Accessibility risk levels: default WCAG 2.2 AA target vs product/legal risk-based level.
  • FSD auto-detection: imports, aliases, public API violations, cross-slice references.
  • Core Web Vitals measurement selector: Lighthouse, WebPageTest, Playwright trace, field RUM.
  • Browser/device support policy: desktop web, mobile web, embedded webview, Electron/desktop shell.
  • Data privacy for UI artifacts: screenshots, stories, mocks, generated fixtures and demo accounts.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS routing
docs.text:
• workspace-discovery-auditor detects frontend stack, routes, Storybook, Playwright, design system, FSD-like structure, test commands and browser/runtime constraints.
  • requirements-author captures user flow, acceptance scenario, accessibility expectations, supported viewports and content/i18n constraints.
  • implementation-planner blocks risky UI work when component states, design-system boundary, API contract or verification path is missing.
  • test-eval-designer selects Storybook, unit/component, Playwright, visual, accessibility, performance and manual browser checks.
  • risk-reviewer reviews public component APIs, accessibility gaps, design-system drift, screenshot privacy and performance risk.
  • docs-maintainer updates component cards, Storybook docs, visual evidence packet and methodology/source references.

docs.title: Candidate readiness gates
docs.text:
• frontend_user_flow_acceptance_present: user goal, route/screen and acceptance scenario are present.
  • frontend_component_state_matrix_present: loading, empty, error, disabled, focus, success, long-content and responsive states are documented where applicable.
  • frontend_component_docs_present: reusable component/design-system change has story, component card, Autodocs/MDX note or explicit docs gap.
  • frontend_design_system_boundary_present: design-system reuse or extension decision is recorded.
  • frontend_fsd_boundary_reviewed: FSD layer/slice/public API/import direction is clear when FSD applies.
  • frontend_api_contract_alignment_present: UI data dependency is tied to contract examples, auth, permission, errors and cache behavior.
  • frontend_accessibility_review_present: keyboard, focus, labels/names, semantic controls, errors and contrast are checked or marked as gap.
  • frontend_keyboard_focus_contract_present: dialog/menu/listbox/form/navigation focus behavior is specified.
  • frontend_responsive_viewport_matrix_present: mobile and desktop expectations are documented for layout/visual work.
  • frontend_visual_evidence_present: screenshot, Storybook visual baseline, Playwright evidence or explicit gap exists.
  • frontend_runtime_console_evidence_present: browser console/runtime status is checked where preview/dev server is available.
  • frontend_interaction_test_evidence_present: interaction change has user-observable test or manual evidence.
  • frontend_performance_budget_present: LCP/INP/CLS budget or explicit non-applicability is recorded.
  • frontend_browser_support_present: supported browsers/devices or known gaps are named.
  • frontend_content_i18n_boundary_present: long text, localization, user-generated content and truncation assumptions are documented.

docs.title: Candidate eval fields
docs.text:
• User flow, route/screen and acceptance scenario are present.
  • Component state matrix covers loading, empty, error, disabled, focus, success, long content and responsive states where applicable.
  • Reusable component has story, component card, Autodocs/MDX note or explicit docs gap.
  • Design-system reuse or extension decision is recorded.
  • FSD layer/slice/public API/import direction is clear when FSD applies.
  • UI data dependency links to contract examples, auth, permission, error and cache behavior.
  • Keyboard, focus, labels/names, semantic controls, errors and contrast are checked or marked as gap.
  • Visual/runtime evidence includes browser, viewport, console status and screenshot/trace where relevant.
  • Performance budget covers LCP/INP/CLS or explains non-applicability.
  • UI artifacts contain no secrets or private customer data.

docs.title: Tooling candidates
docs.text: Tooling area Candidate Notes Frontend structure Feature-Sliced Design Use only when layers/slices reduce real coupling; record public API rules. Component docs Storybook Autodocs / MDX Useful for reusable components and design-system primitives; autodocs signals generated component docs. Component interaction checks Storybook interaction tests Good for component states and user events; play functions are a Storybook interaction-test signal. Visual/runtime checks Playwright screenshots, Trace Viewer Browser evidence for layout, state, trace and console issues. Accessibility WCAG 2.2, WAI-ARIA APG, Testing Library, MDN Use semantic queries and user-observable behavior. Performance Web Vitals, INP, Lighthouse/RUM where available Choose field or lab measurement by release risk. Design-system docs design-tokens-reference.md, components.json Token and component registry when project uses generated UI metadata. Story coverage storybook-story-map.md, Autodocs Tracks story/state coverage and docs gaps.

docs.title: Проверки
docs.text:
• UI behavior maps to user flow and acceptance scenario.
  • Component state matrix is current or gap is explicit.
  • Storybook docs or component card exist for reusable components.
  • FSD public API/import rule is respected when FSD applies.
  • API/data contract examples cover loading, empty, error and permission states.
  • Keyboard/focus behavior is tested manually or automatically for interactive UI.
  • Responsive matrix covers at least one mobile and one desktop viewport for visual/layout work.
  • Visual/runtime check is current: Playwright, Storybook visual, browser screenshots or explicit gap.
  • Browser console has no relevant runtime errors where preview/dev server is available.
  • Performance budget covers LCP/INP/CLS for user-facing routes or explains non-applicability.

docs.title: Типовые сбои
docs.text:
• UI work starts from component hierarchy while user flow and acceptance scenario are vague.
  • Folder structure imitates FSD but imports violate layer or public API rules.
  • Storybook exists but only documents happy path.
  • Component docs list props but omit loading, empty, error, disabled, focus, long text and responsive states.
  • Accessibility is reduced to addon output; keyboard, focus, labels and semantic controls are not checked.
  • UI completion is claimed after code inspection only.
  • Screenshots cover desktop only and miss mobile, loading/error/empty, long text or theme variants.
  • Visual baselines are generated in unstable environments and create noisy diffs.
  • API data shape is assumed without contract examples, error shapes or permission states.
  • Design-system changes add new tokens/variants without owner review or migration notes.

docs.title: Unsupported claims not adopted
docs.text:
• "FSD should be mandatory for every frontend project." Not adopted; it is conditional on project size, coupling and ownership boundaries.
  • "Storybook proves UI quality by itself." Not adopted; stories need interaction, accessibility, visual/runtime evidence and state coverage.
  • "Automated a11y addon output is enough." Not adopted; keyboard, focus, semantic and error-announcement behavior remain acceptance concerns.
  • "A desktop screenshot proves responsive UI." Not adopted; mobile/desktop viewport matrix and relevant state coverage are required for layout work.
  • "Lab Web Vitals always represent production UX." Not adopted; lab checks are useful, but field/RUM evidence is preferred when release risk justifies it.

docs.title: Open questions for future implementation
docs.text:
• Which stack-specific templates should Product-Agent OS generate first: React/Next.js, Vue/Nuxt, Svelte/SvelteKit, Angular or framework-neutral HTML/CSS/JS?
  • When should Storybook be required, optional or too heavy for a small project?
  • What visual evidence is enough for a tiny UI change versus a page redesign or design-system primitive?
  • Should WCAG 2.2 AA be the default target for all public UI, with explicit exceptions?
  • How should FSD auto-detection flag import/public API violations?
  • Which Web Vitals measurement path should be recommended by default: Lighthouse, Playwright trace, WebPageTest or field RUM?

docs.title: LLM / AI / RAG
docs.text:
Source status: official + vendor documentation + tool-assisted + experiment

Источники: OpenAI Responses API, OpenAI text generation, OpenAI prompt engineering, OpenAI Structured Outputs, OpenAI function calling, OpenAI tools guide, OpenAI file search, OpenAI retrieval, OpenAI embeddings, OpenAI evaluation best practices, OpenAI production best practices, OpenAI reasoning best practices, Codex: Add evals to your AI application, OpenAI Agents SDK, Agents SDK orchestration and handoffs, Agents SDK guardrails, Agents SDK tracing, Evaluate agent workflows, OpenAI safety best practices, Promptfoo, Promptfoo expected outputs, Ragas metrics, OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, Context7 research, research dossier.

docs.title: Deep research цель
docs.text:
LLM / AI / RAG слой описывает, как проектировать, менять и проверять AI behavior: prompts, models, structured outputs, tools, retrieval, grounding, agents, guardrails, tracing, safety, latency, cost and regression risk.

Главный принцип: AI behavior нельзя менять “на ощущениях”. До изменения нужен baseline, после изменения нужен eval/runtime evidence, а для RAG и tools отдельно проверяются source grounding, retrieval quality, tool permissions и safety boundaries.

docs.title: Поддержанные факты
docs.text:
• OpenAI Responses API, text generation, prompt engineering, Structured Outputs, function calling, file search, retrieval and embeddings provide the primary OpenAI vocabulary for AI application behavior.
  • OpenAI evaluation guidance and Codex AI app evals recommend baseline evals, datasets, graders, thresholds and rerun evidence before behavior-changing prompt/model/retrieval/tool changes merge.
  • OpenAI Agents SDK docs separate agents, tools, handoffs, guardrails, tracing, human review and evals for code-owned agent applications.
  • OpenAI safety and production best practices support safety, privacy, monitoring, rate limits, latency/cost and deployment readiness concerns.
  • Promptfoo supports declarative LLM app evaluation with expected-output assertions; Ragas provides RAG quality metrics such as faithfulness and context precision/recall.
  • OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions give observability vocabulary for model calls, prompts, completions, tool calls and token/cost signals.

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• OpenAI is the primary source of truth for OpenAI APIs, Codex, Agents SDK, model behavior, tools, safety and production guidance; Context7 is useful only when the underlying source is official or vendor-owned.
  • Product-Agent OS should support AI work without forcing one eval runner. Promptfoo, pytest/Jest app-backed evals, OpenAI eval guidance and Ragas cover different risk profiles.
  • Agents SDK should be introduced when code-owned agent workflows need tools, handoffs, guardrails, sessions, tracing or evals; simple AI features can remain single-call or single-agent.
  • RAG quality requires separate retrieval and answer evaluation. A grounded final answer can still fail if retrieval misses fresh, authoritative or permitted sources.
  • Tool/function calling must be treated as product capability, not prompt decoration: permissions, side effects, idempotency, retries, errors and approvals are part of the contract.

docs.title: Инструкции применения на проекте
docs.text:
1. Классифицировать изменение: prompt, model, output schema, tool, RAG corpus, retrieval config, agent routing, guardrail, eval, latency/cost или safety behavior.
  2. Зафиксировать user-visible AI behavior promise: что функция обещает пользователю, где должна отказаться, где должна попросить уточнение и какие ошибки недопустимы.
  3. Перед prompt/model/retrieval/tool/agent change создать или найти baseline eval.
  4. По возможности проверять application path, который видит пользователь, а не только raw model prompt.
  5. Менять один фактор за раз, если цель - понять причинность. Если меняются сразу prompt, model и retrieval, это migration, а не простая итерация.
  6. Prompt рассматривать как versioned contract: role, goal, context, constraints, uncertainty policy, tools, output format, examples, verification route.
  7. Model decision фиксировать явно: model/snapshot or alias policy, reasoning effort, modality, context window, tool support, latency/cost, fallback.
  8. Structured Outputs использовать, когда output идет в code, UI, API, eval grader или другой agent. Схема должна иметь refusal/fallback/parser failure behavior.
  9. Tool/function calling документировать как capability contract: schema, permissions, side effects, idempotency, retries, errors and approval boundary.
  10. Для RAG фиксировать corpus authority, freshness, ingestion path, chunking, embeddings, vector store, filters, top-k/reranking, citations and unsupported-claim behavior.
  11. RAG quality делить на retrieval quality и answer quality: отдельно смотреть missing chunks, irrelevant chunks, faithfulness, answer relevance and citation correctness.
  12. Agent workflow начинать с минимального single-agent or manager pattern. Handoffs добавлять только когда specialist должен владеть следующим ответом.
  13. Traces использовать для debugging отдельного run; datasets/eval runs - когда поведение стабилизировано и нужно repeatability.
  14. Safety/red-team cases добавлять для prompt injection, sensitive content, private data, risky tools, minors, cybersecurity and irreversible side effects.
  15. Latency/cost считать product constraints: timeout, retry, caching, background/batch mode, smaller model fallback, budget threshold.
  16. Datasets, prompts, examples, fixtures, traces и screenshots не должны содержать secrets, credentials, raw private chats или private customer data.
  17. Quality improvement claim требует свежего eval evidence или explicit inspection-only gap.

docs.title: Проверки
docs.text:
• Baseline eval exists before AI behavior change.
  • Eval dataset policy excludes secrets, credentials, raw private chats and private customer data.
  • Rerun command, threshold and owner are explicit.
  • Prompt contract and model decision record are updated when prompt/model changes.
  • Structured output schema is validated with success and failure cases.
  • Tool call tests cover tool selection, arguments, errors and permission boundary.
  • RAG eval separates retrieval failures from generation failures.
  • Grounded answers cite supported sources or refuse/flag unsupported claims.
  • Agent workflow has trace evidence and handoff/ownership clarity.
  • Safety/red-team cases cover prompt injection, private data and risky actions.
  • Cost/latency budget is measured or explicitly marked as unavailable.

docs.title: Типовые сбои
docs.text:
• Manual spot checks are treated as eval evidence.
  • Prompt, model and retrieval are changed together without migration framing.
  • RAG answer quality is judged without source inspection.
  • Retrieval eval misses missing-source, stale-source or irrelevant-chunk cases.
  • Eval tests raw prompt while production behavior depends on tools, retrieval, state or UI transforms.
  • Structured output schema exists but parser/refusal/fallback behavior is undocumented.
  • Tool schema exists but permissions, idempotency and side effects are not reviewed.
  • Multi-agent workflow is introduced before a simpler baseline fails.
  • Guardrails ignore prompt injection, tool misuse or private data exposure.
  • Eval dataset leaks private data or becomes stale.
  • AI feature ships without latency/cost budget.

docs.title: Unsupported claims not adopted
docs.text:
• "Manual spot checks are enough for AI quality." Not adopted; behavior-changing prompt/model/RAG/tool/agent work needs baseline and rerun evidence or an explicit gap.
  • "Multi-agent architecture is always better." Not adopted; smallest useful workflow remains the default until complexity justifies handoffs.
  • "Citations alone prove RAG correctness." Not adopted; retrieval coverage, source authority, freshness, faithfulness and unsupported-claim handling are separate checks.
  • "A tool schema is enough for safe tool use." Not adopted; permissions, side effects, idempotency, approval boundaries and failure behavior are required.
  • "Model upgrade automatically improves product quality." Not adopted; model changes require eval comparison, latency/cost review and rollback policy.

docs.title: Quality, Testing & Evals
docs.text:
Source status: official + expert reference + vendor documentation + tool-assisted + experiment

Источники: Agile Alliance TDD, Agile Alliance ATDD, Agile Alliance BDD, Practical Test Pyramid, Testing Trophy, ISTQB CTFL v4.0.1, pytest, pytest fixtures, pytest parametrization, Vitest, Vitest coverage, Playwright retries, Playwright Trace Viewer, Playwright visual comparisons, Jest snapshot testing, Pact, Stryker mutation testing, Stryker mutation score, Hypothesis, Codecov coverage guidance, GitHub Actions workflow syntax, GitHub Actions GITHUB_TOKEN, OpenAI evaluation best practices, Codex AI app evals use case, Promptfoo, Promptfoo expected outputs, Ragas metrics, Context7 research, research dossier.

docs.title: Deep research цель
docs.text:
Quality, Testing & Evals слой определяет, как проект доказывает correctness, behavior, contracts, runtime quality, subjective quality and AI quality before completion claims.

Главный принцип: quality claim требует current evidence. Тесты, evals, screenshots, traces, manual QA and CI logs являются evidence только тогда, когда понятны command, environment, expected result, actual result, owner, residual risk and freshness.

docs.title: Поддержанные факты
docs.text:
• TDD, ATDD and BDD describe complementary loops for deterministic tests, acceptance tests and shared behavior language before implementation.
  • Test Pyramid and Testing Trophy are portfolio heuristics, not universal mandates; useful verification mixes static, unit, integration, contract, E2E, manual and eval checks by risk.
  • ISTQB separates confirmation testing, regression testing and impact analysis, which supports bugfix and refactor verification.
  • pytest, Vitest, Playwright, Pact, Hypothesis and Stryker provide concrete mechanisms for unit, integration, browser, contract, property-based and mutation testing.
  • Coverage indicates executed code, but does not prove requirements, assertions, contracts or user outcomes.
  • GitHub Actions workflow permissions and GITHUB_TOKEN scope are part of CI quality gate evidence.
  • OpenAI eval guidance, Codex AI app evals, Promptfoo and Ragas support AI, RAG and subjective quality evaluation with datasets, assertions, metrics and thresholds.

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• Product-Agent OS should select the smallest useful verification path by risk and feedback speed.
  • Completion evidence belongs in RUNLOG.md or evidence packet; durable quality strategy belongs in TEST.md and EVALS.md.
  • CI is a verification surface, not automatically an approval surface; external CI writes stay approval-bound.
  • Coverage thresholds are useful only when paired with requirement, critical-path and regression coverage.
  • Manual QA can be evidence when it has charter, environment, criteria, reviewer, notes and result.

docs.title: Инструкции применения на проекте
docs.text:
1. Для каждого slice назвать user-visible behavior или technical contract, который надо доказать.
  2. Выбрать smallest useful verification path: static/unit/integration/contract/E2E/runtime/manual/eval.
  3. Связать каждое acceptance criterion с deterministic check, contract check, runtime check, eval, manual charter или explicit gap.
  4. Для bugfix сначала получить reproduction evidence, если это практически возможно: failing test, command, log, screenshot, trace или точные шаги.
  5. TDD использовать для deterministic logic, parsers, validators, business rules and bugfixes: Red-Green-Refactor evidence важнее самого факта наличия теста.
  6. ATDD/BDD использовать для behavior scenarios, где product/business language должна перейти в executable checks или eval criteria.
  7. Test portfolio строить по risk and feedback speed: больше быстрых targeted checks, меньше дорогих high-level checks, но без потери critical path coverage.
  8. Для refactor, migration, dependency update or shared-code change фиксировать regression impact map.
  9. Для API/event/package changes требовать contract source и consumer/provider compatibility evidence.
  10. Для UI changes фиксировать runtime, responsive, visual, keyboard/focus and accessibility evidence, если изменение затрагивает пользователя.
  11. Для backend/runtime behavior проверять unit/integration/API/log/observability path, а не только code inspection.
  12. Для native/mobile/desktop behavior использовать platform build/run/log/screenshot evidence.
  13. Для AI, docs, UX, search, ranking or subjective outputs использовать eval spec: dataset, rubric, grader, threshold, rerun command.
  14. Coverage использовать как gap-finding signal, а не как proof of correctness. Coverage threshold должен быть связан с critical paths.
  15. Mutation/property-based testing применять выборочно для critical deterministic logic, где ordinary examples могут пропустить weak assertions или edge cases.
  16. Flaky tests не скрывать retries. Ретрай может собрать evidence, но нужен owner, root-cause class, expiry and follow-up.
  17. Manual QA принимать как evidence только с charter, environment, criteria, reviewer, notes and result.
  18. CI workflow changes держать staged, пока нет explicit approval на внешние writes. CI claims требуют свежего run evidence.
  19. Fixtures, eval datasets, traces, screenshots and logs не должны содержать secrets, credentials, raw private chats или private customer data.
  20. Не писать "works", "tested", "verified", "ready" или "quality improved", если в текущем run нет relevant evidence или explicit inspection-only gap.

docs.title: Применяемые методологии разработки
docs.text: Методология Когда применять Как выглядит в проекте TDD / Red-Green-Refactor Deterministic logic or bugfix Failing test first, failing output, minimal fix, passing output, refactor with checks green. ATDD / BDD Product behavior, workflows, business rules Acceptance scenarios map requirements to checks/evals and forbidden behavior. Test portfolio design Любой большой проект Static, unit, integration, contract, E2E, manual and eval checks selected by risk. Risk-based testing Ограничены time/CI budget или high-risk change Test scope follows impact, likelihood, user harm, data/security exposure and failure history. Confirmation + regression testing Bugfix, migration, refactor, dependency update Original failure is checked, then impacted unchanged behavior is rerun. Contract testing API/event/schema/public package changes OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/Pact/schema checks and consumer/provider compatibility evidence. Integration testing Behavior depends on database/service/filesystem/queue/network Real or high-fidelity dependency with reset strategy and failure evidence. E2E/runtime testing User-visible workflow or platform behavior Browser/simulator/API/runtime path, logs, screenshots, traces, reports. Visual and accessibility testing UI layout, design system, custom widgets Stable screenshots, component states, keyboard/focus/a11y checks, accepted diffs. Property-based testing Invariants, parsers, serializers, permissions, state machines Generated inputs, properties, seed/shrink evidence, preserved failing examples. Mutation testing Tests pass but assertion quality is doubtful Mutants, mutation score, surviving mutants and follow-up tests. Flaky test management Intermittent CI/runtime failures Classification, owner, quarantine expiry, rerun evidence and root-cause tracking. CI quality gates Shared branches, PRs, release readiness Commands, jobs, permissions, artifacts, exit codes and rerun path. Eval-driven quality AI/docs/UX/search/subjective quality Dataset, rubric, grader, threshold, baseline/current run and failure analysis. Exploratory testing Unknown risk, new workflow, usability Time-boxed charter, environment, notes, findings and follow-up checks. Evidence-before-completion Every meaningful slice Current command/eval/runtime/manual evidence or explicit gap before success claims.

docs.text:
• Quality maturity levels: baseline, team, production, regulated.

docs.text:
• Every acceptance criterion has a check/eval/manual charter or explicit gap.
