def rollback_merge(workspace: str | Path, rollback_manifest: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    workspace_path = Path(workspace).resolve()
    manifest_path = Path(rollback_manifest).resolve()
    if not manifest_path.exists():
        raise MergeInfrastructureError(f"rollback manifest does not exist: {manifest_path}")
    manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    rolled_back: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for entry in manifest.get("entries", []):
        target = _safe_child(workspace_path, entry["target_path"], "target path")
        current = file_digest(target) if target.exists() and target.is_file() else ""
        if current != entry["digest_after"]:
            raise MergeInfrastructureError(
                f"current digest differs from rollback manifest for {entry['target_path']}"
            )
        backup = Path(entry["backup_path"]).resolve()
        if not backup.exists():
            raise MergeInfrastructureError(f"rollback backup does not exist: {backup}")
        if entry["existed_before"]:
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            shutil.copyfile(backup, target)
        else:
            target.unlink()
        rolled_back.append(entry)
    return {
        "status": "rolled_back",
        "merge_plan_id": manifest.get("merge_plan_id", ""),
        "entries": rolled_back,
        "verification": {"ok": True, "checks": ["rollback digests verified", "rollback applied"]},
    }

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from product_agent_os.validators import is_forbidden_secret_assignment


OPENAI_TERMS = re.compile(r"\b(Codex|Agents SDK|OpenAI|MCP|hooks?|approvals?|models?|automation)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
OFFICIAL_SOURCE_HINTS = [
    "developers.openai.com",
    "openai.github.io",
    "github.com/openai",
    "Source status: `official",
    "source registry",
]


def validate_source_policy(workspace: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    root = Path(workspace)
    files = []
    errors = []
    secret_findings = []
    registry_updates_required = []
    docs_root = root / "docs"
    markdown_files = sorted(docs_root.rglob("*.md")) if docs_root.exists() else []
    for path in markdown_files:
        relative = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        file_report = _scan_file(relative, text)
        files.append(file_report)
        errors.extend(file_report["errors"])
        secret_findings.extend(file_report["secret_findings"])
        if file_report["registry_update_required"]:
            registry_updates_required.append(relative)
    status = _status(files, errors, secret_findings)
    return {
        "source_policy_report": {
            "status": status,
            "files": files,
            "registry_updates_required": registry_updates_required,
            "secret_findings": secret_findings,
            "errors": errors,
        },
        "status": status,
        "files": files,
        "registry_updates_required": registry_updates_required,
        "secret_findings": secret_findings,
        "errors": errors,
    }

Add helpers:

def _scan_file(relative: str, text: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    source_status = _source_status(text)
    errors: list[str] = []
    assumptions: list[str] = []
    unsupported_claims: list[str] = []
    missing_context: list[str] = []
    freshness_risks: list[str] = []
    secret_findings: list[str] = []
    if relative not in {"docs/index.md", "docs/sources/registry.md"} and source_status == "missing":
        errors.append(f"{relative}: missing Source status")
    for line_no, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
        if is_forbidden_secret_assignment(line):
            secret_findings.append(f"{relative}:{line_no}: secret-like literal")
    if OPENAI_TERMS.search(text) and not any(hint in text for hint in OFFICIAL_SOURCE_HINTS):
        missing_context.append("semantic source review required for OpenAI behavior claim")
    if "community" in text.lower() and "trust_level" not in text:
        unsupported_claims.append("community claim lacks trust_level")
    if any(term in text for term in ["models", "pricing", "security", "approval", "automation"]):
        freshness_risks.append("current behavior may require freshness review")
    return {
        "path": relative,
        "source_status": source_status,
        "supported_facts": [],
        "assumptions": assumptions,
        "unsupported_claims": unsupported_claims,
        "missing_context": missing_context,
        "freshness_risks": freshness_risks,
        "registry_update_required": bool(freshness_risks),
        "secret_findings": secret_findings,
        "errors": errors,
    }


def _source_status(text: str) -> str:
    match = re.search(r"Source status:\s*`([^`]+)`", text)
    return match.group(1).strip() if match else "missing"


def _status(files: list[dict[str, Any]], errors: list[str], secret_findings: list[str]) -> str:
    if errors or secret_findings:
        return "blocked"
    if any(item["missing_context"] or item["unsupported_claims"] for item in files):
        return "needs_review"
    return "ok"

# Product-Agent OS Agents SDK Runner Design

Source status: `official + experiment`

Sources: Product-Agent OS production hardening design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-14-product-agent-os-production-hardening-design.md`), source registry entries for Codex with Agents SDK and OpenAI Agents SDK Python.

This document defines the optional Agents SDK runner boundary for Product-Agent OS. It is not part of default plugin activation.

## Goal

Design a future programmable runner that can orchestrate Product-Agent OS roles while preserving Codex sandbox, approvals, source policy, and evidence trail.

## Runtime Boundary

- Codex App, CLI, skills, and project `.codex/agents` remain the default workflow.
- Agents SDK runner is an advanced optional layer.
- Codex MCP performs workspace work only with explicit sandbox and approval policy.
- Runner must fail closed when credentials, source status, approval state, or ownership are unclear.

## Manager Agent

- Owns lifecycle state and final output.
- Reads `AGENTS.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `PLAN.md`, `TEST.md`, `EVALS.md`, and `RUNLOG.md`.
- Routes to specialist agents or tools.
- Rejects handoffs missing constraints, sources, files, evidence, risks, or stop reason.

## Specialist Roles

| Role | Model and reasoning | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Product Manager | project default, medium/high | requirements and acceptance criteria |
| Architect | project default, high/xhigh | decomposition, ownership, rollback |
| Builder | project default, medium/high | one approved implementation slice |
| Tester | project default, medium/high | deterministic checks and eval evidence |
| Reviewer | project default, high/xhigh | findings-first review |
| Release Operator | project default, medium/high | staged PR and release packets |

## Credentials

- Credentials are read from environment variables or platform configuration.
- Plaintext credential values are never written to prompts, docs, fixtures, runlogs, traces, sessions, or memory.
- Missing credentials stop runner execution before workspace mutation.

## Sessions And Tracing

- Sessions preserve application conversation continuity only.
- Sessions do not replace checked-in project memory or `RUNLOG.md`.
- Traces record tool names, handoffs, latency, failures, and approval events.
- Traces redact secrets, private customer data, raw private chat logs, and absolute user-specific paths before persistence.

## Eval Gates

- Handoff completeness.
- Source fidelity.
- Tool boundary.
- Approval handling.
- Secret retention.
- Rollback or shutdown behavior.

## Non-Goals

- No default dependency installation.
- No default network access in plugin verification.
- No active automation scheduling.
- No replacement for Codex App, CLI, project skills, or `.codex/agents`.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS Codex Runtime Runner Implementation Plan
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: реализовать Track 5: dependency-free Codex runtime runner для product-agent-os, который внутри Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, skills и subagents читает control-plane artifacts, определяет lifecycle state, строит route packet, проверяет guardrails и возвращает machine-readable codex_runner_result.

Architecture: runner остается локальным contract-first helper под plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/codex_runtime_runner/. Он не вызывает внешние модели, не требует credentials, не устанавливает зависимости и не запускает MCP/service runtime; Codex остается execution plane, а runner только читает workspace, валидирует boundary и выдает следующий безопасный маршрут.

Tech Stack: Python 3 standard library, unittest, argparse, dataclasses, json, pathlib, existing product_agent_os validators, synthetic fixtures, MkDocs.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
План реализует Product-Agent OS Codex Runtime Runner Design.

Входит в scope:

  • contract schemas for codex_runner_request, codex_route_packet, codex_runner_handoff, codex_runner_result;
  • read-only context loader for AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md;
  • deterministic lifecycle state detector;
  • lifecycle-to-skill/subagent route planner;
  • validators for request, route packet, handoff, approval boundary, source policy, automation boundary, result evidence, redaction;
  • deterministic redaction for secret-like literals, private markers, raw chat markers, and local absolute paths;
  • contract-mode CLI wrapper;
  • fixture eval extension with codex_runtime_runner_status and runner checks;
  • synthetic runner fixtures only;
  • plugin structure assertion that runner is present but not default-active.

Не входит в scope:

  • standalone OpenAI Agents SDK app;
  • direct OpenAI API calls;
  • external credentials, environment-provided model access, or external credential setup;
  • external Agents SDK runtime dependency;
  • external Codex MCP bridge;
  • HTTP server, deployment target, background service, schedule, recurring automation, GitHub Action, or external workflow;
  • global Codex config mutation;
  • automatic subagent spawning from deterministic tests;
  • workspace writes from runner default mode.

docs.title: Execution Model
docs.text:
Recommended execution: Inline Execution using superpowers:executing-plans, because current workspace is not a git repository and the first implementation slice is tightly coupled across tests, runner package, and fixture eval.

If subagents are explicitly requested later, split ownership as:

  • Worker A: contracts/state/routes tests and implementation.
  • Worker B: guards/redaction tests and implementation.
  • Worker C: CLI, fixture eval, synthetic fixtures, plugin structure tests.
  • Main agent: integration review, docs checks, full verification.

Workers are not alone in the codebase. They must not revert edits made by others and must preserve Track 1-4 behavior.

docs.title: Contract Decisions
docs.text:
Use dictionaries and pure functions rather than dataclass instances as public return values. Existing plugin tests assert JSON-like dictionaries, and this keeps CLI output simple.

Status values:

  • runner result: route_ready, needs_context, needs_approval, blocked, completed, failed;
  • fixture eval runner status: route_ready, needs_context, needs_approval, blocked, not_applicable;
  • source policy: reuse ok, needs_review, blocked;
  • approval status: not_required, required, approved, rejected, stale.

Write policies:

  • read_only - no approval required;
  • staged_only - may propose staged artifacts but runner itself writes nothing by default;
  • approved_write - requires explicit approval record before route readiness;
  • blocked - unsafe or incomplete route.

Route mapping:

State Skill Subagent role Write policy uninitialized workspace-discovery-auditor empty read_only infrastructure_planned requirements-author empty staged_only requirements_ready implementation-planner empty staged_only plan_ready agent-team-designer empty staged_only team_ready test-eval-designer empty staged_only build_active empty builder approved_write quality_gate risk-reviewer empty read_only review_ready pr-release-operator empty staged_only release_ready learning-loop-maintainer empty staged_only learning_ready automation-promoter empty staged_only maintenance project-lifecycle-orchestrator empty read_only

Lifecycle inference order:

  1. If request explicitly provides a valid task.lifecycle_state, use it.
  2. If AGENTS.md is missing, use uninitialized.
  3. If REQUIREMENTS.md is missing or lacks acceptance criteria, use infrastructure_planned.
  4. If PLAN.md is missing or lacks verification strategy, use requirements_ready.
  5. If project agent configs are missing, use plan_ready.
  6. If TEST.md or EVALS.md is missing required quality gates, use team_ready.
  7. If RUNLOG.md contains build-active marker, use build_active.
  8. If RUNLOG.md contains quality-gate marker, use quality_gate.
  9. If RUNLOG.md contains review-ready marker, use review_ready.
  10. If RUNLOG.md contains release-ready marker, use release_ready.
  11. If RUNLOG.md contains learning-ready marker, use learning_ready.
  12. Otherwise use maintenance.

Required marker strings are intentionally simple and synthetic-friendly:

  • acceptance criteria: Критерии приемки;
  • verification strategy: Verification;
  • build active: lifecycle_state: build_active;
  • quality gate: lifecycle_state: quality_gate;
  • review ready: lifecycle_state: review_ready;
  • release ready: lifecycle_state: release_ready;
  • learning ready: lifecycle_state: learning_ready.

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any


ALLOWED_RUNNER_STATUSES = ["route_ready", "needs_context", "needs_approval", "blocked", "completed", "failed"]
ALLOWED_RUNTIME_SURFACES = ["Codex App", "CLI", "IDE extension", "codex exec", "subagent", "skill"]
ALLOWED_WRITE_POLICIES = ["read_only", "staged_only", "approved_write", "blocked"]
ALLOWED_APPROVAL_STATUSES = ["not_required", "required", "approved", "rejected", "stale"]
ALLOWED_LIFECYCLE_STATES = [
    "uninitialized",
    "infrastructure_planned",
    "requirements_ready",
    "plan_ready",
    "team_ready",
    "build_active",
    "quality_gate",
    "review_ready",
    "release_ready",
    "learning_ready",
    "maintenance",
]
REQUIRED_RESULT_FIELDS = [
    "schema_version",
    "status",
    "workspace",
    "lifecycle_state",
    "route_packet",
    "handoffs",
    "files_touched",
    "files_proposed",
    "verification_evidence",
    "source_policy_status",
    "approval_status",
    "redactions",
    "errors",
    "warnings",
    "next_action",
]


def validate_runner_request(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    errors: list[str] = []
    if payload.get("schema_version") != 1:
        errors.append("schema_version:must_be_1")
    if not _non_empty_string(payload.get("workspace")):
        errors.append("workspace:required")
    task = payload.get("task")
    routing = payload.get("routing")
    approval = payload.get("approval")
    if not isinstance(task, dict):
        errors.append("task:required")
        task = {}
    if not isinstance(routing, dict):
        errors.append("routing:required")
        routing = {}
    if not isinstance(approval, dict):
        errors.append("approval:required")
        approval = {}
    state = task.get("lifecycle_state")
    if state not in ("", None) and state not in ALLOWED_LIFECYCLE_STATES:
        errors.append("task.lifecycle_state:unknown")
    for field in ["constraints", "allowed_sources", "expected_artifacts"]:
        if field in task and not isinstance(task[field], list):
            errors.append(f"task.{field}:invalid")
    surface = routing.get("preferred_surface")
    if surface not in ALLOWED_RUNTIME_SURFACES:
        errors.append("routing.preferred_surface:unknown")
    if not isinstance(routing.get("allow_subagents"), bool):
        errors.append("routing.allow_subagents:invalid")
    if not isinstance(routing.get("allow_workspace_writes"), bool):
        errors.append("routing.allow_workspace_writes:invalid")
    approval_status = approval.get("approval_status")
    if approval_status not in ALLOWED_APPROVAL_STATUSES:
        errors.append("approval.approval_status:unknown")
    if routing.get("allow_workspace_writes") and approval_status != "approved":
        errors.append("routing.allow_workspace_writes:approval_required")
    return errors


def build_result(
    *,
    status: str,
    workspace: str,
    lifecycle_state: str,
    route_packet: dict[str, Any],
    source_policy_status: str,
    approval_status: str,
    next_action: str,
    handoffs: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
    files_touched: list[str] | None = None,
    files_proposed: list[str] | None = None,
    verification_evidence: list[str] | None = None,
    redactions: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    errors: list[str] | None = None,
    warnings: list[str] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "schema_version": 1,
        "status": status,
        "workspace": workspace,
        "lifecycle_state": lifecycle_state,
        "route_packet": route_packet,
        "handoffs": handoffs or [],
        "files_touched": files_touched or [],
        "files_proposed": files_proposed or [],
        "verification_evidence": verification_evidence or [],
        "source_policy_status": source_policy_status,
        "approval_status": approval_status,
        "redactions": redactions or {"count": 0, "categories": []},
        "errors": errors or [],
        "warnings": warnings or [],
        "next_action": next_action,
    }


def validate_runner_result(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    errors: list[str] = []
    if list(payload.keys()) != REQUIRED_RESULT_FIELDS:
        errors.append("result:field_order_or_shape")
    if payload.get("schema_version") != 1:
        errors.append("schema_version:must_be_1")
    if payload.get("status") not in ALLOWED_RUNNER_STATUSES:
        errors.append("status:unknown")
    if payload.get("lifecycle_state") not in ALLOWED_LIFECYCLE_STATES:
        errors.append("lifecycle_state:unknown")
    if not isinstance(payload.get("route_packet"), dict):
        errors.append("route_packet:invalid")
    for field in ["handoffs", "files_touched", "files_proposed", "verification_evidence", "errors", "warnings"]:
        if not isinstance(payload.get(field), list):
            errors.append(f"{field}:invalid")
    redactions = payload.get("redactions")
    if not isinstance(redactions, dict) or not isinstance(redactions.get("count"), int):
        errors.append("redactions:invalid")
    if payload.get("status") == "completed" and not payload.get("verification_evidence"):
        errors.append("verification_evidence:required_for_completed")
    return errors


def _non_empty_string(value: Any) -> bool:
    return isinstance(value, str) and bool(value.strip())

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any


CONTROL_PLANE_FILES = ["AGENTS.md", "REQUIREMENTS.md", "PLAN.md", "TEST.md", "EVALS.md", "RUNLOG.md"]


def load_control_plane_context(workspace: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    root = Path(workspace)
    files: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for name in CONTROL_PLANE_FILES:
        path = root / name
        files[name] = _read_file(path)
    return {
        "workspace": str(root),
        "exists": root.exists(),
        "is_dir": root.is_dir(),
        "files": files,
        "missing": [name for name, item in files.items() if not item["exists"]],
        "unreadable": [name for name, item in files.items() if item["exists"] and item["error"]],
    }


def _read_file(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not path.exists():
        return {"exists": False, "text": "", "error": ""}
    if not path.is_file():
        return {"exists": True, "text": "", "error": "not a file"}
    try:
        return {"exists": True, "text": path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "error": ""}
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
        return {"exists": True, "text": "", "error": "unable to read file as utf-8 text"}

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from codex_runtime_runner.contracts import ALLOWED_LIFECYCLE_STATES


def infer_lifecycle_state(context: dict[str, Any], request: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    requested = request.get("task", {}).get("lifecycle_state") if isinstance(request.get("task"), dict) else ""
    if requested in ALLOWED_LIFECYCLE_STATES:
        return str(requested)
    files = context.get("files", {})
    if not files.get("AGENTS.md", {}).get("exists"):
        return "uninitialized"
    requirements = files.get("REQUIREMENTS.md", {}).get("text", "")

from __future__ import annotations

import re


SECRET_ASSIGNMENT = re.compile(r"(?im)^\\s*[A-Z_]*(?:SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|KEY)[A-Z_]*\\s*[=:]\\s*[^\\r\\n]+")
WINDOWS_USER_PATH = re.compile(r"C:\\\\Users\\\\[^\\s\\\\]+(?:\\\\[^\\s]+)*", re.IGNORECASE)
PRIVATE_MARKERS = re.compile(r"(?i)(private customer data|raw private chat log|raw chat log)")


def redact_text(text: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, object]]:
    categories: list[str] = []
    redacted = text
    redacted, secret_count = SECRET_ASSIGNMENT.subn("[REDACTED_SECRET_ASSIGNMENT]", redacted)
    if secret_count:
        categories.append("secret")
    redacted, path_count = WINDOWS_USER_PATH.subn("[REDACTED_LOCAL_PATH]", redacted)
    if path_count:
        categories.append("absolute_path")
    redacted, private_count = PRIVATE_MARKERS.subn("[REDACTED_PRIVATE_DATA]", redacted)
    if private_count:
        categories.append("private_data")
    return redacted, {"count": secret_count + path_count + private_count, "categories": sorted(set(categories))}


def validate_redaction(text: str) -> list[str]:
    errors: list[str] = []
    if SECRET_ASSIGNMENT.search(text):
        errors.append("redaction:secret_retained")
    if WINDOWS_USER_PATH.search(text):
        errors.append("redaction:absolute_path_retained")
    if PRIVATE_MARKERS.search(text):
        errors.append("redaction:private_data_retained")
    return errors

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Any

from codex_runtime_runner.routes import ROUTES


ACTIVE_AUTOMATION_PATTERN = re.compile(r"(?i)\\b(active|recurring|scheduled)\\s+automation\\b|\\bcreate\\s+.*automation\\b")


def validate_route_packet(route: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    errors: list[str] = []
    state = route.get("lifecycle_state")
    expected = ROUTES.get(str(state))
    if not expected:
        return ["route:lifecycle_state_unknown"]
    expected_skill, expected_subagent, expected_write_policy, _ = expected
    if route.get("write_policy") != expected_write_policy:
        errors.append("route:unexpected_write_policy_for_state")
    if expected_skill and route.get("recommended_skill") != expected_skill:
        errors.append("route:unexpected_skill_for_state")
    if expected_subagent and route.get("recommended_subagent_role") not in {expected_subagent, ""}:
        errors.append("route:unexpected_subagent_for_state")
    return errors


def validate_approval_boundary(route: dict[str, Any], approval: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    write_policy = route.get("write_policy")
    approval_status = approval.get("approval_status")
    if write_policy == "approved_write" and approval_status != "approved":
        return ["approval:required_for_write"]
    return []


def validate_codex_handoff(handoff: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    required = [
        "lifecycle_state",
        "role",
        "goal",
        "constraints",
        "sources_used",
        "assumptions",
        "verified_claims",
        "unsupported_claims",
        "files_touched",
        "files_proposed",
        "commands_run",
        "verification_evidence",
        "approval_requirements",
        "open_risks",
        "recommended_next_role",
        "stop_reason",
    ]
    errors = [field for field in required if field not in handoff]
    for field in ["constraints", "verification_evidence"]:
        value = handoff.get(field)
        if value is not None and not isinstance(value, list):
            errors.append(f"{field}:invalid")
        elif value == []:
            errors.append(f"{field}:empty")
    for field in ["files_touched", "files_proposed"]:
        if field in handoff and not isinstance(handoff[field], list):
            errors.append(f"{field}:invalid")
    if handoff.get("files_touched") == [] and handoff.get("files_proposed") == []:
        errors.append("files:empty")
    return errors


def validate_automation_boundary(text: str) -> list[str]:
    if ACTIVE_AUTOMATION_PATTERN.search(text):
        return ["automation:active_request_blocked"]
    return []

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from codex_runtime_runner.context_loader import load_control_plane_context
from codex_runtime_runner.contracts import build_result, validate_runner_result
from codex_runtime_runner.guards import validate_approval_boundary, validate_route_packet
from codex_runtime_runner.redaction import redact_text, validate_redaction
from codex_runtime_runner.routes import plan_route
from codex_runtime_runner.state import infer_lifecycle_state


def run_contract(workspace: str | Path, *, allow_subagents: bool = False, approval_status: str = "not_required") -> dict[str, Any]:
    context = load_control_plane_context(workspace)
    request = {
        "task": {"lifecycle_state": ""},
        "routing": {"allow_subagents": allow_subagents, "allow_workspace_writes": False},
        "approval": {"approval_status": approval_status},
    }
    state = infer_lifecycle_state(context, request)
    route = plan_route(state, allow_subagents=allow_subagents)
    errors = []
    warnings = []
    if context["unreadable"]:
        errors.extend(f"context:unreadable:{name}" for name in context["unreadable"])
    route_errors = validate_route_packet(route)
    approval_errors = validate_approval_boundary(route, {"approval_status": approval_status})
    errors.extend(route_errors)
    if approval_errors:
        warnings.extend(approval_errors)
    status = _status_for(context, route, errors, approval_errors)
    result = build_result(
        status=status,
        workspace=str(workspace),
        lifecycle_state=state,
        route_packet=route,
        source_policy_status="not_evaluated",
        approval_status=approval_status,
        next_action=route["next_action"],
        files_proposed=[] if route["write_policy"] == "read_only" else ["staged handoff packet"],
        verification_evidence=["codex_runtime_runner contract mode completed"] if status == "route_ready" else [],
        errors=errors,
        warnings=warnings,
    )
    redacted_text, redactions = redact_text(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))
    result = json.loads(redacted_text)
    result["redactions"] = redactions
    result["errors"].extend(validate_redaction(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True)))
    result["errors"].extend(validate_runner_result(result))
    if result["errors"] and result["status"] == "route_ready":
        result["status"] = "blocked"
    return result


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run Product-Agent OS Codex runtime runner in contract mode.")
    parser.add_argument("workspace")
    parser.add_argument("--contract", action="store_true", help="Run deterministic offline contract mode.")
    parser.add_argument("--allow-subagents", action="store_true", help="Allow subagent route recommendations.")
    parser.add_argument("--approval-status", default="not_required")
    parser.add_argument("--output", help="Optional JSON output file.")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if not args.contract:
        print("error: choose --contract", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    result = run_contract(args.workspace, allow_subagents=args.allow_subagents, approval_status=args.approval_status)
    text = json.dumps(result, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
    if args.output:
        Path(args.output).write_text(text + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(text)
    return 0 if result["status"] == "route_ready" else 1


def _status_for(
    context: dict[str, Any],
    route: dict[str, Any],
    errors: list[str],
    approval_errors: list[str],
) -> str:
    if errors:
        return "blocked"
    if context["missing"] and route["lifecycle_state"] != "uninitialized":
        return "needs_context"
    if approval_errors:
        return "needs_approval"
    return "route_ready"

def _codex_runtime_runner_eval(path: Path) -> tuple[str, dict[str, bool]]:
    if not path.name.startswith("codex-runner-"):
        return "not_applicable", {}
    checks: dict[str, bool] = {"contract_mode_offline": True}
    if path.name == "codex-runner-ready":
        result = run_contract(path)
        checks["route_matches_lifecycle_state"] = (
            result["lifecycle_state"] == "quality_gate"
            and result["route_packet"]["recommended_skill"] == "risk-reviewer"
        )
        return str(result["status"]), checks
    if path.name == "codex-runner-missing-context":
        result = run_contract(path)
        checks["missing_context_detected"] = result["status"] == "needs_context"
        return str(result["status"]), checks
    if path.name == "codex-runner-approval-required":
        result = run_contract(path, allow_subagents=True)
        checks["approval_required_for_writes"] = result["status"] == "needs_approval"
        return str(result["status"]), checks
    if path.name == "codex-runner-handoff-incomplete":
        errors = validate_codex_handoff({"lifecycle_state": "quality_gate", "constraints": [], "verification_evidence": []})
        checks["handoff_incomplete_blocked"] = "constraints:empty" in errors and "verification_evidence:empty" in errors
        return "blocked", checks
    if path.name == "codex-runner-automation-blocked":
        errors = validate_automation_boundary((path / "RUNLOG.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        checks["active_automation_blocked"] = "automation:active_request_blocked" in errors
        return "blocked", checks
    if path.name == "codex-runner-secret-redaction":
        redacted, _report = redact_text("TOKEN=fixture-secret\nC:\\Users\\person\\workspace")
        checks["secret_redaction_enforced"] = validate_redaction(redacted) == []
        return "blocked", checks
    return "not_applicable", {}

docs.title: Track 9 Methodology Intelligence Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Build Track 9 so Product-Agent OS can read a user workspace, classify complexity and maturity, build a Delivery Map, recommend applicable methodology domains, and stage methodology artifacts only after approval.

Architecture: Add a methodology intelligence layer on top of existing Track 8 scenario routing. The layer has a machine-readable methodology catalog, a read-only audit engine, a report/JSON output contract, recommendation priority rules, domain-by-domain integrations, and a final cross-domain synthesis pass. Existing staged-first and approval-bound renderer behavior remains the write boundary.

Tech Stack: Python standard library, unittest, JSON catalog assets, Markdown templates, existing plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/product_agent_os/* modules, existing fixture eval runner, MkDocs documentation checks.

docs.title: Scope Check
docs.text:
The approved spec covers a large product program, not a single narrow feature. This plan decomposes it into independently testable slices:

  1. Repository hygiene before Track 9 work.
  2. Track 9 foundation: shared schemas, catalog loader, audit contract, report renderer, CLI wrapper and discovery integration.
  3. Twelve methodology domain integrations, one source file at a time.
  4. Cross-domain synthesis to remove duplicates, conflicts and over-applied gates.
  5. Final docs, evals and baseline refresh.

Every task must be implemented with a focused commit. Do not batch multiple domain integrations into one commit.

import unittest

class MethodologyCatalogContractTest(unittest.TestCase):

        from product_agent_os.methodology_catalog import load_methodology_catalog

        catalog = load_methodology_catalog()

                "applicable_missing",
                "present_unverified",
                "present_verified",
                "proposal_staged",
                "explicit_gap_accepted",
                "approval_required",

        self.assertEqual(
            catalog["recommendation_priorities"],
            [
                "P0_blocker",
                "P1_high_risk",
                "P2_recommended",
                "P3_optional_maturity",
                "not_applicable",
            ],
        )
        self.assertEqual(catalog["maturity_levels"], ["baseline", "team", "production", "regulated"])
        self.assertEqual(catalog["complexity_profiles"], ["simple", "standard", "complex", "high_risk"])

    def test_catalog_contains_all_track_nine_domains_in_order(self):

        catalog = load_methodology_catalog()
        self.assertEqual(
            [domain["id"] for domain in catalog["domains"]],

                "requirements_domain",
                "solution_architecture",
                "quality_testing_evals",
                "codex_agentic_workflow",

                "database_data",

"""Methodology catalog loading and validation for Product-Agent OS Track 9."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any


READINESS_STATUSES = [
    "not_applicable",
    "applicable_missing",
    "present_unverified",
    "present_verified",
    "proposal_staged",
    "explicit_gap_accepted",
    "approval_required",
]

RECOMMENDATION_PRIORITIES = [
    "P0_blocker",
    "P1_high_risk",
    "P2_recommended",
    "P3_optional_maturity",
    "not_applicable",
]

MATURITY_LEVELS = ["baseline", "team", "production", "regulated"]
COMPLEXITY_PROFILES = ["simple", "standard", "complex", "high_risk"]

DOMAIN_KEYS = {
    "id",
    "title",
    "source_file",
    "purpose",
    "applies_when",
    "not_applicable_when",
    "maturity_impact",
    "complexity_impact",
    "track8_scenarios",
    "artifacts",
    "gates",
    "eval_fields",
    "overlaps",
}


def _plugin_root() -> Path:
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]


def catalog_path() -> Path:
    return _plugin_root() / "assets" / "methodology" / "methodology-catalog.json"


def load_methodology_catalog(path: str | Path | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    catalog_file = Path(path) if path is not None else catalog_path()
    data = json.loads(catalog_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    errors = validate_methodology_catalog(data)
    if errors:
        raise ValueError("; ".join(errors))
    return data


def validate_methodology_catalog(data: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    errors: list[str] = []
    if data.get("version") != 1:
        errors.append("version must be 1")
    if data.get("readiness_statuses") != READINESS_STATUSES:
        errors.append("readiness_statuses mismatch")
    if data.get("recommendation_priorities") != RECOMMENDATION_PRIORITIES:
        errors.append("recommendation_priorities mismatch")
    if data.get("maturity_levels") != MATURITY_LEVELS:
        errors.append("maturity_levels mismatch")
    if data.get("complexity_profiles") != COMPLEXITY_PROFILES:
        errors.append("complexity_profiles mismatch")
    domains = data.get("domains")
    if not isinstance(domains, list) or not domains:
        errors.append("domains must be a non-empty list")
        return errors
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for index, domain in enumerate(domains):
        if not isinstance(domain, dict):
            errors.append(f"domains[{index}] must be an object")
            continue
        domain_id = str(domain.get("id", f"index-{index}"))
        if domain_id in seen:
            errors.append(f"duplicate domain id: {domain_id}")
        seen.add(domain_id)
        if set(domain) != DOMAIN_KEYS:
            errors.append(f"{domain_id} keys mismatch")
        for field in [
            "applies_when",
            "not_applicable_when",
            "maturity_impact",
            "complexity_impact",
            "track8_scenarios",
            "artifacts",
            "gates",
            "eval_fields",
            "overlaps",
        ]:
            if not isinstance(domain.get(field), list):
                errors.append(f"{domain_id}.{field} must be a list")
    return errors

import tempfile

class MethodologyAuditContractTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_empty_workspace_returns_baseline_simple_with_questions(self):
        from product_agent_os.methodology_audit import build_methodology_audit

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            result = build_methodology_audit(Path(tmp), intent_hint="new MVP idea")

        self.assertEqual(result["maturity_level"]["selected"], "baseline")
        self.assertEqual(result["complexity_profile"]["selected"], "simple")
        self.assertIn("delivery_map", result)
        self.assertIn("questions_for_owner", result)
        self.assertIn("safe_next_action", result)
        self.assertEqual(result["write_policy"], "read_only")

    def test_workspace_with_api_database_and_ci_routes_complex(self):
        from product_agent_os.methodology_audit import build_methodology_audit

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            root = Path(tmp)
            (root / "openapi.yaml").write_text("openapi: 3.1.0\ninfo:\n  title: API\n  version: 1.0.0\npaths: {}\n", encoding="utf-8")
            (root / "migrations").mkdir()

Implement deterministic workspace signal checks for these paths:

  • package.json, pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, Cargo.toml, go.mod, pom.xml, build.gradle;
  • openapi.yaml, openapi.yml, openapi.json;

  • docs/, README.md, AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md;

  • evals/, prompts/, rag/, vector, embeddings.

  • [ ] Step 2: Implement basic classification rules

Use these deterministic rules:

  • Empty or README-only workspace: maturity_level=baseline, complexity_profile=simple.
  • API contract plus migrations or CI: at least complexity_profile=complex.
  • Production intent with CI, release files or deployment manifests: at least maturity_level=production.
  • Security, privacy, payment, PII, compliance, healthcare, finance, production data, auth, authorization or secret intent: complexity_profile=high_risk.
  • Regulated intent terms regulated, compliance, audit, HIPAA, PCI, SOC2, finance, healthcare, minors: maturity_level=regulated.

Intent terms affect intent_signals and confidence, but must not be represented as observed file evidence.

  • [ ] Step 3: Add domain applicability

Use catalog domains and map these signals:

  • business_product: applicable for behavior/product/MVP/release/user/value/metric intent.
  • requirements_domain: applicable for non-empty projects and behavior-changing intent.
  • solution_architecture: applicable for complex, team, production, API, data, AI, runtime or multi-surface projects.
  • quality_testing_evals: applicable for every non-trivial project.
  • codex_agentic_workflow: applicable when Product-Agent OS is used.
  • frontend: applicable for frontend framework/package signals or UI intent.
  • backend: applicable for server, API, service, worker, queue or backend framework signals.
  • api_integrations: applicable for OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, protobuf, webhook, external integration or API intent.
  • database_data: applicable for migration, DB schema, ORM, data store or production data signals.
  • llm_ai_rag: applicable for prompt, model, eval, RAG, vector, embedding or AI intent.
  • security_privacy_compliance: applicable for high-risk, auth, secrets, PII, payment, compliance or regulated signals.

  • delivery_release_operations: applicable for production, CI, release, deploy, package, Docker, Kubernetes or operations signals.

  • [ ] Step 4: Generate default recommendations

Recommendations must be deterministic and modest:

  • Always include codex_agentic_workflow recommendation for missing control-plane files in Product-Agent OS context.
  • If no test command or test evidence is detected, add P0_blocker for quality_strategy_present.
  • If API signals exist without contract tests, add P1_high_risk for api_contract_source_present.
  • If DB migration signals exist, add P1_high_risk for database_migration_plan_present.
  • If high-risk signals exist, add P1_high_risk for security_risk_review_present.

  • If production/release signals exist, add P1_high_risk for release_evidence_present.

Modify docs/sources/product-agent-os-track-9-backlog.md before code implementation and record these T9-D1 deep-audit deltas from docs/methodologies/business-product.md:

  • value_proposition_evidence_present is required in addition to the original Task 8 gate list.
  • analytics_tracking_plan_present is required when product usage data or product analytics is claimed.
  • qualitative_feedback_loop_present is required for user research, support, sales, customer-success signal or accepted qualitative evidence gap.
  • release_measurement_evidence_present is required before product success claims after release.
  • tracking-plan.md is a required candidate artifact for product analytics governance.
  • Severity resolution: missing product_hypothesis_present is P2_recommended for discovery-only or empty workspace audits, but becomes P1_high_risk or stronger when the user asks to implement, ship or release a behavior-changing slice without hypothesis, metric/gap and owner evidence.
  • decision_horizon must be recorded as discovery, MVP, beta, production or scale; it determines how much formality the Product-Agent OS recommendation should require.
  • business_outcome, product_outcome and feature_traction_metric must be separated so a local feature metric is not treated as a North Star metric.
  • HEART metrics are optional UX/product quality lenses, not a mandatory full set; when used, record which of Happiness, Engagement, Adoption, Retention and Task success applies.
  • release-notes.md is part of the Business/Product surface because user-facing changes need affected users, measurement window and rollback/disable signal.
  • PLAN.md, EVALS.md and RUNLOG.md must carry outcome-driven planning, AI product eval and post-release measurement evidence, not only REQUIREMENTS.md and metric-spec.md.
  • metric_scope must be explicit as required, not_applicable or accepted_gap.
  • tracking-plan.md is required only when product usage data, analytics events, dashboards, event properties or product analytics claims exist; plain metric hardening can stay in metric-spec.md.
  • If production telemetry does not exist, post-release measurement can use manual, qualitative, support or owner review evidence, but product success claims must remain blocked until current evidence or accepted gap exists.

  • Internal workflow promotion can use engineering time saved plus verification, owner and safety boundary evidence; it does not always need an external product metric.

  • Current Track 8 already covers acceptance scenarios, conditional DDD, bounded-context-to-architecture traceability, ubiquitous-language traceability and simple CRUD / simple MVP false-positive protection; T9-D2 must extend, not duplicate, those gates.

  • Requirement quality criteria must be represented: atomicity, clarity, testability, feasibility, traceability, source and owner.
  • Stable requirement IDs are needed for multi-slice, regulatory, risky or long-lived work.
  • Requirement registry needs status, owner, source and linked artifacts.
  • Stakeholder/owner map is a first-class Requirements & Domain artifact because source-backed domain meaning and business rules need accountable reviewers.
  • User story and story slicing evidence must preserve value slice, MVP boundary, deferred slices, risk and non-goals; a story title alone is not a requirement.
  • Business rules need source, owner, enforcement layer, exceptions and failure behavior.
  • Example Mapping is needed when stories are unclear, large or disputed: story -> rules -> examples -> questions.
  • Domain discovery workshop evidence is needed for complex workflow, cross-silo process or overloaded domain language.
  • requirement_quality_present must cover atomicity, clarity, testability, feasibility, traceability, source and owner instead of being hidden inside scope.
  • Constraint evidence must cover compliance, privacy, security, operational, performance, platform, accessibility, data retention, localization, cost, rollout and rollback when relevant.
  • Acceptance scenarios must be declarative: no UI selectors, database internals, function names or test harness details in business-facing scenarios.
  • Domain events crossing boundaries need meaning, producer, consumers, schema link, ordering/idempotency assumptions and privacy classification.
  • Invariants and failure modes are required when domain state transitions matter.
  • API/UI/data traceability is distinct from DDD traceability: requirement/domain term -> API/event/schema/UI/data/code/test/eval.
  • Domain expert review is required for business-critical, compliance, finance/legal or AI-generated domain claims.
  • Requirement change impact review is required when requirements/domain rules change after planning: tests/evals, API, DB, UI, docs, rollout and rollback.
  • Accepted gaps are valid only with owner, reason, scope, review date, downstream risk and follow-up condition.
  • docs-maintainer owns requirement IDs, source registry, glossary/ubiquitous-language docs and traceability docs after the requirements packet exists.

  • Unsupported claims must be rejected: BDD replaces testing, Gherkin is mandatory, a user-story template is a complete requirement, a glossary is ubiquitous language, OpenAPI is requirements source of truth.

  • The compact task list below must represent quality as current evidence, not as a generic "tests exist" signal.

Deep-audit update from docs/methodologies/frontend.md and docs/sources/methodology-research/frontend.md:

  • The compact task list below must represent frontend as user-observable behavior and browser evidence, not as component hierarchy or code inspection.
  • Required gates include frontend_user_flow_acceptance_present, frontend_component_docs_present, frontend_component_state_matrix_present, frontend_design_system_boundary_present, frontend_fsd_boundary_reviewed, frontend_api_contract_alignment_present, frontend_accessibility_review_present, frontend_keyboard_focus_contract_present, frontend_responsive_viewport_matrix_present, frontend_visual_evidence_present, frontend_runtime_console_evidence_present, frontend_performance_budget_present, frontend_browser_support_present, frontend_content_i18n_boundary_present, and frontend_interaction_test_evidence_present.
  • Existing artifacts must be reused where possible: component-card.md, acceptance-scenarios.md, api-contract-review.md, quality-strategy.md, test-eval-matrix.md, manual-qa-evidence.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, and RUNLOG.md.
  • New template scope for this slice is intentionally five artifacts unless implementation proves separate ownership for additional candidates: frontend-flow-spec.md, frontend-state-matrix.md, frontend-visual-qa.md, frontend-accessibility-review.md, and frontend-performance-budget.md.
  • Candidate artifacts not in the compact task list must be explicitly mapped or deferred: route-page-inventory.md, storybook-story-map.md, design-system-inventory.md, design-tokens-reference.md, frontend-boundary-map.md, fsd-boundary-record.md, frontend-api-dependency-map.md, responsive-viewport-matrix.md, keyboard-focus-map.md, visual-evidence-packet.md, frontend-interaction-test-matrix.md, frontend-browser-support-matrix.md, and frontend-content-i18n-record.md.
  • Discovery must recognize route/page/component directories, .storybook/, stories, Playwright, Vite, Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro, React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, Solid, Testing Library, axe, Chromatic, design tokens, themes, components.json, browser assets, viewport/accessibility/performance terms, and UI intent.
  • False-positive behavior must preserve backend-only, data-only, CLI-only, docs-only, native-only, dependency-only and simple CRUD work. Storybook, FSD, Playwright, performance budgets and visual baselines must stay conditional.
  • Recommendations must reject unsupported claims as evidence: FSD is mandatory for every frontend project, Storybook proves UI quality, automated accessibility addon output is enough, a desktop screenshot proves responsive UI, lab Web Vitals always represent production UX, and code inspection proves UI completion.
  • The implementation must resolve source open questions instead of leaving them implicit: Storybook required/optional policy, minimum visual evidence thresholds, WCAG/default accessibility target, FSD boundary review depth, Web Vitals measurement path, browser/device support, content/i18n boundary and screenshot/story privacy policy.

docs.text:
Files: - Source: docs/methodologies/backend.md - Modify: catalog, audit - Create: backend-service-overview.md - Create: backend-runtime-behavior.md - Create: backend-dependency-failure-matrix.md - Create: backend-observability-map.md - Create: backend-slo-sheet.md - Create: backend-health-check-contract.md - Create: backend-job-queue-contract.md - Create: backend-data-consistency-record.md - Create: backend-config-secrets-manifest.md - Create: backend-release-rollback-notes.md - Create: backend-operational-runbook.md

Deep-audit update from docs/methodologies/backend.md and docs/sources/methodology-research/backend.md:

  • The compact task list below must represent backend as runtime behavior, production failure modes, operational evidence and owner-reviewed boundaries, not as package structure or service count.
  • Required gates include backend_service_boundary_present, backend_runtime_behavior_present, backend_dependency_failure_matrix_present, backend_observability_contract_present, backend_slo_or_gap_present, backend_health_probe_contract_present, backend_job_queue_contract_present, backend_data_consistency_strategy_present, backend_config_secrets_boundary_present, backend_security_reviewed, and backend_rollback_plan_present.
  • Backend unit classification must cover module, monolith subsystem, service, worker, scheduler, consumer, API backend, integration adapter and migration runner. Microservices stay conditional and must not be recommended as the default maturity badge.
  • Existing artifacts must be reused where possible: architecture-overview.md, domain-modeling.md, api-contract-review.md, quality-strategy.md, test-eval-matrix.md, manual-qa-evidence.md, migration-plan.md, security-risk-review.md, release-packet.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, and RUNLOG.md.
  • New template scope for this slice is intentionally eleven artifacts unless implementation proves a separate owner for additional candidates: backend-service-overview.md, backend-runtime-behavior.md, backend-dependency-failure-matrix.md, backend-observability-map.md, backend-slo-sheet.md, backend-health-check-contract.md, backend-job-queue-contract.md, backend-data-consistency-record.md, backend-config-secrets-manifest.md, backend-release-rollback-notes.md, and backend-operational-runbook.md.
  • Candidate artifact aliases must be explicitly mapped or deferred: module/service boundary map to backend-service-overview.md or architecture-overview.md, ports/adapters map to backend-service-overview.md, security notes to security-risk-review.md, SLO ownership overlaps to Delivery/Operations, and distributed workflow recovery evidence to backend-data-consistency-record.md plus backend-operational-runbook.md.
  • Discovery must recognize backend/server/service/worker/job/queue/scheduler/consumer/adapter/repository/migration directories, Docker/Procfile/docker-compose/Kubernetes/Helm/serverless manifests, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/protobuf contracts, backend frameworks, queue/job libraries, remote dependency clients and terms such as retry, timeout, idempotency, circuit breaker, health check, readiness, liveness, SLO and runbook.
  • False-positive behavior must preserve frontend-only, docs-only, CLI-only, native-only, dependency-only, package-name-only and simple CRUD work. src/domain/* alone, a package named service, or documentation about backend must not force backend gates without runtime backend evidence.
  • Recommendations must reject unsupported claims as evidence: backend means only business-logic files, microservices are the professional default, retries make systems reliable, a health endpoint solves readiness, logs are observability, and SLOs only matter for large companies.
  • The implementation must resolve source open questions instead of leaving them implicit: modular-monolith default, stack-specific template neutrality, platform-neutral health checks versus Kubernetes vocabulary, bounded resilience library guidance, retry/idempotency detection depth, and Backend versus Delivery ownership for SLO/runbook evidence.

Deep-audit update from docs/methodologies/api-integrations.md and docs/sources/methodology-research/api-integrations.md:

  • The compact task list below must use the full API & Integrations source contract, not only the initial subset.
  • api_contract_test_matrix_present is a derived Product-Agent OS gate for Track 9 implementation. The methodology source lists api-contract-test-matrix.md and contract verification as artifact/eval evidence; implementation must make this explicit so schema validation, provider verification and consumer-driven tests are not collapsed into "contract file exists".
  • API-only contract fixtures must not force Backend runtime blockers. OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL/protobuf/Pact files make api_integrations applicable, but Backend gates require runtime/server/service/worker evidence.
  • Unsupported claims must be rejected as evidence: rendered API docs are enough, internal APIs do not need compatibility review, schema validation is the same as contract testing, GraphQL/gRPC/event-driven is always better, OAuth means API security is handled, and generated SDKs are mechanical.
  • External writes remain approval-bound. T9-D8 may stage external-integration-approval.md, but must not perform external writes, update external systems, run generated client publication, or mutate provider state without explicit approval.
  • Final verification must not auto-commit. Commit remains a separate user-approved action, matching the recent T9-D5 through T9-D7 execution pattern.

docs.title: Task 16: T9-D9 Database & Data Integration
docs.text:
Files: - Source: docs/methodologies/database-data.md - Modify: catalog, audit, database-dictionary.md, data-migration.md - Create: database-inventory.md - Create: database-migration-plan.md - Create: database-expand-contract-record.md - Create: database-backfill-runbook.md - Create: database-rollback-feasibility.md - Create: database-backup-restore-evidence.md - Create: database-data-classification-matrix.md - Create: database-data-quality-checks.md - Create: database-data-contract.md - Create: database-lineage-map.md - Create: database-query-performance-review.md - Create: database-retention-deletion-policy.md - Create: database-synthetic-fixtures-policy.md - Create: database-production-access-approval.md

Deep-audit update from docs/methodologies/database-data.md and docs/sources/methodology-research/database-data.md:

  • database_data is currently a stub in the methodology catalog; implementation must promote it to a full domain, not only extend the existing data_migration usage-mode workflow.
  • Database methodology applies beyond SQL migrations: schema source, data dictionary, migration/backfill safety, transaction/concurrency design, constraints/indexes, query performance, backup/restore, data quality, retention/deletion, lineage, privacy classification, synthetic fixtures and production data access are separate gates.
  • Tooling choices are candidates, not defaults. T9-D9 must not force PostgreSQL, Liquibase, Flyway, Alembic, Prisma, Rails/Django migrations, dbt, Great Expectations, OpenLineage, DBML, dbdocs, SchemaSpy or schema-diff tooling as universal Product-Agent OS defaults.
  • DB introspection, production DB access, production data access, migration execution, destructive cleanup, backup restore and retention mutation remain approval_required.
  • SQL/ORM destructive-change detection must be lightweight and conservative: DROP, rename, truncate, destructive cleanup and unsafe retention signals create owner questions/recommendations, not automatic execution or full parser claims.
  • Unsupported claims must be rejected as evidence: ORM schema is the database source of truth, migration applied means migration safe, rollback is just down migration, backups exist so restore is safe, manual SQL is enough, anonymized production data is safe by default and lineage can be reconstructed later.
  • Analytics and AI/RAG data movement creates cross-domain overlap with llm_ai_rag; PII/sensitive/production data creates overlap with Security/Privacy; schema/API/data contract changes overlap with API, Backend, Quality and Delivery.

import json

from pathlib import Path

catalog = json.loads(Path("plugins/product-agent-os/assets/methodology/methodology-catalog.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

docs.title: Self-Review Checklist For This Plan
docs.text:
Spec coverage:

  • Goal, core product principle, two-step onboarding, classification model, Delivery Map, report/JSON outputs, recommendations, all 12 domains, adaptive deep-dive loop, cross-domain synthesis, safety, verification and definitions of done are mapped to tasks.

No unsupported broad implementation:

  • The plan does not ask for direct target workspace writes.
  • The plan keeps staged artifacts approval-bound.
  • The plan keeps methodology conditional.
  • The plan requires false-positive coverage.

Residual risks:

  • Domain catalog entries will be large; review each domain diff carefully.
  • Domain tasks can reveal more sub-slices than listed here; add them to docs/sources/product-agent-os-track-9-backlog.md before implementing.
  • Deterministic tests prove contract shape; semantic methodology quality still needs human review and future eval refinement.

docs.title: Track 10 Guided Questions And Status Dashboard Implementation Plan
docs.text:
Source status: local implementation planning

For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Build Track 10 so Product-Agent OS can guide users with bounded, methodology-aware questions, maintain a single offline HTML status artifact for project progress, stage a self-verification loop for agents, skills and harness modernization decisions, generate a project code graph for dependency-aware navigation, and close the remaining live runtime/provider/canonical-mutation gates in one final Task 26 before real project testing.

Architecture: Extend the existing Track 8 usage-mode route and Track 9 methodology packet with a typed question protocol, answer ledger, status snapshot, staged static dashboard renderer, local-first metrics loop for self-verification, staged code-graph pipeline, and final approval-gated live semantic runtime closure. JSON, JSONL and Markdown remain the source of truth; HTML artifacts are generated, reviewable views that are staged first and never silently mutate the target workspace. Task 26 is the final Track 10 umbrella for approved live local runtime, external provider adapters, human-reviewed canonical graph mutation, observability, rollback and real-testing readiness.

Tech Stack: Python standard library, ast, unittest, JSON/JSONL contracts, Markdown control-plane artifacts, static HTML/CSS/vanilla JavaScript, owner-selected locally bundled Cosmos.gl for graph visualization, Graphology-compatible payloads for graph/query interchange, optional Sigma.js compatibility/fallback evaluation, existing plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/product_agent_os/* modules, existing Codex runtime runner, fixture eval runner, transcript eval runner, docs checks, MkDocs.

docs.title: Scope Check
docs.text:
Track 10 is a new user-facing capability, not part of Track 9 final documentation sync.

It includes these implementation tasks:

  • Task 23: Guided Question Protocol And Project Status Dashboard
  • Task 24: Self-Verification And Modernization Loop
  • Task 25: Project Code Graph And HTML Cockpit Visualization
  • Task 26: Final Live Semantic Runtime, Canonical Graph Governance And Real Testing Readiness

Track 10 must start only after Track 9 Task 22 closes the current Product-Agent OS documentation baseline. This prevents Task 22 from becoming a moving target while Track 10 changes runtime packets, renderer output, evals and docs.

docs.title: Numbering Note
docs.text:
The Track 9 plan now keeps the former Task 23: Final Verification Baseline only as a legacy checklist section under Task 22. Task 22 absorbs that verification baseline into T22-U-M23, so Track 10 uses Task 23 for the next product capability:

  • typed guided questions;
  • answer ledger;
  • status snapshot;
  • offline status.html dashboard.
  • agent/skill/harness self-verification and staged modernization candidates.
  • project code graph scanner, compact graph packets and offline HTML cockpit visualization.
  • final approved live semantic runtime, external provider gates, canonical graph mutation governance and real-testing readiness.

Task 26 absorbs all remaining Track 10 extension gates. There must be no Task 27, Task 28 or later Track 10 task for leftover live runtime, provider, mutation, verification, packaging, docs or real-testing-readiness work. Any work after Task 26 is either the real testing phase itself or a separately approved new track with a new product goal, not a hidden continuation of Track 10.

Do not implement Track 10 unless Track 9 docs keep the legacy final baseline absorbed into Task 22 and current verification evidence exists.

docs.title: Product Outcome
docs.text:
After Track 10, a user should be able to enable Product-Agent OS in a real project and see:

  • one or zero blocking questions at a time;
  • optional follow-up questions grouped by product, technical, verification, approval and ownership category;
  • why each question matters and what artifact it affects;
  • a stable status page showing current lifecycle state, usage mode, methodology readiness, evidence gaps, approvals, staged artifacts, open risks and next safe action;
  • stale/evidence warnings when the dashboard is generated from inspection-only or old command evidence.
  • staged self-verification reports for generated agents, skills, prompt or policy packs, router/tool policies and harness versions, with modernization candidates separated from approval.
  • a project code graph that shows code, docs, templates, contracts and generated artifacts as dependency nodes with confidence-labelled edges and compact agent read-order hints.
  • a final readiness packet for real project testing that states which live/provider/mutation surfaces are enabled, disabled, rolled back, accepted as gaps or blocked.

The plugin must keep forward momentum. It should ask only questions that block safe planning, approval, evidence or the next artifact.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
These non-goals apply to Tasks 23-25 and to any Task 26 slice that has not received explicit approval. Task 26 may narrow only the specific live-runtime/provider/mutation boundaries named in its approval packet; production deployment, external writes and irreversible side effects remain outside scope unless separately approved.

  • Do not add a production web server, public network service or always-on daemon. A Task 26 local read-only runtime is allowed only as a disabled-by-default approved local server with lifecycle, auth, log cleanup and shutdown evidence.
  • Do not add a production database or make a database the source of truth. Task 26 may use bounded local stores, caches or query backends only when JSON, JSONL and Markdown source artifacts remain canonical unless accepted mutation governance explicitly applies a reviewed graph change.
  • Do not add a live model call, OpenAI API dependency, external embedding/reranker/LLM provider call or Agents SDK app outside the Task 26 approval packet. Approved provider calls must pass redaction, cache, budget, eval, rollback and audit gates before use.
  • Do not activate MCP servers, hooks, GitHub Actions, recurring automations or external writes.
  • Do not make HTML the source of truth.
  • Do not create browser-based editing of project files in this track.
  • Do not claim universal semantic code intelligence from file/path scans, unsupported language parsers or inferred dependency edges.
  • Do not store secrets, credentials, private customer data, raw private chat logs, production screenshots or absolute user-specific paths.
  • Do not automatically apply self-modernization candidates, rewrite skills, enable recurring evaluation schedules or promote automation without explicit owner approval and rollback evidence.

docs.title: Task 24: Self-Verification And Modernization Loop
docs.text:
Task 24 adds a staged control-plane capability for Product-Agent OS to evaluate the agents, skills, prompt or policy packs, router/tool policies and harness versions that were created or used during real user work. The mechanism is not an autonomous mutation system. It reads implemented task evidence, optional redacted traces and synthetic regression cases; computes per-target scorecards; stages daily and weekly review packets; and generates modernization candidates only when evidence, rollback and approval state are explicit.

Design input comes from the local agentic_harness_metrics.md research brief and from the implemented Track 9/Track 10 contracts. The implementation must reuse existing boundaries: agent_eval_workflow_present, skill_promotion_evidence_present, automation_manual_stability_present, redaction policy, staged renderer behavior, status snapshot, offline dashboard, fixture eval runner, transcript eval runner and explicit-only git boundary.

Task 24 product outcome:

  • show a registry of evaluated targets with status healthy, watch, regression, blocked or no_data;
  • separate agent outcome metrics, trajectory metrics, harness reliability metrics and skill-specific metrics;
  • explain the recommended self-verification cadence with L0, L1, L2 or L3 maturity;
  • preserve an append-only scorecard ledger with raw counts, confidence evidence, baseline, current and candidate versions;
  • generate an offline HTML evaluation report as a review artifact, not an approval record or source of truth;
  • stage modernization candidates with reason, expected impact, risk, rollback target and approval state;
  • keep active schedules, external eval systems, live model calls, Agents SDK apps, GitHub Actions, MCP activation and write updates approval-bound.

docs.title: Task 25: Project Code Graph And HTML Cockpit Visualization
docs.text:
Task 25 adds a staged, read-only mechanism for scanning a user project, building a graph of dependent code and documentation entities, and rendering that graph into the Product-Agent OS HTML cockpit. It closes the gap between the existing workspace discovery model, which is mostly file/path/marker based, and the user-visible need for a dependency map that helps both humans and coding agents find relevant code faster.

The mechanism must not become a live IDE, database, autonomous editor or source-of-truth replacement. Source code, checked-in docs and generated JSON/JSONL graph artifacts remain the evidence layer. HTML is a generated review surface.

Task 25 product outcome:

  • scan a workspace without mutating it and produce .codex/product-agent-os/project-code-graph.json;
  • represent project entities as stable nodes: workspace, package, module/file, class, function, method, test, fixture, template, generated artifact, Markdown page, MkDocs page, OpenAPI/Swagger or AsyncAPI contract, DBML or SQL schema, Mermaid/PlantUML diagram and control-plane artifact;
  • represent dependencies as confidence-labelled edges: contains, imports, calls, exports, tests, verifies, documents, renders, generates, configures, owns, references and impacts;
  • expose compact agent query packets for neighbors, path, trace, impact, affected_tests, read_order, hotspots, node, status and search;
  • expose graph freshness, workspace/worktree provenance, validation, analysis report and code-flow views so humans and agents can distinguish current evidence from stale, cross-worktree, unsupported or inferred topology;
  • expose observation lineage, scan-to-scan deltas and advisory temporal validity so removed or changed dependencies are invalidated/superseded in generated graph artifacts rather than silently erased;
  • render a generated eight-page project cockpit shell with top-level pages Overview, Project Map, Docs & Sources, Code Intelligence, Contracts, Quality & Metrics, Operations & Risk and Proposal Ledger, while preserving all detailed sections as local page sections;
  • render an offline HTML project cockpit graph with filters, clustering and level-of-detail so 1k, 5k and 10k node graphs stay navigable;
  • produce a Graphology-compatible visual projection with layout, size, color, community, label-priority and level-of-detail metadata derived from the canonical graph artifact, not from browser state;
  • initialize a local Cosmos.gl interactive renderer when bundled assets are available, with selected-node evidence, filter state, graph navigation commands, mobile behavior and static fallback views;
  • keep graph visualization assets local. Cosmos.gl is the owner-selected visualization library; Graphology-compatible payloads remain the internal interchange format; Sigma.js is fallback/compatibility-only. Vendored assets require version/license/hash records; no CDN, network fetch or external runtime dependency is allowed.

Task 25 future-gated extension analysis:

  • Product reason: the Batch 13-18 baseline is enough for safe navigation, source orientation and agent read-order. Static indexes, runtime backends and semantic extraction become useful only when users need repeated low-latency search over larger graphs, better natural-language retrieval or summarized rationale across code/docs. These are product accelerators, not baseline correctness requirements.
  • Product risk: each extension can make generated graph output look more authoritative than source. The UI and runtime must keep "generated orientation evidence" wording, stale/fresh labels, source-read safe next actions and owner-review gates visible.
  • Technical reason for sequencing: a static search index should come before any live database/server because it proves index schema, freshness, cache invalidation and search-quality thresholds without process lifecycle risk. A local backend should come before embeddings because it provides stable storage/query contracts and rollback controls. Embeddings and cross-encoder reranking should come before LLM extraction because they can be evaluated with deterministic retrieval metrics before introducing generative interpretation.
  • Technical risk: live server/database work adds process lifecycle, port, persistence, cleanup, concurrency, API contract and rollback risks. Embedding/cross-encoder/LLM work adds privacy, cost, latency, model drift, cache invalidation, dataset leakage, false-positive semantic links and unsupported completion-claim risks.
  • Approval gate: Batch 19 was approved by the explicit user request to execute Batch 19 and is limited to an offline static search index. Batch 20 was approved by the explicit user request to execute Batch 20 and is limited to a generated local file-store backend gate with disabled-by-default server lifecycle, no production server and graph-only fallback. Batch 21 was approved by the explicit user request to execute Batch 21 and is limited to a generated semantic retrieval index using local deterministic embeddings/cross-encoder eval, redacted graph/static-index inputs, cache policy, token budget, eval threshold and rollback/disable path. Batch 22 was approved by the explicit user request to execute Batch 22 and is limited to local deterministic LLM extraction-style proposal generation from redacted graph/semantic-index inputs with prompt/model policy, structured JSON, human review, AI incident workflow and rollback/disable path. Batch 23 was approved by the explicit user request to execute Batch 23 and is limited to generated future extension verification, rollback/data deletion proof and closure through project_graph_extension_closure.py, verify-extensions and disable-extensions. Live database/server, live external embedding/cross-encoder/LLM calls and canonical graph mutation remain blocked_without_new_explicit_approval; any future approval must name allowed surfaces, data classification, redaction boundary, cache policy, token budget, eval threshold, rollback/disable path, owner and accepted residual risks. Planning matrix presence is not implementation evidence.
  • Source boundary: approved Batch 21 semantic retrieval artifacts are generated orientation evidence only. Semantic hits are present_unverified, point back to graph observation IDs, source spans, redaction status and current-run eval evidence, and do not rewrite canonical graph edges. Future LLM semantic nodes, rationale snippets or comment summaries are never source of truth.
  • Stop condition: do not start live database/server, live model/API calls beyond the approved local deterministic Batch 21 surface, semantic extraction or rationale/comment extraction from Task 25 baseline closure alone. Start only when the explicit approval packet exists and the RED tests for that future batch are written first.
