docs.title: Task 26: Final Live Semantic Runtime, Canonical Graph Governance And Real Testing Readiness
docs.text:
Task 26 is the final Track 10 task. It absorbs all remaining blocked_without_new_explicit_approval surfaces left after Task 25 Batch 23: live local runtime, external embedding/cross-encoder/LLM provider calls, human-reviewed canonical graph mutation, live-action audit, security/privacy gates, observability, packaging smoke, docs/control-plane closure, the handoff into real project testing and the approval-bound first real-testing execution matrix. This section is a planning matrix only until the user explicitly approves each implementation batch. It does not start a server, call a provider, mutate canonical graph facts or authorize git staging, commit, push or PR actions by itself.

Task 26 closure analysis from previous tracks:

  • Tracks 1-2 created the Product-Agent OS plugin core, contracts and lifecycle skills. Product value: the system already knows how to route work through requirements, planning, testing, review, docs and release roles. Task 26 must reuse those skills instead of inventing another orchestration layer.
  • Tracks 3-4 established staged infrastructure, approval records, merge safety, rollback, hook/automation gates and source-policy validation. Product value: users can trust that generated artifacts are proposals until approved. Task 26 must keep live runtime and canonical mutation under the same staged-first and rollbackable model.
  • Track 5 added the Codex runtime runner with contract mode, route validation, redaction, approval and inactive-by-default boundaries. Product value: Product-Agent OS can participate in real Codex workflows without silent external side effects. Task 26 must remain additive, disabled by default and contract-visible.
  • Tracks 6-7 hardened engineering standards, architecture/doc/source/eval policies and false-positive guards. Product value: the plugin became useful across real project types, not just demo repos. Task 26 must prove live/provider/mutation behavior through standards-backed gates, not through optimistic model output.
  • Track 8 packaged use-case scenarios, acceptance/eval templates, two-stage review, fresh-context handoff, domain/context gates and scenario false-positive fixtures. Product value: real testing can be organized by user workflow archetype. Task 26 must produce the final pilot matrix and handoff packet that maps real testing to those archetypes.
  • Track 9 built methodology intelligence, cross-domain synthesis, route finish options and final docs/runtime closure. Product value: agents can surface methodology gaps without over-asking or over-claiming. Task 26 must keep LLM and semantic results as source-backed proposals until human review accepts them.
  • Track 10 Tasks 23-25 added bounded guided questions, status dashboard, self-verification, read-only project graph, cockpit visualization, offline search, local deterministic semantic retrieval, local deterministic proposal generation and future-extension rollback closure. Product value: the user now has the offline baseline and generated-view safety labels needed before live testing. Task 26 closes the remaining live/provider/mutation/pre-real-testing gap; no later Track 10 task outside Task 26 should appear for that scope.

Task 26 product outcome:

  • users can opt into a local live read-only project graph runtime when the approval packet, lifecycle controls and graph-only fallback are present;
  • semantic search can use approved external embeddings, hybrid retrieval and reranking only when redaction, cache, budget, provider metadata and eval thresholds are satisfied;
  • LLM output remains proposal-only until a human review ledger accepts it with source evidence;
  • canonical graph mutation is possible only through accepted proposals, dry-run mutation plans, append-only journals and verified rollback;
  • agents and skills get explicit handoff rules for live/provider/mutation work, so file ownership, stop conditions and evidence are visible;
  • security, privacy, observability, performance, packaging and docs closure are complete before the project moves to real testing execution;
  • Batch 35 captures the first approval-bound real-testing execution evidence or a documented blocked/accepted-gap decision for each live/browser/provider/mutation/git surface, so the next post-Task-26 artifact is owner handoff, not Task 27.

Task 26 technical and product analysis:

  • Product value: live runtime and provider-backed retrieval reduce repeated manual graph/query work, improve natural-language discovery over large projects and make accepted graph improvements reusable. The user benefit is faster orientation, better search precision, fewer repeated context reads and controlled graph evolution.
  • Product risk: live outputs can appear authoritative even when they are generated, inferred or stale. Every live result must preserve source evidence, generated-view wording, confidence labels, owner review state and fallback path.
  • Technical value: approval schema, redaction, cache policy, provider adapters, eval thresholds, review ledger, mutation journal and rollback engine create a reversible path from local generated evidence to canonical graph updates.
  • Technical risk: local server work adds process lifecycle, port/auth/log/cleanup, concurrency and operational risk. External providers add privacy, cost, latency, model drift, cache invalidation and dataset leakage risk. Canonical mutation adds source-of-truth and rollback risk. Real testing adds reproducibility, target selection and user expectation risk.
  • Sequencing rule: governance first, read-only local runtime second, external retrieval third, LLM proposals fourth, human review and canonical mutation fifth, real-testing readiness and staged QA sixth, packaging/docs closure seventh, approval-bound real-testing execution last.
  • Approval gate: each Task 26 batch needs an explicit approval packet naming allowed surfaces, data classification, redaction boundary, provider/cache policy, token/cost/latency budget, eval thresholds, runtime controls, rollback path, owner signoff and accepted residual risks.
  • Stop condition: if approval is incomplete, redaction fails, eval threshold is missed, rollback proof is absent, provider budget is exceeded, a proposal lacks owner review, live runtime cannot cleanly shut down or real-testing targets are not approved, implementation must stop or degrade to graph-only mode.

Task 26 Batch 34 decomposes T10-LIVE-M35..M36 into B34-DOC-M01..M15. The work is approval_required, planned before execution and not implementation evidence by itself. Batch 34 preserves the same safety boundary as Batch 33: staged evidence only, generated artifacts are not source of truth, no live server, no browser automation, no provider/live external model/API calls, no canonical graph mutation and no git stage/commit/push/PR unless a later explicit owner approval says otherwise.

Verification order is fixed for this batch: source docs -> registry -> docs tests -> check_docs.py -> strict MkDocs -> optional full closure. docs.title: Batch 36: System File Hygiene Audit And Candidate Automation Maintenance
docs.text:
Batch 36 is an owner-requested maintenance addendum for preventing Product-Agent OS system files from accumulating stale implementation ledgers, duplicated rules, unsafe automation text or confusing agent instructions. It is not Task 27, does not reopen live/runtime/provider/canonical-mutation scope and does not authorize active automation. The default execution mode is read_only; any recurring schedule remains candidate_only_until_approved and must record schedule_status: not_created until a later explicit owner approval includes rollback/disable evidence.

Product outcome:

  • agents can detect oversized or polluted system files before they become confusing context;
  • users can see which project-maintenance surface owns each piece of information;
  • compaction candidates route to the right artifact instead of being deleted or duplicated;
  • future automation can be promoted only after manual stability evidence and explicit approval;
  • the offline HTML status artifact can show system-file, agent and skill state, last update dates and audit status without becoming an evidence source by itself.

Trigger policy:

Trigger When it fires Audit scope Gate / stop condition Weekly full hygiene audit Once per week when the project is active. Full maintained system-file inventory. Read-only report only; no schedule exists until approved. Monthly deep ownership review Once per month or before major plugin release work. Ownership, source-of-truth routing and stale historical ledgers. Any compaction remains a separate focused slice. On-change audit After edits to AGENTS.md, control-plane files, subagents, skills, workflows, hooks, evals, docs source-control files or plugin package control files. Changed system files plus adjacent owners. Stop if a change creates duplicate rules, active schedule text, secrets or hard-size violations. Size-threshold audit When soft or hard byte/line thresholds are exceeded. Oversized file plus likely destination artifacts. Soft limit creates review_required; hard limit creates blocked until owner routing exists. Release/automation approval audit Before plugin packaging, release packets, active schedule promotion, GitHub workflow activation or Codex App automation creation. System files, automation candidates, approval records and rollback/disable evidence. No active automation without two successful manual runs, explicit approval and disable path.

Maintained system-file classes:

Class File patterns Primary owner Maintenance rule Root control plane AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md Product Manager, Architect, Tester, Docs Maintainer Keep current rules, requirements, plan, verification, evals and run handoff compact; move history to source packets/backlogs/registry. Project entrypoint README.md Product Docs Lead Keep product/onboarding copy and route implementation history to internal evidence files. Nested instructions **/AGENTS.md Area owner Keep durable local rules only; avoid batch logs, stale command evidence and duplicated global policy. Codex config and MCP .codex/config.toml, .codex/settings.json, .mcp.json, .codex/*.mcp.json Architect + Release Operator Detect unsafe config drift, secrets, active external surfaces and undocumented MCP changes. Subagents .codex/agents/*.toml Agent Team Designer Keep role, ownership, model/reasoning policy and stop conditions current. Skills .codex/skills/**/SKILL.md, skills/**/SKILL.md Skill Maintainer Keep trigger, inputs, outputs, verification and failure modes focused; route broad methods to playbooks/plugins. Workflows .codex/workflows/*.md Product Manager + Builder Keep repeatable manual workflows executable, source-bound and approval-aware. Artifact templates .codex/artifact-templates/*.md Docs Maintainer + Tester Keep templates structured, secret-free and mapped to source/evidence owners. Automation candidates .codex/automation-candidates/*.md Release Operator Keep candidate-only state; block cron, RRULE or active schedule markers before approval. Hooks .codex/hooks/* Release Operator + Security Reviewer Treat hooks as inactive templates unless explicitly approved; verify no destructive default behavior. Evals .codex/evals/*.json, evals/*.json Tester + Eval Owner Keep eval schemas current, deterministic and tied to acceptance criteria. PR/release packets .codex/pr/*.md, .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE*.md Reviewer + Release Operator Keep release, review and PR evidence routes explicit and approval-bound. Docs source-control files docs/sources/*, docs/insights/*, docs/playbooks/*, docs/product-agent*/*, docs/runtime/*, docs/artifact-templates/*, mkdocs.yml, tools/check_docs.py Docs Maintainer Preserve source status, registry coverage, public/internal boundary and docs checks. External automation policy .github/workflows/*, CODEOWNERS, SECURITY.md, .github/dependabot.yml Release Operator + Security Reviewer Detect external writes, permission drift and unapproved activation. Plugin control files plugins/*/.codex-plugin/plugin.json, plugins/*/README.md, plugins/*/.mcp.json, plugins/*/skills/**/SKILL.md, plugins/*/assets/templates/**/*.md, plugins/*/assets/templates/**/*.json Plugin Owner Keep packaged plugin contracts, skills, MCP config and generated templates compatible with Codex App, CLI and IDE extension.

Batch grouping:

  • Batch 36A: Scope, Trigger And Packet Contract (T10-HYG-M01..M03, read_only)
  • Batch 36B: Validator, Findings And Report Output (T10-HYG-M04..M06, read_only)
  • Batch 36C: Templates, Docs, Source Registry And Tests (T10-HYG-M07..M09, read_only)
  • Batch 36D: Candidate Automation Promotion Gate (T10-HYG-M10..M12, candidate_only_until_approved)
  • Batch 36E: HTML System Hygiene Report Page (T10-HYG-M13..M17, read_only)

T10-HYG-M13 36E Architect + Builder Add status projection for HTML reporting. system_file_hygiene.py, status_snapshot.py, tests. Audit output exposes bounded file_statuses with relative path, class, owner, state, severity, finding count, size, line count, mtime_utc, age_days, content digest and last audit timestamp; no absolute paths, raw file bodies or secrets are embedded. T10-HYG-M14 36E Product Manager + Docs Maintainer Define HTML information architecture for system files, agents and skills. status-dashboard/status.html, optional project_cockpit_model.py section mapping. status.html gets a System Hygiene page or top-level section; project cockpit, if touched, keeps exactly eight top-level pages and places the report under Operations & Risk with anchor system-file-hygiene. HTML shows counts by ok, review_required, blocked, missing, unreadable, stale and owner_unknown; tables are grouped by root control plane, agents, skills, workflows, automation candidates, hooks, evals, docs source-control and plugin control files; rows show file, owner, state, last updated date, age and top finding. Tests prove no external URLs, no raw absolute local paths, no secret-like values, bounded embedded JSON, generated-view-only wording, visible stale evidence banner and deterministic sorting by severity then file class then path. Fixture eval records system_file_hygiene_dashboard_present, system_file_status_dates_present, agent_skill_file_status_present and system_hygiene_dashboard_not_source_of_truth; docs explain that update dates come from filesystem metadata and are freshness hints, not semantic proof that content is correct.

The work used implementation-planner, agent-team-designer and test-driven-development; three read-only explorer subagents independently checked inventory/ownership, trigger policy and JSON packet validation. Current executable contract records maintained system-file classes with owners, per-trigger write_policy: read_only and stop_conditions, and nested packet validation for trigger records, class records, inventory, findings and summary status. No active automation, hook activation, external write, provider call, canonical graph mutation or git stage/commit/push/PR is performed by Batch 36A.

docs.title: Batch 37: Task Matrix Plan Files And Completion Reports
docs.text:
Batch 37 is a planned Product-Agent OS planning-format addendum for making task-matrix plan files first-class artifacts when development methodologies, documentation standards, specs, ADRs, verification gates or agent handoffs apply. It does not authorize runtime implementation, live server startup, browser automation, provider/live external model/API calls, canonical graph mutation, active automation, target-workspace writes or git stage/commit/push/PR. Planned task rows are not implementation evidence; every completion claim must be written only after the slice is implemented and verified in the current run.

Batch 37 task matrix addendum:

Every Batch 37 task row follows the task-matrix entry contract below. Planned rows use pending_execution_timestamp until the task is implemented and verified in the current run. implemented status is invalid without factual touched files, current verification evidence and actual implementation date/time in DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm.

The summary table below is a planning index, not the final validator target. The future task-matrix-plan.md artifact must render each task as a detailed task block with one explicit field per line, then optionally include a compact summary table for scanning.

Required task entry fields: Task, Date and time of task implementation, Source, Short description, Technical value, Product value, Scope, Non-goals, Expected result, Acceptance criteria, Verification gates, Risks / approval gates, Complexity, Estimated execution time, Agents, Skills, Output artifacts, Next step, and Completion Report.

Batch 37 implementation extension fields: Status, Depends on, Blocks, Schema version, Timezone, Plan trigger, and Validator target. These fields prevent hidden sequencing, distinguish detailed task blocks from summary tables, and keep lightweight work from being forced into heavyweight methodology artifacts.

Required completion report fields: what was done, files touched / work locations, technical value delivered, product value delivered, actual implementation date and time, verification evidence, residual risks, and follow-up.

Task matrix trigger policy: task-matrix plans are required for methodology-heavy work, specs/ADRs, multi-slice delivery, risky changes, cross-agent handoffs, evidence-heavy QA, release/approval work and any task that needs factual completion reporting. Small docs, formatting or mechanical edits may use a lightweight exception only when reason, reduced evidence path and residual risk are explicit.

Batch 37 S1 implementation contract:

  • B37-S1 implemented scope: T10-PLAN-M01..M03, T10-PLAN-M18.
  • Schema version: task_matrix_plan_v1 until a later validator slice explicitly changes it.
  • Timezone: Europe/Moscow; actual implementation timestamps use DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm.
  • Allowed task statuses: planned, in_progress, implemented, blocked, accepted_gap.
  • Status policy: planned rows use pending_execution_timestamp; implemented rows require factual touched files or work locations, current verification evidence and actual implementation date/time; blocked rows require blocker, owner or external-state dependency and safe next action; accepted_gap rows require owner/risk rationale and follow-up.
  • Dependency policy: Depends on and Blocks must be explicit task fields, not hidden in prose.
  • Validator target: detailed task blocks with one explicit field per line. Summary tables are planning indexes only and cannot become the final validator target.
  • Plan-file placement policy: .codex/artifact-templates/task-matrix-plan.md is the staged target for the future template; checked-in template source belongs under plugins/product-agent-os/assets/templates/artifact-templates/task-matrix-plan.md when S2 registers it; concrete project task matrices use owner-approved files such as docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<scope>-task-matrix.md or a project-specific equivalent.
  • Root PLAN.md adjacency rule: root PLAN.md keeps compact sequencing pointers and active boundaries; detailed task matrices live in source-owned plan files, then closure evidence moves to RUNLOG.md, Track backlogs and docs/sources/registry*.md as appropriate.
  • Real plan-file ownership rule: any new real-plan directory must have an owner/class decision before use; for this repository docs/superpowers/plans/ remains the source-owned plan location and generated .codex/artifact-templates/ remains staged output.
  • Lightweight exception fields: reason, reduced_evidence_path, residual_risk. Lightweight exception is allowed for typo fixes, small formatting changes and mechanical docs edits only when no methodology, risk, handoff, release, approval or factual completion-reporting trigger applies.
  • Planned rows are not implementation evidence. Generated views and detected task matrices are orientation evidence only until source files and current verification evidence support the claim.

docs.title: Batch 39: Product-Agent OS Functional Pilot Test Matrix And Automatic Result Collection
docs.text:
Batch 39 is the measurement and reproducibility layer before a meaningful B38-PROD-M12 post-pilot learning and release decision. Batch 38 proved the package source, local cache refresh, pilot design, safety/rollback procedure and one read-only docs-only target pilot. Batch 39 must convert that evidence into comparable pilot runs across Product-Agent OS capabilities and target archetypes, with automatic result collection, redaction, no-mutation proof, dashboard aggregation and a go/no-go packet.

Batch 39 is local-only/internal R&D unless the owner gives a separate public/team release decision. The default execution mode is read-only and staged-first. It does not mutate target workspaces, start live servers, run browser automation, call providers/live external model/API endpoints, mutate canonical graph sources, activate hooks/automations, publish externally or perform git stage/commit/push/PR without a separate exact approval packet.

Batch 39 matrix rows use the Batch 37 task-matrix contract: planned rows keep pending_execution_timestamp; implementation evidence must be added only after the exact slice runs with current command evidence, touched files or work locations, residual risks and follow-up.

Before any B39-S1..B39-S5 execution starts, the root prod_test.md ledger must exist and be updated for every test attempt. Each B39-TEST-* row needs attempt count, latest status, evidence refs, failure classification, Product-Agent OS change refs and retest status. If a test fails, the failure must be logged before Product-Agent OS is changed; any fix must name changed files and must remain fixed_pending_retest until the failed gate passes in a later attempt.

Batch 40 update: B40-S2 through B40-S5 added the local/manual completion-skeptic verifier loop, doubt_verification_packet_v1, completion_skeptic_manual_pilot_ledger, completion_skeptic_scorecard_calibration, completion_skeptic_go_no_go_closure and the final Batch 40 decision manual_only / not_promoted. Batch 39 must treat these as production-hardening inputs, not release proof. Any Batch 39 pilot, scorecard, dashboard, closure or readiness claim that says work is done, verified, release-ready or promotable must either link current completion-skeptic evidence or record an owner-reviewed accepted gap with owner, reason, residual risk and follow-up. Synthetic-local B40 rows can seed regression checks, but they cannot prove real pilot value, semantic usefulness, automation readiness or public/team release readiness.

B39-S5 Source-owned closure and go/no-go B39-TEST-M34..M36 Sequential docs/source closure after all M01..M54 evidence exists Source registry, backlog, root control-plane files and the B38-PROD-M12 decision packet must reflect actual pilot and hardening evidence, not planned intent. Stop when Batch 39 evidence is source-owned, no-unapproved-actions proof is recorded, and the owner has a clear release, block, defer or next-slice recommendation.

Batch 39 closure criteria: no B38-PROD-M12 release/readiness recommendation is supported until Batch 39 has at least one clean positive pilot, one expected-block negative pilot, coverage across the representative archetypes or accepted gaps for missing archetypes, current dashboard/rollup evidence, redaction and no-mutation proof, functional regression/repeatability evidence, production/mass-user hardening evidence for B39-TEST-M37..M54, complete prod_test.md attempt/failure/fix/retest ledger, source-owned closure and a final no-unapproved-actions review. After Batch 40, closure must also show that completion-skeptic evidence or owner-reviewed accepted gaps cover Batch 39 completion/readiness claims, that synthetic-local B40 calibration is not treated as release proof and that completion-skeptic remains manual_only / not_promoted unless real pilots, owner review and exact approval support a different decision. If those conditions are not met, B38-PROD-M12 must remain blocked, deferred or learning_only rather than release_ready.

docs.title: Batch 39 S4 Graph-Scope Depth Addendum
docs.text:
This addendum captures the planned implementation matrix for deeper graph-scope hardening after the S4 real-target retest fixed the imported-corpus scope blocker. It does not create Task 27, reopen closed Track 10 work, activate live runtime/browser/provider/MCP/Agents SDK surfaces, mutate target workspaces or turn the generated project graph into source truth. The goal is to upgrade project graph usefulness for AI agents: the graph should narrow the reading surface to verified or confidence-labelled entities, while source files and current verification remain required before edits, impact claims, readiness claims or completion claims.

Current graph-depth baseline:

  • project_graph_manifest.py collects bounded file metadata, fingerprints, language classification, freshness and scope_policy, including excluded imported skill/vendor-like prefixes.
  • project_graph_adapters.py already extracts Python packages, modules, classes, functions, methods, imports, direct/local calls, test links and unresolved calls with confidence labels.
  • project_graph_chunking.py already extracts structured Markdown headings, diagrams, OpenAPI operations, AsyncAPI channels, DBML/SQL tables and JSON/YAML top-level keys.
  • project_graph_queries.py already supports bounded neighbors, path, trace, search, hotspots, read_order, impact, affected_tests, changed_since and why_changed packets.
  • TypeScript/JavaScript currently remain mostly file_only / unsupported for entity-level graph depth, which limits SOL-style frontend and desktop/local-first target usefulness.

Batch 39 S4 graph-scope depth task matrix:

ID Priority Task Agents / skills Scope Technical value Product value Acceptance criteria Verification gates Risks / approval gates Status B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-00 P0 Decide layered graph ontology before parser expansion. Architect + Reviewer + Tester / implementation-planner, risk-reviewer, test-eval-designer Split graph ontology into structural_core, framework_extension and semantic_overlay; decide whether terms such as component, hook, api_route, store, event_handler, api_client, schema, table, operation and test_case are registered or kept as metadata. Prevents parser work from emitting ad-hoc node types, keeps graph schema compatibility explicit and gives later adapters a stable contract. User gets a graph that names entities the way agents and humans reason about projects, without pretending framework metadata is verified runtime behavior. Ontology decision packet records chosen node/edge terms, rejected terms, compatibility impact, migration/no-migration decision, query/filter behavior, framework-extension boundary and source-read boundary wording. Ontology validator tests; fixture expectation update; query filter tests for any new terms; docs/plan consistency check. Adding ontology terms is schema-visible and must stay backward-compatible; taxonomy alone cannot support readiness or completion claims. planned; pending_execution_timestamp B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-01 P0 Add synthetic mixed Python + TypeScript graph-depth fixture. Architect + Tester / implementation-planner, test-eval-designer Create a synthetic fixture with Python services, React component/hook, API client, backend handler, OpenAPI operation, schema/table node, tests, docs/contracts, changed/stale file case and deliberate ambiguous edges. Defines the pass/fail contract before extending parsers; prevents real-target-only tuning and proves stale/rejected-link behavior deterministically. User sees whether the graph can orient agents across backend, frontend, docs, tests and contracts without reading the whole project. Fixture expected nodes include Python symbols, TypeScript exported symbols/components/hooks, imports/exports, contract/schema chunks, affected tests, stale markers, rejected links and unresolved/unsupported edge inventory. RED/GREEN unit tests for fixture graph counts, node IDs, confidence labels, stale blocks, rejected links, no raw source, no absolute paths, bounded query packets and search quality. Synthetic fixture cannot prove SOL usefulness; keep real-target retest separate. planned; pending_execution_timestamp B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-02 P0 Add minimal TypeScript/JavaScript entity adapter. Builder + Tester + Security/Data Owner / test-eval-designer, risk-reviewer Extend language overlays to extract TS/JS modules, imports, exports, exported functions/classes, React components and hooks with line spans after ontology and parser-dependency decisions are recorded. Turns frontend-heavy projects from file-level orientation into entity-level navigation while preserving conservative confidence and explicit unsupported-syntax inventory. Agents can find components, hooks, API clients and relevant tests without broad recursive source reads. Adapter emits stable existing or registered extension node types; parser errors, JSX/TSX dynamic constructs, ambiguous patterns and unsupported syntax are recorded as unsupported or inferred, not verified. Focused adapter tests; parser-error fixture; JSX/TSX fixture; unsupported dynamic construct fixture; no-source-body/redaction tests; graph ontology validation; search/affected-tests regression. No external parser dependency unless approved; if stdlib-only parsing is insufficient, stage dependency decision separately. planned; pending_execution_timestamp B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-03 P0 Retest SOL read-only graph usefulness after TypeScript depth. Architect + Product Manager + Tester / workspace-discovery-auditor, test-eval-designer Run read-only SOL graph dry-run and graph query packets after synthetic adapter passes. Measures whether the new adapter improves a real frontend/desktop-local-first target without target mutation. User gets evidence that SOL graph is no longer mostly file inventory and can answer agent orientation questions. SOL summary records node/edge/observation counts, TS entity counts, top path prefixes, unsupported-language inventory, sample searches, affected-tests packets and safe-next-action wording. scan_project_code_graph.py <SOL> --dry-run; graph query packets against staged/temporary graph artifact; comparison with previous S4 summaries. SOL remains read-only; source-policy/runtime blocks remain; no browser/runtime/provider/git/external action. planned; pending_execution_timestamp B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-04 P0 Add agent reading packet for graph-first workflows. Architect + Agent Team Designer + Tester / agent-team-designer, test-eval-designer, risk-reviewer Add a bounded query/output contract that returns target entity, top related entities, read order, source spans, confidence, unresolved edges, affected tests, stale status, rejected links and must-read-before-edit warnings. Converts raw graph/search output into the primary safe handoff surface for AI agents and makes source-read compliance machine-checkable. Agents can ask the graph first, then read only the necessary source files before editing or making claims. Packet includes source_boundary, generated_view_policy, confidence_summary, must_read_source_before_edit, source_read_required, unsupported_claims, affected_tests, budget, stale_status, rejected_links and safe_next_action. Unit tests for packet shape, truncation, stale graph block, unsupported language warnings, rejected-link visibility, no proof/readiness wording and fixture/search quality cases. Packet is orientation evidence only; no autonomous agent launch, no parallel subagent activation and no completion/readiness claim from graph hits alone. planned; pending_execution_timestamp B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-05 P1 Add cross-language link planning and conservative linker fixture. Architect + Backend/API Reviewer + Tester / implementation-planner, risk-reviewer, test-eval-designer Stage a linker contract for frontend API clients to backend handlers, OpenAPI operations and schema/table nodes, starting with synthetic explicit naming evidence only. Separates entity extraction from relationship inference and prevents cross-language edges from being guessed. Agents can see where a frontend call may connect to backend/API/data layers, while knowing which links are verified, inferred, rejected or unsupported. Linker packet defines allowed evidence sources, edge confidence rules, unresolved link inventory, rejected heuristics, rejected-link evidence and source-read requirements; synthetic fixture covers positive, ambiguous and false-positive cases. Linker fixture tests; graph validation; trace/path query tests; false-positive tests for similarly named operations and routes; rejected-link ledger check. Do not infer runtime behavior, auth, data flow or production API compatibility from static links alone. planned; pending_execution_timestamp B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-06 P1 Add graph usefulness scorecard for agent navigation. Product Manager + Tester + Learning Loop Maintainer / test-eval-designer, learning-loop-maintainer Measure symbol recall, top-k/MRR, affected-test precision, false positives, reading-scope reduction, unsupported-language rate, stale-block behavior, tool-call/file-read/token/time deltas, time-to-first-safe-action and real-target comparison deltas. Moves graph quality from "valid JSON" to measurable agent-navigation usefulness. User can decide whether graph-first workflows actually save time, reduce project rereads and make agent handoffs safer. Scorecard records deterministic fixture metrics, SOL comparison metrics, accepted gaps, unsupported claims, cost/time deltas and thresholds that block readiness/promotion claims. Search-quality tests; fixture eval markers; SOL read-only comparison artifact; no-generated-view-as-proof checks; metric schema regression. Metrics from synthetic fixtures or one read-only target do not prove broad semantic usefulness or release readiness. planned; pending_execution_timestamp B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-07 P0 Stage TypeScript parser dependency decision. Architect + Security/Data Owner + Release Operator / risk-reviewer, test-eval-designer Decide between a conservative stdlib tokenizer, vendored local parser, existing project dependency reuse, tree-sitter WASM as a first-class option or deferred parser support before implementation. Avoids hidden dependency installation, supply-chain drift and brittle regex parsing claims. User sees the cost, precision, safety and maintenance tradeoff before parser work expands. Decision records parser option, no-network/default behavior, dependency/vendoring status, license/hash expectations, rollback, unsupported syntax classes, tree-sitter WASM feasibility and exact approval needs. Dependency-decision fixture; no-install proof; docs check; adapter tests must cite decision status before passing. Installing or vendoring a new parser requires exact approval; parser choice cannot authorize browser/runtime/provider/git/external actions. planned; pending_execution_timestamp B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-08 P0 Add graph entity coverage map. Architect + Tester + Docs Maintainer / implementation-planner, test-eval-designer, docs-maintainer Define and emit coverage by language, path prefix, file type, node type, unsupported parser class, skipped file reason and generated/vendor/imported scope policy. Makes graph blind spots explicit and prevents node count from hiding missing language or module coverage. User and agents can see where the graph is reliable, partial or intentionally silent before relying on it. Coverage map records covered files, partial files, skipped files, unsupported languages, unsupported syntax, confidence distribution and owner-readable recommended next parser/linker action. Unit tests for coverage map schema; fixture with supported, partial and skipped files; redaction/no-absolute-path checks; status/dashboard rollup check. Coverage is diagnostic, not proof of semantic correctness; generated/vendor/imported exclusions remain policy-controlled. planned; pending_execution_timestamp B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-09 P0 Add stale graph and freshness gates. Builder + Tester + Risk Reviewer / test-eval-designer, risk-reviewer Block action-oriented graph packets when source fingerprints, manifest timestamps or changed-since checks show stale or partial graph state. Prevents agents from following outdated graph edges after file changes. User gets safer graph-first workflows because stale outputs become refresh prompts, not confident advice. Freshness gate marks packets as fresh, partial, stale or unknown; stale packets suppress edit/readiness language and point to the smallest refresh action. Unit tests for changed fixture files; changed_since / why_changed query regression; packet suppression tests; no false freshness from generated HTML. Freshness cannot authorize target mutation or watcher activation; no background watcher is enabled without exact approval. planned; pending_execution_timestamp B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-10 P1 Integrate agent graph packets into first-run artifact and status surfaces. Builder + Product Manager + Docs Maintainer / agent-team-designer, docs-maintainer, test-eval-designer Add packet summaries, source-read warnings, coverage map, freshness status and safe next action to first-run JSON, status snapshot and HTML artifact inputs. Connects graph depth to existing Batch 39 artifact flow instead of creating a separate disconnected output. User opens one artifact pack and sees what agents can use, what humans should inspect and what remains unsafe. First-run packet contains graph packet digest, coverage/freshness summary, unsupported claims, source-read-before-edit wording and links to graph artifacts without raw source bodies. Renderer/input schema tests; first-run artifact fixture; redaction report check; previous-baseline diff check; docs/source-registry consistency when source-backed claims change. HTML/status remains orientation evidence only and must not become proof, release evidence or target source of truth. planned; pending_execution_timestamp B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-11 P1 Add framework semantics layer. Architect + Frontend Reviewer + Tester / implementation-planner, test-eval-designer, risk-reviewer Detect common React/Next/Vite/Electron/Tauri patterns as framework-extension metadata separate from generic TS extraction. Gives richer navigation without corrupting the core graph with framework guesses. Agents can distinguish components, hooks, routes, stores, runtime entrypoints and shell/native boundaries when evidence is explicit. Semantics layer records evidence source, confidence, unsupported framework version/signature and fallback to generic TS nodes when framework evidence is weak. Synthetic framework fixture tests; false-positive route/component tests; unsupported framework inventory; query filter tests. Framework semantics are static hints, not proof of runtime routing, auth, browser behavior or native packaging. planned; pending_execution_timestamp B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-12 P1 Add rejected-link ledger. Tester + Risk Reviewer + Learning Loop Maintainer / test-eval-designer, risk-reviewer, learning-loop-maintainer Persist rejected candidate links with reason codes for weak naming, ambiguous route, missing target, generated/vendor boundary, stale source or unsupported parser class. Makes conservative inference auditable and turns false-positive prevention into testable evidence. User can trust the graph more because it explains what it refused to connect and why. Ledger records rejected link source, target candidate, rule, reason, confidence, source-read requirement and whether a future parser/linker task could resolve it. Rejected-link fixture tests; false-positive regression; HTML/packet visibility check; no raw source/body leakage. Rejected candidates cannot be treated as hidden dependencies or impact proof. planned; pending_execution_timestamp B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-13 P2 Add guided project tour derived from graph communities and evidence. Product Manager + UX Reviewer + Docs Maintainer / docs-maintainer, test-eval-designer Generate a bounded orientation tour: entrypoints, major subsystems, data/API flow candidates, tests, docs/contracts, hotspots, unsupported zones and next read order. Turns graph data into an onboarding narrative without requiring manual graph interpretation. End user gets a faster first understanding of a project and knows where the generated view is uncertain. Tour pages label every claim as source-backed, graph-derived, inferred, rejected or unsupported; every section links to source artifacts and safe next action. Fixture tour snapshot tests; redaction checks; no generated-view-as-proof wording; HTML navigation smoke via static file checks. Tour is a guided orientation artifact, not architecture truth or readiness proof. planned; pending_execution_timestamp B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-14 P1 Calibrate graph benchmark and promotion thresholds. Product Manager + Tester + Completion Skeptic / test-eval-designer, completion-skeptic, learning-loop-maintainer Define thresholds for graph packet usefulness, stale handling, false positives, reading-scope reduction and real-target deltas before any promotion/readiness language. Prevents subjective "the graph feels better" closure and ties future implementation to measured improvement. User gets a clear go/no-go basis for deciding whether graph-first agent workflows are worth using beyond experiments. Benchmark packet defines minimum fixture scores, accepted gaps, target-retention checks, failure labels and conditions that keep graph work manual_only / not_promoted. Fixture scorecard; SOL/Neural Flow comparison when applicable; doubt packet review; docs/control-plane sync. Thresholds from small target sets remain local calibration, not production/mass-user proof. planned; pending_execution_timestamp B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-15 P1 Upgrade HTML artifact into a deep project explainer. Builder + Product Manager + UX Reviewer / docs-maintainer, test-eval-designer Replace generic per-page evidence tables with page-specific sections for architecture, graph, code flow, risks, recommended reads, unsupported zones, rejected links, coverage and freshness. Makes the offline artifact useful as a human inspection surface, not just a schema-valid export shell. User can open HTML and understand what the project contains, what the graph found, what it refused to infer and what to check next. HTML artifact includes page-specific narrative, source status labels, graph coverage visuals/tables, guided tour, rejected-link summary, freshness warnings, safe next actions and no raw private source bodies. Renderer snapshot tests; manifest/page digest tests; static HTML checks; redaction report; no-overclaim wording tests; previous-baseline comparison. HTML remains generated orientation evidence and must not be promoted to source truth, runtime proof or release evidence. planned; pending_execution_timestamp

Graph-scope depth sequencing recommendation:

Slice Tasks Execution mode Why this grouping Stop / handoff condition B39-S4-GD-S0 Ontology and parser decision B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-00, B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-07 Sequential, planning-first Parser output must have stable ontology and an approved dependency/supply-chain boundary before code changes. Stop when node/edge taxonomy and parser option are recorded, or when an exact dependency approval is needed. B39-S4-GD-S1 Synthetic contract B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-01 Sequential, TDD-first The mixed fixture defines exact graph semantics before implementation touches parser logic. Stop when RED/GREEN tests prove the expected entity, edge, confidence and query packet contract. B39-S4-GD-S2 TS/JS adapter B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-02 Sequential, adapter-owned TypeScript/JavaScript depth is the highest-value missing implementation layer for SOL-style projects. Stop when focused adapter, ontology, query and safety tests pass, or when dependency approval is needed. B39-S4-GD-S3 Framework and linker hardening B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-05, B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-11, B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-12 Sequential, conservative-linker-first Entity extraction alone does not connect frontend, backend, contracts and data; linker/framework rules must reject weak guesses and record rejected evidence. Stop when explicit synthetic links work, ambiguous links stay unresolved and rejected-link evidence is visible. B39-S4-GD-S4 Coverage and freshness B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-08, B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-09 Sequential safety layer Agents need to know which graph zones are reliable and whether the graph is stale before using packets. Stop when coverage and freshness gates block unsafe action-oriented packets and surface a refresh/read-order recommendation. B39-S4-GD-S5 Real-target retest B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-03 Read-only target evidence Real-target usefulness must be measured after synthetic correctness, not before. Stop when SOL comparison shows improved entity usefulness or records a specific blocker without readiness claims. B39-S4-GD-S6 Agent handoff and usefulness scorecard B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-04, B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-06, B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-14 Sequential contract + eval Agent value depends on compact reading packets, measurable reading-scope reduction and thresholded promotion rules, not raw graph dumps. Stop when agent reading packets reduce reading scope in fixtures, preserve source-read-before-edit boundaries and record usefulness metrics without readiness claims. B39-S4-GD-S7 Artifact integration and guided HTML B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-10, B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-13, B39-S4-GRAPH-DEPTH-15 Sequential artifact layer The graph needs both machine-readable agent packets and human-readable HTML explanations, with the same boundaries and evidence labels. Stop when first-run JSON/status/HTML expose packet, coverage, freshness, guided tour and rejected-link summaries without raw source or overclaim wording.

Known graph-scope depth gaps to analyze before implementation:

  • TypeScript/JavaScript extraction may require either a conservative stdlib tokenizer or an approved local parser dependency; dependency installation or vendoring requires a separate decision.
  • React/Next/Vite/Electron/Tauri semantics need framework-specific recognition; do not claim universal frontend intelligence from generic TS symbols.
  • Cross-language links from frontend API clients to backend routes, OpenAPI operations and database schemas are not covered by Python or TS symbol extraction alone.
  • Method/function call precision must distinguish verified import/export edges from inferred direct calls and unsupported dynamic dispatch.
  • Agent packets need freshness and provenance fields so stale graph artifacts block action-oriented claims.
  • Existing first-run HTML pages are still mostly page shells with generic evidence tables; deep project explanation needs page-specific sections, guided tour, coverage/freshness summaries and rejected-link visibility.
  • Rejected links are positive product evidence because they show where the graph refused weak inference instead of creating misleading relationships.
  • HTML and graph packets must repeat generated_view_only and must_read_source_before_edit boundaries; no raw private source snippets, secrets or absolute user-specific paths should be persisted.
  • Graph quality must be measured as agent navigation usefulness: recall, MRR, false positives, affected-test precision, reading-scope reduction, tool-call/file-read/token/time deltas, time-to-first-safe-action and real-target comparison deltas, not only validation success or node count.

docs.title: Batch 39 M20 Addendum: First-Run Project Intelligence Artifact
docs.text:
This addendum captures the planned implementation matrix for a first-run project intelligence artifact. It does not create Task 27, reopen closed Track 10 work, activate hooks, start browser/runtime automation, use external stage paths or turn HTML into source of truth. The goal is to compose existing Product-Agent OS discovery, runtime routing, status dashboard, project graph and cockpit capabilities into one versioned, multi-page offline artifact pack created directly inside the user's project under .codex/product-agent-os/analysis/.

Current implementation baseline:

  • discovery.py already detects stack, control-plane files, .codex assets, usage mode, methodology signals, methodology gaps, route inputs, risks and guided-question seeds.
  • render_status_dashboard.py, status_snapshot.py and status_dashboard.py already build a read-only status snapshot and offline .codex/product-agent-os/status.html / status.json.
  • scan_project_code_graph.py already stages .codex/product-agent-os/project-code-graph.json and .jsonl with graph shrink guards and no raw source body policy.
  • project_graph_renderer.py already stages .codex/product-agent-os/project-cockpit.html / .json using project graph and code-flow templates.
  • offline_artifact_export.py already has an approval-aware offline HTML export contract, but current exports are single-surface contracts rather than one versioned multi-page first-run artifact pack.

Planned artifact shape:

.codex/product-agent-os/analysis/
  analysis-manifest.json
  first-run-analysis.json
  discovery.json
  runtime-route.json
  source-policy.json
  methodology-audit.json
  status-snapshot.json
  project-code-graph.json
  project-code-graph.jsonl
  project-cockpit.json
  redaction-report.json
  pages/
    index.html
    overview.html
    inventory.html
    architecture.html
    control-plane.html
    methodology.html
    runtime-route.html
    project-graph.html
    code-flow.html
    quality-evals.html
    risks.html
    recommendations.html

Batch 39 M20 first-run artifact task matrix:

ID Priority Task Agents / skills Scope Technical value for project Product value for user Acceptance criteria Verification gates Risks / approval gates Status B39-FRIA-M20.1 P0 Define first_run_analysis_packet_v1. Architect + Tester / implementation-planner, test-eval-designer Add a schema contract that composes discovery, runtime route, methodology audit, control-plane state, source policy, graph summaries, status snapshot, redaction summary, page registry and safe next action. Creates a stable source packet instead of relying on scattered dashboard, graph and command outputs. User gets one baseline project snapshot that future runs can diff and maintain. Packet has schema_version, artifact_version, generated_at, target label, write policy, source artifacts, generated pages, digests, redaction status, evidence status and generated-view policy. Schema unit tests; JSON round-trip; no-placeholder field coverage; stale/inspection-only fixture. Packet is source evidence container, not readiness proof; no raw source bodies, secrets or absolute user-specific paths. implemented; 2026-06-18; evidence: B39-FRIA-M20.1-A01, tests/product_agent_os/test_first_run_analysis.py, plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/product_agent_os/first_run_analysis.py B39-FRIA-M20.2 P0 Add first-run orchestrator CLI. Builder + Architect / workspace-discovery-auditor, implementation-planner Create run_first_project_analysis.py and/or product_agent_os/first_run_analysis.py to run read-only preflight, discovery, runtime route, methodology audit, hygiene audit, graph generation, cockpit model and status snapshot in deterministic order. Converts independent analyzers into a repeatable pipeline with explicit dependencies and stop conditions. User can run one command and get a complete in-project analysis pack instead of separate manual steps. CLI supports --dry-run and a direct in-project write mode that writes only under .codex/product-agent-os/analysis/; it must not require an external stage path or external dependency. CLI contract tests; generated-path boundary tests; read-only target mutation proof outside the generated artifact directory; expected-block fixture. Writes are limited to the generated analysis directory; live server, browser automation, provider calls, unrelated target writes and git actions remain blocked without exact approval. implemented; 2026-06-18; evidence: B39-FRIA-M20.2-A01, plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/run_first_project_analysis.py, tests/product_agent_os/test_first_run_analysis.py B39-FRIA-M20.3 P0 Build analyzer adapter layer. Architect + Builder / workspace-discovery-auditor, risk-reviewer Normalize existing outputs from analyze_workspace, run_contract, methodology audit, build_status_snapshot, graph scanner and cockpit model into one packet with explicit provenance. Prevents tight coupling between renderers and low-level analyzer internals. User sees where every conclusion came from and which evidence is missing. Every section names source module, source artifact, evidence freshness, confidence, unsupported claims and accepted gaps. Adapter tests with docs-only, frontend, backend, AI/RAG, data, desktop/local-first and plugin fixtures. Detection remains present_unverified until current command/runtime/owner evidence exists. implemented; 2026-06-18; evidence: B39-FRIA-M20.3-A01, adapt_first_run_analysis_sections, tests/product_agent_os/test_first_run_analysis.py B39-FRIA-M20.4 P0 Add multi-page offline artifact renderer. Builder + Product Manager + Docs Maintainer / test-eval-designer, docs-maintainer Add analysis_artifact_renderer.py with a declarative page registry and templates for overview, inventory, architecture, methodology, runtime route, control plane, graph, code flow, quality/evals, risks and recommendations. Reuses existing status/cockpit rendering safety while making the first-run artifact maintainable and versionable. User gets an immediately inspectable HTML artifact with all important project pages from the first launch. Renderer outputs offline HTML pages plus analysis-manifest.json directly under .codex/product-agent-os/analysis/; every page links back to source artifacts and shows generated-view-only wording. HTML safety tests; no external URLs/scripts; mobile viewport static checks; section coverage tests; embedded JSON escaping tests. HTML is generated orientation evidence only and cannot support completion, release or readiness claims by itself. implemented; 2026-06-18; evidence: B39-FRIA-M20.4-A01, analysis_artifact_renderer.py, offline HTML safety tests B39-FRIA-M20.5 P0 Add manifest, digest and diff baseline support. Builder + Tester / test-eval-designer Extend artifact manifest handling for multi-file analysis packs with stable page IDs, content digests, source artifact digests and previous-baseline comparison metadata. Enables version control and regression detection for first-run and repeated-run artifacts. User can compare what changed between the first project scan and later scans. Manifest records page/source digests, renderer version, plugin version, target fingerprint, previous baseline status and changed/added/removed page/source summaries. Manifest digest tests; previous-baseline fixture; suspicious shrink/change guard; deterministic sort tests. Digests must not expose private contents; target fingerprint must be bounded and redacted. implemented; 2026-06-18; evidence: B39-FRIA-M20.5-A01, analysis_artifact_renderer.py, manifest digest and previous-baseline tests B39-FRIA-M20.6 P0 Add redaction, privacy and source-policy guardrails. Security/Data Owner + Reviewer / risk-reviewer, test-eval-designer Apply one no-secrets/no-raw-source/no-absolute-path policy to packet JSON, graph JSON/JSONL, page HTML, manifests and generated recommendations. Makes first-run artifacts safe for internal review and future versioning. User can keep the artifact in the project without leaking private data. Redaction report records blocked categories, counts and accepted false positives; unsafe values block artifact finalization. Secret/path/raw-body negative tests; private path fixtures; source-policy expected-block fixture. Real target details stay read-only; source-policy block must stop apply/promotion, not hide the artifact's diagnostic value. implemented; 2026-06-18; evidence: B39-FRIA-M20.6-A01, packet secret-like validation, renderer redaction report and source-policy gate tests B39-FRIA-M20.7 P1 Integrate first-run artifact into status dashboard and pilot rollups. Builder + Product Manager / test-eval-designer, learning-loop-maintainer Add snapshot fields and rollup references so status.html, pilot manifests and Batch 39 rollups can point to the analysis pack without duplicating it. Keeps generated surfaces coherent and avoids parallel sources of truth. User can open status/rollup and navigate to the full first-run analysis. docs.title: Batch 40: Doubt / Verifier Loop Completion-Skeptic Gate
docs.text:
Batch 40 is an owner-requested Task 26 planning addendum for turning the researched "doubt technique" into a Product-Agent OS verification-first completion gate. It is based on output/doubt-technique-comparative-report.md and output/doubt-verifier-loop-batch-task-matrix.md. It does not create Task 27, reopen completed Track 10 live/provider/canonical-mutation work or authorize implementation by itself.

Batch 40 must implement the recommended architecture as worker_output -> doubt_verification_packet -> completion-skeptic -> revise_or_pass. The gate must follow CoVe-style claim extraction, CRITIC-style tool/source/test-backed verification and evaluator-optimizer routing. It must not become an unconditional self-reflection rewrite prompt: the verifier finds evidence-backed gaps first, and the reviser changes only those gaps.

Batch 40 is local-only/internal R&D unless the owner gives a separate public/team release decision. The default execution mode is staged-first. It does not mutate target workspaces, start live servers, run browser automation, call providers/live external model/API endpoints, mutate canonical graph sources, activate hooks/automations, publish externally or perform git stage/commit/push/PR without a separate exact approval packet.

Batch 40 matrix rows use the Batch 37 task-matrix contract: planned rows keep pending_execution_timestamp; implementation evidence must be added only after the exact slice runs with current command evidence, touched files or work locations, residual risks and follow-up. Dashboard/status projections remain generated review views and cannot prove completion by themselves.

Second-pass architecture audit adds one correction to the first Batch 40 shape: the Doubt / verifier loop must be implemented as a layered evidence policy, not only as a new skill. The current system already has codex_runtime_runner route packets, verified_claims / unsupported_claims handoff fields, status snapshot warnings, source policy, transcript evals, task-matrix completion reports and agent_skill_metrics_loop; Batch 40 must connect to those existing surfaces before considering hooks, MCP, Agents SDK guardrails or automation candidates.

docs.title: Risk Register
docs.text: Risk Mitigation The plugin asks too many questions and stalls the user. Enforce one blocking question in first response and max eight total questions. HTML dashboard becomes stale and misleading. Show generated_at, evidence freshness, inspection-only banner and source digests. Dashboard is treated as source of truth. Docs and snapshot policy state JSON/Markdown control-plane is source of truth. Dashboard leaks local paths or private data. Reuse runtime redaction and add dashboard-specific tests for path/secret leakage. Existing project dashboard files are overwritten. Preserve unmarked files as companion proposals and use staged-first merge flow. Question answers become hidden memory. Store answers only in explicit ledger artifacts, never user-level memory. New runtime fields break schema-v1 compatibility. Add fields only inside existing route packet surfaces and validate bounded shape. Self-verification is mistaken for approval to rewrite agents, skills or harness policy. Stage scorecards and update candidates only; require owner approval, rollback target and current evidence before any later apply flow. Metrics overfit to recently implemented tasks and miss regressions. Keep holdout, prior-failure, synthetic regression and flaky-case groups separate; require raw numerator/denominator counts and confidence evidence. Agent/skill evidence leaks private traces or local user paths. Reuse redaction gates before dataset, ledger, report or dashboard generation and block scoring when redaction fails. Metrics-loop automation is activated before the manual workflow is stable. Ship daily and weekly automation files as candidate templates only and require automation_manual_stability_present plus explicit approval before promotion. Docs-only or simple maintenance work triggers agentic modernization overhead. Add discovery false-positive fixtures and keep agent_skill_metrics_loop applicable only when real agent, skill, subagent, router/tool policy, automation candidate or harness surfaces are detected. Code graph overwhelms the browser or agent context on large projects. Use graph summaries, chunked JSON/JSONL, clustering, top-N subgraphs, hidden labels and query packets for 1k, 5k and 10k node cases. Code graph implies false dependency precision. Require confidence labels, unsupported-language statuses and tests that distinguish AST/static evidence from inferred edges. Static analysis invents cross-file call edges in ambiguous code. Prefer import-guided resolution, emit inferred global calls only on single-candidate matches and record ambiguous calls as explicit uncertainty. Incremental cache reports stale topology as fresh. Store manifest freshness with separate AST/semantic hashes, changed/unchanged/added/deleted file sets and graph freshness status. Failed scans silently replace a rich graph with a much smaller artifact. Add shrink guard and stage-local backups before overwrite; require explicit acceptance for suspicious graph collapse. Agent graph queries expand through high-degree hub nodes and waste context. Add token-budgeted BFS/DFS traversal, hub suppression, context filters, seed scoring and truncation metadata. Graph artifacts leak source code, secrets or local user paths. Exclude raw file contents by default, keep line spans/hashes only, reuse redaction policy and block secret-like values in renderer/query output. HTML graph is treated as source of truth. Keep code/docs plus graph JSON/JSONL as source/evidence layers; HTML remains generated cockpit review output. Graph visualization libraries introduce network or supply-chain risk. Use owner-selected Cosmos.gl only as locally bundled, version-recorded assets with no CDN; keep Graphology-compatible payloads as internal interchange, Sigma.js as fallback/compatibility-only, and preserve a static/table fallback renderer. Cockpit navigation hides important warnings after page grouping. Preserve every detailed section exactly once, add local section navigation and test Source Conflicts, Verification Gates and Security/Risk visibility. Eight-page cockpit shell becomes a second documentation site instead of a project map. Keep pages action-oriented: source links, graph packets, stale flags, verification gates, approval boundaries and proposal lifecycle must remain visible.

docs.title: Track 11 Documentation Architecture Refresh Plan
docs.text:
Source status: local implementation planning

For agentic workers: REQUIRED ROUTING: use docs-maintainer for documentation/source-registry alignment, implementation-planner for task slicing, completion-skeptic before readiness claims, and test-eval-designer for docs/site verification gates. Do not treat generated site/, HTML cockpits, graph outputs, dashboards, scorecards or memory as source truth.

Goal: Refresh Product-Agent OS documentation so the public/docs layer matches the deeper current implementation: Batch 41 first-run orchestration, Architecture Intelligence Cockpit, graph/code/schema surfaces, evidence/risk hierarchy, visual/accessibility gates, Batch 42 instruction/tool-use compliance planning, Batch 44 Self-Learning Loop activation planning, Batch 45 professional code authoring standards planning, and the source-vs-generated trust boundary.

Architecture: Track 11 is a docs architecture track, not a runtime/product implementation track. It turns current source-owned evidence from RUNLOG.md, Track 10 plan/backlog files, Product-Agent OS docs, renderer contracts, tests and spec artifacts into reader-facing documentation, diagram atlas updates, artifact contract maps and site-refresh gates. Source Markdown and registry/backlog files remain canonical; generated site/ is a rebuild output and stale until strict MkDocs evidence exists.

Tech Stack: Markdown, MkDocs Material, Mermaid/static diagrams, local Product-Agent OS docs contracts, tools/check_docs.py, tests.product_agent_os.test_product_agent_os_docs, strict MkDocs, git diff hygiene, optional source-safe generated diagrams and no external runtime/provider/browser/git/cache/global-config action without separate approval.

docs.text:
Track 11 includes documentation planning and later documentation implementation for:

  • current docs-vs-site drift after Batch 41 and Batch 42 compliance planning, captured under Batch 43 docs refresh;

  • artifact schema and generated-view trust boundaries;
  • diagram atlas expansion for source/generated/evidence/runtime boundaries;
  • Batch 42 instruction/tool-use compliance documentation;
  • Batch 44 Self-Learning Loop activation and improvement planning;
  • Batch 45 professional code authoring standards and leverage planning;
  • site rebuild and publication-readiness gates.

Track 11 does not implement runtime features, refresh installed plugin cache, mutate global Codex config, activate hooks/automations/MCP, call providers, run browser automation, create git actions, publish docs, or claim release readiness.

docs.title: Batch 44 Self-Learning Loop Activation And Improvement Plan
docs.text:
Source status: local implementation planning with arXiv research intake

Batch 44 plans the next implementation path for Product-Agent OS Self-Learning Loop. It starts from the current local gap: the repository has staged learning, metrics and automation-candidate infrastructure, but no active weekly scheduler, no real Codex session satisfaction ingestion and no populated operational metrics ledger. The loop scope is Product-Agent OS project work only: it must not analyze all user Codex sessions, hidden app logs or unrelated projects. Batch 44 must preserve the existing safety boundary: no self-applied updates, no raw private chat logs, no active schedule, no hook activation, no provider/model calls and no external writes without a later exact approval packet.

Research window: arXiv papers submitted or revised from 2025-06 through 2026-06. These papers are planning inputs, not source truth for Product-Agent OS runtime behavior.

docs.title: Batch 44 Research Synthesis
docs.text: Source Mechanism observed Batch 44 planning implication arXiv:2507.21046, A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents Frames self-evolving agents around what evolves, when evolution happens and how adaptation is driven across model, memory, tools and architecture; also calls out evaluation, safety and co-evolution risks. Split Product-Agent OS loop into explicit evolution targets: prompt/context, memory/preferences, skill text, routing policy, eval datasets and harnesses. Every target needs a separate candidate, evidence window, rollback target and owner review. arXiv:2508.07407, A Comprehensive Survey of Self-Evolving AI Agents Presents a feedback-loop framing with system inputs, agent system, environment and optimisers, plus evaluation/safety/ethics as first-class concerns. Make self_learning_state, feedback ledger, metrics ledger and optimizer/candidate generator separate bounded components instead of one hidden daemon. arXiv:2507.19457, GEPA Uses natural-language reflection over trajectories, tool calls and outputs to diagnose problems and propose/test prompt updates, combining lessons through a Pareto-style selection process. Generate modernization candidates from run evidence and reflection, but keep them staged-only; candidate ranking should cite metric deltas and risk, not auto-apply prompt or skill edits. arXiv:2510.04618, Agentic Context Engineering Evolves offline contexts such as system prompts and online contexts such as memory using natural execution feedback. Treat Codex/project instructions, skills, memory policy and retrieval context as separate versioned context layers; update proposals require eval reruns and rollback. arXiv:2510.09801, PULSE Evaluates human-agent interaction by collecting user feedback, predicting user satisfaction and combining human ratings with pseudo-labels; reports that benchmark performance may diverge from in-the-wild satisfaction. User satisfaction must be a first-class Product-Agent OS metric. Agent completion claims cannot substitute for owner feedback, revision acceptance, user effort or follow-up complaints. arXiv:2603.20939, VARS Uses long-term and short-term user preference vectors updated from weak scalar user rewards to bias retrieval and reduce user effort without per-user fine-tuning. Add explicit, privacy-safe preference summaries and weak feedback fields, but keep them owner-readable/editable and never store raw private sessions. arXiv:2510.09720, PAMU Refines preference memory with sliding-window and exponential-moving-average signals to capture short-term shifts and long-term tendencies. Track both recent satisfaction/revision signals and long-horizon owner preferences; stale preference summaries should decay or require owner confirmation. arXiv:2507.05257, MemoryAgentBench Evaluates memory agents on accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding and selective forgetting in incremental multi-turn settings. Batch 44 evals must test not only recall, but also update quality, forgetting/redaction and long-horizon usefulness. arXiv:2511.20857, Evo-Memory Evaluates self-evolving memory over continuous task streams where agents search, adapt and update memory after each interaction; introduces action-think-memory refinement. Build a streaming eval fixture for Product-Agent OS work: task outcome, feedback, reflection, memory/update candidate and next-run behavior. arXiv:2603.03329, AutoHarness Iteratively synthesizes code harnesses from environment feedback to prevent illegal actions and improve agent behavior. Treat hook/rule/harness changes as guarded candidates with negative tests for forbidden actions, not as direct runtime activation. arXiv:2510.26852, CATArena Separates static generation proficiency from evolutionary potential through multi-turn tournaments and execution feedback. Add metrics that distinguish one-shot task quality from improvement after feedback; do not promote a loop that only looks good on initial outputs. arXiv:2510.23595, Multi-Agent Evolve Uses proposer, solver and judge roles to co-evolve task generation, solving and judging. Use role-separated subagents only for staged candidate generation/evaluation when file ownership is independent; avoid letting the same agent both propose and approve its own update. arXiv:2506.15841, MEM1 Maintains compact evolving state across long-horizon interactions to reduce unbounded memory growth. Product-Agent OS should store compact summaries, metric rows and preference signals, not full transcripts or unlimited memory dumps. arXiv:2512.16301, Adaptation of Agentic AI Organizes adaptation across post-training, memory and skills, including agent-output-signaled and tool/skill adaptation. Keep adaptation target taxonomy explicit: agent instructions, skills, memory, datasets, graders, harnesses and tool policy each need separate ownership and verification.

docs.title: Batch 44 Design Principles
docs.text:
• Manual-first: the first implementation must be --dry-run / --stage, not a daemon.
  • Due-check is not execution: a weekly check may say a run is due, but cannot run the loop unless an approved command or automation invokes it.
  • Product-Agent OS project scope only: session and feedback analysis is eligible only for workspaces with explicit Product-Agent OS evidence such as .codex/product-agent-os/, a Product-Agent OS config/skill/plan artifact or an owner-approved scope marker; unrelated user sessions and hidden app telemetry are out of scope.
  • User satisfaction is evidence: owner feedback, revision acceptance, usefulness and user effort are stronger than an assistant saying done.
  • Privacy first: no raw private chat logs, raw Codex transcripts, secrets, credentials, customer data or unredacted PII in ledgers, fixtures, reports or memory.
  • Append-only metrics: baseline/current/candidate versions, score deltas, confidence intervals and accepted gaps must be recorded before comparing improvement or regression.
  • Progress is a project artifact: every approved run must persist resumable progress state and render a project-local offline HTML artifact that displays due status, run progress, metric deltas, blockers and owner-review state; generated HTML remains orientation evidence, not proof by itself.
  • Candidate-only modernization: skill/prompt/routing/hook/automation changes are proposals until owner approval, rollback target and verification evidence exist.
  • Separation of roles: collection, reflection, judging and approval must be distinct enough that the loop cannot silently approve its own changes.

docs.title: Batch 44 Execution Slices
docs.text:
Execution policy: run the slices sequentially unless a later owner-approved agent-team plan splits independent read-only, test or docs work. Each slice must close with current evidence in its owned artifact, docs/control-plane sync when touched and no promotion beyond the Batch 44 acceptance ceiling.

docs.title: Batch 44 Acceptance Ceiling
docs.text: Batch 44 can make the Self-Learning Loop implementation-ready only when the plan, schemas, tests and staged artifacts exist. It still cannot claim active weekly automation, global user-session analysis, real-session satisfaction analysis outside owner-approved Product-Agent OS project scope, production readiness, installed-cache repair, global Codex behavior, provider-backed eval quality, Promptfoo execution, live HALO service behavior, repair-worker execution, browser/runtime proof, external telemetry, project HTML proof or automatic self-improvement without future implementation evidence and separate owner approval.

docs.title: Batch 45 Professional Code Authoring Standards And Leverage Plan
docs.text: Batch 45 turns the two code-quality research packets and current Product-Agent OS code-writing surfaces into a staged implementation plan. The intended behavior is not more ceremony before code; it is the opposite: force agents to spend the first effort finding the smallest existing path, deleting or reusing code where possible, and writing custom logic only after evidence shows that simpler enterprise-grade routes are insufficient.

docs.title: Batch 45 Two-Loop Research Synthesis
docs.text: Loop Inputs inspected Findings Planning implication B45-R1 source synthesis ai-agent-coding-standards-research.md, ai-agent-coding-literature-research.md, current source registry route markers. The standards packet emphasizes refactoring, simplicity, comments, naming, reviewability, tests, debt control and source-backed engineering practice. The literature packet adds a stronger senior leverage ladder: delete code, configure behavior, call standard library or framework APIs, reuse project abstractions, add a small adapter, then write custom logic only when needed. Batch 45 must add explicit enterprise_leverage_check, existing_capability_scan, one_line_candidate, negative_dependency_rule, deep_module_check, legacy_seam_check and cleverness_budget fields to task packets, workflows and review gates. B45-R2 implementation-entity audit development-standards.md, build-slice.md, review-slice.md, legacy-onboarding.md, agent-task-packet.md, quality-strategy.md, plan-quality-check.md, api-style-guide.md, eval fixtures and template registry code. Existing surfaces already cover evidence, ownership, test-first work, review stages, source boundaries and approval discipline. Missing surfaces are the professional coding gates that prevent custom-code bloat, unnecessary dependencies, shallow abstractions, large unreviewed rewrites, stale style rules and comments that explain the obvious. Batch 45 should retrofit existing entities instead of creating a parallel standards universe. New artifacts must register through templates.py, be validated by focused tests/evals, and update public docs plus registry only where source-backed claims change. B45-R3 completeness re-audit Agent role templates, subagent context/result packets, acceptance/test/eval templates, readiness and Codex compatibility artifacts, cross-domain workflows, methodology/discovery/first-run route code and focused tests. The first Batch 45 matrix covered the core workflow and documentation layer but did not fully account for role prompts, subagent handoff continuity, acceptance-to-test traceability, readiness/compatibility signals, domain-specific workflows or discovery/routing visibility. Add B45-PCA-M15..M19 so the professional coding standard is carried through agent roles, handoffs, evals, readiness checks, cross-domain templates and public docs without claiming runtime activation.

docs.title: Batch 45 Design Principles
docs.text:
• existing_capability_first: search current project APIs, framework features, standard library and configuration paths before custom logic.
  • delete_or_reuse_before_add: prefer deleting code, using existing behavior or composing a local abstraction before introducing new code.
  • negative_dependency_rule: reject new dependencies unless native/project options are insufficient, lifecycle risk is acceptable, and supply-chain review is recorded.
  • one_line_candidate_rule: for small behavior, require the agent to name the simplest direct expression or framework call before writing a multi-line helper.
  • deep_module_over_shallow_module: hide real complexity behind stable interfaces; do not create wrappers that merely rename calls.
  • comments_explain_why: comments document intent, tradeoff, invariants and hazards; they do not narrate obvious statements.
  • legacy_seam_before_rewrite: add characterization evidence and seam strategy before refactoring old or tangled code.
  • cleverness_budget: clever code needs a measurable payoff, tests, naming clarity and review rationale.
