docs.text:
• B45-S0 Research And Gap Ledger: execute B45-PCA-M01 and B45-PCA-M20; keep the two-loop source synthesis and activation policy separate from implementation/runtime claims.
  • B45-S1 Artifact And Workflow Contracts: execute B45-PCA-M02..M04 to create the core checklist, workflow and handoff contract.
  • B45-S2 Existing Workflow Retrofit: execute B45-PCA-M05..M09, B45-PCA-M15 and B45-PCA-M17 to update old Product-Agent OS entities instead of building a disconnected coding standard.
  • B45-S3 Evals, Behavioral Guardrails And Activation Visibility: execute B45-PCA-M10..M11, B45-PCA-M16, B45-PCA-M18, B45-PCA-M21 and B45-PCA-M22 to make shortcut resistance testable and visible in hooks, readiness/discovery, runtime route and HTML surfaces without unsupported activation claims.
  • B45-S4 Public Docs And Closure-Through-S4: execute B45-PCA-M12..M13, B45-PCA-M19 and closure-through-S4 evidence for B45-PCA-M14 with docs, registry, tests and unsupported-claim ledger.
  • B45-S5 Learning And Automation Candidates: execute B45-PCA-M23 as candidate-only learning-loop/automation policy, then finalize B45-PCA-M14 source closure. Future promotion needs owner approval, at least three successful manual pilot runs, rollback, false-positive audit, flake replay and cost evidence.
  • B45-S6 Advisory Validation And Behavior Proof: execute B45-PCA-M24..M27 to measure broad false positives, wire approved non-blocking local advisory signal, prove or falsify real AI-agent behavior improvement and record the promotion/no-go decision.
  • B45-S7 Architecture V2 And Real-Project Scenario Harness: execute B45-PCA-M28..M36 to deepen the architecture, inventory real target scenarios, define sanitized fixture policy, build approved fixture packs, run baseline/refactor comparisons, calibrate scorecards and decide whether a smaller treatment v2 or disposable runtime/browser pilot is worth a later approval.
  • B45-S8 Promotion-Grade Eval: execute T16-T22 as a staged route only. T16 adds the task group, T17 freezes the metadata-only held-out corpus manifest in docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t17-frozen-heldout-corpus.json, T18 defines the same-model eval design and strict schema in docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t18-promotion-grade-eval-design.json, T19 defines cost/timeout/retry/abort/raw-temp-only retention in docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t19-cost-timeout-retention-policy.json, T20 keeps historical approval packets plus the consumed cost-waived approval in docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t20-promotion-grade-eval-approval-packet-cost-waived.json, T21 preflights are historical blocks in docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t21-promotion-grade-eval-run-preflight-blocked.json, docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t21-promotion-grade-eval-run-preflight-timeout-mismatch.json and docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t21-promotion-grade-eval-run-preflight-cost-unknown.json, current T21 strict-schema abort is in docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t21-promotion-grade-eval-results.json, and current T22 records no-go in docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t22-promotion-grade-decision-packet.json because T21 has no valid pair set. docs.title: Batch 45 Acceptance Ceiling
docs.text:

  • Short description: заменить повторяющиеся packet-specific exact assertions generic schema/registry/traceability и parameterized invariants, сохранив fault detection, затем ввести pure deterministic quality-metric aggregation без model self-score promotion.

  • Product value: Product-Agent OS сможет сравнивать качество изменений по воспроизводимым локальным доказательствам без хрупкой тестовой церемонии и без доверия к самооценке модели.

  • Acceptance criteria: T28 записывает текущий baseline, доказывает equivalent fault detection и не использует LOC ratio как gate; T29 не разрешает promotion от одного warning/coverage/size/self-score proxy, не превращает missing в zero/success и требует current benchmark только для performance-applicable изменений.
  • Verification gates: red-before-green на согласованных public seams; T28 before/after LOC и assertion-family inventory; seeded-corruption и active-contract suites; T29 metric calculation, aggregation, missing-evidence, mutation/regression и performance applicability cases; relevant full unittest route; JSON parse; independent reviewer и completion-skeptic; RU/EN task validators; docs tests; python tools\check_docs.py; git diff --check.
  • Risks / approval gates: остановиться при утрате fault detection, изменении historical IDs, shared-test collision, запуске T29 до T28 gate, self-score/single-proxy promotion, missing-as-success, смешивании T30 reviewer logic или любом внешнем действии.
  • Complexity: high
  • Estimated execution time: 4-6 hours
  • Agents: architect замораживает T28/T29 seams и metric semantics; tester владеет T28 и T29 RED tests в последовательных окнах; plugin-runtime-builder пишет только T29 module/schema; reviewer и completion-skeptic read-only; docs-maintainer синхронизирует A06 после gate.
  • Skills: implementation-planner; agent-team-designer; tdd; python-design-patterns; python-code-style; project-local docs и control-plane sync.
  • Output artifacts: T28 test inventory/refactor и test_batch45_packet_contracts.py; T29 code_quality_metrics.py, code-quality-metrics.json, test_batch45_code_quality_metrics.py; A06 evidence sync.
  • Next step: T28/T29 локально приняты как A06; следующий dependency route — T30, без запуска provider/model/reviewer и без promotion claim.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS Agents SDK Runner Design
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

Sources: Product-Agent OS production hardening design, source registry entries for "Codex with Agents SDK", "OpenAI Agents SDK Python", "Codex models", "Codex app", "Codex CLI", "Sandbox", "Agent approvals and security", and "Agents SDK sessions".

Этот документ фиксирует только design boundary для будущего Agents SDK runner. Он не активирует runner, не создает каталог plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/agents_sdk_runner/, не устанавливает зависимости и не меняет default workflow Product-Agent OS.

docs.title: Цель
docs.text:
Опциональный runner может понадобиться командам, которым нужна программируемая orchestration поверх Product-Agent OS. Базовый путь остается прежним: Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, skills, subagents, staged renderer, approval-gated merge и локальные validators.

Runner должен координировать роли Product-Agent OS, но не обходить sandbox, approvals, source policy, ownership и verification gates.

docs.title: Runtime Boundary
docs.text:
• Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, project skills и .codex/agents остаются default runtime.
  • Agents SDK runner является advanced optional layer и включается только отдельным утвержденным планом.
  • Codex MCP рассматривается как execution backend для работы с workspace, а не как bypass для approvals.
  • Любая workspace mutation требует явного ownership, approval state и rollback/shutdown path.
  • При неизвестных credentials, source status, approval state или file ownership runner должен fail closed.

docs.title: Manager Agent
docs.text:
Manager agent владеет lifecycle state и final output:

  • читает AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md и RUNLOG.md;
  • выбирает specialist role по ownership, inputs, outputs и stop conditions;
  • отклоняет handoff без sources/context used, assumptions, files touched/proposed, verification evidence, open risks и recommended next role;
  • сохраняет решения в checked-in artifacts, а не только в session memory.

docs.title: Specialist Roles
docs.text:
Role model and reasoning Boundary Product Manager project default, medium/high requirements и acceptance criteria Architect project default, high/xhigh decomposition, ownership, rollback Builder project default, medium/high one approved implementation slice Tester project default, medium/high deterministic checks и eval evidence Reviewer project default, high/xhigh findings-first review Docs Maintainer project default, medium/high source policy и documentation updates Release Operator project default, medium/high staged PR/release packet

Model policy должен задавать default model, reasoning effort, escalation rules, downgrade rules и cost/latency budget. Runner не должен молча повышать модель или reasoning для bounded mechanical work.

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
• Credentials читаются только из environment variables или platform configuration.
  • Plaintext credential values не пишутся в prompts, docs, fixtures, runlogs, traces, sessions, memory или templates.
  • Missing credentials останавливают runner до tool calls и до workspace mutation.
  • Credential creation и key rotation не входят в default runner path.

docs.title: Sessions And Tracing
docs.text:
• Sessions дают application conversation continuity, но не заменяют AGENTS.md, source registry, RUNLOG.md или checked-in memory artifacts.
  • Tracing фиксирует tool names, handoffs, latency, failures, approval events и stop reasons.
  • redaction обязателен до persistence: secrets, private customer data, raw private chat logs и absolute user-specific paths удаляются или заменяются synthetic labels.
  • Retention policy должен быть задан до использования runner на реальном проекте.

docs.title: Eval Gates
docs.text:
Runner нельзя считать готовым без eval gates:

  • handoff completeness;
  • source fidelity;
  • tool boundary;
  • approval handling;
  • secret retention;
  • rollback или shutdown behavior;
  • trace/session redaction.

Каждый gate должен иметь deterministic fixture или reviewable evidence artifact.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Нет default dependency installation.
  • Нет default network access в plugin verification.
  • Нет active automation scheduling.
  • Нет silent changes в global Codex config.
  • Нет замены Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, project skills или .codex/agents.
  • Нет реализации runner directory в Track 4 Tasks 6-10.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS Generated Infrastructure Design
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

Sources: Codex build plugins, Codex hooks, Subagents, AGENTS.md.

This design defines Track 3 for the Product-Agent OS plugin spec. It builds on the completed Track 1 core plan and Track 2 lifecycle skills design.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Track 3 turns product-agent-os from a lifecycle guide into a project infrastructure generator. The plugin gains templates and scripts that can produce a staged infrastructure package for a user's workspace: control-plane files, project-scoped Codex assets, hooks, workflow packets, eval skeletons, and release packet templates.

The core rule is staged-first. Track 3 does not silently mutate a user's project. It renders a reviewable plan and staged artifacts, validates them, and leaves actual project writes behind explicit approval and merge-safe behavior.

docs.title: Design Choice
docs.text:
Use a staged infrastructure generator.

The plugin package owns reusable templates and rendering code. When applied to a project, it reads a workspace audit, lifecycle packets, and a complexity profile, then renders proposed artifacts into an output directory or dry-run JSON. A later approved write step may merge managed sections into project files, but hidden writes are not part of the default path.

Rejected approaches:

  • Direct project writer: faster, but too risky for existing projects with user-authored AGENTS.md, .codex/, workflow files, and local conventions.
  • Templates only: safe, but not a working tool because Codex would still need to assemble infrastructure manually.

docs.title: Existing Foundation
docs.text:
Track 1 already provides:

  • plugin manifest and package skeleton under plugins/product-agent-os/;
  • contracts.py with lifecycle states, complexity profiles, control-plane file names, and handoff validation;
  • discovery.py and detect_project.py for workspace audits;
  • validators.py and wrappers for control-plane files, agents, and hooks;
  • merge_markdown.py for managed Markdown sections;
  • fixture projects and run_fixture_eval.py.

Track 2 already provides:

  • lifecycle skills that produce staged packets rather than direct writes;
  • shared references for lifecycle state, handoff, source policy, and complexity routing;
  • static tests that enforce staged-only boundaries and candidate-only automation.

Track 3 should reuse these contracts and scripts. It should not duplicate lifecycle routing inside template files.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Track 3 adds:

  • template registry and template completeness tests;
  • control-plane file templates for AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, and RUNLOG.md;
  • project-scoped .codex/config.toml proposal template;
  • project-scoped .codex/agents/*.toml templates;
  • hook templates that are packaged but not enabled automatically;
  • staged hook lifecycle config template for .codex/hooks/hooks.json;
  • .codex/workflows/*.md task packet templates;
  • .codex/evals/*.json eval skeletons;
  • .codex/runlogs/archive/ or docs/runlogs/archive/ compaction proposal templates;
  • .codex/automation-candidates/*.md candidate-only automation packets;
  • PR and release packet templates;
  • staged renderer that creates an infrastructure plan and rendered artifacts;
  • CLI wrapper for dry-run and staged output generation;
  • fixture coverage for greenfield, existing config, missing tests, monorepo, docs projects, unsafe write requests, and failed verification evidence.

docs.title: Out Of Scope
docs.text:
Track 3 does not create active automations, scheduled jobs, or recurring runs. Automation stays candidate-only until Track 4 hardening and explicit user approval.

Track 3 does not add the optional Agents SDK runner, Codex MCP orchestration runtime, or external system integrations.

Track 3 does not change global Codex config, write user-level memory, install dependencies, use network access, call external systems, or publish PRs.

Track 3 does not claim tests, builds, hooks, or evals pass unless the current run executes the relevant checks and records evidence.

docs.title: Package Layout
docs.text:
Track 3 should create this package structure:

plugins/product-agent-os/
  assets/
    templates/
      control-plane/
        AGENTS.md
        REQUIREMENTS.md
        PLAN.md
        TEST.md
        EVALS.md
        RUNLOG.md
      config/
        config.toml
      agents/
        product-manager.toml
        architect.toml
        explorer.toml
        builder.toml
        tester.toml
        reviewer.toml
        docs-maintainer.toml
        release-operator.toml
      hooks/
        hooks.json
        session_start_context.py
        pre_tool_use_policy.py
        permission_request_summary.py
        post_tool_use_evidence.py
        stop_runlog_reminder.py
      workflows/
        source-context-pack.md
        worktree-ownership.md
        build-slice.md
        review-slice.md
        release-packet.md
        runlog-compaction.md
      runlogs/
        archive/
          README.md
      evals/
        project-readiness.json
        handoff-completeness.json
        renderer-fixtures.json
      automations/
        automation-candidate.md
      pr/
        pr-body.md
        release-notes.md
  scripts/
    product_agent_os/
      templates.py
      infrastructure.py
    render_infrastructure.py

The exact template list may grow later, but Track 3 should keep the first version deliberately small and complete.

docs.title: Data Model
docs.text:
The renderer should accept a WorkspaceAudit-like dictionary from discovery.py and an optional lifecycle packet bundle from Track 2 skills.

The renderer should return:

infrastructure_plan:
  status: "ready | blocked | needs_approval"
  profile: "guided-small | standard-product | production-team | ai-product | enterprise-governed | autonomous-maintenance"
  create: []
  update: []
  leave_unchanged: []
  blocked: []
  approval_required: []
  warnings: []
  questions: []
rendered_artifacts:
  root: ""
  files:
    - target_path: ""
      staged_path: ""
      action: "create | update | leave_unchanged | blocked"
      write_policy: "staged_only | approved_write_required"
  managed_sections: []
  validation:
    ok: true
    checks: []

create means the target file does not exist. update means a managed section or staged companion artifact is proposed. leave_unchanged means a user-authored file exists and no safe managed section is available. blocked means the renderer cannot proceed without user input or approval.

docs.title: Template Rules
docs.text:
All templates must be deterministic, portable, and safe for fixtures.

Required rules:

  • no secrets, tokens, private keys, credentials, customer data, PII, or raw private logs;
  • no absolute user-specific paths;
  • no hidden network access, dependency installation, destructive commands, or global config mutation;
  • no active automation or schedule creation;
  • no plugin-root lifecycle config that would activate hooks on install;
  • no claims that checks passed;
  • no instructions that bypass sandbox or approvals;
  • managed sections use <!-- product-agent-os:start <section-id> --> and <!-- product-agent-os:end <section-id> -->;
  • examples use synthetic data only.

Templates may include placeholders only if the renderer replaces them deterministically before writing output. Source docs must not contain unreplaced placeholder markers or vague filler.

docs.title: Control-Plane Templates
docs.text:
Control-plane templates should be concise and role-oriented:

  • AGENTS.md: durable project rules, source policy, safety boundaries, verification policy, and pointer to deeper workflow docs.
  • REQUIREMENTS.md: goal, users, scope, non-goals, constraints, acceptance criteria, assumptions, and open questions.
  • PLAN.md: implementation slices, ownership, dependencies, risks, rollback, verification gates, and approval needs.
  • TEST.md: deterministic checks, manual checks, visual/runtime checks, known gaps, and evidence format.
  • EVALS.md: subjective rubrics, LLM-as-judge checks where relevant, thresholds, artifacts, and regression notes.
  • RUNLOG.md: current lifecycle state, decisions, commands, verification evidence, failures, risks, and handoff summary.

Existing user content must be preserved. If a file already exists and lacks a managed section, the renderer should propose a staged append or companion artifact rather than overwriting it.

docs.title: Project Config Template
docs.text:
Track 3 should package a .codex/config.toml proposal template for project-scoped Codex defaults. The renderer must stage it as .codex/config.toml only when the project does not already have config, or as a managed companion proposal when config exists.

The template may include:

  • project-scoped [agents] concurrency defaults;
  • model and reasoning guidance as comments or proposed values;
  • sandbox and approval policy notes;
  • pointers to project agent files and workflow packets.

The template must not modify global ~/.codex/config.toml, must not add secrets, and must not enable broad network access, active automation, or external writes. Existing project config without managed markers should be classified as leave_unchanged plus a staged companion proposal.

docs.title: Agent Templates
docs.text:
Project-scoped agents live under .codex/agents/ in the target project.

Track 3 should package templates for:

  • product-manager
  • architect
  • explorer
  • builder
  • tester
  • reviewer
  • docs-maintainer
  • release-operator

Every agent template must include:

  • name
  • description
  • developer_instructions
  • ownership boundary
  • inputs and outputs
  • stop conditions
  • model/reasoning guidance
  • handoff requirements

The templates should validate with the existing validate_agents.py wrapper.

Agent templates should align with Track 2 lifecycle packets:

  • product-manager owns requirements, scope, non-goals, and acceptance criteria;
  • architect owns decomposition, ownership, rollback, and risk routing;
  • explorer owns read-only codebase and source mapping;
  • builder owns one approved implementation slice;
  • tester owns deterministic checks, manual checks, eval gaps, and evidence capture;
  • reviewer owns findings-first review, missing tests, regressions, and security risk;
  • docs-maintainer owns documentation and runlog updates;
  • release-operator owns PR/release packet drafts and rollout notes.

docs.title: Hook Templates
docs.text:
Hook templates are packaged examples, not silently enabled enforcement.

Track 3 should package:

  • hooks.json: staged lifecycle config for a target project's .codex/hooks/hooks.json, not plugin-root auto-activation;
  • session_start_context.py: summarizes active control-plane state for SessionStart;
  • pre_tool_use_policy.py: detects obvious destructive commands, forbidden paths, and secret-risk writes;
  • permission_request_summary.py: formats why an approval is needed for PermissionRequest;
  • post_tool_use_evidence.py: formats command evidence for a runlog buffer or staged note;
  • stop_runlog_reminder.py: reminds the agent to update RUNLOG.md when evidence exists.

Hooks must not store secrets. They must not call network services. Blocking behavior must be narrow and auditable. The templates should validate with the existing validate_hooks.py wrapper.

The packaged plugin root must not include an active hooks/hooks.json that Codex would load automatically on install. Track 3 stages hook lifecycle config for the target project only, and the final response must call out that enabling hooks requires explicit approval.

docs.title: Workflow Templates
docs.text:
Workflow packet templates should represent repeatable manual workflows, not active automations.

Initial workflows:

  • source-context-pack.md: official-source and Context7 research packet with source status, freshness, unsupported claims, and registry/update notes;
  • worktree-ownership.md: worktree and write-scope map for parallel implementation;
  • build-slice.md: one approved implementation slice with inputs, ownership, commands, evidence, and stop conditions;
  • review-slice.md: review packet with findings-first format, missing tests, risks, and verdict;
  • release-packet.md: PR/release preparation with checks, user impact, rollback, residual risks, and approval requirements;
  • runlog-compaction.md: hot/warm/cold context summary and archive proposal that preserves evidence.

These workflows are warm context. They should keep AGENTS.md small and prevent long operational guidance from accumulating in durable rules.

docs.title: Context Archive Templates
docs.text:
Track 3 should stage context overflow infrastructure, not perform archival automatically.

The renderer should include proposals for:

  • .codex/runlogs/archive/ or docs/runlogs/archive/ depending on detected project conventions;
  • a runlog-compaction.md workflow that summarizes old iterations into decisions, failures, evidence, risks, and next actions;
  • a context pack format for source notes, active constraints, current plan, and open questions.

The archive proposal must preserve raw evidence until the user approves compaction. It must not store raw private chat logs, secrets, credentials, customer data, or PII.

docs.title: Eval Templates
docs.text:
Eval templates should be small JSON fixtures that validate agent operating quality, not application behavior.

Initial evals:

  • project-readiness.json: checks that generated infrastructure names required artifacts, safety boundaries, and verification gaps;
  • handoff-completeness.json: checks that handoff packets include sources, assumptions, files, evidence, risks, and stop reason.
  • renderer-fixtures.json: checks greenfield, existing config, missing tests, unsafe write, monorepo ownership, docs source conflict, and failed verification cases.

They should not require network access or secrets. They should be usable by future Track 4 fixture hardening.

docs.title: Automation Candidate Templates
docs.text:
Track 3 should include a candidate-only automation packet template under assets/templates/automations/automation-candidate.md.

The template must require manual stability evidence, stable inputs and outputs, owner, cadence, verification, failure modes, rollback or disable path, and explicit write policy. It must not create a schedule, recurring run, GitHub Action, Codex automation, or external workflow.

docs.title: Renderer Behavior
docs.text:
The renderer should support two modes:

  1. dry-run: print JSON infrastructure plan and proposed artifact paths without writing files.
  2. stage: render artifacts into an output directory such as .product-agent-os/staged/ or a caller-provided staging directory.

Default behavior should be dry-run. Stage mode writes only inside the requested staging directory unless the user explicitly approves project writes.

The renderer should:

  1. run or accept workspace discovery;
  2. infer profile and required artifact set;
  3. compare target files against existing files;
  4. decide create/update/leave_unchanged/blocked actions;
  5. render deterministic artifacts;
  6. validate generated agents, hooks, eval JSON, and staged config;
  7. detect project config conflicts, duplicate managed sections, and unmarked user-authored files;
  8. return a JSON plan with warnings, questions, and approval requirements.

docs.title: Profile Routing
docs.text:
The profile changes depth, not lifecycle order.

Profile Track 3 artifacts guided-small control-plane files, minimal workflows, reviewer/tester agent suggestions, no automation standard-product control-plane files, project config proposal, core agent templates, optional hook staging, test/eval skeletons production-team full agent templates, worktree ownership workflow, stricter handoff and review gates ai-product eval templates, source-context workflow, prompt/context policy sections, regression notes enterprise-governed strict approval notes, forbidden paths, audit-focused hook templates, config conflict reporting autonomous-maintenance automation candidate packet and runlog compaction proposal only, no active schedules

docs.title: CLI Contract
docs.text:
render_infrastructure.py should support:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\render_infrastructure.py <workspace> --dry-run
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\render_infrastructure.py <workspace> --stage <output-dir>

Ожидаемое поведение:

  • dry-run exits 0 with JSON when a plan can be produced;
  • invalid workspace exits non-zero with a clear error;
  • stage mode creates only files under the output directory;
  • generated agents, hooks, eval JSON, staged config, and managed-section targets are validated before success;
  • failures are reported without Python tracebacks for expected user errors.

docs.title: Safety And Approvals
docs.text:
Track 3 must preserve the safety model from the plugin spec:

  • user-authored content outside managed sections is preserved;
  • direct project writes require explicit approval;
  • global config changes are forbidden;
  • active automation is forbidden;
  • external writes are forbidden;
  • secrets are never stored or repeated;
  • source-of-truth updates require staged draft first;
  • generated artifacts document verification gaps instead of claiming success.
  • hook lifecycle config is staged for the target project and never activated from the plugin root by default.

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
Track 3 tests should be deterministic unittest tests:

  • template registry includes all required categories and files;
  • every template file exists and has no forbidden placeholders or secret-like values;
  • .codex/config.toml proposal is staged and existing project config is preserved;
  • staged hooks.json exists for target projects, while plugin-root hook activation is absent;
  • agent templates validate with validate_agent_file;
  • hook templates validate with validate_hook_file;
  • dry-run produces create/update/leave_unchanged decisions for fixtures;
  • stage mode writes only under the staging directory;
  • existing fixture files are not overwritten;
  • existing AGENTS.md without markers yields a staged companion proposal;
  • duplicate managed sections are reported as blocked;
  • rendered control-plane files include managed section markers;
  • generated eval JSON is valid;
  • workflow templates cover source context, worktree ownership, build slice, review slice, release packet, and runlog compaction;
  • automation candidate template is candidate-only and requires manual stability evidence;
  • renderer handles invalid workspace paths without traceback;
  • full fixture eval still passes.

docs.title: Критерии приемки
docs.text:
Track 3 is complete when:

  • the plugin package includes templates for control-plane files, project config, agents, hooks, workflows, evals, automation candidates, and PR/release packets;
  • the renderer produces a staged infrastructure plan for every existing fixture project;
  • dry-run does not write files;
  • stage mode writes only to the staging directory;
  • existing user-authored files are preserved;
  • generated agents and hooks pass validators;
  • generated eval JSON and staged config pass deterministic checks;
  • existing project config, existing AGENTS.md, duplicate managed sections, monorepo ownership, source conflict, unsafe write, and failed verification cases are covered by tests;
  • no template stores secrets or claims checks passed;
  • automation remains candidate-only;
  • python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v passes;
  • python tools\check_docs.py passes;
  • strict MkDocs build exits 0.

docs.title: Residual Risks
docs.text:
Static template validation does not prove that generated infrastructure works well in every real project. Track 4 should add stronger fixture evals, failure-log based regression cases, safe merge hardening, source policy checks, automation promotion gates, and optional Agents SDK runner design.

Track 3 should not broaden into Track 4. The goal is a safe, reviewable infrastructure generator that makes the next production hardening layer possible.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS Lifecycle Skills Design
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

This design defines Track 2 for the Product-Agent OS plugin spec. It builds on the completed Track 1 core plan and focuses only on packaged lifecycle skills.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Track 2 turns product-agent-os from a core package into a usable lifecycle guide. The plugin gains packaged skills that can audit a workspace, route the project lifecycle, produce staged action packets, and enforce handoff contracts without silently creating project infrastructure.

The output of Track 2 is not generated project files. The output is a set of reusable skill instructions that tell Codex how to move through the project lifecycle safely.

docs.title: Existing Foundation
docs.text:
Track 1 already provides:

  • plugin manifest and package skeleton under plugins/product-agent-os/;
  • lifecycle state constants and handoff validation in contracts.py;
  • workspace discovery in discovery.py and detect_project.py;
  • validators for control-plane files, agents, and hooks;
  • managed Markdown merge utility;
  • fixture projects and fixture eval runner;
  • test package shim for unittest discover -s tests.

Track 2 should reuse these contracts and scripts instead of duplicating their logic inside skill bodies.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Track 2 creates SKILL.md packages under plugins/product-agent-os/skills/:

  • project-lifecycle-orchestrator
  • workspace-discovery-auditor
  • requirements-author
  • implementation-planner
  • agent-team-designer
  • test-eval-designer
  • risk-reviewer
  • pr-release-operator
  • learning-loop-maintainer
  • automation-promoter

Each skill package contains:

<skill-name>/
  SKILL.md
  agents/
    openai.yaml

The plugin package also includes shared lifecycle references:

plugins/product-agent-os/skills/references/
  lifecycle-states.md
  handoff-contract.md
  source-policy.md
  complexity-routing.md

docs.title: Out Of Scope
docs.text:
Track 2 does not create .codex/agents/*.toml, active hooks, project templates, workflow files, automations, MCP servers, or an Agents SDK runner. It may describe proposed files in output packets, but actual generation belongs to Track 3.

Track 2 does not change global Codex config, write user-level memory, install external dependencies, use network access, or call external systems. Skills may instruct Codex to ask for approval when these actions become relevant.

docs.title: Skill Anatomy
docs.text:
Every SKILL.md must include YAML frontmatter with only:

---
name: skill-name
description: Clear trigger description that says when to use this skill.
---

Every SKILL.md body must include these headings:

  • # <Human Skill Name>
  • ## Trigger
  • ## Boundaries
  • ## Inputs
  • ## Process
  • ## Outputs
  • ## Verification
  • ## Failure Modes
  • ## Final Response Contract

Skill bodies should be concise. Long lifecycle, source, and routing details live in skills/references/ and are loaded only when needed.

Every skill also has agents/openai.yaml:

interface:
  display_name: "Human name"
  short_description: "Short UI description"
  default_prompt: "Use $skill-name to ..."
policy:
  allow_implicit_invocation: false

allow_implicit_invocation is false for these lifecycle skills because they handle source-sensitive project state, write planning, risk review, release packets, and automation candidates. The user or orchestrator should invoke them intentionally.

docs.title: Shared References
docs.text:
lifecycle-states.md defines lifecycle order, valid transitions, and stop conditions. It mirrors LIFECYCLE_STATES from contracts.py.

handoff-contract.md defines the required fields from REQUIRED_HANDOFF_FIELDS, including constraints, sources, evidence, file ownership, risks, next task, and stop reason.

source-policy.md defines source status rules: official docs are source of truth, Context7 is accepted as official only when the underlying source is official, community claims are intake material, and secrets must never be stored.

complexity-routing.md defines how guided-small, standard-product, production-team, ai-product, enterprise-governed, and autonomous-maintenance change depth and gates without changing lifecycle order.

docs.title: Orchestrator Contract
docs.text:
project-lifecycle-orchestrator is the entrypoint. It must:

  1. Read AGENTS.md, existing control-plane files, .codex/, and Track 1 discovery output when available.
  2. Determine the current lifecycle state.
  3. Detect missing blockers and ask only blocking questions.
  4. Select exactly one next lifecycle skill or return a stop condition.
  5. Produce a staged action packet with proposed next files or questions.
  6. Avoid skipping required gates.

The orchestrator cannot move from uninitialized directly to build_active. It cannot create automation, edit global config, or assert checks passed without evidence.

docs.title: Routing Rules
docs.text:
Lifecycle state Primary skill Output uninitialized workspace-discovery-auditor read-only workspace audit packet infrastructure_planned requirements-author requirements packet requirements_ready implementation-planner implementation plan packet plan_ready agent-team-designer role and ownership packet team_ready test-eval-designer verification and eval packet build_active risk-reviewer risk and review packet quality_gate risk-reviewer blocking findings or clearance packet review_ready pr-release-operator PR or release packet release_ready learning-loop-maintainer lessons and update candidates learning_ready automation-promoter automation candidate packet maintenance project-lifecycle-orchestrator next maintenance route

Complexity profile modifies depth, not order:

  • guided-small: keep outputs lightweight; no custom agent generation.
  • standard-product: require explicit acceptance criteria, test commands, and release notes.
  • production-team: require ownership boundaries and reviewer handoff.
  • ai-product: require eval criteria and prompt/context source policy.
  • enterprise-governed: require stricter approval, forbidden paths, and audit evidence.
  • autonomous-maintenance: require manual stability evidence before automation candidates.

docs.title: Skill Contracts
docs.text: Skill Trigger Required inputs Output packet Hard boundary project-lifecycle-orchestrator User asks Product-Agent OS to guide a project or continue lifecycle user goal, workspace path, existing control-plane files, discovery output if present lifecycle route packet never skip lifecycle gates workspace-discovery-auditor Project needs read-only audit or profile inference workspace path, allowed read scope workspace audit packet no writes requirements-author Goal needs requirements, scope, users, acceptance criteria audit packet, user goal, constraints requirements packet do not invent product decisions implementation-planner Requirements are stable and implementation needs decomposition requirements packet, audit, constraints implementation plan packet no code changes agent-team-designer Work needs roles, handoffs, ownership, or parallelism plan packet, complexity profile agent team design packet do not create .codex/agents/*.toml in Track 2 test-eval-designer Project needs verification or eval gates requirements, plan, stack, risk profile test and eval packet do not claim checks pass risk-reviewer Diff, plan, or quality gate needs review diff summary or proposed changes, requirements, verification evidence risk review packet findings first; no silent approval pr-release-operator Work is ready for PR or release packet checks, review, runlog, rollback notes PR or release packet no external publish without approval learning-loop-maintainer Delivery completed or runlog needs compaction final result, failures, decisions, reusable lessons learning loop packet no durable rule promotion without evidence automation-promoter Stable recurring workflow may become automation manual success history, inputs, outputs, failure modes automation candidate packet no active automation creation

docs.title: Output Packet Schemas
docs.text: Skills should emit Markdown with a YAML-like packet block. The packet is a communication contract, not a machine parser requirement in Track 2.

docs.title: Safety Rules
docs.text:
All Track 2 skills must state:

  • do not store secrets, tokens, credentials, private keys, private customer data, or raw private chat logs;
  • do not mutate global config;
  • do not perform destructive commands;
  • do not create active automations;
  • do not write generated infrastructure directly in this track;
  • do not claim verification passed without command evidence from the current run;
  • ask for approval before external writes, permission changes, deployment, billing, auth, database, or production operations.

docs.title: Validation Strategy
docs.text:
Track 2 is verified with Python unittest tests that inspect packaged skill files and references. The tests should not execute Codex skills. They validate:

  • all required skill directories and SKILL.md files exist;
  • every skill has required frontmatter fields;
  • every skill has required body headings;
  • every skill has agents/openai.yaml with display name, short description, default prompt, and allow_implicit_invocation: false;
  • orchestrator routing covers every lifecycle state from contracts.py;
  • no skill claims it can perform out-of-scope writes for Track 2;
  • no skill stores or asks to store secrets;
  • no skill creates active automations;
  • reference files exist and include lifecycle, handoff, source policy, and complexity routing content;
  • references named in skill bodies resolve to existing files.

The final verification commands are:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
python tools\check_docs.py
$env:PYTHONPATH='C:\tmp\codex_docs_mkdocs'; python -m mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Критерии приемки
docs.text:
Track 2 is complete when:

  • packaged lifecycle skills exist under plugins/product-agent-os/skills/;
  • each skill is concise and follows the common contract;
  • each skill has UI metadata in agents/openai.yaml;
  • routing covers all lifecycle states from Track 1 contracts;
  • skills produce staged packets and do not silently write project infrastructure;
  • tests validate structure, routing, boundaries, references, UI metadata, and source or secret policy;
  • docs checks and strict MkDocs build pass.

docs.title: Self-Review
docs.text: This design is intentionally limited to lifecycle skills. It does not include generated project infrastructure, project-scoped agents, hooks, active automations, or an Agents SDK runner. Those remain separate tracks so each layer can be tested and reviewed independently.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS Production Hardening Design
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

Sources: Product-Agent OS plugin spec, Track 1 core plan, Track 2 lifecycle skills design, Track 3 generated infrastructure design, Track 3 implementation plan, source registry.

This design defines Track 4 for the product-agent-os plugin. It starts from the completed Track 3 baseline: deterministic staged infrastructure rendering, dry-run JSON output, staged artifact generation, fixture eval coverage, generated templates, validators, and clean verification on 2026-05-14.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Track 4 turns the staged-first infrastructure generator into a production-hardened workflow that can be used on real projects without weakening the safety model.

The output is a hardened Product-Agent OS layer with:

  • a safe approved merge workflow for applying staged artifacts;
  • a staged artifact manifest that records provenance, digests, renderer validation, and intended write policy;
  • an explicit approval record that is separate from the merge plan id;
  • stronger fixture evals and failure-log regression cases;
  • source-policy validation for docs and generated guidance;
  • automation promotion gates that keep recurring work candidate-only until evidence and approval exist;
  • an optional Agents SDK runner design path that remains separate from the default plugin workflow.

docs.title: Design Choice
docs.text:
Use a gated hardening layer.

Track 4 should keep Track 3's default behavior unchanged: render plans and staged artifacts first, then require explicit approval before project writes. Production behavior is added through separate validators, merge plans, approval records, and eval reports.

Rejected approaches:

  • Direct apply by default: faster for greenfield projects, but too risky for existing AGENTS.md, .codex/config.toml, hooks, workflows, and user-authored project conventions.
  • Only add more templates: safe, but does not solve the real production gaps: approved merge, regression evidence, source drift, and automation readiness.
  • Build a full Agents SDK runtime immediately: powerful, but it expands the risk surface before the plugin's local hardening layer is proven.

Recommended approach:

  1. Harden local merge and validation first.
  2. Expand fixture evals around real failure modes.
  3. Add source and automation gates as deterministic validators.
  4. Keep the Agents SDK runner as an optional Track 4B design/prototype path, not part of default plugin activation.

docs.title: Existing Foundation
docs.text:
Track 1 already provides:

  • plugin manifest and package skeleton under plugins/product-agent-os/;
  • lifecycle state and handoff contracts in contracts.py;
  • workspace discovery in discovery.py and detect_project.py;
  • validation wrappers for control-plane files, agents, and hooks;
  • merge_markdown.py for managed Markdown sections;
  • fixture projects and fixture eval runner.

Track 2 already provides:

  • lifecycle skills under plugins/product-agent-os/skills/;
  • shared references for lifecycle state, handoff, source policy, and complexity routing;
  • static tests that prevent lifecycle skills from creating infrastructure, active automations, hooks, MCP servers, or an Agents SDK runner.

Track 3 already provides:

  • templates.py template registry;
  • infrastructure.py dry-run and stage renderer;
  • render_infrastructure.py CLI wrapper;
  • templates for control-plane files, .codex/config.toml, agents, hooks, workflows, evals, runlog archive, automation candidates, and PR/release packets;
  • renderer actions: create, update, leave_unchanged, blocked;
  • validation for agents, hooks, hook lifecycle config, eval JSON, staged config, and unresolved substitution markers;
  • fixture behavior checks for existing config, duplicate managed sections, monorepo ownership, source registry warning, unsafe write, and failed verification evidence.

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text:
Track 3 proves that Product-Agent OS can produce safe staged proposals. It does not yet prove that the proposals can be applied safely to a real project.

Production use introduces additional risks:

  • a staged artifact can be stale by the time a user approves it;
  • a merge can escape the workspace through path traversal, symlinks, or malformed staged paths;
  • user-authored files can be overwritten if unmarked content is treated as generated content;
  • source-backed documentation can drift from official OpenAI docs or local source registry entries;
  • automation candidates can become active recurring work without enough manual evidence;
  • fixture evals can pass structurally while missing behavior-level regressions;
  • an Agents SDK runner can blur ownership, approvals, and secrets unless it is isolated from default plugin behavior.

Track 4 must close these gaps without turning Product-Agent OS into an uncontrolled writer.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: Track 4 adds five workstreams.

docs.title: 1. Safe Approved Merge
docs.text:
Add a merge workflow that can apply staged artifacts only after an explicit approval step.

Required capabilities:

  • produce a merge plan from a workspace and a Track 3 staging directory;
  • require a staged manifest generated by the renderer before any apply command;
  • require an explicit approval record before any apply command;
  • verify target paths stay inside the workspace;
  • reject symlink escapes and parent-directory traversal;
  • compute target and staged content digests;
  • detect stale targets before applying a plan;
  • preserve user-authored content outside managed sections;
  • apply managed Markdown section updates only when the target has a safe marker state or an approved append strategy;
  • keep unmarked .toml, .json, .py, and hook files as companion proposals unless a later narrower rule proves a safe merge;
  • keep hook activation as a separate approval gate;
  • write backups and a rollback manifest before any project write;
  • provide a rollback command that can restore a recorded apply only when current digests still match the post-apply manifest;
  • report every write, skip, and block in a machine-readable result.

docs.title: 2. Stronger Fixture Evals
docs.text:
Expand fixture evals from structural renderer checks into behavior-level regression checks.

Required capabilities:

  • convert documented failure logs into deterministic regression cases;
  • fixture cases for stale merge plans, symlink escape attempts, path traversal, invalid staged manifest, broken rollback backup, missing approval, invalid source policy, and invalid automation promotion;
  • stable JSON results with expected checks, observed decisions, evidence paths, and failure reasons;
  • golden behavior summaries that explain why a fixture is ok, blocked, or needs_approval;
  • full fixture eval remains deterministic and requires no network access or secrets.

docs.title: 3. Source-Policy Hardening
docs.text:
Add deterministic source-policy checks for docs and generated guidance.

Required capabilities:

  • verify every non-index docs page keeps Source status:;
  • verify source-backed Product-Agent OS pages declare official docs, local specs, or source registry entries;
  • keep community claims under insight cards or explicitly marked community or experiment;
  • reject source-policy output that stores secrets, credentials, private customer data, or raw private chat logs;
  • mark freshness risk for current APIs, models, security, approvals, hooks, Agents SDK, MCP, and automation behavior;
  • produce a source-policy report that separates supported facts, assumptions, unsupported claims, and missing context;
  • classify semantic source ambiguity as needs_review instead of pretending deterministic text scanning can prove every factual claim.

docs.title: 4. Automation Promotion Gates
docs.text:
Harden automation candidates without creating active schedules.

Required capabilities:

  • parse automation candidate packets;
  • require owner, cadence, stable inputs, stable outputs, verification, failure modes, rollback or disable path, write policy, and explicit approval status;
  • require at least two manual successful runs or equivalent fixture evidence before a candidate can be marked ready for manual approval;
  • classify promotion state as candidate_only, ready_for_manual_approval, or blocked;
  • never create Codex App automations, GitHub Actions, schedules, recurring jobs, or external workflows inside Track 4 validators.

docs.title: 5. Optional Agents SDK Runner Design
docs.text:
Define an optional runner path for teams that need programmable orchestration.

Track 4 may add a design packet and validation contract for an Agents SDK runner. It should not make the runner part of the default Product-Agent OS plugin path.

Required design boundaries:

  • Manager agent owns lifecycle state and final output;
  • specialist agents are tools or handoff targets with explicit ownership;
  • every durable runner role has model and reasoning policy, escalation rules, downgrade rules, and cost or latency budget;
  • Codex MCP is treated as an execution backend, not as an approval bypass;
  • guardrails validate handoff completeness, source fidelity, tool boundaries, and secret retention;
  • sessions and tracing are application-level concerns and must not replace checked-in project rules, RUNLOG.md, or source registry records;
  • traces and sessions must have redaction and retention rules before real project use;
  • dependency installation and network access are separate setup steps, not implicit fixture behavior;
  • OpenAI credentials are read from environment or platform configuration only and never written to templates, fixtures, docs, memory, or runlogs.

docs.title: Use-Case Alignment
docs.text:
Track 4 maps to official use-case archetypes recorded in Codex use cases deep analysis.

Track 4 workstream Use-case group Why it matters Safe approved merge Tooling; PR and production review Creates an agent-friendly local CLI and prevents unreviewed production changes. Stronger fixture evals AI quality; PR and production review Converts hardening behavior into repeatable regression checks. Source-policy hardening Knowledge and product; PR and production review Keeps docs and generated guidance grounded in source status and reviewable claims. Automation promotion gates Operations and collaboration Prevents premature recurring work and aligns automation with verified operations. Optional Agents SDK runner Tooling; long-running creation Provides a later programmable orchestration path without making it the default plugin runtime.

Implementation plans for Track 4 should reference these groups when adding new playbooks, skills, plugin metadata, or automation candidates.

docs.title: Out Of Scope
docs.text:
Track 4 does not:

  • silently mutate user projects;
  • replace user-authored files without managed-section boundaries and explicit approval;
  • change global Codex config;
  • enable packaged hooks automatically;
  • install dependencies or use network access during fixture evals;
  • create active automations, scheduled jobs, GitHub Actions, recurring Codex App automations, or external workflows;
  • store secrets, credentials, private customer data, raw private chat logs, or absolute user-specific paths;
  • claim project tests, builds, hooks, evals, or automations work unless the current run produced evidence;
  • implement a full production Agents SDK app as part of the default hardening path.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Track 4 adds a hardening layer beside the existing renderer.

flowchart TD
    A["Workspace audit"] --> B["Track 3 renderer"]
    B --> C["Staged artifacts"]
    B --> D["Dry-run infrastructure plan"]
    C --> E["Track 4 merge planner"]
    D --> E
    E --> F{"Safe to apply?"}
    F -->|"No"| G["Blocked merge report"]
    F -->|"Needs approval"| H["Approval packet"]
    H --> I["Approved merge apply"]
    I --> J["Backup and rollback manifest"]
    I --> K["Applied project files"]
    C --> L["Fixture eval hardening"]
    D --> M["Source-policy validator"]
    D --> N["Automation promotion validator"]
    O["Optional Agents SDK runner design"] --> P["Separate gated prototype"]

The renderer remains the source of staged artifacts. Track 4 does not duplicate template rendering. It consumes renderer output, validates it more strictly, and controls the approved transition from staged artifacts to project files.

docs.title: Merge Workflow Contract
docs.text:
Track 4 should add a merge planner module and CLI wrapper.

Proposed files:

plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/product_agent_os/merge_infrastructure.py
plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/merge_infrastructure.py
tests/product_agent_os/test_merge_infrastructure.py

CLI contract:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\merge_infrastructure.py <workspace> <stage-dir> --plan
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\merge_infrastructure.py <workspace> <stage-dir> --apply --approval-file <approval-file>
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\merge_infrastructure.py <workspace> <stage-dir> --rollback <rollback-manifest>

Plan mode is read-only. Apply mode writes only when:

  • the user explicitly selected --apply;
  • the staged manifest exists and matches the current staged files;
  • the approval file exists and names the current merge plan id;
  • the approval file names the approved target paths and write scope;
  • every write decision is included in the approved target path list;
  • the target digest still matches the digest recorded during plan generation;
  • every target path resolves inside the workspace;
  • no target parent or target file is a symlink;
  • validation passes for staged content and merge decisions;
  • every write has a rollback entry.

Approval id alone is not sufficient. A merge plan id proves that a plan is stable; it does not prove that the user approved the write. Track 4 approval is represented as a separate approval record.

Plan output should include an approval record template that a user or higher-level approved workflow can complete. The merge tool must not infer approval from its own plan output.

Staged manifest shape:

stage_manifest:
  schema_version: 1
  renderer: "product-agent-os"
  renderer_version: ""
  workspace_audit_digest: ""
  infrastructure_plan_digest: ""
  generated_at: ""
  validation:
    ok: true
    checks: []
    errors: {}
  files:
    - target_path: "AGENTS.md"
      staged_path: "AGENTS.md"
      action: "create | update | leave_unchanged | blocked"
      write_policy: "staged_only | approved_write_required | blocked"
      digest: "sha256:..."
      managed_section: "project-rules"

Approval record shape:

approval:
  schema_version: 1
  merge_plan_id: ""
  approved_by: "user"
  approved_at: ""
  approved_targets:
    - "AGENTS.md"
  approved_actions:
    - "create_file"
    - "append_managed_section"
    - "replace_managed_section"
  accepted_risks: []
  denied_targets: []
  notes: ""

The approval record is local evidence for the merge command. It is not a substitute for platform-level sandbox or filesystem approvals when those are required by the current runtime.

Merge plan shape:

merge_plan:
  id: "stable digest from workspace, stage manifest, and generated_at"
  status: "needs_approval | blocked | applied"
  workspace: ""
  stage_root: ""
  generated_at: ""
  decisions:
    - target_path: "AGENTS.md"
      staged_path: ""
      action: "create_file | append_managed_section | replace_managed_section | companion_only | blocked"
      reason: ""
      target_digest_before: ""
      staged_digest: ""
      approval_required: true
      rollback_entry: ""
  blocked:
    - target_path: ""
      reason: ""
  warnings: []
  verification:
    ok: true
    checks: []
    errors: {}

Allowed merge actions:

Action Allowed when Write behavior create_file target does not exist and parent path is safe create file after backup manifest records absence append_managed_section target is Markdown, has no conflicting markers, and user approved append append managed Product-Agent OS section replace_managed_section target has exactly one matching managed section replace only that section companion_only target exists without safe managed merge path no project write; keep staged proposal blocked path, marker, digest, validation, or approval is unsafe no project write

Rollback requirements:

  • before writing, copy existing target content or record that the file was absent;
  • store rollback manifest under the staging directory, not in global user config;
  • for created files, rollback can remove only files whose current digest still matches the generated digest;
  • for updated files, rollback can restore only when the current digest matches the post-apply digest;
  • rollback reports are evidence artifacts, not hidden state.

Rollback manifest shape:

rollback_manifest:
  schema_version: 1
  merge_plan_id: ""
  applied_at: ""
  entries:
    - target_path: "AGENTS.md"
      action: "created | updated"
      existed_before: false
      digest_before: ""
      digest_after: "sha256:..."
      backup_path: ""
  verification:
    ok: true
    checks: []

Rollback mode is conservative. It refuses to restore or remove a file when the current target digest differs from the recorded post-apply digest, because that means another actor changed the file after apply.

docs.title: Hook Activation Gate
docs.text:
Track 3 stages hook scripts and .codex/hooks/hooks.json as target-project assets. Track 4 may merge hook files into a workspace, but activation remains a separate decision.

Rules:

  • hook scripts can be merged only after validator success and explicit approval;
  • .codex/hooks/hooks.json defaults to companion_only unless the approval record includes enable_hooks;
  • enabling hooks requires an approval record that names hook events, scripts, blocking behavior, and rollback path;
  • pre_tool_use_policy.py blocking rules must stay narrow and auditable;
  • hook activation must never happen from plugin-root lifecycle config;
  • fixture eval must include one case where hook scripts are staged but hook activation is not approved, and one case where approval enables hook config safely.

Hook approval extension:

approval:
  enable_hooks: false
  approved_hook_events: []
  blocking_hooks:
    - "PreToolUse"
  hook_rollback: "remove or restore .codex/hooks/hooks.json when current digest matches post-apply digest"

docs.title: Fixture Eval Hardening
docs.text:
Track 4 should extend run_fixture_eval.py rather than replace it.

Additional fixture projects:

plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/stale-merge-plan/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/path-traversal-stage/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/symlink-escape/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/hook-activation-unapproved/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/hook-activation-approved/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/source-policy-conflict/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/automation-candidate-valid/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/automation-candidate-invalid/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/rollback-required/
plugins/product-agent-os/assets/fixtures/failure-log-regression/

Fixture result shape:

fixture: ""
ok: true
profile: ""
renderer_status: ""
merge_status: ""
source_policy_status: ""
automation_status: ""
expected_checks:
  safe_paths: true
  stale_digest_blocked: true
  source_policy_enforced: true
  automation_candidate_gated: true
evidence:
  files_inspected: []
  commands: []
  reports: []
risks: []

Behavior-level checks:

  • dry-run still writes no files;
  • stage mode writes only under the requested staging directory;
  • merge plan mode writes no files;
  • apply mode requires staged manifest and approval record;
  • unapproved apply is blocked;
  • stale target digest is blocked;
  • symlink and path traversal attempts are blocked;
  • existing unmarked .codex/config.toml remains companion-only;
  • hook scripts can be merged without activating .codex/hooks/hooks.json unless enable_hooks is approved;
  • failed verification evidence remains visible;
  • failure log entries can generate deterministic regression cases;
  • invalid automation candidate remains candidate-only or blocked;
  • source-policy conflict does not become an official claim.

docs.title: Failure-Log Regression Contract
docs.text:
Product-Agent OS should turn real hardening failures into future deterministic checks.

Input sources:

  • current RUNLOG.md;
  • .codex/runlogs/archive/;
  • fixture eval reports;
  • rollback manifests;
  • source-policy reports;
  • automation promotion reports.

Regression case shape:

regression_case:
  id: "stale-merge-plan-blocked"
  source: "RUNLOG.md#2026-05-14"
  failure_summary: ""
  reproduction_fixture: "stale-merge-plan"
  command: "python plugins\\product-agent-os\\scripts\\run_fixture_eval.py"
  expected_status: "blocked"
  expected_checks:
    stale_digest_blocked: true
  evidence_to_preserve:
    - "merge_plan.id"
    - "target_digest_before"
    - "blocked reason"

Rules:

  • a failure-log regression must name the original evidence source;
  • regression fixtures must use synthetic data only;
  • sensitive logs are summarized, not copied raw;
  • every regression case must have an expected command and observable expected result;
  • failure-log conversion may propose fixture additions but must not silently edit production projects.

docs.title: Source-Policy Validator
docs.text:
Track 4 should add a deterministic source-policy validator.

Proposed files:

plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/product_agent_os/source_policy.py
plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/validate_source_policy.py
tests/product_agent_os/test_source_policy.py

CLI contract:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\validate_source_policy.py <workspace>

Report shape:

source_policy_report:
  status: "ok | needs_review | blocked"
  files:
    - path: ""
      source_status: "official | official + experiment | community | experiment | missing"
      supported_facts: []
      assumptions: []
      unsupported_claims: []
      missing_context: []
      freshness_risks: []
  registry_updates_required: []
  secret_findings: []
  errors: []

Rules:

  • docs pages must include Source status: unless exempt by project docs policy;
  • OpenAI, Codex, Agents SDK, model, approvals, hooks, MCP, and automation behavior claims require official sources or an explicit freshness risk;
  • Context7 is accepted as official only when the underlying source is official;
  • community claims require insight-card handling with trust_level and verification_status;
  • generated examples cannot contain secrets, private customer data, raw private chat logs, or absolute user-specific paths;
  • missing or stale source evidence yields needs_review unless the claim is safety-sensitive, in which case it yields blocked.

Deterministic boundary:

  • the validator can prove document structure, required markers, source registry references, forbidden literals, stale checked_at dates, and known unsupported-source patterns;
  • the validator cannot prove full semantic truth for every sentence;
  • when semantic truth is uncertain, output must be needs_review with a specific file path and reason;
  • only explicit high-risk patterns, forbidden literals, missing source status, or unsafe promotion of community claims should become blocked.

docs.title: Automation Promotion Validator
docs.text:
Track 4 should add an automation candidate validator.

Proposed files:

plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/product_agent_os/automation_policy.py
plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/validate_automation_candidate.py
tests/product_agent_os/test_automation_policy.py

CLI contract:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\validate_automation_candidate.py <candidate-file>

Report shape:

automation_promotion_report:
  status: "candidate_only | ready_for_manual_approval | blocked"
  candidate_file: ""
  required_fields_present: true
  manual_success_count: 0
  owner_present: true
  cadence_present: true
  verification_present: true
  failure_modes_present: true
  rollback_or_disable_present: true
  write_policy_present: true
  explicit_approval_present: false
  errors: []
  warnings: []

Promotion rules:

  • candidate_only is the default state;
  • ready_for_manual_approval requires stable inputs, stable outputs, owner, cadence, verification, failure modes, rollback or disable path, explicit write policy, and at least two manual successful runs or equivalent fixture evidence;
  • blocked is required for missing owner, missing verification, missing rollback or disable path, ambiguous writes, external side effects without approval, or any secret-like content;
  • validator output must not create schedules or call automation APIs.

docs.title: Optional Agents SDK Runner Boundary
docs.text:
Track 4 should include only a bounded runner design unless the user separately approves implementation.

Proposed design artifact:

docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-14-product-agent-os-agents-sdk-runner-design.md

Possible future implementation root:

plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/agents_sdk_runner/

Runner responsibilities:

  • read Product-Agent OS control-plane artifacts;
  • create a Manager agent that owns lifecycle routing;
  • expose specialist roles as tools or handoff targets;
  • call Codex MCP only within explicit sandbox and approval policy;
  • validate handoff payloads before continuing;
  • keep sessions and tracing separate from checked-in project memory;
  • fail closed when credentials, sources, approval state, or write ownership are unclear.
  • record model, reasoning, tool, handoff, latency, failure, and approval events in traces without storing secrets.

Runner non-goals:

  • no default dependency installation;
  • no default network access in plugin verification;
  • no credential creation or storage;
  • no direct replacement for Codex App, CLI, project skills, or .codex/agents;
  • no automation scheduling from inside the runner.

Runner design must define:

  • dependency setup path and offline test fallback;
  • model and reasoning defaults per role;
  • environment variable names for credentials without exposing values;
  • session retention and redaction policy;
  • tracing retention and redaction policy;
  • eval suite for handoff completeness, source fidelity, tool boundary, approval handling, and secret retention;
  • rollback or shutdown path for partial runner execution.

docs.title: Security And Approval Model
docs.text:
Track 4 must preserve least privilege.

Approval required for:

  • applying staged files to a workspace;
  • appending managed sections to unmarked Markdown files;
  • enabling hooks;
  • creating or updating automation schedules outside Track 4 validators;
  • writing external systems;
  • changing source-of-truth docs, registry records, or release artifacts;
  • using an Agents SDK runner against a real workspace.

Blocked by default:

  • path traversal and symlink escape;
  • stale merge plans;
  • destructive commands embedded in generated assets;
  • global Codex config mutation;
  • broad network access in tests or fixture evals;
  • secret-like literals in templates, fixtures, examples, docs, runlogs, automation candidates, or runner config;
  • active automation without manual stability evidence and explicit approval.

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
Track 4 tests should remain deterministic unittest tests.

Required tests:

  • staged manifest is required before apply;
  • approval record is required before apply and cannot be replaced by a bare plan id;
  • approval record must name approved targets and actions;
  • merge planner produces read-only plans;
  • apply mode rejects missing approval record;
  • apply mode rejects approval records that do not match the current merge plan id;
  • apply mode rejects stale target digest;
  • apply mode rejects path traversal and symlink escape;
  • managed Markdown section replacement preserves user content outside markers;
  • unmarked Markdown append requires explicit approval;
  • unmarked .codex/config.toml stays companion-only;
  • hook scripts can be applied without enabling hook lifecycle config;
  • hook lifecycle config requires enable_hooks approval;
  • backups and rollback manifest are created before writes;
  • rollback mode restores created or updated files only when current digests match the post-apply digest;
  • rollback refuses to overwrite changed post-apply content;
  • source-policy validator detects missing source status and unsupported OpenAI behavior claims;
  • source-policy validator returns needs_review for semantic ambiguity instead of claiming proof;
  • source-policy validator separates official, community, experiment, and unsupported claims;
  • automation validator blocks incomplete candidates;
  • automation validator classifies complete candidates as ready for manual approval without creating a schedule;
  • fixture eval includes merge, hook activation, source-policy, automation, rollback, and failure-log regression statuses;
  • optional Agents SDK runner design is not part of default plugin activation.

Required verification commands after implementation:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py
python tools\check_docs.py
$env:PYTHONPATH='C:\tmp\codex_docs_mkdocs'; python -m mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Критерии приемки
docs.text:
Track 4 is complete when:

  • the plugin can generate a merge plan from Track 3 staged artifacts without writing to the workspace;
  • Track 3 stage output includes a manifest or Track 4 can create a verified manifest from staged artifacts before apply;
  • apply requires a separate approval record with approved target paths, actions, accepted risks, and approval timestamp;
  • approved apply mode writes only allowed files and sections inside the workspace;
  • stale, ambiguous, unsafe, or unapproved merge plans are blocked;
  • hook lifecycle config is not activated unless the approval record explicitly enables hooks;
  • every apply creates a rollback manifest and evidence report;
  • rollback can be executed and refuses unsafe restore conditions;
  • failure-log regression cases can be generated or validated from synthetic evidence;
  • fixture eval covers merge safety, stale state, path safety, hook activation, source-policy conflict, automation readiness, rollback behavior, and failure-log regression behavior;
  • source-policy validator produces deterministic ok, needs_review, or blocked reports;
  • automation validator keeps candidates candidate-only until evidence and explicit approval are present;
  • active automations are not created by Track 4 code;
  • optional Agents SDK runner remains isolated from the default plugin path;
  • full verification pack exits 0 in the current run.

docs.title: Residual Risks
docs.text:
Even after Track 4, Product-Agent OS still cannot prove that every generated workflow is product-correct for every real project. It can prove stronger safety properties around merge behavior, evidence, source policy, and automation readiness.

The optional Agents SDK runner remains a higher-risk architecture layer. It should move forward only after local hardening is implemented and a separate plan defines dependencies, credential handling, MCP boundaries, evals, and rollback.

Automation promotion remains a human-owned decision. Track 4 can validate readiness and produce an approval packet, but it should not infer business ownership, legal acceptability, customer impact, or operational cadence without explicit user input.

docs.title: Implementation Handoff
docs.text:
Implementation should be split into focused tasks:

  1. Stage manifest and approval record contracts.
  2. Merge plan data model and read-only planner.
  3. Approved apply mode with backup and rollback manifest.
  4. Rollback command and safety checks.
  5. Hook activation gate.
  6. Merge, hook, rollback, and failure-log fixture cases.
  7. Source-policy validator and tests.
  8. Automation promotion validator and tests.
  9. Fixture eval result expansion.
  10. Optional Agents SDK runner design artifact.
  11. Documentation, navigation, and full verification.

Each task must start with failing tests where practical, preserve Track 3 staged-first behavior, and avoid unrelated refactors.

docs.title: Spec Self-Review
docs.text:
Coverage:

  • stage manifest and approval record are specified as separate contracts;
  • safe approved merge is specified through merge plan, apply, rollback, and path-safety contracts;
  • hook activation is separated from hook file merge;
  • fixture eval hardening has explicit new fixtures and expected behaviors;
  • failure-log regression has input sources and case shape;
  • source-policy hardening has report shape and blocking rules;
  • automation gates have report shape and promotion states;
  • optional Agents SDK runner has a boundary and non-goals;
  • verification commands match project rules.

Scope check:

  • Track 4 is broad but still one coherent hardening layer around an existing plugin package;
  • the optional runner is explicitly separated so the implementation plan can defer it or place it in a gated final task.

Ambiguity check:

  • default behavior remains staged-first;
  • active automation creation is out of scope;
  • direct writes require explicit apply mode plus approval record;
  • bare merge plan id is not treated as user approval;
  • unmarked user-authored files are preserved unless a safe managed Markdown append is explicitly approved.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS Codex Runtime Runner Design
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

Sources: Product-Agent OS plugin spec, Product-Agent OS production hardening design, Product-Agent OS production hardening plan, Product-Agent OS Agents SDK runner boundary, source registry, Codex plugins, Codex skills, Codex subagents, Codex hooks, Agent approvals and security, Codex workflows.

This design supersedes the Track 5 standalone Agents SDK runner idea. The plugin will run only inside Codex surfaces: Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, plugin skills, subagents, hooks, staged renderer, approval-gated merge, and local validators. Track 5 therefore implements a Codex runtime runner, not an API-backed application and not a separate OpenAI Agents SDK service.

docs.title: Read-Only Analysis
docs.text:
The original Product-Agent OS spec defined four implementation tracks and treated Agents SDK as an advanced optional surface. Track 4 kept that path design-only because the default Product-Agent OS plugin already had a safer local workflow: lifecycle skills, staged infrastructure, explicit approval records, safe merge, rollback, source-policy validation, automation promotion validation, and fixture eval.

The current implementation confirms that this local Codex-first layer is the strongest foundation. Track 1-2 provide contracts, discovery, validators, lifecycle skills, and handoff references. Track 3 provides staged templates and renderer. Track 4 provides manifest-bound merge/apply/rollback and policy validators. The clean baseline before this spec change was: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v ran 194 tests with OK, python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py exited 0, and python tools\check_docs.py passed.

The implementation gap is now narrower: Product-Agent OS needs a Codex-only orchestrator that can read control-plane artifacts, choose the next lifecycle action, validate handoffs, route to packaged skills or project-scoped subagents, and emit evidence. It must not introduce separate API credentials, external runtime dependency installation, or an out-of-Codex agent service.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Implement the smallest useful Codex runtime runner that turns Product-Agent OS from a set of skills and validators into a coherent local orchestration layer inside Codex.

The runner must:

  • read Product-Agent OS context from AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, and RUNLOG.md;
  • infer lifecycle state and recommended next action;
  • route to packaged Product-Agent OS skills and generated subagent role configs;
  • validate structured handoffs before lifecycle advancement;
  • validate source policy, approval state, ownership boundaries, tool boundaries, and redaction;
  • produce a machine-readable codex_runner_result;
  • run deterministically in tests without network, external credentials, or package installation;
  • write nothing by default and never create active automations.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
Track 5 does not:

  • implement a standalone OpenAI Agents SDK app;
  • call OpenAI APIs directly;
  • require API keys, external credentials, or environment-provided model access;
  • install openai-agents or other runtime dependencies;
  • run Codex as an MCP server from outside Codex;
  • make an external service, deployment target, or HTTP server;
  • bypass Codex sandbox, approvals, or plugin boundaries;
  • change global Codex config;
  • create Codex App automations, GitHub Actions, schedules, recurring jobs, or external workflows;
  • store secrets, private customer data, raw private chat logs, raw traces, or absolute user-specific paths.

docs.title: Design Choice
docs.text:
Use a Codex-only contract runner.

Rejected approaches:

  • Standalone Agents SDK runner: unnecessary for a plugin that will run only in Codex, and it would add credential, dependency, network, tracing, and deployment concerns.
  • Codex MCP bridge: useful when an external Agents SDK app wants Codex as a backend, but not needed when the plugin is already executing in Codex.
  • Implicit skill auto-runner: convenient, but too opaque. The runner must return a route packet and require explicit handoff/approval gates rather than silently invoking broad workflows.

Recommended approach:

  1. Add a dependency-free codex_runtime_runner package under the plugin scripts.
  2. Make it read-only by default and contract-first.
  3. Route lifecycle actions to existing Product-Agent OS skills, templates, validators, and generated subagent role configs.
  4. Extend fixture eval with runner status and regression checks.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["Codex workspace"] --> B["Control-plane loader"]
    B --> C["Lifecycle state detector"]
    C --> D["Route planner"]
    D --> E["Policy validators"]
    E --> F{"Safe next action?"}
    F -->|"No"| G["Blocked or needs context result"]
    F -->|"Yes"| H["Skill or subagent route packet"]
    H --> I["Handoff validator"]
    I --> J["Codex runner result"]
