docs.title: Playbook: designing an AI-native team
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: Building an AI-Native Engineering Team, Codex use cases, Agent Skills.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Design a set of agent roles and repeatable workflows for a team or project.

docs.title: Role Map
docs.text: Role Workflow Artifact Researcher Source and requirements collection source cards, brief Planner Implementation plan implementation plan Builder Scoped implementation diff, tests Reviewer Risk-based review findings Maintainer Docs and changelog update docs update

docs.title: Design Questions
docs.text:
• Which tasks repeat more than three times?
  • Which rules must live in AGENTS.md?
  • Which workflows should be extracted into skills?
  • Which tasks are read-heavy and fit subagents?
  • Where is memory needed, and where are checked-in docs enough?
  • Which verification commands are mandatory?

docs.title: Prompt
docs.text:
Design an AI-native operating model for the project "{project}".

Return:
- repeatable workflows;
- which of them should become skills;
- which agent roles are needed;
- which rules should go into AGENTS.md;
- which memory boundaries are needed;
- which checks prove quality.

docs.title: Playbook: build full feature with agents
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: How OpenAI uses Codex, Codex workflows, Codex best practices, A practical guide to building agents.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Take a feature from idea to PR with managed agent roles and verification.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Create REQUIREMENTS.md.
  2. Ask Codex to prepare PLAN.md without changing code.
  3. Split work by ownership: backend, frontend, tests, docs, release.
  4. Run builder tasks in separate worktrees or with non-overlapping write scopes.
  5. Run test/review agents.
  6. Run evals or visual/manual QA.
  7. Prepare the PR body and release notes.
  8. Move the repeatable method into a skill or AGENTS.md.

docs.title: Prompt
docs.text:
Build this feature as a product-agent workflow.

Read:
- AGENTS.md
- REQUIREMENTS.md

Before changing files:
- produce PLAN.md;
- name ownership boundaries;
- identify required tests and evals;
- list risks and rollback.

During implementation:
- make one focused slice at a time;
- run verification after each meaningful slice;
- update RUNLOG.md.

Final output:
- changed files;
- commands run;
- test/eval result;
- PR summary;
- release notes draft;
- lessons for AGENTS.md or skills.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• Requirements, plan, tests and run log are explicit.
  • No agent edits outside its ownership without approval.
  • PR summary includes verification evidence.
  • Reusable lessons are captured.

docs.title: Playbook: code review through Codex
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: Codex workflows, Codex subagents, Agent approvals and security.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Use Codex as a reviewer that looks for bugs, regressions, test gaps, security risks and maintainability issues.

docs.title: Prompt for one agent
docs.text:
Review current changes as a code reviewer.

Prioritize:
1. Bugs and behavioral regressions.
2. Security or data-safety risks.
3. Missing tests for changed behavior.
4. Professional coding failures that create real debt: unnecessary custom code, missing existing-capability scan, needless dependency, weak abstraction, brittle refactor or low-signal comments.
5. Maintainability issues only if they affect correctness.

Output findings first.
Each finding must include file, line, severity, and why it matters.
Do not rewrite code unless asked.

docs.title: Professional Coding Review
docs.text:
For non-mechanical code changes, the reviewer checks Professional Code Authoring Standards, .codex/workflows/coding-standards.md and .codex/artifact-templates/coding-standard-checklist.md when they are present in the task packet. Findings should call out:

  • custom code where delete/configuration/standard library/framework/current dependency/project helper would solve the same need;
  • new dependency without negative_dependency_rule, rejected alternatives, compatibility and rollback/removal evidence;
  • refactor that changes legacy seams without characterization tests or explicit accepted gap;
  • shallow wrapper, clever abstraction or comments that restate code instead of explaining intent, invariant, risk or trade-off;
  • unsupported claims such as "clean", "simple", "senior", "safe" or "minimal" without evidence.

Style-only preferences are not blockers unless they create behavioral, operational, security or maintainability risk.

docs.title: Parallel review
docs.text:
For larger PRs, you can explicitly ask for subagents:

Use one parallel subagent per review track:
- Security risks
- Correctness bugs
- Test gaps
- Maintainability

Wait for all agents and return a consolidated review.
Do not include duplicate findings.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• Check that findings refer to real files and lines.
  • Request a reproduction or failing test for every high-severity bug.
  • Do not accept stylistic comments as blockers without behavioral risk.
  • Treat missing professional-coding evidence as a review gap, not as proof that runtime behavior was exercised.

docs.title: Playbook: Context7 deep research
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: Context7 results for OpenAI docs, Source registry.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Use Context7 as a fast retrieval layer for expanding the knowledge base while preserving official-source discipline.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. State the research question as a list of capabilities, not as a broad query.
  2. Resolve the library ID for each library.
  3. Query docs for no more than the three most important directions in one pass.
  4. Split results into:
  5. official facts;
  6. examples/recipes;
  7. architecture implications;
  8. claims that need direct source verification.
  9. Add or update source cards.
  10. Apply changes to docs.
  11. Run checks.

docs.title: Good Query
docs.text:
Extract authoritative design details for the OpenAI Agents SDK:
Agent, Runner, tools, handoffs, guardrails, sessions, tracing,
context, multi-agent orchestration, and recommended architecture patterns.
Focus on concepts useful for documenting multi-agent systems with memory.

docs.title: Bad Query
docs.text:
Tell me everything about agents.

It is too broad: the result will be hard to verify and move into the source registry.

docs.title: Output contract
docs.text:
context7_libraries:
  - library_id: ""
    source_reputation: "High | Medium | Low"
findings:
  - claim: ""
    source_url: ""
    target_doc: ""
    action: "add | update | reject | verify_directly"
risks:
  - ""
verification:
  - "python tools/check_docs.py"
  - "python -m mkdocs build --strict"

docs.title: Playbook: documentation update
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment Sources: Codex changelog, Codex workflows.

Use this playbook when Codex, Agents SDK, Product-Agent OS or project behavior changes and the documentation must stay source-backed.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Changed source docs, official references, source registry entries and affected pages.
  • Project rules for Russian/English terminology, source status and approvals.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Updated documentation pages, source registry entry and focused docs tests when needed.
  • Current verification evidence for docs structure and MkDocs build.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Recommended order:

python tools\check_docs.py
python -m mkdocs build --strict
git diff --check

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Adding claims without registry support can make docs drift from source truth.
  • Rebuilding generated site/ without source updates does not prove the docs are correct.

docs.title: Playbook: Doubt / verifier loop
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

Sources: Grounded answering, Hallucination Control, Artifact Contracts, Behavioral evals, Batch 40 source-transfer packet.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The Doubt / verifier loop turns a manual "check again" request into a reviewable completion gate. The operating shape is worker_output -> doubt_verification_packet -> completion-skeptic -> revise_or_pass.

The point is not to make the agent anxiously rewrite the answer. The point is to extract checkable claims, requirements, evidence gaps and approval boundaries, then change only the parts where the verifier found a concrete defect or missing evidence.

docs.title: Trigger
docs.text:
Use completion-skeptic when one of these signals appears:

  • the user asks "check again", "did we miss anything", or "check before final";
  • the agent is about to say "done", "ready", "works", "fixed", "verified" or an equivalent claim;
  • code, docs/source registry, architecture contracts, security/release/eval layers changed;
  • the answer depends on current facts, source-sensitive docs, tool output or generated views;
  • there is false-pass, false-rewrite, stale-evidence or approval-bypass risk.

Skip the loop for a small deterministic answer when there is no completion claim, risk class or user-trigger.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Preserve the artifact under review: worker output, diff summary, doc draft, plan row or final answer candidate.
  2. Extract the claim ledger: each checkable claim gets claim_type, status, evidence_refs and residual_risk.
  3. Extract the requirement ledger: user request, acceptance criteria, non-goals, approval constraints and missing context.
  4. Fill the evidence ledger: source registry, local files, current commands, eval runs, owner decisions, approved browser/runtime/web checks or explicit missing check.
  5. Run the skeptic pass: completion-skeptic returns pass | revise | needs_more_context | blocked_by_approval | accepted_risk.
  6. The reviser changes only confirmed gaps. Rule: do not rewrite first.
  7. The final answer names what was checked, what changed and what remains an accepted_gap or residual risk.

docs.title: Packet Excerpt
docs.text:
doubt_verification_packet_v1:
  artifact_under_review: "final answer candidate"
  claim_ledger:
    - id: "C1"
      claim: "The docs navigation includes the new playbook."
      claim_type: "docs_behavior"
      status: "supported"
      evidence_refs: ["mkdocs_nav_current_run"]
  requirement_ledger:
    - id: "R1"
      requirement: "Document architecture, diagrams and examples."
      status: "covered"
  evidence_ledger:
    - id: "mkdocs_nav_current_run"
      provider: "current_command"
      provenance_kind: "command"
      status: "available"
  verdict:
    status: "revise"
    reason: "One example category is missing."
  accepted_gaps:
    - owner: "Product owner"
      reason: "Manual pilot evidence is B40-S5 scope."
      residual_risk: "Usefulness is not proven by docs alone."
      follow_up: "Run the B40-S5 pilot ledger."

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Example id Task type Trigger Packet focus Safe final style docs_research_example docs/research answer "Check sources" source registry, official/community split, needs_fresh_check Separate supported facts, assumptions and unsupported claims. code_check_example code change "Done?" current command evidence, lint/test gaps, approval boundary Name commands run and missing checks; avoid a works claim without run evidence. architecture_review_example architecture/spec "Did we miss anything?" requirements, non-goals, dependency and rollback gaps Revise only confirmed architecture gaps. product_planning_example feature plan "Check the matrix" acceptance criteria, user value, dependencies, stop conditions Return missing tasks and accepted scope cuts. security_release_example release/security "Can we ship?" approval gates, source status, rollback, no-unapproved-actions proof Block or accepted_risk instead of a release claim. ai_eval_example AI/eval work "Check quality" baseline, current eval, scorecard thresholds, false pass/rewrite Keep manual-only until pilot and owner review.

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• False pass: the packet says pass while evidence is stale, generated-only or approval-blocked.
  • False rewrite: the skeptic rewrites correct content without a confirmed gap.
  • Fake evidence: command output, source IDs or tool traces are invented.
  • Context leak: raw private chat logs, secrets or local absolute paths enter packet examples.
  • Automation drift: manual success is skipped and the loop becomes an active hook, MCP server, Agents SDK runner or automation.

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text: No active hook, automation, MCP server, Agents SDK runner or provider call is created by this playbook. It documents the manual and plugin-local path only. Future guardrail or runtime integration requires a separate approval packet, privacy review, scorecard evidence and rollback/disable path.

docs.title: Next Artifact
docs.text: For one task, produce a doubt_verification_packet and a short final answer update. For repeated success, record failure examples, eval cases and owner review, then consider the normal promotion chain: manual -> playbook -> skill -> plugin -> automation candidate.

docs.title: Playbook: eval-driven improvement loop
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: Iterate on difficult problems, Model optimization, OpenAI Cookbook, Responses API.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Solve hard tasks through a scored improvement loop, not through a one-off prompt.

docs.title: Loop
docs.text:
1. Run baseline eval.
  2. Identify the biggest failure mode.
  3. Make one focused change.
  4. Re-run eval.
  5. Inspect generated artifacts.
  6. Log scores and decision.
  7. Continue until deterministic score and LLM-judge average meet thresholds.

docs.title: Eval matrix
docs.text: Check type What it checks Example Deterministic Formal constraints tests pass, lint, broken links, schema LLM-as-judge Subjective quality usefulness, readability, visual quality Artifact inspection Real output screenshot, report, generated page Regression Old scenarios no previous pass regressed

docs.title: Stopping rule
docs.text:
overall_score_min: 0.90
llm_judge_average_min: 0.90
no_blocking_regressions: true
artifact_review_required: true

docs.title: RUNLOG rule
docs.text:
Each iteration must record:

  • baseline or previous best;
  • change made;
  • score before/after;
  • artifact inspected;
  • bottleneck;
  • next attempt.

docs.title: Playbook: grounded answering
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: Prompting, Structured Outputs, Model optimization, OpenAI Cookbook.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Give a GPT-model answer with minimal hallucination risk: retrieve, constrain, answer, cite, verify, escalate uncertainty.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Determine the question type: factual, design, coding, current data, opinion.
  2. Collect context from allowed sources.
  3. Package context with source IDs.
  4. Formulate the prompt contract.
  5. Require citations or structured output.
  6. Pass the answer through a verifier.
  7. If context is insufficient, return missing context instead of guessing.

docs.title: Prompt
docs.text:
# Role
You are a grounded answer generator.

# Goal
Answer the user question using only the provided sources.

# Context
<source id="S1" type="official" url="...">
...
</source>

# Rules
- Every factual claim must cite a source ID.
- If a claim is not supported, put it in unsupported_claims.
- If sources conflict, describe the conflict.
- If context is insufficient, do not guess.

# Output
Return:
- answer
- citations
- assumptions
- unsupported_claims
- missing_context
- confidence: high | medium | low

docs.title: Verifier prompt
docs.text:
Check the answer against the provided sources.

For each factual claim:
- supported
- unsupported
- contradicted
- needs_fresh_check

Return verdict: pass | fail | needs_more_context.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• No factual claims without citation.
  • No invented source IDs.
  • Missing context is named explicitly.
  • If confidence is below high, the answer explains why.
  • For current facts, fresh verification was performed or the inability to verify is stated.

docs.title: Playbook: maintain agent operating docs
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: AGENTS.md docs, Codex best practices, AGENTS.md open format.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Maintain AGENTS.md, skills, playbooks and templates as the project's living operating system.

docs.title: Update triggers
docs.text:
• Agent repeatedly asks the same clarification.
  • Test command changed.
  • Workflow repeated three or more times.
  • New failure mode appears in review.
  • Automation failed due to missing setup.
  • Team adds new package, service, or deployment path.

docs.title: Maintenance loop
docs.text:
1. Collect recurring friction from RUNLOG and review notes.
  2. Decide destination:
  3. always-on rule -> AGENTS.md;
  4. task method -> skill;
  5. one-off lesson -> insight;
  6. source-backed fact -> source registry and docs.
  7. Keep instructions short and scoped.
  8. Run docs checks.
  9. Verify a sample Codex prompt can follow the updated instructions.

docs.title: Anti-patterns
docs.text:
• Put every possible rule into root AGENTS.md.
  • Hide task-specific workflows in persistent instructions.
  • Create broad skills that overlap.
  • Automate before manual workflow is stable.
  • Keep run logs only in chat history.

docs.title: Playbook: product-ready PR with Codex
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: How OpenAI uses Codex, Codex GitHub integration, Codex best practices.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Prepare a PR that a reviewer can evaluate without repeating the investigation.

docs.title: PR packet
docs.text:
## Summary
- What changed
- Why it changed
- Product/user impact

## Verification
- Command:
- Result:
- Manual/visual QA:
- Evals:

## Risks
- ...

## Rollback
- ...

## Agent notes
- Sources:
- Assumptions:
- Follow-ups:

docs.title: Review gates
docs.text:
• Tests and evals run after final diff.
  • No unresolved unsupported claims.
  • No broad permissions hidden in automation.
  • Risky behavior has rollback note.
  • Release notes are written if user-facing behavior changes.

docs.title: Prompt
docs.text:
Prepare this branch for a product-ready PR.

Read AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md and RUNLOG.md.
Return:
- PR title;
- PR body;
- verification evidence;
- risks and rollback;
- release notes draft.
Do not claim tests pass unless you ran them in this turn.

docs.title: Playbook: multi-agent research loop
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: Codex subagents, Codex workflows, Agent Skills.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Create a managed research loop for updating the knowledge base: source discovery, separation of official facts from community signals, claim verification and release of a documentation change.

docs.title: When to use
docs.text:
• A new Codex changelog entry appeared.
  • A section needs to be added for a new capability.
  • There is a community trick that may be useful but needs verification.

docs.title: Single-agent mode
docs.text:
Research the topic "{topic}" for the Codex knowledge base.

Do:
1. Find official OpenAI sources.
2. Create source cards.
3. Separate community claims from official claims.
4. Propose documentation changes.
5. Name verification commands.
Do not mix unverified tricks with official instructions.

docs.title: Parallel mode
docs.text:
Use only when you explicitly want subagents:

Use parallel subagents for this research task.

Agent 1: official Codex docs.
Agent 2: Agents SDK docs for memory/orchestration.
Agent 3: community insight backlog.

Each agent returns verified claims, uncertain claims, and source cards.
Wait for all agents. Then synthesize one update plan and do not include raw logs.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• New official claims have source cards.
  • Community claims live only in docs/insights/.
  • Every proposed edit has verification status.
  • MkDocs build passes.

docs.title: Context7 enrichment
docs.text: When the topic is related to OpenAI SDK, Responses API, Codex or Agents SDK, add a separate pass through Context7 deep research. Its goal is to find SDK-level details: primitives, method contracts, tool types, structured output examples and observability patterns. After retrieval, still update the source registry instead of inserting unsigned claims directly.

docs.title: Playbook: use case to plugin
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment Sources: Codex use cases, Save workflows as skills, Create a CLI Codex can use, Codex plugins, Build plugins.

Use this playbook to turn a repeated Codex workflow into a plugin with narrow skills, clear inputs and outputs, safe write policy, verification and owner maintenance.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Official use case archetype or proven internal workflow.
  • Manual run evidence, failure log, candidate skills and expected verification commands.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Playbook, skill candidate, plugin blueprint and eval cases.
  • Permission model, packaging/update process and owner handoff.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Keep the promotion order: manual workflow, playbook, skill, plugin, automation. Run eval cases before packaging and keep automation approval separate.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Packaging too early can turn an unproven prompt into a reusable failure.
  • A plugin with unclear permissions can bypass the project approval boundary.

docs.title: Playbook: workflow to skill
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: Agent Skills, Codex best practices, Codex automations.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Turn a repeatable workflow into a Codex skill that can be used manually, then tested and automated when necessary.

If the workflow should become a plugin, use Playbook: use case to plugin after the first skill has passed real validation.

docs.title: When a workflow is ready for a skill
docs.text:
• It has been run manually at least several times.
  • Inputs and outputs are stable.
  • There is a clear trigger.
  • There is a verification command or checklist.
  • Risks and forbidden actions are known.

docs.title: Skill rubric
docs.text: Criterion Requirement Scope One job, not "do everything" Trigger Description contains explicit trigger words Inputs Required inputs are listed Outputs Result format is fixed Progressive disclosure SKILL.md is short; references are loaded as needed Scripts Only for deterministic behavior or external tooling Evals Cases exist: should trigger, should not trigger

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    M["Manual workflow"] --> D["Draft skill"]
    D --> T["Trigger tests"]
    T --> U["Use in real tasks"]
    U --> F["Failure log"]
    F --> R["Refine"]
    R --> P["Package as plugin"]
    P --> A["Automation candidate"]

For completion-skeptic, the same path is mandatory: manual -> playbook -> skill -> plugin -> automation candidate. The failure log must capture false pass, false rewrite, fake evidence, missing checks, accepted gaps and owner review. Eval cases must cover trigger and non-trigger behavior before any automation candidate is promoted.

Automation blockers: no schedule, hook, MCP server, Agents SDK runner, provider call or external write is allowed without separate approval, rollback/disable path and scorecard evidence.

Use lowercase contract labels in handoffs when needed: eval cases and automation blockers.

docs.title: Candidate product skills
docs.text:
• product-spec-writer
  • implementation-planner
  • test-gap-finder
  • release-note-writer
  • eval-loop-runner
  • ui-visual-reviewer
  • workspace-readiness-auditor

docs.title: Playbook: workspace readiness audit
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment Sources: Codex best practices, AGENTS.md docs, Agent approvals and security, Codex automations.

Use this playbook to decide whether a workspace is ready for product-agent workflows.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Workspace files, project rules, setup/build/test commands and source policy.
  • Existing skills, automations, evals, sandbox and approval constraints.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Readiness score, blockers, recommended docs/skill additions and first workflow to stabilize.
  • Clear accepted gaps when evidence is missing but the owner accepts residual risk.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: The audit should remain read-only. It should name commands and evidence gaps without changing project files unless a later implementation slice is approved.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Treating an audit as proof of readiness can hide missing runtime evidence.
  • Broad recommendations without a safe next action can expand scope unnecessarily.

docs.title: Control-plane files
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: Codex best practices, AGENTS.md docs, AGENTS.md open format, Iterate on difficult problems.

docs.title: Why control-plane files are needed
docs.text: A long session should not be the only place where requirements and decisions live. Control-plane files make work resumable, reviewable and suitable for skills or automations.

docs.title: File set
docs.text: File Purpose Updated when AGENTS.md Durable project rules A rule must live across work items REQUIREMENTS.md Scope, users, acceptance criteria Before planning PLAN.md Decomposition, ownership, sequence Before implementation TEST.md Deterministic checks, manual QA, visual QA Before review EVALS.md LLM-as-judge, score thresholds, artifacts For subjective or long-horizon work RUNLOG.md Iterations, scores, decisions, current best During a long cycle

docs.title: What goes into AGENTS.md
docs.text:
Appropriate content:

  • setup commands;
  • build/test/lint commands;
  • code style;
  • security constraints;
  • architecture map;
  • PR/release rules;
  • rules that every agent run must know.

Not appropriate:

  • rare long reference material;
  • transient work details;
  • raw logs;
  • secrets;
  • policy that belongs in sandbox/approval config.

docs.title: Nested AGENTS.md
docs.text: For a monorepo, use the root AGENTS.md for shared rules and nested files for individual packages or services. The nearest instructions should clarify the root policy, not duplicate it.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Project rules, requirements, plan, tests, evals and run history.
  • Current owner decisions, approvals and accepted gaps.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Durable files that keep the work resumable, reviewable and evidence-backed.
  • Clear separation between project rules, transient run history and verification records.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Check that control-plane files match the current slice before claiming readiness or closure.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Storing transient logs or secrets in durable files can leak private data.
  • Letting memory replace checked-in rules can make future runs inconsistent.

docs.title: Product lifecycle
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: How OpenAI uses Codex, Codex best practices, Iterate on difficult problems, Codex workflows.

docs.title: End-to-end loop
docs.text: Stage Agent work Artifact Gate Idea Clarify user value, hypothesis, metric and constraints REQUIREMENTS.md Scope and success metric are explicit Spec Turn the idea into behavior and acceptance criteria REQUIREMENTS.md User intent and source-of-truth docs are locked Plan Decompose work, architecture boundary and ownership PLAN.md Work items are independent enough Build Implement one focused slice at a time Diff Test-first or eval-first path exists Eval Score deterministic, subjective and AI quality TEST.md, EVALS.md, reports Threshold met or gap accepted Review Find bugs, security risks and test gaps Review findings No unresolved blocker PR Prepare branch, PR body, docs impact and release notes PR / changelog Verification evidence included Learn Capture the reusable method AGENTS.md, skill, insight Next run improves

docs.title: Ask Mode before Code Mode
docs.text:
OpenAI Codex guidance recommends starting large changes with a plan before implementation. In this project, that means:

First produce PLAN.md from REQUIREMENTS.md.
Do not edit product code until the plan names:
- files or subsystems;
- acceptance criteria;
- verification commands;
- risks and rollback;
- what is out of scope.

docs.title: Start brief hook guard
docs.text:
For Product-Agent OS non-mechanical work, the start brief is now backed by a staged hook mechanism:

  • the lifecycle contract lives in .codex/config.toml and .codex/workflows/task-plan-lifecycle.md;
  • packaged hook templates live in plugins/product-agent-os/assets/templates/hooks/;
  • the PreToolUse hook blocks mutating or non-read-only commands when .codex/product-agent-os/lifecycle-state.json has not been created after the user-visible start brief;
  • the Stop hook reminds the agent to show a completion brief and run control-plane sync when scope, plan, tests, evals, runlog, or evidence state changed.

This is a guardrail, not proof by itself. Completion and readiness claims still require current command, runtime, or eval evidence, or an explicit accepted gap.

docs.title: Work granularity
docs.text: Good Codex work is scoped enough that a human could complete it in a focused block. If one request spans product, design, backend, frontend, tests, docs and release, split it into lifecycle stages and use control-plane files as the handoff.

docs.title: Learning loop
docs.text:
Every finished product-agent workflow should answer:

  • Which instructions should move into AGENTS.md?
  • Which repeated steps deserve a skill?
  • Which check should become an automation?
  • Which failure needs an eval?
  • Which source or architecture decision should be documented?
  • Which metric or user feedback should drive the next product iteration?

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Product goal, requirements, source context and project constraints.
  • Existing control-plane files and verification commands.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• A staged lifecycle path from idea to review, release packet and learning.
  • Updated durable rules, skills or evals when the evidence justifies promotion.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Moving to build before plan and ownership can create broad, unverifiable changes.
  • Capturing learning without source evidence can turn stale memory into policy.

docs.title: Product-Agent Workflows
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: How OpenAI uses Codex, Codex best practices, A practical guide to building agents, Agent Skills, AGENTS.md.

docs.title: What this layer adds
docs.text:
Earlier sections explain Codex, prompts, context, memory and agents. Product-Agent Workflows connect them into an operating system for product development:

  • AGENTS.md stores durable repository rules;
  • control-plane files record requirements, plan, checks and run log;
  • skills turn repeated methods into reusable workflows;
  • subagents and Agents SDK help split bounded work;
  • eval loops and PR checks prove quality;
  • runtime tools run the workflow in Codex App, CLI, cloud, GitHub or automation.

docs.title: Main idea
docs.text:
A real product should not be built through one long prompt. Treat it as a controlled delivery loop:

flowchart LR
    I["Idea"] --> S["Spec"]
    S --> P["Plan"]
    P --> B["Build"]
    B --> T["Tests and evals"]
    T --> R["Review"]
    R --> PR["PR"]
    PR --> REL["Release notes"]
    REL --> L["Lessons to AGENTS.md / skills"]

docs.title: When Codex is enough, and when agents and skills are needed
docs.text: Situation Sufficient level One-off edit with a clear diff Codex App / CLI Repeated procedure Skill Background recurring check Automation Complex feature with several roles Product-Agent Workflow Programmable orchestration Agents SDK + Codex MCP Product improvement loop Evals + RUNLOG + artifact inspection

docs.title: Product-Agent OS plugin
docs.text: To package this operating model as a portable Codex plugin, use Product-Agent OS plugin. That section describes the plugin purpose, current capabilities, installation boundary, Codex-only runtime runner, guardrails and diagram-level operating principles.

docs.title: Definition of ready
docs.text:
Before starting a product-agent workflow, the project should have:

  • a clear goal and non-goals;
  • selected runtime: Codex App, CLI, cloud, codex exec, MCP or GitHub Action;
  • control-plane files;
  • test/eval commands;
  • ownership for files or subsystems;
  • policy for sandbox, approvals, secrets and network;
  • a stop condition.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Product intent, constraints, source docs and current project rules.
  • A chosen Codex runtime surface and approval policy.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• A controlled delivery loop from idea to reviewable product artifact.
  • Candidate skills, evals or automation only after manual success evidence exists.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Use control-plane files, current checks, evals and review findings before claiming readiness.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• One long prompt can hide missing requirements, approvals and verification evidence.
  • Automation before manual stability can repeat failures at scale.

docs.title: Specification: Product-Agent OS plugin
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: Codex plugins, Build plugins, Agent Skills, Subagents, Codex MCP, Codex hooks, AGENTS.md, Codex with Agents SDK, Product-Agent Workflows, Product-Agent OS.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Product-Agent OS is a portable Codex plugin that packages a product delivery operating model: control-plane artifacts, lifecycle skills, staged infrastructure templates, methodology routing, evals and compatibility checks. It helps a Codex worker move from user intent to verifiable product output without hiding approvals, live actions or source boundaries.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text: The plugin does not publish itself, install dependencies, start live servers, activate hooks, create schedules, call providers, mutate production data, change hosted docs, stage/commit/push/open PRs or certify legal/security/compliance readiness. Those actions require explicit owner approval and current evidence.

docs.title: Target users
docs.text:
• Product engineers using Codex App, CLI or IDE extension for real projects.
  • Teams that need repeatable product-agent workflows and handoff artifacts.
  • Docs and release maintainers who need source-backed claims and verification evidence.
  • Operators who want staged proposals before enabling live systems or automations.

docs.title: Supported surfaces
docs.text: Surface Use Codex App Ambiguity resolution, steering, review and local workspace work. CLI Deterministic checks, renderers, validators and staged artifact generation. IDE extension Navigation, implementation support and review context. skills Repeatable methods with inputs, outputs, verification and failure modes. subagents Specialized or parallel work when ownership is clear. MCP Declared integration context with approval boundaries. Agents SDK Optional product/runtime architecture when explicitly selected.

docs.title: Plugin package
docs.text:
The plugin package should include:

  • .codex-plugin/plugin.json;
  • lifecycle skills;
  • artifact templates;
  • staged infrastructure renderer;
  • eval fixtures and transcript sessions;
  • validation scripts;
  • documentation and source-boundary notes;
  • compatibility checks for Codex surfaces.

The manifest describes capabilities. It is not publication approval, external-system access or proof that runtime actions are safe.

docs.title: Lifecycle state machine
docs.text:
Product-Agent OS follows a conservative lifecycle:

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Intake
    Intake --> Requirements
    Requirements --> Plan
    Plan --> Build
    Build --> Verify
    Verify --> Review
    Review --> ReleaseReadiness
    ReleaseReadiness --> Learn
    Learn --> [*]
    Verify --> Gap
    Review --> Gap
    Gap --> Requirements

Each transition needs source context, expected evidence, approval boundary, stop condition and either current verification or an accepted gap.

docs.title: Complexity profiles
docs.text: Profile Use when Expected path Lightweight Mechanical, docs-only or low-risk work. Focused edit, source labels, docs check or explicit inspection-only gap. Standard Bounded feature or review with known ownership. Requirements, plan, implementation, focused verification and handoff. High-risk Public contracts, data, security, release, AI behavior, migrations or production systems. Domain packet, owner review, stronger verification, rollback and approval gates. Cross-domain Several domains overlap or recommendations conflict. Methodology synthesis, owner/consumer domains and risk-ordered safe next action.

docs.title: Initialization behavior
docs.text: Initialization should inspect the workspace read-only, discover existing control-plane files and source constraints, then stage missing artifacts only when requested or approved. It must preserve user-authored files and avoid broad scaffolding before the route is accepted.

docs.title: Usage-mode implementation status
docs.text: The plugin supports route decisions for first-run intake, bug rescue, greenfield idea, complex system acceleration, PR review, legacy onboarding, API migration, AI/RAG eval regression, native/mobile work, desktop local-first work, data migration, security-sensitive change, CI stabilization, release packaging, docs-only work, standard feature work and maintenance.

docs.title: Generated project files
docs.text: Generated files are proposals or managed artifacts. Typical outputs include REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md, ADRs, architecture overview, component cards, API contract reviews, database dictionaries, release readiness notes, operations runbooks, eval reports and approval records.

docs.title: System file update policy
docs.text: AGENTS.md, .codex/config.toml, hooks, workflows and automation files are sensitive. Existing unmarked files are user-authored content. The plugin should stage companion proposals unless a managed section and approved merge path exist.

docs.title: Context and information overflow policy
docs.text: Context should be source-backed and bounded. Use summaries, route packets and handoffs instead of dumping entire histories. Memory and chat recall are useful context, not source of truth. Raw private chats, secrets, credentials and customer data must not be stored in prompts, docs, fixtures or templates.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text:
Skills should each do one job. A Product-Agent OS skill needs:

  • trigger;
  • inputs;
  • outputs;
  • source constraints;
  • approval boundary;
  • verification commands;
  • failure modes;
  • stop conditions.

Skills may recommend or stage actions. They cannot grant external permission or override stronger instructions.

docs.title: Agent team
docs.text:
Agent teams are designed around ownership, handoff artifacts, verification and stop conditions. Roles such as Product Manager, Architect, Builder, Tester, Reviewer, Docs Maintainer and Release Operator are useful only when their file/subsystem boundaries and expected evidence are explicit.

Subagents are appropriate when work is independent. Parallel work without ownership split increases risk and should fall back to sequential execution.

docs.title: Handoff contracts
docs.text:
Every handoff should include:

  • sources/context used;
  • assumptions;
  • files touched or proposed;
  • ownership and forbidden files;
  • verification evidence;
  • open risks;
  • recommended next role or stop reason.

Fresh-context handoffs are required when a new worker or subagent starts from a packet rather than the full thread.

docs.title: Safety and approvals
docs.text:
The approval boundary is strict:

  • external writes require approval;
  • live provider/model/API calls require approval;
  • browser automation and local runtime launch require approval when the current route forbids them;
  • hosted docs, production DB/data access and security-system mutations require approval;
  • hooks and automations are staged/inactive until approved;
  • git staging, commit, push and PR creation remain explicit actions.

Approvals are specific. Approval for one surface does not grant another.

docs.title: Hooks and rules
docs.text: Packaged hooks are examples or staged target-project assets. The plugin must not activate hooks at plugin root or in a target project without explicit approval. Durable rules belong in AGENTS.md; transient run details belong in RUNLOG.md.

docs.title: Runtime selection
docs.text:
Choose runtime by the job:

  • Codex App or IDE extension for ambiguous work, steering and review;
  • CLI for local deterministic checks and renderers;
  • codex exec for stable non-interactive jobs;
  • GitHub Action for PR/CI workflows when approved;
  • MCP or Agents SDK for programmable orchestration when the contract is clear;
  • automation only after a stable manual workflow or skill exists.

docs.title: Context7 and source policy
docs.text: Official OpenAI and Codex documentation are the source of truth for OpenAI behavior. Project-authored behavior can cite repository artifacts, tests and source packets. Community claims must stay under docs/insights/ with trust and verification labels until verified.

docs.title: Evals and verification
docs.text:
The plugin should keep deterministic verification close to the behavior being changed:

python tools\check_docs.py
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\validate_codex_compatibility.py

Use the full unit suite when scripts, templates, fixtures or lifecycle behavior change:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v

Use transcript evals for multi-turn shortcut resistance and privacy/no-secrets checks.

docs.title: Automation promotion
docs.text: Promotion order is manual workflow, playbook, skill, plugin, automation. Automation candidates need manual success evidence, stable inputs/outputs, owner, cadence, verification, failure modes, value evidence and rollback/disable path. Product-Agent OS can stage an automation candidate; it must not create active automation without explicit approval.

docs.title: Optional Agents SDK runner
docs.text: Agents SDK can be used for a product/runtime app architecture when explicitly selected. It is not the hidden runtime layer for the plugin and should not bypass Codex sandbox, approvals, source policy or package compatibility boundaries.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text:
• Generated dashboards or graph views are treated as source of truth.
  • A skill expands work instead of preserving the route boundary.
  • Subagents receive incomplete context or overlapping ownership.
  • Compatibility checks are interpreted as live readiness.
  • Automation is created before manual stability evidence exists.
  • A source-backed claim is added without Source status: and registry support.
  • A live or external action is bundled into unrelated approval.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
Product-Agent OS is acceptable when:

  • package metadata is valid for Codex;
  • skills have clear triggers, inputs, outputs, verification and failure modes;
  • generated infrastructure is staged-first;
  • control-plane files preserve source boundaries and evidence;
  • evals catch shortcut behavior and false-positive routing;
  • docs include Source status:;
  • compatibility checks do not require provider calls or hidden external runtimes;
  • approval-bound actions stay disabled until explicitly approved.

docs.title: Product capability areas
docs.text:
The product capability areas are:

  • lifecycle routing and control-plane artifacts;
  • staged infrastructure and safe merge planning;
  • methodology intelligence and engineering standards;
  • behavioral and transcript evals;
  • Codex compatibility checks;
  • graph/cockpit orientation;
  • release, packaging and closure evidence;
  • approval-bound real testing;
  • skill, plugin and automation promotion.

Next artifact: use Product-Agent OS architecture for the system model and Technical features and installation for operator commands.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Codex plugin package metadata, skills, templates, eval fixtures and docs.
  • Owner approval records and current verification evidence for risky surfaces.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• A portable Product-Agent OS plugin contract with lifecycle routing, staged artifacts and compatibility checks.
  • Reviewable boundaries for skills, subagents, MCP, hooks, automation and optional Agents SDK use.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Validate plugin metadata, docs structure, fixture evals and Codex compatibility before release claims.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Compatibility checks are not publication approval.
  • Bundling live actions into the plugin contract can bypass the explicit approval model.

docs.title: Agent team roles
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: A practical guide to building agents, Codex with Agents SDK, Subagents, Codex models, Agents SDK models and providers, Reasoning best practices, Build AI-native engineering teams.

docs.title: Role map
docs.text: Role Primary input Output Does not do Product Manager User request, business goal REQUIREMENTS.md, acceptance criteria Does not write production code Architect Requirements, codebase map PLAN.md, component boundaries Does not expand scope Builder Plan, ownership Code diff, tests Does not edit another worker's write scope Tester Requirements, diff, test plan Test gaps, failing cases, eval report Does not accept unverified claims Reviewer Diff, risk model Findings ordered by severity Does not rewrite without request Docs Maintainer Diff, sources, decisions Docs, release notes Does not mix official and community claims Release Operator Verification, PR body PR, changelog, rollout notes Does not skip failing checks

docs.title: Model and reasoning profile
docs.text:
Every role needs an execution profile. This is especially important for programmable Agents SDK workflows and Codex custom agents, where the model and reasoning effort can be set explicitly.

Role Model policy Reasoning effort Escalation rule Product Manager gpt-5.5 or project default medium / high Raise to high when requirements conflict or a tradeoff must be chosen Architect gpt-5.5 high / xhigh Use xhigh for multi-system architecture, migrations or deep debugging Builder project default; gpt-5.4-mini for small scoped edits medium / high Use high when shared contracts or several modules change Explorer gpt-5.4-mini or project default low / medium Use medium when discovered dependencies must be synthesized Tester project default medium Use high when failure is non-deterministic or eval-driven Reviewer gpt-5.5 high Use xhigh when review touches security, data loss, concurrency or auth Docs Maintainer project default low / medium Use medium when several official sources must be checked Release Operator project default medium Use high when rollout is irreversible or approvals are ambiguous

Minimal role card:

role: "Architect"
owns: "Architecture, decomposition, risk analysis"
model_policy:
  model: "gpt-5.5"
  reasoning_effort: "high"
  cost_latency_budget: "quality-first"
  inherit_from_parent_when_unspecified: true
  override_allowed_by:
    - "run-level workflow config"
    - "human approval"
  escalation_rules:
    - "Use xhigh for multi-system migration or ambiguous architecture."
    - "Use medium for bounded implementation planning."
handoff:
  inputs: "REQUIREMENTS.md, codebase map, constraints"
  outputs: "PLAN.md, risks, open questions, verification strategy"

The project default should live in PLAN.md or a project-scoped agent config. Durable rules for when to raise reasoning effort can live in AGENTS.md; one-off runtime overrides are better recorded in RUNLOG.md.

docs.title: Manager pattern
docs.text:
For product delivery, the default is the Manager pattern:

  • Manager keeps the goal, scope and gates.
  • Specialist agents perform bounded work.
  • Verifier/Reviewer checks the result.
  • Manager publishes the result and decides what should move into docs or skills.
flowchart TD
    M["Manager"] --> PM["Product spec"]
    M --> A["Architecture plan"]
    M --> B["Builder"]
    M --> T["Tester"]
    M --> R["Reviewer"]
    M --> D["Docs maintainer"]
    PM --> M
    A --> M
    B --> M
    T --> M
    R --> M
    D --> M

docs.title: Handoff rule
docs.text:
Every role must return more than output. The handoff must include:

  • sources used;
  • assumptions;
  • files touched or proposed;
  • verification evidence;
  • open risks;
  • recommended next role.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Requirements, plan, source context and ownership constraints.
  • Model and reasoning policy for the role and risk level.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Role cards, handoff packets, verification evidence and stop conditions.
  • A clear escalation path when ambiguity, security or release risk increases.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Vague titles without file ownership create overlap and hidden gaps.
  • Overusing high reasoning or large agent teams can add latency without improving evidence.

docs.title: Agent/skill modernization loop
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This page describes agent_skill_metrics_loop for Product-Agent OS: a local read-only evaluation loop for agents, subagents, skills, prompt/policy packs, router/tool policies, memory policies, dataset/grader surfaces and harness versions after real work has produced verifiable evidence records.

The loop is not autonomous auto-update. Its purpose is to collect source-backed evidence, show scorecards, identify modernization candidates and prepare daily/weekly candidate packets for owner review. This is a staged candidate-only pipeline with no self-applied updates, active schedules or live eval/model/API calls.

docs.title: Source-of-truth boundary
docs.text:
Source of truth for metrics:

  • control-plane artifacts: AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md;
  • run records, trace packets and eval packets;
  • accepted gaps with owner, review date and residual risk;
  • staged scorecard ledger records when they cite explicit run/eval/trace evidence.

Not source of truth:

  • generated dashboard/report HTML;
  • memory and raw chat logs;
  • unsupported community claims;
  • one noisy daily report;
  • modernization candidate without rollback target, owner review and approval state.

Any generated report is a review view. It does not prove that the project is ready, a skill is high quality or an update can be applied.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Minimum input packet:

  • target registry: agents, skills, prompt/policy packs, router/tool policies, automation candidates, config and harness targets;
  • trace intake: agents_sdk, opentelemetry_genai, tool_report or accepted_gap trace sources with model/tool/handoff/final_response spans;
  • evidence dataset: implemented work items, real trace samples, prior failures, critical slices, edge/adversarial cases, holdout cases, synthetic regression cases and known flaky cases;
  • grader/judge calibration: human labels, judge labels, thresholds for precision, recall, Cohen kappa and sample size;
  • version context: baseline, current and candidate versions;
  • cost/latency/safety/reliability records when the target can affect production, external systems or user-visible quality.

Raw prompts, raw tool outputs, secrets, private customer data and unredacted PII are not valid inputs.

docs.title: Outputs And Artifacts
docs.text:
The loop stages review artifacts only:

  • target registry packet from collect_target_registry;
  • trace packet from build_trace_packet;
  • evidence dataset and quality packet from build_evidence_dataset and evaluate_dataset_quality;
  • judge calibration summary from build_judge_calibration_summary;
  • metric aggregation and scorecards from build_metric_aggregation and calculate_scorecards;
  • cadence recommendation packet with L0, L1, L2 or L3;
  • append-only scorecard ledger record via agent-skill-scorecard-ledger.md;
  • offline reports, including agent-skill-evaluation-report.html rendered by render_agent_skill_metrics_report.py;
  • daily candidate packet via agent-skill-daily-eval-report.md;
  • weekly verification packet via agent-skill-weekly-verification.md;
  • modernization proposal via agent-skill-update-candidate.md.

Modernization candidates may target skill text, agent instructions, prompt/policy packs, router/tool policies, memory policy, dataset, grader or harness configuration. They cannot apply patches by themselves.

docs.title: Workflow And Cadence
docs.text:
1. Inventory targets with read-only local inspection.
  2. Build trace and evidence packets from current control-plane, run/eval artifacts and accepted gaps.
  3. Run redaction and dataset quality checks before scoring.
  4. Calibrate grader/judge output against human labels. If calibration is missing or below threshold, judge-derived metrics stay reportable_gap_only.
  5. Calculate scorecards and guardrail blockers. Headline score improvement cannot override safety, false-pass, flake, trace completeness, cost or owner-review blockers.
  6. Recommend cadence:
  7. L0: on-change or low-risk review;
  8. L1: periodic review for medium risk or mild flake/trace gaps;
  9. L2: elevated review for high risk, high usage or approval-bound/write tools;
  10. L3: production/reliability risk, automation candidates or major trace/flake issues.
  11. Emit daily packet for triage: no-op, investigate, block promotion, stage candidate for review or request human audit.
  12. Emit weekly verification only when rollback target, owner review, holdout check, false-pass audit, flake replay and cost regression check are present or explicitly accepted as gaps.

Cadence is a recommendation, not an active schedule. The loop must not create Codex App automations, GitHub Actions, recurring jobs or external workflows.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Expected verification evidence:

  • dataset quality status is ready, or blockers are recorded as accepted gaps;
  • duplicate rate, leakage status, missing splits and real trace coverage are visible;
  • judge calibration is calibrated before judge-derived metrics support candidate approval;
  • scorecards include guardrail blockers and denominator/numerator evidence;
  • daily/weekly packets cite evidence windows and current versions;
  • each update candidate has owner, affected targets, metric deltas, expected impact, risk, approval state and rollback target;
  • report rendering is dry-run or stage-only, with no write into the target workspace unless a later approved merge path exists.

Read-only smoke command for the report plan:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\render_agent_skill_metrics_report.py <workspace> --dry-run

Stage-only report rendering must use an output directory outside the target workspace:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\render_agent_skill_metrics_report.py <workspace> --stage C:\tmp\product-agent-os-metrics-stage

docs.title: Risks And Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Treating a report as proof of quality creates false readiness.
  • Low sample size, duplicate cases, holdout leakage or missing real traces can make scorecards misleading.
  • Uncalibrated LLM-as-judge output can produce false passes or false regressions.
  • A daily noisy run can trigger unnecessary changes if it is mistaken for weekly acceptance evidence.
  • Modernization candidates can become unsafe if they lack rollback target, owner review or cost/safety regression checks.
  • Running live eval/model/API calls would violate the read-only modernization boundary unless a later explicit approval packet changes scope.
  • Auto-applying candidate updates would turn the loop into autonomous auto-update, which is explicitly out of scope.

docs.title: Self-Learning Loop Docs Contracts And Closure
docs.text:
self_learning_docs_contracts_closure_v1 defines documentation and promotion-gate contracts for the Self-Learning Loop.

Current status:

  • Local/schema/fixture evidence exists for scope, state, manual progress, feedback, metrics and candidate-only safety.
  • The docs closure documents state, feedback, metrics, privacy, trigger and candidate boundaries.
  • Automation promotion remains candidate_only.
  • Candidate packet: .codex/automation-candidates/self-learning-automation-candidate.md.
  • minimum_manual_successful_runs: 3.
  • Owner approval record, rollback/disable path, false-positive audit, flake replay and cost check are required before activation.

This closure does not import a real Codex App session export, does not use hidden telemetry, does not store raw transcripts, does not call providers or live eval services, does not mutate target workspaces, does not auto-apply candidates and creates no active scheduler.

docs.title: Next Action
docs.text: Use this page when agent/skill evidence needs to be interpreted or packaged for owner review. The next safe artifact is a staged scorecard ledger, daily report, weekly verification packet or update candidate. Applying any update remains a separate owner-approved implementation slice.

docs.title: Approval-bound real testing
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This page describes the approval-bound real-testing execution matrix for Product-Agent OS. The matrix is not a bundled approval: each live/runtime/browser/provider/canonical/git action remains separately scoped, separately approved and separately evidenced.

Real testing starts only after current closure evidence exists for governance, runtime contract, audit/observability, target consent, QA/performance/stabilization and packaging/docs closure.

Current source-backed status: M37-M41 have execution evidence or owner closure: M37-M40 passed for approved local runtime, browser smoke, Codex-session provider pilot and staged canonical mutation pilot. M41 is closed as owner_closed_no_op_git_release_pr, and no git stage/commit/push/PR has been performed.

docs.title: Approvals And Source-Of-Truth Boundary
docs.text:
Each real-testing action has a separate approval packet. Approval for a live server pilot does not allow browser automation. Approval for browser automation does not allow provider/API calls. Approval for a provider/API pilot does not allow canonical mutation. Approval for canonical mutation does not allow git release/PR action.

Source of truth:

  • checked-in source docs and control-plane artifacts;
  • owner approval packet for the exact action;
  • generated evidence files only as staged evidence;
  • audit/security/observability packets that cite source evidence.

Not source of truth:

  • generated HTML/dashboard/cockpit views;
  • provider output without human review;
  • LLM proposals without accepted ledger item;
  • screenshots or smoke output without source-boundary context;
  • memory, chat recall or unstaged local cache.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Before any real-testing action, collect:

  • current governance and runtime evidence summary;
  • owner-approved target workspace class and data policy;
  • allowed commands and explicitly blocked commands;
  • data classification and redaction policy;
  • credential boundary and provider budget when providers are involved;
  • rollback path and cleanup/deletion proof;
  • audit event schema and evidence destination;
  • accepted gaps with owner, reason, review date, residual risk and follow-up condition.

Inputs must be sanitized. Do not place secrets, tokens, credentials, private keys, raw source bodies, private customer data or unredacted PII into approval packets, prompts, logs, screenshots, fixtures or generated evidence.

docs.title: Outputs And Artifacts
docs.text:
Action artifacts and current evidence:

Action Evidence artifact Current status approved_local_runtime_launch live-server-run-evidence.json Passed in M37; short-lived local server bound to 127.0.0.1, health/query/auth/public-bind/write-block checks, server_shutdown_complete: true and redaction.ok: true. actual_browser_automation_smoke browser-automation-smoke.json, desktop.png, mobile.png Passed in M38; Playwright Chromium, console_errors: 0, network_failures: 0, mobile_overflow: false, generated-view labels, source-boundary labels and clean shutdown. approved_provider_api_pilot provider-call-evidence.json, provider-eval-report.json Passed in M39; provider surface codex_user_session, OPENAI_API_KEY used: false, direct API call from workspace shell: false and provider_secret_stored: false. approved_canonical_mutation_pilot canonical-mutation-run.json, graph-mutation-journal.jsonl, rollback-proof.json Passed in M40 as stage_root_only; canonical_graph_source_mutated: false, operation_count: 1, journal_entry_count: 1 and rollback_restores_previous_graph_digest: true. explicit_git_release_pr_action git-release-pr-evidence.md, PR packet Closed in M41 by owner decision as owner_closed_no_op_git_release_pr; no git stage/commit/push/PR.

These artifacts are evidence only for the exact approved action that actually ran. They do not approve any other action, and generated evidence remains staged/source-boundary evidence until checked-in source docs or owner-reviewed packets cite it.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Freeze current closure state and confirm no hidden unresolved live-runtime gates.
  2. Select exactly one real-testing action to request approval for.
  3. Write an approval packet with owner, target, allowed commands, data policy, source boundary, rollback, budget, audit destination and stop conditions.
  4. If approval is missing or incomplete, stop at approval_required.
  5. If approved, run only the named action and collect only its evidence.
  6. Validate cleanup, fallback and audit records.
  7. Record result as passed, blocked, disabled, rollback-complete or owner-accepted gap.
  8. Reassess before requesting approval for the next action.

docs.title: Action Matrix
docs.text: Action Planned purpose Separate approval must name Hard boundary approved_local_runtime_launch Start the disabled-by-default local read-only runtime on an approved target. target, bind/auth/port policy, PID/log path, health check, shutdown evidence, fallback. No launch without owner approval; local-only; no write endpoints; no provider calls. actual_browser_automation_smoke Replace staged browser QA assumptions with real browser evidence. runtime URL, browser tool, viewports, allowed network, screenshots, console/network capture. No browser automation without approval; no unapproved external requests; labels and no mobile overflow must be checked. approved_provider_api_pilot Measure approved embedding/reranker/LLM provider behavior under real gates. provider, model, credential env var, redaction, cache, budget, eval threshold, audit path. external_call_performed may become true only inside this packet; no secrets/raw source/absolute paths. approved_canonical_mutation_pilot Apply and rollback an owner-accepted graph change. accepted ledger item, dry-run plan, conflict checks, journal path, digest comparison, rollback proof. No mutation without accepted item and dry-run; accepted_gap remains non-mutating. explicit_git_release_pr_action Publish only the verified owner-approved change set. exact files, verification summary, unrelated-change check, commit/push/PR intent. No git add, git commit, git push or PR without explicit user command.

docs.title: Current Execution Status
docs.text: Step Action Status Evidence boundary M37 approved_local_runtime_launch passed Local-only runtime evidence; no browser automation, provider/API call, canonical graph mutation or git action from this approval. M38 actual_browser_automation_smoke passed Browser evidence only; no provider/API call, canonical graph mutation or git action from this approval. M39 approved_provider_api_pilot passed Codex-session provider pilot evidence only; no canonical graph mutation or git action from this approval. M40 approved_canonical_mutation_pilot passed Staged canonical mutation/rollback proof only; canonical_graph_source_mutated: false and no git action. M41 explicit_git_release_pr_action owner_closed_no_op_git_release_pr Git release/PR did not run; future git write requires fresh preflight, release branch or push target, commit message, PR base branch, PR title/intent and explicit branch/write policy.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
For approval-bound real testing, a completion claim is valid only for the exact approved action and only after current-run evidence exists.

Expected checks:

  • local runtime pilot: health, local-only bind, auth rejection where applicable, no write endpoints, clean shutdown, graph-only fallback;
  • browser smoke: console errors, network requests, mobile overflow, generated-view labels, source-boundary labels, screenshots;
  • provider/API pilot: redaction pass, no secrets/raw source/absolute paths, cache metadata, budget usage, eval threshold, fallback on failure, audit event;
  • canonical mutation pilot: accepted ledger item, dry-run plan, previous/new digest, append-only journal, rollback proof;
  • git action: current diff hygiene, explicit requested files, verification summary and no unrelated staging.

A docs-only update cannot create new passed evidence. It can only cite current-run evidence from the source packet and must keep new live/browser/provider/canonical/git actions approval-bound.

docs.title: Risks And Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Treating all real testing as complete because M37-M40 passed; M41 and any new live/browser/provider/canonical/git action remain separate approvals.
  • Treating the matrix as implemented because it exists.
  • Reusing approval from one action to authorize another action.
  • Starting a local runtime before target/data policy and shutdown evidence are explicit.
  • Running browser automation that makes unapproved external requests.
  • Performing provider calls without redaction, cache, budget, threshold and audit evidence.
  • Accepting provider or LLM output as canonical fact without human review ledger.
  • Applying canonical mutation without rollback proof.
  • Running git stage/commit/push/PR as part of testing instead of as a separately requested release action.

docs.title: Next Action
docs.text: The next safe step is either documentation/source closure for the current real-testing evidence, or owner-provided M41 git release fields. Until those fields are supplied, git release/PR stays blocked. Any new live server, browser automation, provider/API, canonical mutation or git action still needs its own narrow approval packet.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS architecture
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

Sources: Codex plugins, Build plugins, Agent Skills, Subagents, AGENTS.md, Codex hooks, Codex MCP, Codex workflows, Codex with Agents SDK.

Product-Agent OS packages a product-delivery operating model for Codex. It combines durable project rules, lifecycle skills, staged artifacts, evals and approval boundaries while keeping live systems disabled until the owner explicitly approves a specific action.

docs.title: Layered Model
docs.text: Layer Responsibility Boundary Codex surface Codex App, CLI, IDE extension and MCP declarations. Runs under sandbox and approvals. Plugin package Manifest, skills, templates, scripts, examples and compatibility checks. Package presence is not activation or publication. Control plane AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md. Source-backed decisions, not generated-site output. Methodology layer Read-only routing, domain gates and false-positive control. Recommends and stages; it does not mutate targets. Verification layer Unit tests, fixture evals, transcript evals, docs checks and compatibility checks. Claims require current evidence or accepted gaps. Live layer Runtime, browser, providers, graph mutation and git/release actions. Disabled until a specific approval packet exists.

docs.title: Operating Flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    U["User intent"] --> A["Read-only workspace audit"]
    A --> R["Route and methodology packet"]
    R --> Q{"Evidence sufficient?"}
    Q -->|No| O["Owner question or accepted gap"]
    Q -->|Yes| P["Plan or focused slice"]
    P --> B["Build / docs / review work"]
    B --> V["Verification evidence"]
    V --> H["Handoff packet"]
    H --> L{"Live action needed?"}
    L -->|No| D["Done or next artifact"]
    L -->|Yes| X["Specific approval boundary"]

docs.title: Graph And Live Boundary
docs.text: Generated project graphs, cockpit views, runtime summaries and analysis reports are orientation evidence. They help a worker find source files, stale assumptions and review targets, but they are not sources of truth. Any live runtime launch, browser automation, provider call, canonical graph mutation or git/release action needs a separate approval packet, current evidence and rollback or stop condition.

docs.title: Completion-skeptic Route
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    W["worker_output"] --> P["doubt_verification_packet"]
    P --> C["completion-skeptic"]
    C --> V{"verdict"}
    V -->|pass| A["final answer with evidence"]
    V -->|revise| R["reviser changes only confirmed gaps"]
    V -->|needs_more_context| Q["ask or record missing_context"]
    V -->|blocked_by_approval| B["stop at approval boundary"]
    V -->|accepted_risk| G["accepted_gap with owner and follow-up"]

The packet has a claim ledger, requirement ledger and evidence ledger. The claim ledger records supported, unsupported, contradicted and needs_fresh_check items. The requirement ledger keeps user requirements, non-goals and approval constraints visible. The evidence ledger records source registry, local files, current commands, evals, owner decisions or explicit missing checks.

Completion-skeptic route is a manual/local Product-Agent OS gate, not a live runtime proof.

The reviser changes only confirmed gaps. If the verifier finds only speculative concerns, the route returns residual risk instead of rewriting correct content.

docs.title: Agents SDK Output Guardrail Candidate
docs.text: This is a design-only direction. The same packet can later become an Agents SDK output guardrail candidate with a tripwire for fake evidence, pass without evidence, approval-blocked pass, missing source status or unsafe private data. The current boundary: docs/site work does not create an Agents SDK runner, MCP server, tracing export, provider call or live guardrail.

docs.title: Engineering Standards Route
docs.text: The engineering standards route maps workspace evidence to product, architecture, frontend, backend, API, data, AI/RAG, security, release and cross-domain gates. Detection creates present_unverified; readiness requires command evidence, runtime/eval proof, owner-reviewed evidence or an accepted gap.

docs.title: Lifecycle Routing
docs.text:
Lifecycle routing chooses the smallest useful next move:

  • answer directly when the request is bounded and source-backed;
  • stage a proposal when writing into a target workspace would be premature;
  • request approval when an external or live action is required;
  • run focused verification when evidence is available locally;
  • stop on a gap when source evidence is missing.

Routes must include source context, assumptions, files owned, expected evidence, approval boundary and stop condition before delegating work to a skill or subagent.

docs.title: task and plan architecture
docs.text:
This architecture records how Product-Agent OS creates plan files, manages a task matrix, cleans accumulated history and returns a user-facing completion report after implementation. It applies when work includes development methodology, related work items, architecture decisions, agent roles, skills, subagents, approval boundaries or staged delivery.

flowchart TD
    A["User request or methodology-heavy work"] --> B["Read-only inventory and methodology audit"]
    B --> C{"task matrix trigger?"}
    C -->|No| D["Lightweight exception: reason, reduced evidence, residual risk"]
    C -->|Yes| E["implementation-planner creates plan-file proposal"]

    E --> F["task-matrix-plan.md template"]
    F --> G["Staged artifact in .codex/artifact-templates"]
    G --> H["Owner-approved concrete plan file"]

    H --> I["Validator: fields, status, timestamp, dependencies, evidence"]
    I --> J{"Valid?"}
    J -->|No| K["Repair plan before implementation"]
    J -->|Yes| L["Execute focused slice"]

    L --> M["Update row: status, files, checks, actual time"]
    M --> N["RUNLOG.md concise current-cycle evidence"]
    M --> O["agent-task-packet.md for subagent handoff"]
    M --> P["Docs, registry or backlog for source-backed claims"]
    M --> Q["Read-only status projection when useful"]

    P --> R["Package closure: accepted gaps, residual risks, next slice"]
    N --> R
    O --> R
    Q --> R

A plan file is created when work requires staged delivery, architecture capture, multiple roles, multiple verification gates, rollback, evals or a user-facing completion report. A small mechanical edit can use a lightweight exception, but the reason, reduced evidence and residual risk must be stated in the response or RUNLOG.md.

Plans are cleaned by moving detail to the correct owning artifact, not by losing useful history: current sequencing stays in PLAN.md or a batch-specific plan file, concise decisions and failures go to RUNLOG.md, source-backed history goes to docs/sources/registry.md or a backlog, and repeated workflows move through manual workflow, playbook, skill, plugin and automation candidate.

Element Controls Noise control task matrix Source, scope, non-goals, expected result, acceptance criteria, verification, risks, agents, skills and dependencies Each row bounds scope and owner Completion report What was done, files touched, technical value, product value, actual date and time Filled after implementation, not in advance RUNLOG.md Current-cycle decisions, latest evidence and failures Does not store the full historical ledger docs/sources/registry.md Source-backed claims and historical evidence pointers Does not accept unsupported claims Status projection Read-only operational status Does not replace the plan file, tests or source registry

task-matrix-plan.md is a staged planning artifact. Its presence can guide planning, handoffs and validation, but it is not source truth, execution evidence, verification evidence, dashboard readiness or release approval by itself.

The methodology connection stays practical: Scrum and Kanban provide sequencing and WIP discipline, ADR records architecture decisions and non-goals, test-driven development defines verification gates, docs-as-code requires output artifacts and registry updates, and eval-driven AI work adds baseline, rubric, threshold and residual quality risk.

docs.title: Route Packet
docs.text:
A route packet should include:

  • usage_mode.primary and optional secondary mode;
  • confidence and routing reasons;
  • source artifacts used;
  • minimum artifacts required for the next stage;
  • approval boundary;
  • verification gates;
  • residual risks and accepted gaps;
  • finish_options and safe_next_action.

docs.title: Methodology Intelligence
docs.text: Methodology intelligence is read-only. It inspects the workspace, control-plane files and route signals, then returns methodology applicability, packets, owner questions, synthesis and source-artifact mapping. It must avoid forced ceremony: simple work stays simple, while production, public-contract, release, security-sensitive and AI behavior changes require stronger evidence.

docs.title: Usage Mode Coverage
docs.text: Product-Agent OS covers first-run intake, bug rescue, greenfield idea shaping, complex system acceleration, PR review, legacy onboarding, API migration, AI/RAG eval regression, native/mobile work, desktop local-first work, data migration, security-sensitive change, CI stabilization, release packaging, docs-only work, standard feature work and maintenance.

docs.title: Staged-First Infrastructure
docs.text: Infrastructure generation is staged-first. Renderers may inspect a target workspace and write proposals into an explicit staging directory. They must preserve user-authored files, avoid direct target mutation unless a later approved merge path exists, and keep hooks and automations inactive by default.

docs.title: Codex Runtime Runner
docs.text: The Codex runtime runner is a package-level contract surface for Codex workflows. It can route lifecycle work, validate packets and produce staged artifacts without requiring a separate OpenAI API key. It does not hide a standalone Agents SDK runtime, start servers, call providers or mutate global config by itself.

docs.title: Automation Promotion
docs.text: Automation is the last step in the promotion chain: manual workflow, playbook, skill, plugin, then automation. A candidate needs stable inputs/outputs, owner, cadence, verification, failure modes, value evidence and rollback/disable path. Product-Agent OS can stage a candidate but must not create active automation without explicit approval.

docs.title: Common Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Treating generated graphs, dashboards or reports as source of truth.
  • Using subagents without file ownership, fresh context or stop conditions.
  • Converting a repeated workflow into automation before manual success evidence exists.
  • Claiming readiness from detection alone.
  • Combining approvals across unrelated live surfaces.
  • Letting package compatibility imply publication, deployment or external mutation.

Next artifact: use Scenarios to choose the route, Professional Code Authoring Standards for code-writing gates and Development standards to decide which evidence gates apply.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Current workspace context, control-plane files, source registry and approved route.
  • Agent ownership boundaries, staged artifacts and verification requirements.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS artifact contracts
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

This page lists the main generated Product-Agent OS artifacts for the modernization loop, project code graph, live/runtime governance and approval-bound handoff. It is not a JSON Schema spec; it is an operator-facing contract map: what gets created, why it exists, where the source-of-truth boundary sits and which approval gates apply.

docs.title: Contract Boundary
docs.text:
Generated artifacts are staged evidence only. They are not source of truth unless a later owner-approved process explicitly promotes a fact back into checked-in source documentation or another canonical artifact.

Source of truth remains:

  • project source files and checked-in contracts;
  • AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md;
  • source registry entries with current verification status;
  • command evidence from the current run;
  • owner decisions and accepted gaps with residual risk.

Artifacts must not contain secrets, credentials, raw private chat logs, private customer data, unredacted PII, raw source bodies where a redacted packet is required, or absolute local paths.
