docs.title: First-run analysis artifact
docs.text:
The first-run analysis artifact is a local generated orientation pack for first project review. It helps an operator see inventory, runtime route, control-plane state, graph summary, risks and a safe next action, but it remains orientation_only_not_proof.

This map describes artifact families and view-model contracts used by analysis_artifact_renderer.py and staged B41/B42 evidence. It is not a complete JSON Schema: the repository has contract fields, tests and staged examples, but no standalone exhaustive JSON Schema validation for every nested first-run surface.

Artifact / schema Producer Contract role Boundary .codex/product-agent-os/analysis/first-run-analysis-packet.json run_first_project_analysis.py --write, first_run_analysis.py First analysis packet: target, source artifacts, summaries, generated pages, evidence/redaction status and safe next action. Orientation evidence only; does not prove readiness, release, target mutation, runtime/browser/provider proof or source truth. .codex/product-agent-os/self-learning-state.json State initializer or future approved state writer; consumed read-only by check_self_learning_due.py --dry-run and run_self_learning_loop.py self_learning_state_v1: install timestamp, last analysis/success/failure, next due timestamp, cadence, report/metrics refs, approval state and disable reason. Due-check/manual-run state only; current CLIs do not write this file, create active schedules, ingest sessions, call providers, mutate targets or enable auto-apply. .codex/product-agent-os/self-learning/progress.jsonl run_self_learning_loop.py --stage <dir> Append-style self_learning_progress_v1 phase events for scope_check, due_check, evidence, metrics, feedback, candidates, reporting and owner review. Stage-only in B44-S2; no raw chat, hidden telemetry, absolute target paths or auto-approval controls. .codex/product-agent-os/self-learning/runs/<run_id>/progress.json run_self_learning_loop.py --stage <dir> Per-run progress snapshot with run ID, project scope hash, owner approval state, blockers and latest artifact paths. Generated inspection evidence only; it does not prove quality improvement, owner satisfaction or readiness. .codex/product-agent-os/self-learning/runs/<run_id>/self-learning-run-packet.json run_self_learning_loop.py --stage <dir> self_learning_run_packet_v1 with scope packet, due-check packet, evidence refs, unsupported claims, metrics placeholders and candidate summary. Manual-only/staged-only; provider calls, live eval services, target mutation and auto-apply remain not performed. .codex/product-agent-os/self-learning/self-learning-progress.html run_self_learning_loop.py --stage <dir> Offline generated progress view for scope eligibility, due status, phase progress, blockers and owner-review state. Generated review view only; not source of truth and cannot approve, apply or prove work complete. .codex/product-agent-os/self-learning-candidates.json self_learning_candidates.py / runner candidate_summary self_learning_candidate_packet_v1 and self_learning_forbidden_action_report_v1 for review-only modernization candidates and forbidden-action fixtures. Candidate-only; cannot apply changes to skills, prompts, routes, memory, config, hooks or automation. docs/superpowers/specs/batch44-self-learning-loop-docs-contracts-closure-summary.json Self-Learning Loop docs closure self_learning_docs_contracts_closure_v1 records docs sync, registry parity and promotion gate status. Closure evidence only; it does not prove activation, real session import, provider calls, target mutation or automation readiness. .codex/automation-candidates/self-learning-automation-candidate.md Self-Learning Loop automation promotion proposal Candidate-only promotion packet with owner approval record, minimum_manual_successful_runs, rollback/disable path, false-positive audit, flake replay and cost check. active schedule remains not_created; owner approval record is required before any schedule, hook, Codex App automation, GitHub Action or external workflow. .codex/product-agent-os/analysis/analysis-manifest.json analysis_artifact_renderer.py first_run_analysis_manifest_v1: pages, digests, source digests, manifest_digest, redaction_report, source_policy_gate, baseline comparison and cleanup guidance. Generated-view boundary; source files and current command evidence are stronger. .codex/product-agent-os/analysis/index.html analysis_artifact_renderer.py first_run_cockpit_artifact_v1: primary self-contained architecture cockpit. Local review surface; not WebGL/Cosmos.gl, browser screenshot, WCAG, runtime, release or target-apply proof. first_run_cockpit_artifact_contract_v1 build_first_run_cockpit_artifact_contract() Contract map for primary cockpit pages, graph layers, renderer choice, large-graph policy and unsupported claims. Contract map only; not proof that browser/runtime dependencies executed. architecture_intelligence_design_contract_v1 _architecture_intelligence_design_contract() Design contract for the architecture cockpit shell, section hierarchy and component grammar. Design intent; not browser proof or public readiness. first_run_schema_contract_surface_v1 _first_run_schema_contract_surface() Inventory of API/schema/config/diagram contracts by path and digest. Path-and-digest inventory only; not API compatibility, migration safety or schema completeness. first_run_graph_file_code_surface_v1 _first_run_graph_code_surface() Project Map and Code Intelligence graph/code surfaces. Static fallback unless separate approved browser/WebGL evidence exists. first_run_guided_tour_surface_v1 _first_run_guided_tour_surface() Guided read order and safe next action surface. Does not prove a human completed review or approved action. first_run_evidence_decision_layer_v1 / first_run_evidence_risk_hierarchy_v1 Renderer evidence helpers Supported/unsupported claims, blockers, risks and proposal-only decision surfaces. Evidence organization only; no completion, fixed, verified or ready claim without current evidence. first_run_artifact_cleanup_guidance_v1 _cleanup_guidance() Cleanup preview listing generated files and rollback policy. approval_required: true; deletion_performed: false; no automatic cleanup. first_run_redaction_report_v1 _redaction_report() Redaction guardrail for generated manifest/model payloads. Blocks local absolute paths, raw source fields and secret-like values, but is not full DLP/security certification. batch41_s9_m57_neural_flow_comparison_v1 B41/S9 comparison artifact Read-only staged rerun comparison with digests, key deltas, marker checks and no-unapproved-actions surface. source_policy_gate may allow diagnostic artifacts while keeping apply/promotion disabled. redaction_report must record blocked secret-like values, raw source fields and local absolute paths before a packet is finalized. cleanup_guidance is preview-only: file deletion, target cleanup and rollback actions require separate explicit approval.

docs.title: System File Hygiene Artifacts
docs.text:
Artifact Producer Contract role Boundary JSON output from validate_system_file_hygiene.py system_file_hygiene.py Read-only inventory and findings for maintained system file classes. schedule_status: not_created; no edits, schedules, hooks or external writes. .codex/workflows/system-file-hygiene-audit.md Template registry Operator workflow for hybrid periodic, on-change, size and release/automation triggers. Recommendation only until owner approval enables a real schedule. .codex/artifact-templates/system-file-hygiene-report.md Template registry Staged report for size, duplication, mojibake/BOM, secret, historical-ledger and ownership findings. Review artifact only; compaction remains a separate slice. .codex/automation-candidates/system-file-hygiene-audit.md Template registry Candidate-only automation packet for future scheduled hygiene checks. active schedules remain out of scope until explicit approval and rollback/disable evidence exist.

The system_file_hygiene_audit JSON validator checks nested trigger records, class records, inventory, findings and summary.status; malformed packets are blocked before compaction or automation promotion.

System hygiene JSON fields: audit_trigger, finding_type, compaction_decision, approval_boundary, no_secrets_status and active_schedule_markers. CLI --trigger records the run reason without workspace writes. Staged system-file-hygiene-report.md captures audit trigger, system file class, finding type, owner, compaction decision, active schedule markers, no-secrets status and owner-approved slice boundary.

The HTML/JSON status dashboard projection uses only bounded file_statuses: relative path, class, owner, state, severity, finding count, mtime_utc, age_days, content_digest and top_finding. Dates come from filesystem metadata and are freshness hints, not semantic proof of content correctness, source ownership or completion readiness.

docs.title: Planned Execution Evidence Files
docs.text: Planned artifact Surface Status before approval live-server-run-evidence.json approved_local_runtime_launch Planned only; requires local runtime approval packet. browser-automation-smoke.json actual_browser_automation_smoke Planned only; requires browser automation approval packet. provider-call-evidence.json approved_provider_api_pilot Planned only; provider call blocked until approval/redaction/cache/budget/eval threshold exists. canonical-mutation-run.json approved_canonical_mutation_pilot Planned only; requires accepted ledger item, dry-run plan, journal and rollback proof. git-release-pr-evidence.md explicit_git_release_pr_action Planned only; no git stage/commit/push/PR without explicit user command.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Artifact verification should check:

  • expected artifact_kind and approval_boundary;
  • stage root confinement and rollback/disable path;
  • redaction of secrets, raw source bodies, absolute paths and private data;
  • generated-view or staged-evidence label;
  • source-boundary label when screenshots, cockpit, dashboard or runtime QA evidence is present;
  • fallback path when live/provider/runtime layers are disabled;
  • schedule_status: not_created for system file hygiene outputs unless a later approved automation slice records otherwise;
  • current command evidence before readiness, works, complete or release claims.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Checked-in source docs, control-plane files and generated artifact packets.
  • Approval records, run evidence, redaction state and owner decisions where required.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Reviewable artifact contracts with producer, purpose, boundary and verification expectations.
  • A stable map for docs tests, source registry entries and closure checks.

docs.title: Risks And Failure Modes
docs.text:
• A generated HTML/JSON view can be mistaken for source truth.
  • Stale graph fingerprints or caches can make old source look current.
  • Provider artifacts can leak private data if redaction/cache/budget gates are skipped.
  • Review ledger decisions are invalid without owner and evidence refs.
  • Mutation artifacts are unsafe without rollback proof.
  • Planned artifact names can be mistaken for executed evidence.

docs.title: Next Action
docs.text: Use this contract map when writing docs tests, source registry entries and packaging/closure checks. Navigation and generated site/ refresh are intentionally handled after the source docs packet is stable.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS Artifact Gallery
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

This page shows the reviewable outputs a user normally gets from Product-Agent OS and why each output matters. It is not an execution ledger or proof of readiness. Source of truth remains in project source files, current control-plane artifacts, the source registry, fresh command/eval/runtime evidence, owner decisions and accepted gaps.

docs.title: Quick Overview
docs.text: Category Example outputs User-facing value Trust boundary Control plane AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md The project gets durable rules, scope, plan, checks, quality gates and current handoff. Authoritative only when current, owner-reviewed and consistent with source code. First-run route lifecycle state, risk map, usage_mode, evidence gaps, safe_next_action The user can see where to start without a broad rewrite. Detection is not verification; the next step still needs evidence. Methodology packet recommendations, owner questions, methodology-to-artifact mapping Only risk-relevant gates are activated: DDD, TDD, ADD, FSD, eval-driven work and related practices. present_unverified does not become present_verified without an artifact or owner decision. Status dashboard status.html, status.json, route snapshot The route state, gaps and nearest action are visible quickly. It is an orientation surface; it does not prove completion or readiness. Graph and cockpit project-code-graph.json, project-cockpit.html, query packets Large projects become easier to read through hotspots, read order and affected tests. Generated views help navigation, but canonical files remain authoritative. Real-testing evidence runtime, browser, provider, mutation and git evidence packets Every external or mutating action is visible as a separate decision. One approval never authorizes another action; each run has its own boundary. Scorecards metrics report, scorecard ledger, modernization candidate Agents and skills can improve from evidence instead of impression. Candidate-only: proposals do not self-apply. Release and closure readiness packet, artifact manifest, rollback, handoff PR, package or release decisions have scope, checks and residual risks. No publish, git stage, commit, push or PR occurs without separate explicit approval.

docs.title: Manifest Fields To Check
docs.text: When reading the manifest, check schema_version, pages, page_digests, source_digests, primary_cockpit, cockpit_contract, redaction_report, source_policy_gate, baseline_comparison and cleanup_guidance. These fields describe generated evidence and guardrails; they do not replace source review, owner decisions or current commands.

docs.title: Generated-view Policy
docs.text:
Generated dashboards, graphs, cockpits, scorecards, reports and comparison packets are orientation evidence. They help choose the next action, but they do not replace source files, checked-in contracts, control-plane artifacts, source registry entries, current command/eval/runtime evidence, owner decisions or accepted gaps.

If a first-run artifact looks convincing, the next step must still be source-backed: read the owning source, check the current command or record an explicit accepted gap. Generated site/ freshness remains the final DOC-M25 gate after G2-G5 and does not follow from this gallery.

docs.title: Cleanup Guidance
docs.text: first_run_artifact_cleanup_guidance_v1 in the manifest is guidance, not permission to delete files. Without separate approval, do not delete user-authored files, source docs, project config, .git or anything outside the generated analysis directory. A cleanup list helps reviewers understand renderer output; it is not rollback proof for release, mutation or external-write actions.

docs.title: How To Read Outputs
docs.text:
1. Start with the output category and the user question it answers.
  2. Open the owning source: source file, control-plane artifact, command evidence, eval report or owner decision.
  3. Check the trust boundary: what the output proves and what it only helps review.
  4. Take the nearest safe action instead of treating the whole project map as a command.

docs.title: Completion-skeptic Examples
docs.text:
These completion-skeptic examples are synthetic and source-safe. They show how a doubt_verification_packet changes final answer style without claiming that pilot value is proven.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• The gallery can be mistaken for proof of readiness.
  • Generated dashboard, graph, cockpit, scorecard or report output can become stale faster than source files.
  • Historical evidence and public product copy must stay separate: history explains provenance, while public docs should route the user to the next action.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS behavioral evals
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

Sources: Codex workflows, Codex best practices, Agent approvals and security, Product-Agent OS scenarios, Codex compatibility.

Behavioral evals test whether Product-Agent OS resists shortcuts. They check routes, lifecycle skills, generated artifacts and transcript replay for evidence quality, approval boundaries, source labels and false-positive handling.

docs.title: Runtime Packet Safety
docs.text: Runtime packets must keep live actions disabled until a specific approval exists. They must not start servers, run browser automation, call providers, mutate canonical graph facts, create schedules, write to external systems or perform git actions without explicit owner approval.

docs.title: Live And Graph Behavior Coverage
docs.text: Graph, cockpit and dashboard outputs are generated evidence surfaces. They can help orientation and review, but they do not replace source files, current command evidence, runtime proof, owner review or accepted gaps.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• scenario or methodology gate that needs validation;
  • user prompt or synthetic route input;
  • workspace fixture when behavior depends on files;
  • expected behavior: mode, minimum artifacts, next action, approval boundary and evidence fields;
  • forbidden behavior: scaffold before approval, broad rewrite, unsupported ready claim, external mutation or missing source status;
  • residual risk and reason when a case remains structural only.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• behavioral eval case with id, prompt/context, expected behavior, forbidden behavior and evidence requirements;
  • fixture eval assertion when behavior can be checked through a synthetic workspace;
  • failure note for RUNLOG.md when a route or lifecycle skill misses a shortcut;
  • transcript/session eval report with behavioral_case, expected_terms, forbidden_terms, missing_expected_terms, forbidden_terms_present and privacy_errors.

docs.title: Guided Questions And Dashboard
docs.text:
Guided question protocol uses typed question_queue packets. The first response shows only next_blocking_question, question_counts and question_summary; optional questions stay in the packet and answers route into artifacts or accepted gaps.

Expected behavior: one blocking question maximum, no broad methodology interview, no full queue dump in first response, no dashboard-as-source-of-truth and no success claim from stale evidence.

docs.title: Completion-skeptic Eval Coverage
docs.text:
The local eval suite adds deterministic coverage for the manual "check again" route. Current cases include completion-skeptic-check-again-trigger, completion-skeptic-false-pass-blocked, completion-skeptic-false-rewrite-blocked, completion-skeptic-source-sensitive-docs, completion-skeptic-code-tool-evidence, completion-skeptic-fake-evidence-adversarial and completion-skeptic-scorecard-thresholds.

These cases require a doubt_verification_packet, no-rewrite-first behavior, source/evidence ledgers and fake-evidence resistance. The scorecard thresholds remain manual-only until pilot denominators, user-revision acceptance and owner review are recorded.

docs.title: Self-Verification Metrics Loop
docs.text:
agent_skill_metrics_loop is a staged self-verification metrics loop for agents, skills, prompt/policy packs, router/tool policy and harness-version review. Expected behavior starts with a read-only target registry, trace intake, dataset quality blockers, local grader outputs, grader/judge calibration, cadence recommendation levels L0, L1, L2 and L3, scorecard ledger, agent-skill-evaluation-report.html and modernization candidates with evidence, rollback and owner-review state.

Forbidden behavior includes headline-metric-only approval, raw trace leakage, uncalibrated judge approval, self-applied updates, missing rollback target, live eval/model/API calls, active schedules and modernization candidates that cross approval boundary without explicit owner review.

docs.title: Self-Learning Loop docs/contracts closure eval
docs.text:
self_learning_loop_docs_contracts_closure checks that docs name implemented versus planned surfaces, artifact contracts expose self_learning_docs_contracts_closure_v1, automation promotion remains candidate_only, and the promotion packet requires three manual successful runs, owner approval, rollback/disable path, false-positive audit, flake replay and cost check.

Forbidden behavior: no real Codex App session export import, no hidden telemetry, no raw transcript storage, no live eval/model/provider calls, no target mutation, no active schedule, no hook activation, no GitHub Action or Codex App automation creation, no git/release/deploy/publish/external write and no auto-apply.

docs.title: Expected Behavior
docs.text:
Each case should name behavior, not only a file name.

  • bug_rescue: reproduce or isolate before fix; no fixed claim without current evidence.
  • greenfield_idea: select direction and first vertical slice before scaffold.
  • complex_system_acceleration: require integration catalog and ownership split before parallel work.
  • pr_review: read-only review with spec compliance before quality/risk.
  • api_migration: migration plan and contract compatibility before implementation or release.
  • ai_eval_regression: baseline and rerun command before prompt/model/retrieval/rubric changes.
  • release_packaging: release readiness before publish, tag, upload or package registry mutation.
  • evidence-before-completion: ready/completed/fixed/works/release claims need current evidence or explicit inspection-only gap.
  • methodology-intelligence-read-only-first: methodology audit must return a Delivery Map, prioritized recommendations and owner questions before any staged proposal.
  • solution_architecture_contract_present: architecture gates require scope, boundaries, owner, ADR/tradeoff, observability, rollback, render check and accepted-gap evidence without forcing heavyweight architecture ceremony when not applicable.
  • codex_agentic_workflow_contract_present: Codex workflow gates require control plane, source of truth, read-only discovery, approval boundaries, model/reasoning policy, memory policy, fresh-context handoff, ownership split, subagent safety, MCP review, hook governance, skill promotion, plugin boundary, automation stability and agent eval workflow.
  • frontend_contract_present: frontend gates require user-flow acceptance, component state matrix, design-system boundary, Storybook/FSD routing, API/data state alignment, WCAG 2.2 AA target or accepted exception, browser/runtime evidence, console status, Playwright trace or accepted gap, visual evidence, interaction checks and performance budget where applicable.
  • backend_contract_present: backend gates require backend-service-overview.md, backend-runtime-behavior.md, runtime/failure/observability/security/rollback evidence and owner-reviewed evidence sufficiency for real project risk or accepted gap.
  • api_integrations_contract_present: API gates require a source-of-truth contract, consumer map, compatibility review, security schemes, error contract, contract test matrix, event/webhook delivery evidence, generated SDK manifest, observability and approval_required handling for external writes.
  • database_data_contract_present: Database & Data gates require inventory, dictionary, migration plan, data contract, rollback/backup evidence, data classification, data quality, lineage, query performance, retention/deletion, synthetic fixtures and production access approval where applicable.
  • llm_ai_rag_contract_present: LLM / AI / RAG gates require AI behavior promise, baseline eval, eval rerun evidence, app-backed eval path, prompt contract, model decision record, structured output schema, tool/function/MCP contract, human approval boundary, RAG source inventory, grounding rubric, trace evidence, cost/latency budget and incident workflow.
  • security_privacy_compliance_contract_present: Security, Privacy & Compliance gates require security-sensitive classification, threat surface, risk review, mapping, negative tests, secrets policy, data classification, redaction lifecycle, privacy impact, external-write approval, supply-chain review, audit logging, explicit scan status and current evidence before completion.
  • delivery_release_operations_contract_present: Delivery, Release & Operations gates require release scope, versioning, changelog/release notes, artifact manifest, evidence before completion, rollout strategy, rollback/recovery, environment approval boundary, CI/CD governance, observability/SLO, runbook, incident response, post-release review, automation manual stability and owner-reviewed evidence sufficiency.
  • cross_domain_synthesis_contract_present: Cross-domain synthesis gates require methodology_synthesis, recommendation_groups, owner domains, consumer domains, source_artifact_ledger, semantic evidence sufficiency, risk-aware safe next action and source artifact alias/deferred decisions.
  • question_queue_contract_present: guided question protocol exposes next_blocking_question, question_counts and question_summary while preserving the full typed packet outside the first response.
  • status_dashboard_present: status dashboard generation stages .codex/product-agent-os/status.html and .codex/product-agent-os/status.json from a status_snapshot; dashboard is a generated view and not source of truth.
  • professional_code_authoring: non-mechanical code tasks name existing capability scan, one-line/native candidate, dependency decision, deep module or legacy seam evidence before code-quality claims.
  • false-positive fixtures: backend/native work does not force FSD, simple CRUD src/domain/* does not force DDD, docs-light does not force a docs portal, hosted docs and DB introspection stay approval-required.

docs.title: Forbidden Behavior
docs.text:
Forbidden behavior is the part that catches shortcuts:

  • scaffold before approval;
  • broad rewrite before root cause;
  • parallel work without ownership split;
  • review verdict without spec-compliance stage;
  • compatibility claim without contract check evidence;
  • quality claim for AI/RAG without baseline or rerun;
  • CI health claim from stale logs;
  • release claim without build/test/docs evidence;
  • methodology recommendation that writes target files, enables hooks, creates automation or mutates external systems before approval;
  • Codex workflow recommendation that treats memory as source of truth, subagents as automatically faster, MCP as safe by default, hooks as harmless, Agents SDK as the Codex runtime layer or repeated workflows as immediately automation-ready;
  • source-backed OpenAI/Codex claim without Source status or registry support;
  • professional code authoring completion from a 50-line custom helper, needless dependency, shallow wrapper, noisy comments, rewrite claim or "senior/clean/simple" label without checklist evidence;
  • external write, remote CI mutation, publish, tag, upload or package-registry action without approval;
  • full question queue dump in first response, broad methodology interview, dashboard as source of truth or ready/completed/success claim from stale evidence.

docs.title: Domain Contract Phrases
docs.text:
These exact phrases are kept as public quality contract language for route/eval maintenance:

  • owner reviewed test/eval/runtime evidence sufficiency;
  • Swagger UI is not source of truth;
  • external writes are approval_required;
  • schema-only artifact is not safety proof;
  • production access approval_required;
  • Prompt inspection is not enough;
  • citations alone do not prove grounding;
  • security_sensitive_classification_present;
  • Codex Security scan is implied;
  • privacy compliance is universal;
  • generic quality strategy hides security approval;
  • automation_manual_stability_present;
  • DORA metrics prove individual performance;
  • single observability tool is mandatory;
  • owner-reviewed release evidence sufficiency;
  • GitOps is automatically safe;
  • repeatable automation is automatically safe.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run focused checks after changing behavioral cases:

python -m unittest tests.product_agent_os.test_behavioral_workflow_evals tests.product_agent_os.test_fixture_eval_runner -v
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_transcript_eval.py plugins\product-agent-os\assets\eval-fixtures\transcripts\product-agent-os-synthetic-sessions.json

Run full checks after plugin templates, fixture eval or route logic changes:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\validate_codex_compatibility.py
python tools\check_docs.py

Use strict MkDocs when docs navigation, Mermaid, Markdown extensions or MkDocs config change.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Fixture eval proves expected structure and route outputs, not deep semantic quality of a real product decision.
  • False-positive fixtures cover selected synthetic layouts; unusual real project layouts still need owner review.
  • Behavioral eval cases can become too broad; keep each case focused on one shortcut or route contract.
  • Transcript/session eval runner is deterministic and local; it catches missing terms, forbidden shortcuts and unsafe transcript content, but it is not an LLM semantic judge.
  • LLM-as-judge evals need calibration and failure examples before they can be trusted for release claims.

Next artifact: use Scenarios to choose the route, Professional Code Authoring Standards to inspect code-writing gates and Codex compatibility to confirm package scope.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS CLI reference
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

This page records the local Product-Agent OS CLI surfaces that already exist in plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/. It describes commands as stage/read-only tooling: they do not publish the plugin, start external systems or perform live provider/model/API calls without separate explicit approval.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The CLI layer supports a repeatable local evidence loop:

  • read-only audit or dry-run packet before changes;
  • stage-only generation into an explicit output directory;
  • approval-bound merge or rollback only through a separate approval record;
  • deterministic runtime contract for Codex App, CLI or IDE extension;
  • project graph generation, queries, generated cockpit, local indexes and provider/mutation governance packets;
  • docs/closure verification through separate docs-maintainer and tester slices.

Generated outputs are not source of truth. Source of truth remains checked-in source files, project docs, source registry, control-plane artifacts, current command evidence and owner-approved records.

docs.title: Core Commands
docs.text:
Command Purpose Required inputs Output / boundary python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\render_infrastructure.py <workspace> --dry-run Print an infrastructure render plan. Target workspace path. Read-only JSON/text plan; no staged files. python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\render_infrastructure.py <workspace> --stage <stage-dir> Stage generated control-plane/templates. Workspace and explicit stage directory. Writes only under <stage-dir>; direct target merge remains separate. python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\merge_infrastructure.py <workspace> <stage-dir> --plan Build a read-only merge plan. Workspace and stage directory. No writes to target workspace. python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\merge_infrastructure.py <workspace> <stage-dir> --apply --approval-file <approval.json> Apply approved merge decisions. Approval file matching the plan. Approved target writes only; rollback manifest can be produced by merge tooling. python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\merge_infrastructure.py <workspace> <stage-dir> --rollback <rollback.json> Roll back a prior approved merge. Rollback manifest. Restores scoped files from recorded rollback data. python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_codex_runtime_runner.py <workspace> --contract Produce deterministic Codex runtime route packet. Workspace. Offline contract; no external model call. python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_codex_runtime_runner.py <workspace> --contract --allow-subagents Allow route recommendations that mention subagents. Workspace and explicit subagent permission in the current workflow. Recommendation only; does not create agents by itself. python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\render_status_dashboard.py <workspace> --dry-run Print status dashboard plan. Workspace. No write. python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\render_status_dashboard.py <workspace> --stage <stage-dir> Stage generated status dashboard HTML/JSON. Workspace and explicit stage directory. Generated view only, not source of truth. python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\render_agent_skill_metrics_report.py <workspace> --dry-run Print metrics report plan. Workspace. No write. python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\render_agent_skill_metrics_report.py <workspace> --stage <stage-dir> Stage agent/skill metrics report. Workspace and explicit stage directory. Candidate-only report; no modernization is applied.

Runtime runner optional inputs include --approval-status, --intent-hint and --output. They change the emitted route packet or save JSON; they do not bypass source policy, sandbox, approvals or external-action boundaries.

docs.title: First-Run Analysis CLI
docs.text:
Command Purpose Required inputs Output / boundary python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_first_project_analysis.py <workspace> --full-dry-run Run safe first-run orchestration without writing files. Target workspace path. Read-only preview; no generated files are created. python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_first_project_analysis.py <workspace> --dry-run Print the first-run packet without writing files. Target workspace path. Read-only preview; no generated files are created. python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_first_project_analysis.py <workspace> --stage <dir> Stage first-run generated artifacts into an explicit stage directory. Target workspace and stage directory. Stage root must be outside the target workspace; stage-inside-target is blocked. python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_first_project_analysis.py <workspace> --write-analysis Write generated first-run packet and offline HTML to the local analysis folder. Target workspace path. Writes only under .codex/product-agent-os/analysis/; generated views remain orientation_only_not_proof. python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_first_project_analysis.py <workspace> --write Legacy write route for the first-run packet. Target workspace path. Writes generated packet, including .codex/product-agent-os/analysis/first-run-analysis-packet.json; not target source mutation.

run_first_project_analysis.py chooses exactly one mode: --full-dry-run, --dry-run, --stage <dir>, --write-analysis or --write. DOC-M26 owns the full operator command matrix: see Operator command matrix. Redocly not_applicable until an OpenAPI source contract exists. These commands do not approve live servers, browser automation, provider/API calls, target source mutation, git actions, release, promotion or root site rebuild.

Safe operator examples:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_first_project_analysis.py <workspace> --full-dry-run
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_first_project_analysis.py <workspace> --dry-run
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_first_project_analysis.py <workspace> --stage C:\tmp\product-agent-os-first-run

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --stage C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage

These examples are not the broad command matrix. The full command-policy matrix, docs-tooling smokes, install/runtime variants and approval-state coverage belong to DOC-M26. CLI docs provide safe pointers only and do not expand permission for live servers, browser automation, provider/API calls, canonical mutation, git actions or root site rebuild.

docs.title: Self-Learning Loop Due-Check CLI
docs.text:
Command Purpose Inputs Output / boundary python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\check_self_learning_due.py <workspace> --dry-run Checks whether the owner should be offered a manual Self-Learning Loop run. Product-Agent OS workspace with .codex/product-agent-os/self-learning-state.json. Prints due, not_due, disabled or state_invalid; does not run analysis, write state, create a schedule or enable auto-apply.

In this contract, weekly means a due-check basis, not an active schedule.

docs.title: Self-Learning Loop Manual Runner CLI
docs.text:
Command Purpose Inputs Output / boundary python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_self_learning_loop.py <workspace> --dry-run Builds a Self-Learning Loop run packet without writing files. Product-Agent OS workspace with an explicit marker and self-learning state. Prints self_learning_run_packet_v1, progress events and planned artifact targets; does not write the workspace or auto-apply anything. python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_self_learning_loop.py <workspace> --stage <dir> Generates staged progress state and an offline HTML artifact. Product-Agent OS workspace, stage directory outside the target workspace. Writes only under the stage root: progress.jsonl, run progress.json, self-learning-run-packet.json and self-learning-progress.html. The target workspace is not changed.

The manual runner starts with the Product-Agent OS scope detector and fails closed for out_of_scope, missing_marker and needs_owner_review. It does not create scheduler/hooks/Codex App automation, ingest raw sessions, call providers or perform git/release/deploy/publish actions.

docs.title: Project Graph CLI
docs.text:
scan_project_code_graph.py has exactly-one-mode semantics. Choose one mode per invocation.

Mode Purpose Required inputs Output / boundary --dry-run Build graph packet without writing files. <workspace>. Prints graph JSON; no write. --stage <stage-dir> Stage graph and cockpit artifacts. <workspace>, explicit stage directory. Writes generated graph/cockpit files under stage root. --query <kind> Read bounded query packet from existing graph. --graph <project-code-graph.json> plus query args. Reads existing graph artifact; does not rescan source. --build-index Build offline static search index. --stage, --graph. Generated index cache; not source of truth. --build-backend Stage disabled-by-default local query backend store. --stage, --graph, --backend-approval. Generated file-store; no active server by default. --build-semantic-index Stage local deterministic semantic retrieval index. --stage, --graph, --semantic-approval. Generated semantic cache; provider calls remain blocked unless separately approved. --build-llm-proposals Stage local deterministic LLM-style proposal packets. --stage, --graph, --llm-approval. Proposals only, never canonical facts. --verify-extensions Stage extension verification and rollback closure. --stage, --graph, --verification-evidence. Closure packet and rollback/data deletion proof. --validate-live-governance Stage live governance packet. --stage, --live-approval. No live calls; validates approval/data/redaction/cache/budget boundary. --validate-live-runtime Stage local read-only runtime contract. --stage, --live-runtime-approval, --live-governance. Disabled-by-default local runtime contract; no launch. --validate-embedding-provider Stage embedding provider gate. --stage, --embedding-provider-approval, graph/semantic inputs as required. Provider gate/eval packet; no provider call unless approved in later execution. --validate-reranker-provider Stage reranker provider gate. --stage, --reranker-provider-approval. Provider gate packet; no external call by default. --build-hybrid-retrieval Stage hybrid retrieval pipeline. --stage, graph/index/semantic/reranker inputs. Generated explainable fusion packet; no canonical mutation. --validate-llm-proposal-provider Stage LLM proposal provider gate. --stage, --llm-proposal-provider-approval, proposal/eval inputs. Provider gate and safety eval; proposal-only. --build-review-ledger Stage human review ledger and proposal diff. --stage, --review-ledger-approval, --review-decisions. Owner decision ledger; still non-mutating. --build-canonical-mutation Stage mutation dry-run, journal and rollback artifacts. --stage, --canonical-mutation-approval, review ledger and proposal diff. Staged mutated graph copy only; canonical source graph is not silently changed. --build-live-audit Stage audit/security/observability/handoff packets. --stage, --live-audit-approval, live runtime/actions/security inputs. Redacted audit and operability evidence. --build-real-testing-readiness Stage readiness, target consent and pilot artifacts. --stage, --real-testing-approval and target/gate/pilot inputs. Dry-run pilot/readiness evidence only. --build-runtime-qa Stage runtime QA, performance and stabilization artifacts. --stage, --runtime-qa-approval and QA/performance/stabilization inputs. Staged QA evidence; no live browser automation in docs work.

Disable modes delete generated artifacts under the stage root: --disable-backend, --disable-semantic-index, --disable-llm-proposals, --disable-extensions, --disable-live-governance, --disable-live-runtime, --disable-embedding-provider, --disable-reranker-provider, --disable-hybrid-retrieval, --disable-llm-proposal-provider, --disable-review-ledger, --disable-canonical-mutation, --disable-live-audit, --disable-real-testing-readiness and --disable-runtime-qa.

docs.title: Query Inputs
docs.text:
Graph query mode accepts:

  • --graph for project-code-graph.json or project-code-graph.jsonl;
  • optional --index, --backend, --semantic-index, --hybrid-retrieval and --reranker-provider;
  • --node-id, --target-id and --text for query-specific selectors;
  • --max-results, --max-depth, --max-tokens, --hub-threshold, --node-type, --edge-type, --confidence and --path-prefix for bounded output.

Supported query kinds include neighbors, path, trace, impact, affected_tests, changed_since, why_changed, read_order, hotspots, node, status and search.

docs.title: Cockpit Query Surface
docs.text:
The project graph CLI feeds cockpit data, but it does not turn the cockpit into proof:

  • --stage <stage-dir> writes generated project-code-graph.json, project-code-graph.jsonl, project-cockpit.html and project-cockpit.json inside the stage root.
  • --query read_order --graph <project-code-graph.json> returns bounded guided read order; use it as a reading hint, then inspect source files before edits or impact claims.
  • --query trace, --query impact and --query affected_tests create static query packets; they do not prove runtime routes, dynamic dispatch or test results.
  • --query search may use graph-only search, static index, semantic index or hybrid inputs when provided; returned hits remain orientation evidence.

Examples:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --query read_order --graph C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage\.codex\product-agent-os\project-code-graph.json --max-results 12
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --query trace --graph C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage\.codex\product-agent-os\project-code-graph.json --node-id function:app.main.main --max-depth 3
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --query status --graph C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage\.codex\product-agent-os\project-code-graph.json

Static fallback is the supported visual boundary in this docs slice. Cosmos.gl/WebGL, browser screenshots, interactive canvas behavior, performance proof and accessibility visual proof remain unsupported until a separate approved runtime/browser evidence packet exists.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Staged JSON, JSONL, HTML, report or validation packets under the approved stage boundary.
  • Console output that can be cited as current command evidence when the command actually ran.

docs.title: Verification Commands
docs.text:
Common local verification commands:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_transcript_eval.py plugins\product-agent-os\assets\eval-fixtures\transcripts\product-agent-os-synthetic-sessions.json
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\validate_codex_compatibility.py
python tools\check_docs.py
python -m mkdocs build --strict
git diff --check

Run the smallest relevant set for the current slice. A closure claim requires the full source docs -> registry -> docs tests -> check_docs.py -> strict MkDocs -> optional full closure order.

docs.title: Risks And Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Running a stage command inside a target workspace can blur generated and source-of-truth boundaries.
  • Supplying approval JSON is not enough if the owner, allowed surfaces, data policy, rollback and verification evidence are missing.
  • Query packets can be stale if graph fingerprints no longer match current source.
  • Provider gate commands are not permission to call providers.
  • Canonical mutation dry-run is not permission to mutate checked-in source or graph facts.
  • Git commands remain explicit-only and are outside these CLI reference commands.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS Codex compatibility
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

Sources: Codex plugins, Build plugins, Agent Skills, Subagents, AGENTS.md, Codex hooks, Agent approvals and security, Codex with Agents SDK, Product-Agent OS architecture.

Compatibility means the package fits Codex surfaces. It does not approve live execution, provider calls, external writes, hosted docs, database access, automation activation or git actions.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• current .codex-plugin/plugin.json and packaged plugin metadata;
  • local skills, scripts, templates, MCP declarations and staged hooks;
  • Codex App, CLI and IDE extension workflow expectations;
  • current AGENTS.md, sandbox, approvals and source policy;
  • compatibility validator output and any accepted gaps.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• package compatibility status;
  • supported Codex surfaces and non-goals;
  • approval boundary for live systems, provider calls, external writes, hosted docs, database access, active automation and git actions;
  • verification commands for package and docs closure;
  • residual risks when a compatibility claim depends on current official Codex behavior.

docs.title: Canonical Safety Boundary
docs.text:
Product-Agent OS keeps a conservative Codex boundary:

  • no live model call from compatibility checks;
  • no separate OpenAI API key requirement for the Codex runtime runner;
  • no standalone Agents SDK activation hidden behind the plugin;
  • no global config mutation;
  • no silent MCP/server/hook/automation activation;
  • no unapproved external writes;
  • no hosted docs or DB introspection bypass;
  • no readiness claims from detection.

Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, skills, MCP declarations and staged hooks are supported package surfaces. They are not permission to mutate target workspaces, GitHub, CI, package registries, production databases, hosted documentation, security systems or schedules without explicit approval and current verification evidence.

docs.title: Compatible Surfaces
docs.text: Surface Supported use Boundary .codex-plugin/plugin.json Plugin manifest and packaged capability declaration. Manifest presence is compatibility evidence, not publication approval. Codex App Interactive steering, ambiguity resolution, review and local workspace work. User approvals and sandbox still govern actions. CLI Local deterministic checks, renderers, validators and staged artifact generation. Commands must respect project policy and approval scope. IDE extension Code navigation, review and implementation support. IDE context is not source of truth by itself. skills Repeatable methods with inputs, outputs, verification and failure modes. A skill can recommend actions but cannot grant external permission. subagents Parallel or specialized work when ownership is clear. Handoff must include files, context, expected evidence and stop conditions. AGENTS.md Durable project rules and operating constraints. Local project rules cannot override stronger system/developer instructions. staged hooks Hook templates and staged proposals. Hooks are not silently activated. MCP Declared tool context and integration boundaries. MCP access is not automatically safe or approval-free. Agents SDK Product/runtime app architecture when explicitly chosen. It is not the hidden runtime layer for this plugin.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
Product-Agent OS compatibility checks do not:

  • publish plugins or docs;
  • create schedules, recurring automations or GitHub Actions;
  • start local servers for verification;
  • run browser automation;
  • call external providers or live model/API endpoints;
  • mutate canonical graph facts;
  • stage, commit, push or open PRs;
  • certify legal, security or compliance readiness.

Those actions require explicit owner approval, current evidence and a rollback or stop condition.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Use these checks when package boundaries or docs change:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\validate_codex_compatibility.py
python tools\check_docs.py

Use strict MkDocs when navigation, Mermaid, Markdown extensions or generated site output changes:

python -m mkdocs build --strict

The compatibility validator should stay deterministic. If it needs live provider, browser, hosted docs or database evidence, that evidence belongs in a separate approval-bound route, not in baseline compatibility.

docs.title: Live Execution Boundaries
docs.text:
The live layer stays disabled until each action has its own owner-approved packet:

  • local runtime launch;
  • browser automation smoke;
  • external embedding/reranker/LLM provider pilot;
  • canonical graph mutation pilot;
  • git release, push, PR or publication action.

Approvals are not bundled. Approval for one surface does not grant another.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• A compatible package can still be operationally unsafe if a user activates hooks, MCP servers, automations or external systems without evidence.
  • Generated cockpit/dashboard/report outputs can look authoritative; the docs must keep source-boundary labels visible.
  • Agent handoff quality matters more than the number of subagents. Parallel work without ownership can increase risk.
  • Official Codex behavior can evolve; source-backed claims should be reviewed against current official docs when product surfaces change.

Next artifact: use Packaging And Closure for release evidence and Approval-Bound Real Testing before any live execution.

docs.title: Professional Code Authoring Standards
docs.text:
Source status: project-authored + research-backed + experiment

Sources: Batch 45 research packets plugins/product-agent-os/assets/research/ai-agent-coding-standards-research.md and plugins/product-agent-os/assets/research/ai-agent-coding-literature-research.md, Batch 45 S5 packet docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-professional-code-s5-learning-automation-summary.json, S6 packets docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-agent-behavior-eval-results.json and docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-comment-policy-promotion-decision.json, S7 packets docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-real-project-scorecard.json and docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-real-project-decision-packet.json, M37 remediation packet docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-review-remediation-summary.json, Development Standards, Artifact Contracts, Behavioral Evals, Scenarios, Code Review playbook.

Professional Code Authoring is the Product-Agent OS layer for non-mechanical coding tasks. Its main rule is simple: the agent checks existing capability, standard library support, framework primitives, configuration paths, current dependencies and project helpers before adding custom code. The best implementation may be one line, a deletion or a configuration change when that satisfies the acceptance criteria with less debt.

docs.title: Applied Gates
docs.text: Gate What the agent records When it can be skipped enterprise_leverage_check The existing path checked before custom implementation. Mechanical docs/format-only work with a not_applicable reason. existing_capability_scan Standard library, framework, current dependency, project helper, config and deletion/reuse options. Tiny isolated fix where source and reason are obvious and recorded. one_line_candidate The shortest direct expression or native call before a multi-line helper. Not applicable for behavioral workflow, migration or UI composition work. negative_dependency_rule Why a new dependency is needed, rejected alternatives and rollback/removal path. No new dependency. deep_module_check Why an abstraction hides real complexity instead of creating a shallow wrapper. Direct call is better than abstraction. legacy_seam_check Characterization evidence, seam strategy, rollback or accepted gap. No legacy/refactor impact. comment_policy Comments explain intent, invariant, hazard or trade-off; state machines, algorithms, security/privacy/data/concurrency logic, and functions with non-obvious invariants need a docstring, intent comment, or comment_not_needed_reason. The code is self-explanatory and obvious comments would be noise. cleverness_budget Payoff, tests, naming clarity and reviewer rationale. Direct/simple path chosen.

docs.title: Activation Path
docs.text:
Product-Agent OS applies this standard through staged source artifacts:

Surface How it appears Boundary Workflow .codex/workflows/coding-standards.md from the packaged template. Template registration proves the workflow can be staged, not live enforcement. Checklist .codex/artifact-templates/coding-standard-checklist.md. Review artifact; not source truth without current evidence. Agent task packet .codex/artifact-templates/agent-task-packet.md carries compact handoff fields. Handoff contract, not raw research body. Skills and agents Builder/reviewer/architect/tester/docs-maintainer prompts reference the compact contract. Skills activate by selection/context; they do not launch subagents automatically. Evals behavioral-workflows.json, agent-context contract and focused tests reject shortcut behavior. Local deterministic coverage only. Runtime route and HTML professional_code_authoring appears as recommendation/visibility. Generated view is orientation_only_not_proof.

docs.title: Learning-Loop Improvement Policy
docs.text:
Self-Learning Loop may propose future Professional Code Authoring improvements only as review candidates. Candidate inputs are aggregate metrics, owner feedback, eval failures and manual pilot evidence; raw private chat bodies and hidden telemetry are forbidden.

The candidate may point only to staged update targets: the coding standards workflow, coding-standard checklist, behavioral/agent-context evals, hook-governance candidate docs and learning-loop/automation-promoter skill guidance. Before promotion review, it needs minimum_manual_successful_runs: 3, owner review, rollback/disable path, false-positive audit, flake replay and cost check.

Until a separate approval-gated batch, Product-Agent OS must not auto-apply these candidates, activate hooks, create schedules, change global config, call providers, mutate target projects, ingest raw private chat or perform external writes.

docs.title: Senior Leverage Ladder
docs.text:
Use this order before writing new code:

  1. Delete or avoid the code path entirely.
  2. Use a language construct, standard library or framework primitive.
  3. Reuse a current dependency or project helper already accepted by the repo.
  4. Configure existing behavior instead of adding logic.
  5. Compose a small direct expression.
  6. Add a deep module only when it hides real complexity behind a stable interface.
  7. Add a dependency only after alternatives, lifecycle risk, security and removal path are recorded.

docs.title: Evidence Ceiling
docs.text:
Batch 45 currently supports docs_contract_ready / synthetic_green claims for local source artifacts, templates, eval cases, discovery/readiness visibility, runtime route visibility, generated HTML visibility and candidate-only learning-loop/automation policy. M26 records a live behavior-eval no-go, M27 keeps the M25 advisory local/non-blocking and rejects stronger advisory, CI and blocker promotion, M35 keeps S7 fixture-local/source-only with no-go for treatment v2 promotion, and M37 records local hook/validator hardening plus review remediation docs/control-plane sync only. T17 freezes the metadata-only held-out corpus manifest in docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t17-frozen-heldout-corpus.json / B45-POSTQ4-T17-A01; T18 defines the same-model promotion-grade eval design and strict schema in docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t18-promotion-grade-eval-design.json / B45-POSTQ4-T18-A01; T19 defines the cost/timeout/raw-temp-only retention policy in docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t19-cost-timeout-retention-policy.json / B45-POSTQ4-T19-A01; T20 stages historical exact approval packets in docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t20-promotion-grade-eval-approval-packet.json / B45-POSTQ4-T20-A01 and docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t20-promotion-grade-eval-approval-packet-1000s.json / B45-POSTQ4-T20-A02, then records the consumed cost-waived approval in docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t20-promotion-grade-eval-approval-packet-cost-waived.json / B45-POSTQ4-T20-A03; T21 records blocked preflight history in docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t21-promotion-grade-eval-run-preflight-blocked.json / B45-POSTQ4-T21-PREFLIGHT-A01, docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t21-promotion-grade-eval-run-preflight-timeout-mismatch.json / B45-POSTQ4-T21-PREFLIGHT-A02 and docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t21-promotion-grade-eval-run-preflight-cost-unknown.json / B45-POSTQ4-T21-PREFLIGHT-A03, plus current strict-schema abort evidence in docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t21-promotion-grade-eval-results.json / B45-POSTQ4-T21-COST-WAIVED-RUN-A01 with approved_primary_calls_started=1, reviewer_calls_started=0, valid_pair_count=0, invalid_pair_count=8 and schema_failure_count=1; T22 records a blocked reviewer/no-go decision in docs/superpowers/specs/batch45-postq4-t22-promotion-grade-decision-packet.json / B45-POSTQ4-T22-A02 with reviewer_gate_status=not_run_due_t21_invalid_schema_abort and promotion_allowed=false. They are not valid baseline/treatment pair evidence, reviewer-gate evidence or promotion evidence. They do not prove that AI agents now write enterprise-quality code in real projects; M26/M27/M35/M37/T17/T18/T19/T20/T21/T22 only sharpen that ceiling.

Unsupported without a later approval-gated batch:

  • live runtime or browser behavior;
  • hook activation or blocking enforcement;
  • active automation, schedule creation or Self-Learning Loop auto-apply;
  • provider/model/API calls;
  • installed plugin cache refresh;
  • target workspace mutation;
  • git, release, deploy or publish action;
  • replacement of human review.

docs.title: Quick Checklist
docs.text:
Before a non-mechanical code edit, the agent should be able to answer:

  • What existing capability was checked?
  • What is the one-line/native candidate?
  • Why is custom code still needed?
  • What dependency or legacy debt is added, avoided or removed?
  • What test/eval/runtime evidence will support the claim?
  • Which claims remain unsupported?

Next artifact: use Development Standards to decide whether the gate applies, Artifact Contracts to inspect the checklist boundary and Behavioral Evals to verify shortcut resistance.
