docs.title: Product-Agent OS development standards
docs.text:
Source status: official + verified methodology + experiment

Sources: Product-Agent OS architecture, Product-Agent OS scenarios, Behavioral evals, Professional Code Authoring Standards, Agent approvals and security, Codex workflows.

Development standards turn methodology into concrete reviewable artifacts. They define how Product-Agent OS handles product hypothesis, architecture, tests, evals, docs, security, release and post-release learning without forcing heavy ceremony onto simple work.

Red-Green-Refactor evidence is required where behavior or shared logic changes. Docs-only and inspection-only work can record an explicit gap. The no-forced-ceremony rule remains active: mechanical edits can be not_applicable, docs-light work can avoid heavy portals, backend/native work does not force FSD, simple CRUD does not force DDD, and high-risk work needs owner_reviewed_evidence_sufficient_for_real_project_risk or explicit_gap_accepted.

docs.title: Core Contract
docs.text: Standard Required behavior False-positive guard Product hypothesis Name user/problem, acceptance scenario, metric or explicit gap. Do not invent product outcomes from code structure alone. Architecture boundary Name scope, ownership, alternatives, decision, rollback and observability when architecture changes. Do not force heavyweight diagrams for small mechanical edits. Test/eval-first Establish failing or baseline evidence before changing behavior. Docs-only or formatting work can mark the gate not applicable with reason. Documentation-as-code Update source-backed docs, Source status: and registry when claims change. Do not treat generated site/ output as source of truth. Review Separate spec compliance from quality/risk review for risky changes. Do not produce review verdicts without reading changed files. Release measurement Record build/test/docs evidence, rollout, rollback, owner review and accepted gaps before release claims. CI green alone is not release readiness.

docs.title: Artifact Templates
docs.text:
These templates convert recommendations into concrete outputs that can be reviewed, tested and accepted or rejected:

Template Purpose .codex/artifact-templates/adr.md Architecture decision record with context, decision, consequences, verification and rollback. .codex/artifact-templates/architecture-overview.md System boundary, runtime, dependencies, observability and operational risk. .codex/artifact-templates/domain-modeling.md Domain terms, bounded contexts, ubiquitous language and business rules when complexity warrants it. .codex/artifact-templates/metric-spec.md Product behavior metric, event source, owner, privacy and interpretation caveats. .codex/artifact-templates/api-contract-review.md API source-of-truth, consumers, compatibility, error model, security and rollout. .codex/artifact-templates/component-card.md UI component purpose, states, accessibility, visual evidence and interaction checks. .codex/artifact-templates/database-dictionary.md Table meaning, sensitive fields, retention, migration history and schema verification. .codex/artifact-templates/docs-tooling-decision.md Docs tooling selection, rejected tools, owner, command evidence and approval requirements. .codex/artifact-templates/governance-proposal.md Staged governance proposal for CODEOWNERS status and GitHub Actions least privilege without external activation. .codex/workflows/coding-standards.md Professional code authoring workflow for non-mechanical code work: leverage existing capabilities before custom code. .codex/artifact-templates/coding-standard-checklist.md Evidence checklist for enterprise_leverage_check, one_line_candidate, dependency decisions, deep-module checks and legacy seams.

docs.title: Discovery Signals
docs.text:
workspace-discovery-auditor can identify methodology signals without claiming readiness:

  • architecture docs, ADRs, C4/arc42-style files and runtime diagrams;
  • OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, SDK generation or webhook/event contracts;
  • Storybook, component libraries and optional FSD structure;
  • database docs, migrations, DBML/SQL, retention and backup/restore evidence;
  • CODEOWNERS, CI, release manifests, changelog and versioning files;
  • eval configs, datasets, prompt/model artifacts, traces and RAG source inventories;
  • security/privacy docs, secrets policies, SBOM/provenance, audit logging and compliance overlays;
  • metrics dashboards, product event specs and post-release learning notes.

Signals create present_unverified. Verified readiness needs current command evidence, owner evidence, runtime/eval proof or accepted gap.

Detection alone remains present_unverified, and grouped methodology recommendations need source artifact compatibility, owner domains, consumer domains and approval-bound behavior before they become implementation work.

docs.title: Planning And Handoff Standards
docs.text:
Before build or review, Product-Agent OS expects:

  • exact files owned and forbidden;
  • exact commands and expected outputs;
  • source constraints and approval boundary;
  • rollback or disable path where relevant;
  • expected evidence and stop conditions;
  • fresh-context handoff when subagents or parallel workers are used;
  • placeholder scan or explicit reason it is not applicable;
  • spec-compliance review before quality/risk review for risky public-contract, migration, security, data, release or parallel work.

Subagents are useful only when ownership is clear. A handoff without source context, files, expected evidence and stop condition is not enough.

docs.title: Professional Code Authoring
docs.text:
For non-mechanical code work, Product-Agent OS expects the coding-standard workflow and checklist to be loaded before edits. The default ladder is: delete unnecessary code, configure existing behavior, use standard library or platform capability, use framework API, use an existing dependency, use a project helper, then add a tiny adapter or custom code only when the earlier options are insufficient.

The checklist records enterprise_leverage_check, existing_capability_scan, one_line_candidate, selected leverage path, rejected alternatives, negative_dependency_rule, deep_module_check, legacy_seam_check, cleverness_budget, test/eval evidence and unsupported code-quality claims. Mechanical, docs-only or generated-file sync work can mark the gate not_applicable with a reason.

Template availability is not runtime enforcement. These artifacts do not activate hooks, automation, subagents, HTML reporting or plugin-cache behavior by themselves; they give agents a compact source-of-truth contract when the workflow, skill or role profile is explicitly loaded.

docs.title: Domain-Specific Gates
docs.text:
Domain Gate Frontend User-flow acceptance, component states, design-system boundary, accessibility target or accepted exception, browser/runtime evidence, visual evidence and performance budget when applicable. Backend Runtime behavior, failure modes, observability, security, rollback, CI/deployment discovery and owner-reviewed evidence sufficiency. API & Integrations Source-of-truth contract, consumer map, compatibility, security, error model, events/webhooks, SDK generation and external-write approval. Database & Data Inventory, dictionary, migration plan, expand-contract rollout, data classification, quality, lineage, performance, retention and production access boundary. LLM / AI / RAG Baseline/current eval, prompt/model/tool/RAG contracts, grounding, trace evidence, guardrails, cost/latency, migration policy and AI incident path. Security, Privacy & Compliance Threat surface, risk review, ASVS/SSDF/SAMM mapping, authorization negative tests, secrets, privacy, supply chain, audit logging, scan status and compliance overlay. Delivery, Release & Operations Release scope, versioning, changelog, artifact manifest, rollout, rollback, CI/CD governance, SLO/observability, operations runbook, incident path, post-release review and release integrity handoff. Cross-domain synthesis Grouped recommendations, owner domains, consumer domains, source artifact compatibility, semantic evidence sufficiency and risk-aware safe next action.

Exact gate identifiers:

  • llm_ai_rag_readiness_when_ai_behavior_changes: AI/RAG behavior changes record llm_ai_rag evidence before quality claims.
  • security_privacy_compliance_when_sensitive_surface: Security/Privacy/Compliance-sensitive slices record security_privacy_compliance evidence before completion claims.
  • delivery_release_operations_readiness_when_release_or_operations_changes: Delivery/Release/Operations slices record delivery_release_operations evidence before release, deploy, publish, operational-ready or automation-ready claims.
  • automation_manual_stability_present and release_evidence_sufficiency_owner_reviewed are required when automation or release readiness claims depend on operational evidence.
  • False-positive guard: DORA metrics prove individual performance is not an acceptable release/operations claim.

docs.title: Documentation Standard
docs.text:
Every non-index documentation page needs Source status:. Source-backed claims must link to official or project-authored sources and update docs/sources/registry.md when claims are added or changed.

Use this rule of thumb:

  • official OpenAI/Codex behavior needs official docs as source of truth;
  • project package behavior can cite repository artifacts, tests and source packets;
  • community claims stay under docs/insights/ with trust and verification labels;
  • generated HTML, dashboards, memory and chat recall are not source of truth;
  • secrets, tokens, private keys, credentials, customer data and raw private chats are not allowed in docs, prompts, memory, examples, fixtures or templates.

docs.title: Release And Operations Standard
docs.text:
Release, deploy, publish, package and operations-ready claims require current evidence:

  • release scope and versioning;
  • changelog or release notes;
  • artifact manifest;
  • build/test/docs/eval evidence;
  • rollout and rollback/recovery;
  • environment approval boundary;
  • observability/SLO and operations runbook;
  • incident response and post-release review;
  • owner-reviewed evidence sufficiency or accepted gap.

Automation candidates also need manual success evidence, stable inputs/outputs, owner, cadence, verification, failure modes, value evidence and rollback/disable path. Product-Agent OS can stage a candidate; it must not create active automation without explicit approval.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run focused checks after changing docs standards:

python tools\check_docs.py
python -m unittest tests.product_agent_os.test_product_agent_os_docs -v

Run broader checks after templates, lifecycle skills or fixture behavior change:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\validate_codex_compatibility.py

Use strict MkDocs when documentation navigation, Mermaid or site-generation behavior changes.

docs.title: Important Limits
docs.text:
• Standards are evidence gates, not automatic work expansion.
  • Detection alone does not prove readiness.
  • Owner approval is required for external writes, publishing, production data, live provider calls, hosted docs, CI activation, security scans and active automation.
  • High-risk work needs explicit owner-reviewed evidence sufficiency or accepted gap.
  • Product-Agent OS must preserve staged-first behavior, source policy, sandbox and approvals even when a recommendation is confident.

Next artifact: use Methodology intelligence to decide which gates apply, Professional Code Authoring Standards to inspect code-writing gates and Behavioral evals to check shortcut resistance.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Product scope, source evidence, risk classification and methodology signals.
  • Current checks, evals, owner decisions and accepted gaps.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Proportional engineering gates for requirements, architecture, testing, release and operations.
  • Evidence expectations that can be reviewed without forcing irrelevant ceremony.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Treating standards as automatic work expansion can slow low-risk changes.
  • Detection alone does not prove that the chosen gate is semantically sufficient.

docs.title: First-Run Architecture Intelligence Cockpit
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

This page explains how to read the first-run Architecture Intelligence Cockpit in Product-Agent OS. The cockpit is a local orientation surface: it combines the first project analysis, routing, graph/code/schema signals, evidence and risk hierarchy, and one safe next action into a local HTML/JSON packet. It does not replace source files, current commands, owner decisions, the source registry or control-plane artifacts.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The first-run cockpit answers a practical question: what kind of workspace is this, where are the source boundaries, which artifacts already exist, which route is safe, and which claims need more evidence?

It is useful at the start of a pilot, after a read-only audit or before an architecture review. A good result should not read like an internal ledger: the reader should see the summary, key surfaces, evidence gaps, approval boundary and one safe_next_action.

docs.title: Source Boundary
docs.text:
The cockpit is a generated view and remains orientation_only_not_proof. It can guide navigation and review, but it is not standalone proof of architecture correctness, runtime behavior, security posture, visual quality, release readiness or target apply safety.

Stronger than the cockpit Orientation surface only Project source files and checked-in docs index.html cockpit AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md analysis-manifest.json and renderer summaries Source registry entries and owner decisions Graph/code/schema projections Current command/eval/runtime evidence Scorecards, dashboards, generated pages Accepted gaps with owner, reason, residual risk and follow-up Static visual/a11y gate without browser proof

If the cockpit shows a problem or recommendation, the next step must return to the source: read files, check command evidence, update owning docs or request an owner decision.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
The main input is the first-run analysis packet. It contains workspace metadata, detected project shape, source artifacts, control-plane state, usage_mode, methodology route, risk map, source-policy status, graph/file/code summaries, schema/contract signals, runtime/browser/provider boundaries, generated pages, redaction status, evidence gaps and safe_next_action.

For private or real-project targets, the packet must stay redacted: no secrets, credentials, raw private chat logs, private customer data, unredacted PII, raw source bodies or absolute user-specific paths.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Artifact Role Boundary first-run-analysis-packet.json Machine-readable first analysis packet: route, summaries, gaps, generated pages, source policy and safe next action. Orientation evidence; not release/readiness proof. analysis-manifest.json Renderer manifest: digests, baseline comparison, redaction report, generated page list and cockpit view model. Generated-view boundary; sources and current commands are stronger. index.html Primary self-contained Architecture Intelligence Cockpit. Local review surface; not browser/runtime proof by itself. Additional *.html pages Diagnostic pages for inventory, architecture, methodology, runtime route, control plane, graph, code flow, quality/evals, risks and recommendations. Supporting views, not source truth. Scorecard or comparison packet Reading quality, structural checks, unsupported claim ceilings and static comparison. Review evidence only; owner acceptance and runtime proof are separate.

docs.title: View Model
docs.text:
The primary cockpit is organized around first_run_cockpit_artifact_v1 and architecture_intelligence_design_contract_v1. These names describe the contract surface; they do not mean all claims are proven.

The view model should show:

  • first viewport operator shell: goal, status, route, next action and claim ceiling;
  • architecture/design contract: what the cockpit shows, what questions it answers and where the trust boundary sits;
  • static diagrams: local SVG/Mermaid-style projections without external runtime;
  • schema/contract surface: detected or explicitly missing DB/API/config/contract signals;
  • graph/file/code surface: source graph, selected nodes, read order and graph blockers;
  • guided review route for operator, reviewer and owner;
  • evidence/risk hierarchy: supported, inspection-only, unsupported, approval-required and accepted-gap labels;
  • visual/accessibility acceptance surface with static checks and an explicit browser proof gap.

docs.title: Local-JS Boundary
docs.text:
The cockpit may include local inline JavaScript for reading convenience: search, filters, tabs, expanded diagnostics, navigation highlighting and copy/select controls. This layer is allowed only as self-contained local interaction.

Without separate approval, the cockpit must not include external <script src=...>, external CSS, hosted assets, fetch, network calls, telemetry, provider/API calls, live server launch, browser automation, target mutation, canonical graph mutation, source-doc mutation or hidden runtime checks.

If JavaScript is disabled, the main content must remain readable as static HTML. Local controls improve navigation but do not increase evidentiary strength.

docs.title: Workspace Detection And Routing
docs.text:
First-run routing must classify a workspace narrowly enough to avoid an unsafe next step.

Signal What the cockpit shows Safe interpretation Control-plane files Whether AGENTS.md, requirements, plan, tests, evals, runlog or staged proposals exist. File presence does not prove freshness; read owner source. Stack and artifacts Docs-only, backend/API, web/frontend, AI/RAG, data/migration, PR/review, automation/release or mixed signals. usage_mode is a route hint, not owner approval. Source policy Missing Source status, registry gaps, private target boundaries and unsupported claims. Block apply/promotion until fixed or accepted as an owner gap. Runtime/browser/provider hints Surfaces that need runtime or external proof. Keep approval_required if proof was not run. Graph/code/schema signals Files, contracts and relationships worth reading first. Use for read order, not automatic edit decisions.

The first safe action is usually one of three things: read named source files, fix source-policy blockers or prepare an owner-reviewed accepted gap. A stronger action needs current evidence and an approval boundary.

docs.title: Artifact Relationships
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["Workspace sources"] --> B["first-run analysis packet"]
    B --> C["analysis manifest"]
    C --> D["Architecture Intelligence Cockpit"]
    C --> E["diagnostic HTML pages"]
    D --> F["reader route and safe_next_action"]
    E --> F
    F --> G["source read / owner decision / accepted gap"]

This Mermaid diagram is Markdown source, not browser screenshot proof. Final generated site/ and search/sitemap parity remain a separate final gate.

docs.title: Safe First Actions
docs.text:
After opening the cockpit, the operator should:

  1. Check Source status, generated_view_policy and approval_boundary.
  2. Read safe_next_action and avoid expanding it into runtime, browser, provider, git or target mutation.
  3. Open the named source files or control-plane artifacts before architecture/readiness claims.
  4. If source-policy blockers exist, fix the owning source or record an owner-reviewed accepted gap.
  5. If screenshot/browser proof is needed, prepare a separate approval packet instead of inferring it from static HTML.

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text: Failure mode Why it is risky Correct response Generated HTML treated as source truth A stale or partial view can look convincing. Return to source files and current command evidence. Static visual gate called WCAG proof Static checks are not browser/a11y/runtime proof. Record a browser proof gap or request approved visual QA. Graph edge treated as runtime dependency Static graph does not prove dynamic dispatch, framework wiring or live behavior. Read code and run approved checks. Local JS treated as app runtime Inline controls only manage the HTML view. Do not claim runtime behavior without separate proof. Private target details leak into reader docs The public/internal boundary breaks redaction policy. Keep private labels and paths in source-owned ledgers only. Root site/ freshness claimed after a source edit Generated site can be stale. Wait for the final DOC-M25 rebuild/search/sitemap gate.

docs.title: Unsupported Claims
docs.text:
This page does not claim browser screenshot proof, Cosmos.gl/WebGL runtime execution proof, full WCAG certification, release readiness, publication readiness, target apply safety, provider/API behavior, canonical graph mutation safety or root site/ freshness after G2-G5 source updates.

Those claims require separate current evidence, owner approval or an accepted gap. Static cockpit evidence can only show which proof is needed next.

docs.title: Screenshot And Browser Proof Boundary
docs.text:
Screenshots, canvas pixel checks, responsive layout proof, console/network cleanliness, keyboard/focus verification and actual browser behavior do not appear automatically from Markdown, strict MkDocs or static HTML inspection.

If that proof is needed, the next slice must name the target artifact, redaction policy, browser automation approval, viewport matrix, console/network evidence, screenshot or trace destination, expected failure handling and owner review path. Until then, the status is not_run_approval_required.

docs.title: Final Site Freshness Route
docs.text:
Source docs can be updated before the root site/ rebuild. For this refresh, the final gate is DOC-M25: it should run after G2-G5 source/nav decisions so one final build can prove generated-site freshness, search index and sitemap parity.

Before DOC-M25, the correct claim is: source Markdown is updated, but generated site/ freshness is not claimed.

docs.title: Related Pages
docs.text:
• Artifact Contracts maps generated artifacts and the first-run analysis artifact.
  • Project Code Graph explains graph/query/cockpit source boundaries.
  • Real-project pilot covers first-run operator packets, target consent and evidence ledgers.
  • Technical Setup covers commands, package layout and local capability boundaries.

docs.title: Next Action
docs.text: Use the cockpit as a reader-facing route map: choose safe_next_action, read the owning sources and only then move to docs/source updates, accepted gaps, approved browser proof or the final DOC-M25 site freshness gate.

docs.title: Generated Artifact UX Criteria
docs.text:
Source status: project evidence

This page defines acceptance criteria for local Product-Agent OS HTML, JSON, and report artifacts. It does not prove that a specific file has already been accepted: acceptance still needs current evidence, owner review, or an explicit accepted gap.

Generated artifacts are review surfaces. They can expose structure, claim ceilings, source links, and next safe action, but they do not replace source files, command evidence, or owner decisions.

docs.title: Usable Artifact
docs.text: Area Requirement Do not claim Navigation Main reading path, visible risk section, owning source links, and safe next action. That an artifact replaces source files or review. Readability Dense tables need short headings, stable columns, and clear empty states. That HTML is public-ready without current checks. Offline The artifact should work without external URLs, external scripts, or provider calls. That browser proof ran without evidence. Print Print output should preserve headings, claim ceilings, and evidence refs. That a printable view is a release artifact. Claim language ready, fixed, verified, complete, and release-ready require current command/runtime/eval evidence or an accepted gap. That a generated view is proof by itself.

docs.title: Vale And Language Guard
docs.text: Local Vale is currently advisory. Warnings help find readiness wording, but they are not an automatic blocker until an owner-approved threshold, report retention policy, and rollback path exist.

docs.title: Storybook Trigger
docs.text: Storybook remains deferred. Revisit it only when a component surface, repeated visual states, owner-approved install path, and browser/visual evidence plan exist. Until then, generated artifact UX is checked through docs tests, static HTML checks, and owner review.

docs.title: Acceptance Checklist
docs.text:
• generated_view_policy explicitly says orientation_only_not_proof.
  • Source-boundary labels and unsupported claims are visible.
  • The artifact gives a next safe action, not a hidden mutation recommendation.
  • It contains no raw private chat logs, secrets, credentials, unredacted PII, or raw source bodies.
  • Cleanup guidance is marked preview-only.
  • Browser, runtime, provider, target mutation, release, and publication claims are absent without separate approval.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Minimum gate for this docs slice: docs unittest, tools/check_docs.py, strict MkDocs smoke under .docs-tools/reports, JSON packet validation, and git diff --check. Browser proof, screenshots, broad Vale enforcement, and Storybook remain approval-required.

docs.title: Graph Intelligence Contract
docs.text:
Source status: project evidence

Graph intelligence helps operators orient inside a project, but it remains generated orientation evidence. It does not replace source files, tests, checked-in docs, approval records, or owner decisions.

The graph ontology, rejected-link ledger, freshness gates, and bounded queries are navigation aids. Graph packets remain orientation evidence until source reads, command evidence, owner review, or accepted gaps support a stronger claim.

docs.title: Layer Contract
docs.text: Signal Role Boundary Ontology Node, edge, observation, contract, and semantic overlay types. Does not guarantee runtime behavior. Coverage map Which languages, docs, schemas, and tests the scanner saw. Does not prove full project coverage. Freshness Digest, timestamp, changed-since, and supersession metadata. A stale graph blocks readiness wording. Rejected links Ledger of conservatively rejected edges. Rejection is caution evidence, not failure by itself. Query packets Bounded neighbors, path, trace, impact, affected_tests, read_order, hotspots, status, search. A query result does not replace source reads.

docs.title: Safe Use
docs.text: Use the graph to choose files to read, estimate blast radius, find hotspots, and prepare handoff. Before an edit, fix, readiness, or release claim, open the owning source and run the current verification gate.

docs.title: Unsafe Use
docs.text: Do not perform mutation, provider calls, browser proof, target apply, or git actions from graph evidence alone. Do not upgrade present_unverified to present_verified without command evidence, owner review, or an accepted gap.

docs.title: Freshness Gates
docs.text: A graph is stale when source files changed after generation, manifest digests do not match, the query packet is not tied to the current graph, or baseline comparison shows unreviewed deltas. The next safe action is to refresh the generated graph only within approved/local scope or read source directly.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Minimum docs gate for this page: source registry marker, docs tests, tools/check_docs.py, strict MkDocs smoke, and git diff --check. Focused graph tests are needed only when scanner, ontology, or query code changes.

docs.title: Guided questions and answer ledger
docs.text:
Source status: project evidence

Sources: plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/product_agent_os/question_protocol.py, plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/product_agent_os/question_ledger.py, plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/product_agent_os/first_run_analysis.py, tests/product_agent_os/test_question_protocol.py, tests/product_agent_os/test_question_ledger.py, Scenarios, Artifact Contracts.

Guided questions help Product-Agent OS ask only what blocks the next safe step, without turning owner answers into hidden requirements or source truth.

docs.title: Question Queue
docs.text:
question_queue is a read-only packet. It can include:

Field Meaning questions Typed list of blocking, recommended and optional questions. next_blocking_question The single blocking question that can be shown first. summary Counts for blocking, recommended, optional and remaining questions. policy.max_blocking_questions_in_first_response Limit: 1. policy.max_total_questions Limit: 8. write_policy read_only.

If several inputs look blocking, extra blocking rows are downgraded to recommended so the first response does not become a questionnaire.

docs.title: First Response
docs.text: first_response shows a summary, next_blocking_question, question_counts, route options and safe_next_action. It should not include the full raw question list as conversational pressure. Ambiguous intake may expose two or three route options, but the completion claim remains not_claimed.

docs.title: Answer Ledger
docs.text:
answer-ledger-template.json and answer ledgers are staged_only artifacts. They make an owner answer a reviewable change instead of an implicit mutation of source docs.

Ledger part Purpose entries Owner answers mapped back to question IDs. artifact_updates Proposed docs/control-plane updates after owner review. summary Accepted, blocked, unanswered and total counts. validation Blocks stale, private, secret-like or malicious answers. write_policy staged_only.

The ledger itself is not approval. Apply answers only through staged artifacts, the existing approval flow, source registry updates and relevant verification.

docs.title: Routing Rules
docs.text: Situation Route One missing owner decision blocks safe next action. Ask one blocking question. Several useful clarifications exist but work can continue safely. Put them in recommended/optional packet fields. Answer changes requirements, scope, acceptance or source truth. Stage docs/control-plane update and run docs checks. Answer requests runtime/browser/provider/git/external action. Stop and request an exact approval packet. Answer includes secrets/private data/raw logs. Block, redact and ask for a sanitized restatement.

docs.title: Status Dashboard Boundary
docs.text: A generated status dashboard can show question ledger summary and artifact update proposals. It remains a generated view only; stale dashboard output, unanswered questions or unreviewed answers cannot support a completion, readiness or release claim.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS plugin
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment

docs.title: Executive overview
docs.text:
Product-Agent OS plugin is a local Codex plugin for projects where Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, subagents, skills, AGENTS.md, hooks, evals and automation candidates need to operate as a governed delivery system instead of a set of one-off prompts.

The plugin helps move a project through a full lifecycle: read-only workspace audit, requirements, plan, ownership, staged infrastructure, verification, review, release packet, learning loop and only then an automation candidate. It does not replace the owner, does not apply autonomous changes by itself and does not turn generated evidence into source of truth.

Need Main page Read the generated graph and cockpit Project Code Graph Understand the live runtime/provider/mutation boundary Live Runtime Governance Know when real testing can start Approval-Bound Real Testing Plan the first real-project pilot Real-Project Pilot Evaluate and modernize agents/skills Agent-Skill Modernization Loop Find local plugin commands CLI Reference See user-facing outputs Artifact Gallery Understand JSON/HTML/ledger evidence artifacts Artifact Contracts Make agents write less custom code and reuse more Professional Code Authoring Standards Prepare release packet and handoff Packaging And Closure

docs.title: G4 Operator-Flow Routes
docs.text:
documentation_refresh_G4-A01 adds four operator-facing routes without claiming that the generated root site is fresh. Until final DOC-M25, these pages are source docs and search/sitemap freshness remains a separate gate.

Need Page Instruction and tool-use compliance Instruction and tool-use compliance Operator command matrix Operator command matrix Guided questions and answer ledger Guided questions and answer ledger Source, cache and active-session state Source, cache and active-session state

Sources: Codex plugins, Build plugins, Agent Skills, Subagents, AGENTS.md, Codex hooks, Agent approvals and security, Codex workflows, Product-Agent Workflows.

docs.title: Current operating boundary
docs.text: Surface Allowed without new approval Forbidden without separate explicit approval Static project graph Read-only scan, staged graph/cockpit, bounded query packets. Treat generated graph as source of truth or mutate target files from graph evidence alone. Local runtime Validate disabled-by-default runtime contract and graph-only fallback. Start live server, expose public routes or add write endpoints. Provider retrieval Stage provider gate/eval contracts and threshold fallback. Perform live external model/API calls or provider calls. Human review and mutation Stage review ledger, diff preview and dry-run mutation plan. Mutate canonical graph without accepted owner decision and rollback proof. Audit and real testing Stage audit/security/observability/readiness packets. Run browser automation, provider pilots, canonical mutation pilots or git release actions.

docs.title: First-Run Walkthrough
docs.text:
The first run should produce a route, not scaffolding. A useful starting prompt:

Use Product-Agent OS for this project: start with a read-only workspace audit, identify lifecycle state, usage_mode, methodology gaps, staged artifacts, verification route, approval boundary and safe_next_action.
Step What the plugin does What the user gets Read-only workspace audit Reads project rules, docs, tests, runtime hints and current diff without changing files. A context map, risk map, source boundaries and evidence gaps. Lifecycle state Classifies the project as intake, requirements, planning, build, review, release or learning. A reasoned explanation for the next step. Methodology selection Maps project risks to DDD, TDD, ADD, FSD, eval-driven gates and related practices. Relevant methods become checks and artifacts instead of dogma. Staged artifacts Proposes REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md or domain packets only when needed. Outputs can be reviewed before any target workspace write. Verification route Names commands, evals, runtime checks, owners and rollback path. Readiness has a concrete evidence path. Approval boundary Separates read/staged proposals from live server launch, browser automation, provider/API calls, canonical mutation and git actions. safe_next_action does not cross approvals.

Generated views are not source of truth: graph, cockpit, dashboard and reports help review, but they do not replace source files, command evidence and owner decisions. The default stop line is: no live server launch, no browser automation, no provider/API calls, no canonical graph mutation and no git stage/commit/push/PR without separate explicit approval.

docs.title: Core capabilities
docs.text:
• Packaged lifecycle skills: orchestrator, discovery auditor, requirements author, implementation planner, team designer, test/eval designer, risk reviewer, release operator, learning loop maintainer and automation promoter.
  • Staged infrastructure renderer for control-plane files, project-scoped .codex/agents/, hook templates, workflows, eval templates, PR/release templates and automation candidates.
  • Safe merge tooling with approval record, manifest validation, workspace-bound paths and rollback support.
  • Project Code Graph, bounded query packets and offline cockpit for navigation without treating generated views as truth.
  • Live/runtime/provider governance with approval packets, redaction, budget, fallback, audit and staged-only evidence.
  • Scenario workflows for first-run intake, bug rescue, greenfield idea shaping, complex system acceleration, PR review readiness, legacy onboarding, API migration, AI/RAG eval regression, native/mobile work, desktop local-first work, data migration, security-sensitive change, CI stabilization and release packaging.
  • Engineering standards layer with product hypothesis, architecture boundary, acceptance scenarios, test/eval-first gates, docs-as-code, metric hardening, evidence-before-completion and release measurement.
  • Professional Code Authoring standards: existing-capability scan, one-line/native candidate, negative dependency rule, deep module check, legacy seam evidence and unsupported code-quality claim ledger.
  • Transcript/session eval runner and fixture eval coverage for expected behavior, forbidden behavior, privacy checks and regression replay without external systems.
  • Self-Verification And Modernization Loop for agents and skills through agent_skill_metrics_loop: target registry, trace intake, dataset quality, grader/judge calibration, scorecard ledger, staged modernization candidates, staged evidence only, no live eval/model/API calls, no active schedules and no self-applied updates.

docs.title: Problems It Solves
docs.text: Problem What the plugin does A long Codex session loses context Moves goal, plan, checks and decisions into control-plane files Requirements live only in chat Creates REQUIREMENTS.md with scope, non-goals and acceptance criteria Planning blends into implementation Requires PLAN.md, ownership, verification and rollback before a build slice Subagents work without boundaries Designs roles through ownership, handoff artifacts and stop conditions Checks are named after the fact Separates deterministic checks in TEST.md and quality gates in EVALS.md The agent writes code without engineering method Adds product hypothesis, architecture boundary, test/eval-first path, docs impact and measurement The agent writes 50 lines instead of reusing capability Requires the Professional Code Authoring checklist: check standard library, framework, config, current dependency or project helper before custom code Project rules are scattered across memory Moves durable rules into AGENTS.md and current decisions into RUNLOG.md Hooks and automations are enabled too early Keeps a staged-first and candidate-only boundary until manual approval It is hard to prove that work was verified Requires evidence: commands, fixture evals, source policy and review findings

docs.title: Who It Fits
docs.text: Scenario Benefit Solo developer Structure a feature quickly and keep acceptance criteria visible Product engineer Move from idea to PR packet through verifiable artifacts Engineering team Split worktrees, roles and write scopes without conflicts AI product team Add an eval-driven loop and source/context policy Governed workspace Preserve approvals, staged writes, rollback and audit trail

docs.title: Main Lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["Idea"] --> B["Workspace audit"]
    B --> C["REQUIREMENTS.md"]
    C --> D["PLAN.md"]
    D --> E["Agent team"]
    E --> F["Build slice"]
    F --> G["TEST.md / EVALS.md"]
    G --> H["Review"]
    H --> I["PR or release packet"]
    I --> J["RUNLOG.md learning"]
    J --> K["Automation candidate"]

The plugin keeps the lifecycle sequential. It should not jump from uninitialized directly to build_active: context, requirements, plan, ownership and quality gates come first.

docs.title: Product workflow gates
docs.text: Gate When it activates Required output Workspace discovery At the start of work or before scope changes Evidence-backed audit, source boundaries, risks and next smallest action Requirements Before implementation Scope, non-goals, acceptance scenarios and evidence owner Planning Before build slice Owned files, forbidden files, commands, expected outputs, rollback and verification Agent/team design Before subagents or parallel work Ownership, handoff artifacts, stop conditions and sequential fallback Review For risky/public-contract/migration/security/data/release work Spec compliance first, then quality/risk review Release Before publish/PR/package action Current checks, artifact manifest, rollback, residual risks and explicit owner approval Learning After a meaningful slice RUNLOG evidence, failures, accepted gaps and modernization candidates

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
• The plugin runs inside Codex. It does not require a separate OpenAI API key and does not start a standalone Agents SDK runner.
  • Infrastructure generation is staged-first: dry-run or staging directory before any target workspace write.
  • Hooks are packaged as templates and examples; they are not silently activated.
  • Automation artifacts are candidate-only until manual workflow is stable and explicitly approved.
  • Secrets, private customer data, raw private chat logs and local absolute paths must not enter docs, fixtures, prompts, memory or templates.

docs.title: Public/Internal Documentation Boundary
docs.text:
Public product pages explain capabilities, user route, outputs, boundaries and next action. Internal evidence pages under docs/sources/ store source/history material, acceptance history and verification packets; they should not be the first route for a new user. Generated site/ output is a rendered copy of source docs and review output, not source of truth.

If a public page references a graph, dashboard, cockpit, scorecard or report, it must say that the artifact is an orientation surface. If a claim affects readiness, release, security or approval, it must route to an owning source: source file, source registry, command/eval/runtime evidence, owner decision or accepted gap.

docs.title: G5 Evidence Quality Routes
docs.text:
documentation_refresh_G5-A01 adds the final source-docs layer before DOC-M25: generated artifact quality, graph evidence, privacy/supply-chain boundaries, local HTML interaction boundaries and residual follow-up.

Route When to open it Generated artifact UX criteria Review generated HTML/report quality for internal review, owner review or future public transfer without claiming browser proof. Graph intelligence contract Use graph packets, ontology, rejected links, freshness or query output for orientation before source reads. Privacy, supply-chain and retention Review cache/session summaries, SBOM, dependency audit, remediation and raw report-retention boundaries. Local HTML interaction boundary Separate local tabs/search/filter/diagram controls from approved browser-proof evidence. Residual follow-up and site freshness Follow G1.1 residuals and the final root site/search/sitemap gate through DOC-M25.

docs.title: Where To Go Next
docs.text:
• Technical details and installation - real files, commands, capabilities and install boundary.
  • Artifact Gallery - user-facing outputs and their trust boundary.
  • Doubt / verifier loop - how completion-skeptic uses a doubt_verification_packet before final completion claims.
  • Real-Project Pilot - first-run operator packet, target consent matrix, success metrics and evidence ledger for a safe real-project pilot.
  • Engineering standards layer - how the plugin applies DDD/FSD/TDD/ADD, docs-as-code and eval-driven quality without turning them into dogma.
  • Methodology intelligence - read-only audit, Delivery Map, recommendations, owner questions and staged artifact boundary.
  • Scenarios and usage modes - first response, minimum artifacts, approval boundary and verification gates for product scenarios.
  • Generated artifact UX criteria - practical checklist for generated HTML/report quality without Storybook/browser proof claim.
  • Graph intelligence contract - ontology, freshness, rejected-link ledger and source-read-before-edit boundary.
  • Privacy, supply-chain and retention - privacy, SBOM/audit/remediation and report-retention approval gates.
  • Local HTML interaction boundary - local controls, no-network policy, fallback and browser-proof packet requirements.
  • Residual follow-up and site freshness - final G1.1 residual routing and DOC-M25 generated-site gate.
  • Behavioral evals - expected behavior, forbidden behavior, fixture eval and transcript/session replay.
  • Codex compatibility - Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, .codex-plugin, skills, MCP and staged hooks support boundary.
  • Diagrams and operating principles - state routing, staged-first merge, approval gates and runtime runner flow.
  • Product-Agent Workflows - general operating model without coupling to the plugin package.

docs.title: Doubt / verifier loop
docs.text:
Doubt / verifier loop is the manual and local-plugin completion gate for "check again" work. The user-facing route is doubt-verification-loop.md: completion-skeptic reads a doubt_verification_packet, checks claims, requirements, evidence and accepted gaps, then returns pass, revise, needs_more_context, blocked_by_approval or accepted_risk.

This page only points to the gate. The documentation records the generated site view; manual pilots, scorecard calibration and any promotion beyond internal/manual use remain a separate stage.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• A real project workspace, source documentation and current project rules.
  • Product intent, constraints, approval boundary and expected evidence.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• A staged Product-Agent OS route with requirements, plan, verification, review and learning artifacts.
  • A clear separation between source-backed evidence and generated review views.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Treating generated evidence as proof can hide stale or unsupported claims.
  • Skipping approvals can turn a safe local workflow into an unauthorized external action.

docs.title: Instruction and tool-use compliance
docs.text:
Source status: official + project evidence

Sources: Agent Skills, Plugins, Build plugins, AGENTS.md, Hooks, Permissions, Subagents, Skill exposure and invocation boundary, docs/superpowers/specs/batch42-instruction-tool-use-compliance-matrix.json.

This page documents how Product-Agent OS should handle instruction compliance, tool-use compliance, skill/plugin exposure and self-learning-loop requests. It does not claim that auto-engagement is already fixed. Current status is planned-only for Batch 42 execution and implemented_source_docs_no_site_rebuild for this documentation page.

docs.title: Checked Layers
docs.text: Layer Proves Does not prove Source bundle The repository contains the plugin, skills, scripts, templates and docs. The skill is available in the installed cache or active session. Installed plugin cache A local installed copy may exist. The current Codex session sees every skill or invokes it implicitly. Active session The session actually received some skill/plugin metadata. The route is correct for every prompt. Route/eval evidence The prompt is classified through the intended lifecycle/compliance path. Config/cache mutation, release readiness or external action approval. Fresh-session proof A new session sees the expected state after changes. Older sessions refreshed automatically.

docs.title: Invocation Policy
docs.text:
Official Codex docs describe explicit invocation, where the user names a skill, and implicit invocation, where the task matches the skill description. Product-Agent OS uses a stricter local policy:

Mode Use when Gate explicit_only High-risk skills, release, automation, external writes, cache/config mutation, provider/API, browser/runtime or security-sensitive work. The user explicitly requests the skill/plugin/agent route. narrow_implicit Read-only discovery, docs maintenance, planning, compliance audit or learning-loop triage when the prompt clearly matches the Product-Agent OS boundary. Route/eval evidence and no-unapproved-actions proof. blocked_implicit Any skill with allow_implicit_invocation: false, unclear ownership or missing evidence. Explicit user request or policy-change approval.

allow_implicit_invocation is policy metadata, not quality proof. Even when implicit invocation is allowed, approval settings, sandbox, permissions, hook trust and external-service auth still apply.

docs.title: No-Auto-Apply Learning Loop
docs.text:
The Product-Agent OS self-learning-loop may record a lesson, candidate rule, skill update candidate, eval follow-up or owner question. It must not itself:

  • change ~/.codex/config.toml, project .codex/config.toml, installed plugin cache or global guidance;
  • activate hooks, automations, MCP servers, an Agents SDK runner or external workflows;
  • stage, commit, push, create a PR, publish, deploy or share a plugin;
  • store secrets, raw private chat logs, customer data or unredacted findings.

Every candidate needs owner review, a rollback/disable path and separate approval.

docs.title: Compliance Packet
docs.text:
A claim that "Product-Agent OS now engages correctly" needs a packet with these fields:

Field Required evidence source_bundle_status Source tree path, manifest/skill list, agent metadata and policy class. installed_cache_status Read-only cache inventory or explicit not-inspected gap. active_session_status Fresh-session exposure, missing skills and restart/new-thread boundary. route_eval_status Prompt fixtures or transcript evals for compliance/tool-use prompts. official_source_status Current official Codex docs checked date and supported/unsupported claims. approval_boundary Exact surfaces that remain approval_required. no_unapproved_actions Cache/config/global/external/git/release/browser/provider/automation flags all false unless explicitly approved.

docs.title: Unsupported Claims
docs.text:
This page does not support claims that:

  • all Product-Agent OS skills are visible in every active session;
  • auto-engagement is fixed;
  • the installed cache has been refreshed;
  • global Codex policy or project config has been changed;
  • hooks are trusted in every new session;
  • the self-learning-loop can mutate skills, memory, rules, hooks or automations automatically;
  • docs/source evidence proves runtime/browser/provider behavior, publication or release readiness.

docs.title: Next Safe Action
docs.text: If an operator sees Product-Agent OS fail to engage for a relevant prompt, the first safe step is a read-only source/cache/session packet, followed by a route/eval packet. Cache refresh, global config writes, plugin sharing, hook trust changes and fresh-session proof remain separate approvals.

docs.title: Live runtime governance
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This page describes the Product-Agent OS governance boundary: from approval packet and data classification to disabled-by-default local runtime, provider gates, review ledger, canonical mutation dry-run, audit/observability, real-testing readiness and runtime QA.

This document is an operator guide. It does not start a live server, run browser automation, perform provider/API calls, mutate the canonical graph or run git stage/commit/push/PR. All generated artifacts are staged evidence only and are not source of truth.

docs.title: Approvals And Source-Of-Truth Boundary
docs.text:
Source of truth remains checked-in Markdown/JSON/JSONL control-plane artifacts, official OpenAI documentation for Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, approvals, sandbox, MCP and project-authored source files. Generated graph/runtime/provider artifacts are review views and evidence packets.

Any live/runtime/provider/mutation step requires an approval packet with:

  • explicit_approval: true;
  • owner and allowed surfaces;
  • data classification and redaction boundary;
  • credential boundary: credentials only through environment or trusted local config, with no secrets in docs, prompts, fixtures, caches or logs;
  • cache policy, TTL, invalidation and deletion proof;
  • token/cost/latency budget and fallback on exceed;
  • eval thresholds;
  • rollback path;
  • residual risks and accepted gaps.

Without a complete approval packet, the action remains approval_required, blocked or degrades to graph-only fallback.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Minimum inputs for live governance:

  • governance packet from project_graph_live_governance.py;
  • local read-only runtime packet from project_graph_live_runtime.py;
  • provider gates for embeddings, reranker/hybrid retrieval and LLM proposals;
  • human review ledger and proposal diff preview;
  • canonical mutation dry-run, journal and rollback proof;
  • audit/security/observability/handoff packets;
  • real-testing readiness, target consent, pilot harness and Codex surface smoke;
  • browser QA, performance budget and stabilization ledger.

Inputs must not include raw secrets, credentials, raw private source bodies, raw private chat logs, private customer data or unredacted PII.

docs.title: Outputs And Artifacts
docs.text:
Expected artifacts are staged evidence packets, not canonical truth:

  • live-runtime-approval.json, data-classification.json, cache/budget policies;
  • live runtime contract with local-only, read-only routes and disabled_by_default_not_started;
  • embedding provider gate and eval baseline;
  • reranker provider gate and hybrid retrieval pipeline;
  • LLM proposal provider gate and safety eval;
  • graph-review-ledger.json and proposal-diff.json;
  • mutation_plan.json, graph-mutation-journal.jsonl and rollback proof;
  • audit-log.jsonl, security-privacy.json, runtime-observability.json, agent-skill-handoff.json;
  • real-testing-readiness.json, real-testing-targets.json, pilot-harness.json, codex-surface-smoke.json, real-testing-pilot-matrix.json;
  • project-code-graph-runtime-browser-qa.json, project-code-graph-performance-budget.json, project-code-graph-stabilization-ledger.json.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Validate governance before any live surface.
  2. Keep runtime disabled by default, local-only, read-only, authenticated where required, with graph-only fallback and clean shutdown evidence before real launch is considered.
  3. Gate embedding provider with redaction, cache, budget and eval threshold. If threshold fails, keep semantic_retrieval_or_graph_only.
  4. Gate reranker and hybrid retrieval with bounded candidates, explainable fusion and no canonical mutation.
  5. Gate LLM proposal provider as proposal-only structured JSON. Provider output is never canonical fact and unsafe output routes to incident/fallback.
  6. Route proposals through human review ledger: accepted, rejected or accepted_gap with evidence refs.
  7. Use canonical mutation only as dry-run mutation planning unless accepted proposal, conflict checks, append-only journal and rollback proof are present.
  8. Record redacted append-only audit events, negative security/privacy checks, runtime health, latency, provider errors, budget usage, degraded mode and handoff ownership.
  9. Prove real-testing readiness with owner-approved target/data policy, dry-run pilot harness, Codex App/CLI/IDE extension smoke and use-case pilot mapping.
  10. Record browser QA expectations, console/network checks, mobile overflow, generated-view labels, source-boundary labels, performance budget and stabilization status.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Governance is acceptable only when evidence shows:

  • provider_call_allowed: false and external_call_performed: false unless a later separately approved execution packet changes the specific surface;
  • no live server launch during docs/governance preparation;
  • no browser automation during docs/governance preparation;
  • no canonical graph mutation outside approved dry-run/staged copy paths;
  • no git stage/commit/push/PR;
  • generated artifacts are labeled as staged evidence and not source of truth;
  • budget breach disables live layer or records owner-accepted gap;
  • no open P0/P1 before closure;
  • fallback remains usable when live/provider layers are disabled.

For docs-only preparation, read-only inspection is enough unless a focused docs verification owner later runs targeted checks.

docs.title: Risks And Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Generated views may look authoritative if source-boundary and generated-view labels are missing.
  • Provider payloads can leak secrets, paths or raw source if redaction is bypassed.
  • Credentials can leak if stored in docs, fixtures, prompts, caches or logs.
  • Cache can make stale evidence look current without fingerprint invalidation and deletion proof.
  • Provider eval can be misleading if it lacks baseline, threshold or fallback.
  • LLM proposals can hallucinate or overstate unsupported claims.
  • Human review ledger is invalid if accepted proposals lack owner decision and evidence refs.
  • Canonical mutation is unsafe without dry-run, conflict checks, journal and rollback proof.
  • Runtime QA is incomplete if mobile overflow, console/network, source-boundary labels or performance budget are missing.

docs.title: Next Action
docs.text: Use this page as the governance checklist before any approval-bound real-testing action. The next safe artifact is an approval packet that names exactly one planned action, its owner, allowed target, data policy, command scope, rollback and verification evidence.

docs.title: Local HTML Interaction Boundary
docs.text:
Source status: project evidence

Generated HTML may include local tabs, search, filters, diagrams, and disclosure controls. These interactions are allowed only as an offline review surface and are not runtime/browser proof without a separately approved evidence packet.

The default policy is local-only: no external scripts, no provider calls, no telemetry, no target mutation, and no hidden readiness wording.

docs.title: Allowed Interactions
docs.text: Interaction Condition Tabs and section navigation Work inside one generated file and do not hide claim ceilings. Search/filter Search embedded data only, without network requests. Diagram controls Use local/vendor assets or static fallback. Copy/open helpers Do not mutate files, start shells, or send data. JS-disabled fallback Main information remains readable without script execution.

docs.title: Forbidden Interactions
docs.text:
• External fetch, provider/API call, telemetry, or beacon.
  • File mutation, cleanup execution, shell command, or target apply.
  • Hiding unsupported claims, stale warnings, or approval boundaries.
  • Browser-proof wording without approved browser run, screenshots, console/network evidence, and viewport notes.

docs.title: Browser-Proof Packet
docs.text: If the owner approves browser proof, evidence must name URL/path, tool, viewport set, console errors, network requests, screenshots, source-boundary labels, mobile overflow status, JS-disabled fallback, and cleanup. Without that packet, status remains static_docs_only.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: For this docs slice, static docs checks and strict MkDocs smoke are enough. Real browser automation, screenshots, WCAG proof, visual regression, and external network checks remain approval-required.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS methodology intelligence
docs.text:
Source status: local product design + experiment

Sources: Product-Agent OS architecture, Product-Agent OS scenarios, Behavioral evals, Codex workflows, Agent approvals and security.

Methodology intelligence is the read-only layer that turns workspace evidence into practical delivery guidance. It reads files, control-plane artifacts and route signals, then returns methodology_packet, finish_options, owner_questions, safe_next_action, methodology_synthesis and source_artifact_ledger when they are useful.

Those packets are recommendation and routing evidence. They do not mutate target projects, enable hooks, activate automations, call providers or approve external writes.

docs.title: What It Solves
docs.text:
Product-agent work often fails in two opposite ways: it starts coding before the project contract is clear, or it forces heavy methodology onto simple work. Methodology intelligence gives Product-Agent OS a middle path:

  • read the existing workspace before prescribing process;
  • detect which engineering standards apply;
  • keep lightweight work lightweight;
  • require deeper evidence only for real risk;
  • return owner questions when evidence is missing;
  • stage recommendations instead of silently changing the target workspace.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• user intent or route hint;
  • read-only workspace inventory;
  • AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md;
  • architecture docs, ADRs, API contracts, database docs, Storybook/FSD signals, CI, evals, metrics, release artifacts and security/privacy evidence when present;
  • current source policy, sandbox, approvals and external-system boundaries;
  • accepted gaps and previous failure notes.

docs.title: Project Scanning Principle
docs.text:
The scan is evidence-first and non-mutating. Product-Agent OS reads the user's workspace, combines repository signals with user intent, classifies maturity/complexity and activates only the methodology gates that reduce real project risk. The scan does not write target files, call providers, activate hooks, create automations, mutate canonical graph sources or treat generated dashboards as proof.

Scan layer Examples of signals How Product-Agent OS uses it Workspace inventory Manifests, source folders, tests, docs, CI, release and config files. Classifies simple, standard, complex or high-risk work and avoids heavy process for tiny tasks. Stack and surface detection Frontend, backend, native/mobile, desktop, API, database, AI/RAG, docs, automation and release surfaces. Routes work to the relevant product, architecture, quality, data, AI, security and operations domains. Contract evidence OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, gRPC, JSON Schema, Pact, generated SDKs and webhooks. Activates API contract-first, compatibility, error/auth and contract-test gates. Data evidence Schemas, migrations, ORM models, DB docs, data contracts, backfills and production-data hints. Activates migration planning, data dictionary, rollback, backup/restore, classification and access approval gates. AI/RAG evidence Prompts, evals, model decisions, tools, retrieval config, vector data, datasets and agent traces. Activates baseline evals, prompt/model/tool contracts, grounding, dataset governance and cost/latency checks. Security and privacy evidence Auth, secrets, PII, payments, permissions, compliance, SBOM, audit and security review. Activates threat surface, ASVS/SSDF/SAMM, authz negative tests, privacy and supply-chain review. Codex control-plane evidence AGENTS.md, requirements/plan/test/eval/runlog files, subagents, skills, MCP, hooks and automation candidates. Activates model/reasoning policy, handoffs, ownership, approvals, memory policy and automation maturity checks. User intent Feature, bug, release, migration, AI behavior, PR review, production readiness or regulated risk. Adds intent-only risk when repo evidence is incomplete and asks owner questions instead of guessing.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Purpose methodology_applicability Records which domains apply, why, and what evidence is missing. methodology_packet Route-ready evidence bundle for the next worker. finish_options Safe options such as answer, stage proposal, request approval, run focused verification or stop on gap. owner_questions Smallest blocking questions for decisions that cannot be inferred from source files. safe_next_action The next move that respects source policy, sandbox, approvals and evidence. source_artifact_ledger Mapping from recommendations to the source artifacts that support them. methodology_synthesis Grouped recommendations across domains with risk-aware ordering.

docs.title: Methodology Integration Map
docs.text:
G4 clarifies how methodology signals become operator artifacts. Detection alone remains present_unverified: methodology can propose a route, but it does not turn that route into readiness, source truth or approval.

Signal layer Output field Operator artifact Claim boundary Domain applicability recommendation_groups Grouped recommendations with owner/consumer domains. Recommendation only until current evidence or owner review exists. Source backing source_artifact_ledger Paths, packets, tests or accepted gaps that support each recommendation. Missing source creates present_unverified, not a completion claim. Missing decisions owner_questions One or more owner questions routed to guided question protocol. Answers require staged ledger and owner review before source promotion. Next move safe_next_action Read, stage, request approval, verify or stop on gap. Must not cross sandbox, approvals, provider/API, browser/runtime or git boundaries. API contract signal Redocly not_applicable / OpenAPI-trigger status API docs/lint gate only when an OpenAPI source contract exists. Redocly enforcement is not run or claimed from generic API wording.

This map keeps methodology intelligence tied to real outputs instead of abstract method lists. It also gives downstream agents a stable handoff: which evidence was read, which artifacts are recommended, which owner decision is missing and which action is still safe.

docs.title: Methodology Domains
docs.text:
Domain When it applies Minimum evidence Business & Product Product behavior, MVP, launch, pricing, onboarding, growth or value claims change. User/problem, non-goals, acceptance scenario, metric, guardrail or explicit gap. Requirements & Domain Behavior, workflow, rules, public contract, domain language or multi-slice scope is unclear. Requirement registry, acceptance scenarios, owner questions, business rules, domain model or accepted gap. Solution architecture Boundaries, services, public contracts, runtime topology or irreversible design change. Scope, boundary, decision, alternatives, rollback and owner evidence. Quality, Testing & Evals Ready/done/fixed/works/release claims, behavior changes, regressions, evals or runtime quality matter. Test/eval matrix, risk-based scope, current evidence, manual QA evidence or explicit test gap. Codex / Agentic Workflow Codex App, CLI, IDE extension, subagents, skills, MCP, hooks, plugins, memory, automation or long-running agent work applies. Control plane, source-of-truth boundary, model/reasoning policy, handoff contract, approval boundary and automation maturity evidence. Frontend User-visible UI, interaction, accessibility, visual QA or performance change. User flow, component states, browser/runtime evidence, visual/accessibility gap or proof. Backend Service behavior, jobs, queues, auth, errors, observability or rollback paths. Runtime behavior, failure mode, health/logging, tests and rollback evidence. API & Integrations HTTP API, event contract, SDK, webhook, external provider or consumer contract. Source-of-truth contract, consumer map, compatibility and external-write approval boundary. Database & Data Schema, migration, lineage, retention, sensitive data or production data. Inventory, dictionary, migration plan, rollback/backup, data classification and production access boundary. LLM / AI / RAG Prompt/model/tool/RAG/eval behavior changes. Baseline/current eval, prompt/model/tool contracts, grounding, traces, cost/latency and incident path. Security, Privacy & Compliance Authn/authz, secrets, PII, payments, abuse, supply chain, audit or compliance overlay. Threat surface, risk review, negative tests, secrets/data/privacy evidence, scan status and owner review. Delivery, Release & Operations Publish, deploy, package, release, automation, incidents or operations readiness. Release scope, versioning, changelog, artifact manifest, rollout, rollback, SLO/observability and approval evidence.

These 12 methodology domains are the catalog inputs. Cross-domain synthesis is the output layer that groups overlapping recommendations, resolves conflicts, records owner/consumer domains, checks semantic evidence sufficiency and returns a risk-aware safe_next_action.

Readiness statuses are explicit: not_applicable, applicable_missing, present_unverified, present_verified, proposal_staged, explicit_gap_accepted and approval_required. Detection alone can only create present_unverified; readiness needs current evidence, owner review or an accepted gap.

docs.title: Methodology Examples
docs.text:
Methodology or practice When it activates Example application in Product-Agent OS Product discovery and metric design Product value, launch, growth, onboarding or monetization claims change. Product hypothesis, value proposition, metric spec, guardrails and owner signoff. Requirements engineering Behavior, workflow, rules, public contract or multi-slice scope is unclear. Requirement registry, non-goals, acceptance scenarios, owner questions and traceability. ATDD / BDD acceptance scenarios User-visible behavior or domain correctness needs shared examples. Example scenarios linked to tests, evals, manual QA evidence or explicit gaps. DDD Domain language, bounded contexts, business rules, events, workflows or multi-team ownership matter. Domain model, ubiquitous language, context map, invariants and domain-to-architecture traceability; simple CRUD does not force DDD. Architecture-driven design and ADRs Quality attributes, runtime topology, contracts, persistence, deployment or trust boundaries change. Architecture scope, context/container boundaries, tradeoffs, fitness checks, decision records and rollback assumptions. C4 / arc42-style architecture views Context, container, component, deployment or runtime views are needed. Architecture overview, trust-boundary map, diagrams and architecture review record. TDD / Red-Green-Refactor Behavior-changing code, shared logic, bug fixes, migrations, API/schema/UI logic or risky refactors are planned. Test-first evidence where practical, explicit gap where not, and regression evidence linked to the slice. Risk-based testing and QA Ready, done, fixed, works or release claims need evidence. Unit, integration, contract, runtime, visual, manual QA, CI and flaky-test evidence by blast radius. FSD and frontend boundary discipline Web UI structure, features, widgets, pages, shared components or frontend ownership boundaries exist. Feature boundary review, state matrix, visual QA, accessibility, responsive checks and performance budget. API contract-first delivery OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, gRPC, webhooks, generated clients or external consumers are involved. API inventory, consumer map, error catalog, auth matrix, compatibility record and contract tests. Eval-driven AI / RAG development Prompts, models, tools, retrieval, grounding, AI behavior, datasets or safety claims change. AI behavior spec, baseline eval, prompt contract, model decision, RAG source inventory, rerun evidence and residual risk. Security engineering and release operations Sensitive data, auth, compliance, deploy, publish, CI/CD, production data or external systems are involved. Threat surface, risk review, privacy impact, release readiness, artifact manifest, rollout, rollback and runbook evidence.

Packet identifiers and exact contract phrases:

  • Security/Privacy/Compliance uses security_privacy_compliance_contract_present, data-classification-register.md and vulnerability-response-record.md.
  • Delivery/Release/Operations uses delivery_release_operations_contract_present, release-artifact-manifest.md, operations-runbook.md, post-release-review.md, release mode policy and owner-reviewed release evidence sufficiency.
  • Cross-Domain Synthesis uses recommendation_groups, owner domains, consumer domains, risk-aware safe next action and approval-bound behavior.

docs.title: Read-Only Process
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["Workspace evidence"] --> B["Applicability scan"]
    B --> C["Risk and false-positive check"]
    C --> D["Domain packets"]
    D --> E["Synthesis"]
    E --> F{"Evidence sufficient?"}
    F -->|Yes| G["safe_next_action"]
    F -->|No| H["owner_questions or accepted gap"]
    G --> I{"Write required?"}
    I -->|No| J["Report only"]
    I -->|Yes| K["Staged proposal"]
    K --> L["Explicit approval boundary"]

docs.title: Approval Boundary
docs.text:
The staged artifact boundary is strict:

  • methodology recommendations can produce a report, owner question or staged proposal;
  • release, deploy, publish, DB access, security scan, external write, hook activation and automation activation stay blocked until explicit owner approval and current evidence exist;
  • generated reports and dashboards are evidence surfaces, not sources of truth;
  • detection alone creates present_unverified, not readiness;
  • high-risk, production, release, security-sensitive, AI behavior and public-contract work needs owner-reviewed evidence or explicit accepted gap.

docs.title: False-Positive Control
docs.text:
Methodology intelligence must avoid forced ceremony:

  • docs-only changes do not need a full product/architecture/release process unless they change public contracts or publishing;
  • simple CRUD does not force DDD;
  • backend/native work does not force FSD;
  • hosted docs, CI activation and DB introspection remain approval-required;
  • source-like words in file paths are not enough to infer security, release or data readiness;
  • a generated artifact is not safety proof until the relevant source or owner evidence is current.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Use focused verification when methodology behavior changes:

python -m unittest tests.product_agent_os.test_fixture_eval_runner -v
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py
python tools\check_docs.py

Use broader verification when lifecycle skills, templates or routing logic change:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\validate_codex_compatibility.py
python tools\check_docs.py

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• A read-only audit can still be wrong if workspace evidence is stale, incomplete or misleading.
  • Over-eager methodology routing can force heavy process onto simple work; every recommendation needs applicability and false-positive handling.
  • Generated reports can become stale quickly; completion or release claims still need fresh command, runtime, eval or owner evidence.
  • Domain packet schema can evolve as real projects expose missing fields; additive compatibility should be preserved.

Next artifact: use Scenarios to choose the operating route and Behavioral evals to validate shortcut resistance.

docs.title: Operator command matrix
docs.text:
Source status: project evidence

Sources: plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/run_first_project_analysis.py, plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/product_agent_os/first_run_analysis.py, plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/scan_project_code_graph.py, tools/docs_install.ps1, tools/docs_node_install.ps1, tools/docs_vale_install.ps1, tools/docs_link_secret_install.ps1, tools/docs_mermaid_install.ps1, tools/docs_dependency_audit.ps1, .docs-tools/node/package.json, CLI Reference.

This matrix answers the operator question: which command is safe preview, which command writes only generated artifacts, and which command needs separate approval.
