docs.title: Packaging and closure
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This page records packaging, documentation closure and owner handoff for Product-Agent OS. Closure makes the system understandable, verifiable and ready for approval-bound real testing, but it does not start live execution by itself.

The closure packet describes updated source docs, packaging/install smoke definition, required verification, generated site/ rebuild rule and the approval packet for the next execution step.

docs.title: Source-of-truth boundary
docs.text:
Source of truth:

  • checked-in Product-Agent OS source docs;
  • accepted implementation plan and docs closure scope;
  • source registry and control-plane artifacts after their separate owner-approved/docs-maintainer slice;
  • current command evidence from docs tests, tools/check_docs.py, strict MkDocs, optional full closure and packaging/install smoke;
  • explicit owner approval packets for any later live/browser/provider/canonical/git action.

Not source of truth:

  • generated site/ pages by themselves;
  • packaging/install smoke as a release or publish approval;
  • plugin-cache contents without checked-in source comparison;
  • staged evidence without owner review;
  • planning matrix presence without implementation and verification evidence.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Closure consumes:

  • modernization loop docs and metrics-report boundary;
  • project code graph, cockpit, static search, backend gate, semantic retrieval, deterministic proposal and extension-closure docs;
  • governance/runtime/provider/review/mutation/audit/real-testing-readiness/runtime-QA evidence;
  • accepted docs closure scope;
  • plugin README install and packaging guidance;
  • MkDocs navigation/docs-check requirements from the Builder/Tester slice;
  • known gaps: docs-maintainer plugin-cache gap and Mermaid external asset gap when still unresolved.

docs.title: Outputs And Artifacts
docs.text:
Expected closure outputs:

  • updated docs pages for Product-Agent OS source docs;
  • source registry/backlog/control-plane sync from the owning docs-maintainer slice;
  • updated docs contract tests and tools/check_docs.py from the owning Builder/Tester slice;
  • regenerated site/ using the regular MkDocs site_dir;
  • packaging/install smoke evidence packet;
  • approval packet draft for real testing execution;
  • explicit list of actions not performed without approval.

This worker page covers only the docs packet. It does not update navigation, tests, registry, README, site/, git state or plugin distribution.

docs.title: Packaging And Install Smoke
docs.text:
Packaging/install smoke is evidence only. It should answer:

  • plugin manifest exists and points to the expected bundled skills/MCP metadata;
  • checked-in docs-maintainer guidance is available, or the docs-maintainer plugin-cache gap is recorded;
  • local install path or marketplace candidate can be inspected without publishing;
  • staged templates and scripts remain package-readable;
  • no secrets, credentials or private data are bundled;
  • plugin hooks and automations remain inactive unless explicitly approved;
  • install smoke result records command, environment, output summary, gaps and residual risk.

Install smoke does not publish the plugin, write to external systems, create a marketplace release, upload artifacts, activate hooks, create automations or approve real testing execution.

docs.title: Workflow And Cadence
docs.text:
Closure verification order is fixed:

  1. Source docs.
  2. Source registry.
  3. Docs contract tests.
  4. python tools\check_docs.py.
  5. Strict MkDocs build.
  6. Optional full closure.
  7. Packaging/install smoke.
  8. Approval-bound handoff packet.

The generated documentation site must be rebuilt with the regular MkDocs site_dir:

python -m mkdocs build --strict

Using only a disposable --site-dir is not enough when closure explicitly requires site/ refresh.

docs.title: Required Verification
docs.text:
Minimum closure evidence:

  • focused docs contract test result for new pages, required source status and safety boundaries;
  • python tools\check_docs.py;
  • strict MkDocs build into site/;
  • git diff --check;
  • packaging/install smoke packet;
  • explicit approval-bound handoff packet.

Optional full closure when risk or scope requires:

  • full unittest with long timeout;
  • fixture eval;
  • transcript eval;
  • Codex compatibility validation;
  • reviewer pass over generated site/, long-line IA and accepted gaps.

Do not claim closure is complete unless the current run has matching command evidence or clearly states which verification was not run.

docs.title: Approval-Bound Handoff
docs.text:
Real testing execution remains approval-bound. The handoff packet should list separate approval surfaces:

  • approved_local_runtime_launch;
  • actual_browser_automation_smoke;
  • approved_provider_api_pilot;
  • approved_canonical_mutation_pilot;
  • explicit_git_release_pr_action.

Each surface needs owner, approved target, data policy, redaction/cache/budget boundary where relevant, rollback/disable path, expected evidence, residual risk and stop condition.

Real testing can start only after governance, runtime contract, audit/observability, target consent, QA/performance/stabilization and packaging/docs closure evidence are current.

docs.title: Actions Not Performed Without Approval
docs.text:
Packaging and closure work does not perform these actions without a separate explicit owner approval:

  • no live server launch;
  • no browser automation;
  • no provider calls;
  • no live external model/API calls;
  • no canonical graph mutation;
  • no plugin publication;
  • no external write;
  • no package registry or marketplace upload;
  • no hook activation;
  • no active schedules, automations or GitHub Actions creation;
  • no git add, commit, push or PR;
  • no real testing execution.

docs.title: Risks And Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Treating packaging smoke as publish approval can create an unauthorized release.
  • Rebuilding a disposable site but not site/ leaves stale generated docs.
  • Missing docs registry/control-plane sync can make source-backed claims drift.
  • Plugin-cache mismatch can hide missing checked-in skills, especially docs-maintainer.
  • Mermaid external asset dependency can break offline documentation expectations.
  • Real testing can accidentally start live execution if approval surfaces are bundled together instead of separated.

docs.title: Next Action
docs.text: After docs and packaging evidence are current, the next safe artifact is the approval packet draft. Real testing execution, provider/API calls, canonical mutation and git release/PR actions remain blocked until their separate approvals exist.

docs.title: Privacy, Supply-Chain, And Report Retention
docs.text:
Source status: project evidence

This page defines the storage boundary for source, installed cache, active session, supply-chain reports, and raw findings. It does not authorize cache refresh, dependency remediation, full SBOM, vulnerability audit, or report retention.

docs.title: Storable Evidence
docs.text: Data Allowed form Forbidden form Source/cache/session Counts, filenames, versions, hashes, exposure status, unsupported claims. Raw private source bodies or private chat logs. Synthetic fixtures Synthetic names, bounded snippets, redacted paths. Customer data, secrets, credentials, tokens, unredacted PII. Dependency evidence Package names, versions, advisory counts, pip check, scoped SBOM summary. Remediation claim without command evidence and rollback. Raw findings Summary with severity, owner, redaction, and retention decision. Retained raw scanner output without approval.

docs.title: Approval Boundaries
docs.text: Python vulnerability audit, complete repository SBOM, dependency remediation, npm audit fix, broad secret/link scans, external URL crawling, and raw report retention require separate approval. Each action must name scope, command, output path, retention policy, redaction policy, owner, and rollback.

docs.title: Distribution Labels
docs.text: For local-only/internal R&D, use compact summaries and redacted evidence. Public/team trust labels should not be added automatically: they require owner decision and source registry update.

docs.title: Report Retention
docs.text: If a report contains raw findings, local paths, dependency advisory details, or private target names, the default state is not_retained. Retaining a report needs an owner-approved retention window, redaction status, and cleanup path.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: This docs slice verifies only the documented boundary: docs unittest, tools/check_docs.py, JSON packet validation, strict MkDocs smoke, and git diff --check. It does not run vulnerability audit, SBOM completion, remediation, or external crawling.

docs.title: Project Code Graph
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

This page describes the local Project Code Graph layer in Product-Agent OS. It helps readers navigate a codebase through a generated graph, query packets, cockpit and local indexes, but it does not replace source files, checked-in documentation, tests, approval records or owner decisions.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Project Code Graph provides offline project navigation:

  • scans the workspace and builds a file-level graph with file nodes, contains edges, fingerprints, spans and observation records;
  • adds Python AST overlays for package/module/class/function/method, import/call/test edges and unresolved call summaries;
  • adds docs/contracts/schema overlays for Markdown, OpenAPI/Swagger, AsyncAPI, DBML, SQL, JSON, YAML, Mermaid and PlantUML;
  • emits bounded query packets for graph reading without rereading raw source bodies;
  • renders a static cockpit as a generated view for overview navigation;
  • adds extension surfaces for search index, backend gate, semantic retrieval, deterministic LLM proposals and closure evidence.

docs.title: Source-of-truth boundary
docs.text:
Generated graph artifacts are not source of truth. They are orientation evidence and cache-bound generated views.

Source of truth remains in project source files, checked-in documentation, schema/contracts, tests, approval packets, RUNLOG/TEST/EVALS evidence and explicit owner decisions. Graph, cockpit HTML/JSON, search/backend/semantic indexes, LLM proposal packets and extension closure reports must not be used as standalone proof of architecture, runtime behavior, coverage, security posture or release readiness.

Without separate explicit approval, live server, browser automation, provider/API calls, canonical graph mutation, git stage/commit/push/PR and external writes are forbidden. Query and stage modes must remain local, deterministic and generated-artifact-only.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Main inputs:

  • <workspace> for scan_project_code_graph.py;
  • optional previous manifest/graph for freshness, provenance and temporal edge invalidation/supersession;
  • existing project-code-graph.json or project-code-graph.jsonl for query mode;
  • approval packets only for approval-bound extension modes: backend, semantic index, LLM proposals and extension closure evidence.

The scanner reads local project files, but graph/query packets exclude raw source bodies by default and redact absolute paths or secret-like values. Stage output must be an explicit directory, preferably outside the target workspace.

docs.title: Outputs And Artifacts
docs.text:
Base artifacts:

  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-code-graph.json - main graph JSON with write_policy: read_only, metadata, nodes, edges and observations.
  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-code-graph.jsonl - bounded JSONL serialization for agent consumption.
  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-cockpit.html - offline generated cockpit, review-only.
  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-cockpit.json - structured cockpit model and projection.
  • Graph analysis report from project_graph_analysis.py - source-free orientation report, not completeness proof.
  • Status/runtime summaries from query packets and cockpit model - compact health/orientation summaries.

Extension artifacts:

  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-code-graph-search-index.json - offline static search index with stale-index blocking and rollback path.
  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-code-graph-backend.json - disabled-by-default local query backend store; no active server by default.
  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-code-graph-semantic-index.json - local deterministic semantic retrieval cache; external embedding/cross-encoder providers remain approval-bound.
  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-code-graph-llm-proposals.json - staged local deterministic semantic extraction proposals with provenance, uncertainty and unsupported-claim labels.
  • .codex/product-agent-os/project-code-graph-extension-closure.json - extension verification, rollback/data deletion proof and graph-only fallback report.

docs.title: Cockpit Surfaces
docs.text:
The cockpit collects graph, file and code orientation surfaces into one offline generated view. It is useful for first project reading, but it remains a review surface:

  • Project Map shows graph projection, filters, selected-node evidence and a fallback static table.
  • Code Intelligence shows hotspots, read_order, trace/impact packets and Code Flow.
  • Contracts shows API, schema, diagram and explicit contract overlays.
  • Quality & Metrics shows tests, fixtures, affected-test packets and quality evidence pointers.
  • Operations & Risk shows stale flags, ambiguous edges, scale budget and visual QA hints.
  • Proposal Ledger shows proposal-only items, owner-review boundary and unsupported-claim labels.

Recommended reading order:

  1. Start with Project Map to identify large file/code clusters and selected-node evidence.
  2. Open Code Intelligence and use read_order as a hint for which files to read first.
  3. Check Contracts when a change touches APIs, schemas, diagrams, OpenAPI/Swagger, AsyncAPI, DBML, SQL, JSON or YAML overlays.
  4. Check Quality & Metrics to understand which tests or fixture references might be affected.
  5. Before claiming behavior, readiness or a fix, open source files and run the current verification gates; the cockpit does not prove those claims by itself.

The schema/contract surface shows where the scanner found parseable contracts and schema-like inputs. It does not replace contract tests, owner-approved API changes, source registry updates or runtime evidence.

docs.title: Static Visual Boundary
docs.text:
The current cockpit renders a local-only static fallback: SVG/table projection, selected-node panel, filters and safe embedded JSON. project_graph_visual_model.py marks Graphology/Sigma as not_bundled_static_fallback; the renderer does not fetch external assets.

Cosmos.gl/WebGL is not a confirmed runtime/browser capability of this layer. Until separate approved browser/runtime proof exists, docs must not claim interactive WebGL rendering, canvas performance, browser screenshots, WCAG visual proof or generated site freshness. If a future renderer adds Cosmos.gl, Graphology, Sigma or another browser layer, it must preserve static fallback, local/vendor boundary, source labels, visual QA evidence and a separate approval gate.

docs.title: Operating Modes And Commands
docs.text:
Base scanner and stage-only generation:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --dry-run
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --stage C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage

Graph-only queries read an existing JSON/JSONL artifact:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --query status --graph C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage\.codex\product-agent-os\project-code-graph.json
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --query neighbors --graph C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage\.codex\product-agent-os\project-code-graph.json --node-id function:app.main.main
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --query search --graph C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage\.codex\product-agent-os\project-code-graph.json --text "runtime"

Supported query kinds include neighbors, path, trace, impact, affected_tests, changed_since, why_changed, read_order, hotspots, node, status and search. Query packets are bounded by --max-results, --max-depth, --max-tokens, filters and hub suppression.

Extension modes:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --build-index --stage C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage --graph C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage\.codex\product-agent-os\project-code-graph.json
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --build-backend --stage C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage --graph C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage\.codex\product-agent-os\project-code-graph.json --backend-approval approval.json
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --build-semantic-index --stage C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage --graph C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage\.codex\product-agent-os\project-code-graph.json --semantic-approval approval.json
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --build-llm-proposals --stage C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage --graph C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage\.codex\product-agent-os\project-code-graph.json --llm-approval approval.json
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\scan_project_code_graph.py <workspace> --verify-extensions --stage C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage --graph C:\tmp\product-agent-os-graph-stage\.codex\product-agent-os\project-code-graph.json --verification-evidence evidence.json

Disable modes remove generated extension artifacts under the stage root: --disable-backend, --disable-semantic-index, --disable-llm-proposals and --disable-extensions.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Minimum verification evidence for changes to this layer:

  • graph schema validation through project_graph_ontology.py;
  • redaction checks: no raw source bodies, no absolute local paths, no secret-like values in returned packets;
  • query packet checks for supported query kinds and bounded payloads;
  • cockpit validation: eight-page structure, generated-view wording, no external assets, static fallback path;
  • search-quality evals: symbol recall, top-k/MRR, trace labels, affected-test precision, edge density and thresholds;
  • extension validation: stale index blocking, disabled backend lifecycle, local deterministic semantic retrieval, proposal labels, rollback/data deletion proof and graph-only fallback.

Prior closure evidence recorded focused/full checks for graph/cockpit/search/status/runtime, fixture/lifecycle/docs suites, full unittest, fixture eval, transcript eval, Codex compatibility, strict MkDocs and diff hygiene. For new changes, rerun only the smallest relevant checks unless ownership expands.

docs.title: Risks And Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Dynamic dispatch, framework wiring, runtime routes and actual execution behavior are not fully proven by static graph edges.
  • Semantic hits and LLM proposals are orientation evidence; unsupported or uncertain claims must stay labeled and reviewable.
  • Stale graph/index artifacts can mislead readers if source files changed after generation.
  • Local backend store is a generated file-store and remains disabled by default; it is not a production server.
  • Cockpit is static generated output; visual completeness does not prove source correctness.
  • Stage directories inside a target workspace can blur source/generated boundaries unless explicitly approved.
  • Future provider-backed retrieval, live runtime, canonical mutation and release actions require separate approval packets and rollback plans.

docs.title: Related Pages And Next Action
docs.text:
• docs/product-agent-os/technical.md - current technical summary for Product-Agent OS implementation status.
  • docs/product-agent-os/live-runtime-governance.md - live/runtime/provider governance boundary.
  • docs/product-agent-os/artifact-contracts.md - expected artifact schema reference when available.
  • docs/product-agent-os/cli-reference.md - script/mode reference when available.

Next action for a maintainer: use this page as the reader-facing Project Code Graph guide, then link it from MkDocs navigation and source registry when the public docs map changes.

docs.title: Real-Project Pilot
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This page describes a safe first Product-Agent OS pilot on a real project. It is for an operator who wants to validate plugin value without reading internal ledgers and without hidden changes in the target workspace.

The pilot is read-only and staged-first by default. It produces a first-run operator packet, target consent matrix, success metrics and evidence ledger. It does not launch a live server, run browser automation, call providers or APIs, mutate canonical graph sources, perform external writes or run git stage/commit/push/PR without separate explicit approval.

docs.title: First-Run Operator Packet
docs.text:
Starting prompt:

Use Product-Agent OS for this project. Run a read-only first-run audit and return lifecycle state, usage_mode, risk map, methodology route, staged artifacts, verification route, approval boundary, rollback or remove path, evidence gaps and safe_next_action. Do not write files, start servers, call providers, run browser automation, mutate canonical sources or use git actions.

Expected first response:

Field Required content lifecycle_state Current stage: intake, requirements, planning, build, review, release or learning. usage_mode Nearest scenario: web/frontend, backend/API, docs-only, AI/RAG, data/migration, PR/review or automation/release. source_boundary Which files are source of truth and which generated views are orientation evidence only. staged_artifact_route Which artifacts are proposed and where they will be staged before target writes. verification_route Commands, evals, runtime checks or owner review that will prove the next step. approval_boundary Which actions require separate approval. rollback_remove_path How to remove staged outputs and return to the previous state. safe_next_action One next step that does not cross approvals.

The staged artifact route should use relative project-scoped destinations such as .codex/product-agent-os/pilots/<pilot-id>/, .codex/artifact-templates/ or proposed control-plane files. Absolute user-specific paths, secrets, raw private prompts, credentials, customer data and unredacted logs are not allowed.

generation, cache writes .codex/product-agent-os/pilots/ai-rag/ provider or private corpus access requested data/migration Data owner + release owner synthetic or staging dataset synthetic fixtures or approved redacted data schema/docs inventory and dry-run plan review production writes, destructive migration, external export .codex/product-agent-os/pilots/data-migration/ rollback or backup path missing PR/review Engineering owner existing branch or PR diff diff-only, no unrelated files read-only review, test command proposal staging, commit, push or PR mutation .codex/product-agent-os/pilots/pr-review/ unrelated dirty changes block scope automation/release Release owner + security reviewer staging workflow definition no credentials, least privilege automation candidate review, release packet draft active schedule, GitHub Actions enablement, deploy, publish .codex/product-agent-os/pilots/automation-release/ irreversible external action requested

Owner consent must name owner, target class, data policy, allowed commands, blocked commands, evidence destination and stop condition. A pilot target is not approved just because it appears in this matrix; the owner still approves the exact run.

docs.title: Success Criteria And Metrics
docs.text:
Pilot success is measured with reviewable criteria rather than a single score.

Metric Passing signal Counter-metric time_to_first_route The operator receives lifecycle state, risk map and safe next action quickly enough for the project context. A fast answer that misses approval or data policy boundaries fails. route_accuracy Suggested route matches repo type, current lifecycle and owner intent. Generic methodology lecture or wrong runtime route fails. artifact_usefulness Proposed artifacts are few, reviewable and tied to source files or verification. Artifact sprawl or internal ledger dumping fails. methodology_selection_precision DDD, TDD, eval, architecture or release gates appear only when relevant. Methodology forced without project evidence fails. owner_question_usefulness Questions are few, blocking and tied to a decision the owner can make. Broad intake questionnaire fails. false_positive_rate Generated claims are marked source-backed, proposal, accepted gap or unsupported. Generated views treated as source of truth fail. evidence_sufficiency Each readiness claim names command evidence, source evidence or owner review. Completion claim without fresh evidence fails.

Accepted-gap rules: each gap needs owner, reason, reduced evidence path, residual risk, follow-up condition and review date. An accepted gap cannot authorize a live server, browser automation, provider call, canonical mutation, external write or git action.

docs.title: Pilot Harness And Evidence Ledger
docs.text:
The harness is a dry-run plan, not active automation.

Required ledger fields:

Field Required content pilot_id Stable id for the pilot run. target_class Archetype and target class from the consent matrix. read_only_pilot_commands Commands that only inspect source, docs, tests, config or generated staged outputs. staged_output_locations Relative destinations for proposed artifacts and evidence. runlog_evidence_schema Time, command, exit code, files inspected, files proposed, approvals checked, residual risks and next action. screenshot_log_redaction Rule for redacting screenshots, logs and console output when visual/runtime evidence is separately approved. cleanup_steps How staged outputs, generated caches and pilot evidence can be removed. approval_checks Confirmation that no approval-bound action is performed by default.

The harness must not become active automation, a live server launcher, a provider gateway, a browser runner, a canonical graph writer, an external writer or a git release tool. It may propose those actions only as separate approval packets.

docs.title: Rollback And Cache Recovery Procedure
docs.text:
Before a production pilot, the operator needs a clear rollback/remove path for the plugin and local cache. This procedure does not approve deletion, cache mutation, global config mutation, hook activation/deactivation, automation, publication or git actions. It names what must be confirmed before a separate owner approval.

Step Required boundary pre_rollback_read_only_inspection Inspect the installed plugin cache path, package name/version, expected file count, skill count, manifest, .mcp.json, backup path, staged source digest and active hook/automation status. rollback_evidence_preservation Preserve approval text, inspected paths, before/after counts, command transcript, backup pointer, moved-aside path and residual risks in the staged evidence destination. installed_plugin_remove_path Any remove action uses move-aside/quarantine for the exact approved version path only; silent delete is not allowed. stale_cache_restore_path Restore only from a named backup tied to evidence; after restore, verify file count, skill count and manifest status. cache_clear_recovery_path Cache clear/replace is allowed only for the exact cache root and version id; the path must be resolved and checked before any write. disable_hooks_automations_if_ever_approved If hooks or automations were ever activated, the disable path must name the exact surface, owner, command boundary, evidence target and rollback owner. post_restore_verification After an approved mutation, run cache inspection, Codex compatibility smoke, docs/test checks when docs changed, diff hygiene and record residual risks.

Stop immediately on missing owner approval, unresolved path outside the approved cache root, missing backup, digest/count mismatch, destructive delete request, active automation without owner, secret/customer data in evidence, external write request, provider/API call, live server/browser request, canonical mutation or git stage/commit/push/PR request.

docs.title: What Not To Expect
docs.text:
• No automatic installation, publication or plugin-cache refresh.
  • No production data access.
  • No live server launch.
  • No browser automation.
  • No provider/API calls.
  • No canonical graph mutation.
  • No external writes or active automation.
  • No git stage/commit/push/PR.

docs.title: Private Sample Pilot Evidence
docs.text:
The first owner-approved docs-only pilot ran read-only on a private sample workspace. Reader-facing docs do not expose internal execution labels, private target labels or absolute user-specific paths; exact labels and staged evidence paths remain only in source-owned ledgers.

Field Evidence target_class docs-only / legacy onboarding staged_evidence_root recorded in source-owned ledger usage_mode legacy_onboarding after a clean docs-only intent complexity_profile guided-small source_policy_status blocked staged_outputs infrastructure, status dashboard and project graph validated outside the target target_apply_status blocked until target source-policy/control-plane cleanup target_workspace_mutation_performed false

What this proves: after the local cache refresh, Product-Agent OS can run read-only discovery, methodology audit, runtime routing, staged artifact rendering and static content checks on a real docs-only target. What it does not prove: production readiness, public/team release readiness, target apply safety or product success. The next safe target step is to add or accept gaps for Source status, source registry/control-plane ownership and the smallest local verification contract inside the target.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: For docs-only pilot design changes, use docs contract tests, documentation structure checks, strict MkDocs when navigation/search/sitemap changes and diff hygiene. For any future real pilot execution, add target-specific command evidence, owner approval, rollback proof and redaction review before claiming readiness.

docs.title: Next Action
docs.text: Use the first-run operator packet, then choose one pilot archetype and prepare a target-specific approval packet. The safe default remains read-only inventory plus staged artifacts.

docs.title: Residual Follow-Up And Site Freshness
docs.text:
Source status: project evidence

This page closes G5 residual routing: which G1.1 follow-ups remain approval-required, how to summarize real-target static comparison without exposing private targets, and why final DOC-M25 does not run automatically.

docs.title: Residual Routing
docs.text: Residual Owning row Current state Root site, search, and sitemap freshness DOC-M25 approval_required_not_run after G2-G5 source updates. Browser Mermaid/HTML proof DOC-M08, DOC-M23, DOC-M29 Approval-required; static smoke does not prove browser rendering. Broad lint/format/Vale enforcement DOC-M21, DOC-M26, DOC-M30 Advisory or scoped-only until owner thresholds exist. Link/secret scans and raw report retention DOC-M24, DOC-M30 Do not run broad scans or retain raw reports without approval. Python audit, full SBOM, Node remediation DOC-M24, DOC-M30 Do not claim remediation or complete SBOM without commands and rollback. Docusaurus, Storybook, Structurizr DOC-M21, DOC-M30 Deferred trigger governance; no install.

docs.title: Static Comparison Summary
docs.text: For private or real-target comparison, store only redacted target class, run IDs, digest deltas, page/key deltas, unsupported claims preserved, actions performed, and explicit no-unapproved-actions. Do not publish target names, raw paths, private screenshots, raw source excerpts, or private data.

docs.title: Final DOC-M25
docs.text: Final DOC-M25 may rebuild root site only after separate approval. Until then, source docs may be current while generated site, search index, and sitemap remain stale/unsupported for new G2-G5 pages.

docs.title: DOC-M25 Closure Update
docs.text: DOC-M25 is closed through documentation_refresh_DOC-M25-A01 with status implemented_root_site_search_sitemap_freshness; documentation_refresh_DOC-M25-A02 refreshes generated root site, search index and sitemap after T15 source docs/control-plane sync. Root site, search index and sitemap include the former DOC_M25_PENDING_SITE_PAGES; browser proof, broad scans, dependency remediation, raw report retention, publication, release, deploy and git actions remain outside this closure.

docs.title: Closure Rule
docs.text: G5 can close source docs, nav, tests, registry, and control-plane sync without a root site freshness claim. Full generated-site freshness requires current strict MkDocs build to root site, search/sitemap evidence, and git diff --check in the same approved slice.

docs.title: Product-Agent OS scenarios
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

Sources: Codex workflows, Codex use cases, Agent approvals and security, Product-Agent OS plugin, Behavioral evals, Codex compatibility.

This page answers a practical question: which route should the Product-Agent OS plugin choose when Codex App, CLI or IDE extension sees a real workspace and the user asks for a verifiable outcome, not just "write code".

A scenario does not replace the lifecycle. It chooses the first small step, minimum artifacts, approval boundary and verification gates. If evidence is missing, the route must return a gap, not readiness.

docs.title: Operator Route Map
docs.text:
Scenarios are route decisions, not permission to run live systems. Each route must name source context, expected evidence, approval boundary and stop condition before it hands work to a subagent, skill or implementation slice.

Route When to choose Minimum evidence Stop condition code_graph_orientation Need to understand code/docs topology before build or review. Existing source files plus generated graph/cockpit packet labeled as orientation evidence. Do not claim source truth from generated graph; read source before implementation claims. live_runtime_read_only Need to check local runtime contract or graph-only API fallback. Governance packet and disabled runtime contract. Stop before live server launch unless separate approval packet exists. provider_retrieval_eval Need to evaluate embedding/reranker/LLM provider benefit. Redaction, cache, budget, baseline and threshold fallback packet. Stop before any provider/live external model/API call without explicit approval. canonical_graph_mutation_review Need to check proposal acceptance and mutation readiness. Human review ledger, proposal diff, mutation dry-run plan and rollback proof. Stop before canonical graph mutation unless owner accepted the proposal and rollback evidence is current. real_testing_approval Need to move from staged evidence to controlled real testing. Target/data owner approval, runtime/browser/provider/mutation/git action packet and rollback plan. Stop unless the specific action is approved; approvals are not bundled.

docs.title: G4 Operator Flows
docs.text:
G4 adds four system routes. They do not approve cache refresh, global config writes, live runtime, browser automation, provider/API calls, target mutation, git, release or automation.

Route When to use Evidence boundary instruction_tool_use_compliance Check when a Product-Agent OS skill/plugin route may be selected implicitly and when it needs an explicit user request. Uses official Codex docs, allow_implicit_invocation, explicit_only, narrow_implicit and blocked_implicit; fresh-session proof remains separate. operator_command_matrix Choose a safe command for first-run analysis, graph/cockpit or docs-tooling smoke. Uses help/current command evidence, stages only generated artifacts, and keeps broad scans/root site rebuild approval-bound. guided_question_answer_ledger Ask a question without turning intake into a long questionnaire. Enforces one blocking question maximum; answers_require_staged_ledger_and_owner_review before source promotion. source_cache_session_state Understand why source, installed cache and active session can diverge. Requires read-only comparison fields and fresh-session proof before any fixed/ready claim. professional_code_authoring Limit custom code, dependency debt, shallow wrappers or risky refactor in a non-mechanical coding task. Uses Professional Code Authoring Standards, checklist evidence and shortcut evals; remains a source contract until runtime/owner-pilot proof exists.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• user goal or intent_hint, if passed to the Codex runtime runner;
  • read-only workspace audit: files, stack, test/build commands, docs, CI, contracts and control-plane files;
  • current AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, PLAN.md, TEST.md, EVALS.md, RUNLOG.md;
  • source policy, sandbox, approvals and known external-system boundaries;
  • previous failure notes, if already recorded in RUNLOG.md.

Key routing fields include finish_options and safe_next_action; they tell the next worker whether to answer, stage a proposal, request approval, run focused verification or stop on an evidence gap.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• usage_mode.primary, secondary mode, confidence and routing reasons;
  • first response: one closest useful step without broad scaffold, rewrite or external mutation;
  • minimum artifacts: concrete files or packets needed before build/review/release;
  • approval boundary: what is read-only, staged-only or approval-required;
  • verification gates: commands, evals, screenshots, logs, owner review or accepted gap;
  • residual risk when route is based on detection rather than verified evidence.

docs.title: Guided Question Protocol And Status Dashboard
docs.text:
Guided question protocol uses typed question_queue packets so the first response can show only next_blocking_question, question_counts and question_summary. It asks at most one blocking question, keeps recommended and optional questions in the packet, and routes answers into artifacts or accepted gaps.

The status snapshot is the JSON source for a generated dashboard view. The dashboard stages .codex/product-agent-os/status.html and .codex/product-agent-os/status.json through the existing approval flow. status.html is a generated view only; underlying artifacts remain the source material.

docs.title: Self-Verification And Modernization Loop
docs.text: The agent_skill_metrics_loop route reviews agents, skills, prompt/policy packs, router/tool policy and harness-version behavior. It starts from a read-only target registry, explicit run evidence, trace intake, dataset quality checks, local grader summaries and grader/judge calibration. It can stage scorecard ledger records, daily or weekly packets, agent-skill-evaluation-report.html and modernization candidates, but every output is staged evidence only.

docs.title: Project Code Graph And Cockpit
docs.text:
The graph route provides a read-only project graph foundation and generated cockpit for route orientation. It can produce staged graph JSON/JSONL with file-level nodes, overlays, conservative dependency edges, controlled schema validation, manifest freshness, observation lineage, partition scopes and aliases.

The cockpit renderer can stage offline .codex/product-agent-os/project-cockpit.html and .codex/product-agent-os/project-cockpit.json review surfaces with top-level pages, Code Flow, static projection, local vendor boundary, graph filters, selected-node evidence, fallback tables, mobile layout and no external assets.

Generated graph artifacts, runtime graph summaries, analysis reports and HTML cockpit views are review evidence only. The scanner and renderer do not mutate target workspaces.

docs.title: G5 Evidence-Quality Routes
docs.text:
Use these routes when the question is not about new plugin behavior, but about the quality and boundaries of generated evidence.

route_id When it applies Minimum result Boundary generated_artifact_ux_criteria HTML/report output looks too diagnostic or is being prepared for owner review. Quality checklist, claim ceilings, Vale advisory status, Storybook trigger status. Browser proof and Storybook install remain approval_required. graph_intelligence_contract Graph packets, ontology, rejected links, freshness or query packets are used. Orientation summary, stale/rejected-link handling, source-read-before-edit reminder. Graph packets do not replace source reads or authorize mutation. privacy_supply_chain_retention Cache/session evidence, SBOM, vulnerability audit, remediation or raw reports are discussed. Redaction and retention boundary, approval gates, unsupported claims. Broad scans, remediation and raw report retention require separate approval. local_html_interaction_boundary Generated HTML includes tabs, search, filters or diagrams. Local-only interaction rules, no-network policy, fallback and browser-proof packet fields. Static checks are not browser proof. residual_follow_up_site_freshness G1.1 residuals or final DOC-M25 need closure. Residual routing table, private-target redaction policy, site freshness gate. Root site, search and sitemap are current after documentation_refresh_DOC-M25-A01; documentation_refresh_DOC-M25-A02 refreshes them after T15 source sync; browser proof remains separate.

docs.title: Scenario Matrix
docs.text: usage_mode When it applies first response minimum artifacts approval boundary verification gates first-run-intake Empty workspace, broken verification, existing control-plane or complex first launch. Name mode, confidence, next smallest action and evidence gaps. Intake summary, lifecycle state, next action. No scaffold, broad fix or parallel work before route is accepted. Read-only audit, control-plane check, source policy. bug_rescue User reports broken behavior, failing tests or regression. Reproduce or isolate before changing code. bug-rescue-report.md, failure evidence, root-cause hypothesis. No fix claim without reproduction evidence. Failing command/log, focused regression check, current evidence. greenfield_idea Idea-stage or empty product direction. Shape one vertical slice before scaffold. greenfield-idea-brief.md, selected direction, non-goals. Scaffold requires explicit approval. Acceptance scenarios, first slice plan, lightweight-mode decision. complex_system_acceleration Existing multi-surface app, integrations, multiple services or unclear ownership. Build map before parallelization. integration-catalog.md, ownership split, release gates. No parallel work with overlapping files or unclear external-system owners. Integration inventory, ownership review, release risk gates. pr_review Review or merge-readiness request. Stay read-only and review changed files. PR review readiness, changed-files map, pr-risk-review.md. No push, PR creation, merge or external comment without approval. Two-stage review: spec compliance before quality/risk. legacy_onboarding Old, undocumented or unknown repository. Orient before refactor. onboarding-map.md, entry points, run commands, docs debt. No cleanup/refactor until map and verification status are explicit. Present-unverified labels, source map, run command evidence. api_migration HTTP API, event contract, generated client or consumer change. Plan compatibility before implementation. migration-plan.md, api-contract-review.md, consumers, rollout. Release or breaking change needs owner review and approval. Contract check, backward compatibility, deprecation and rollout evidence. ai_eval_regression AI/RAG quality, prompt, model, retrieval, dataset or judge changes. Baseline first. ai-eval-spec.md, dataset policy, rubric, thresholds. No quality claim from inspection-only evidence. Baseline, rerun command, latency/cost/grounding and failure examples. native_mobile_feature iOS, Android or native mobile behavior. Record platform assumptions before implementation. Platform runtime check, permissions, offline/device plan. Permission, signing or store changes require approval. Build command, simulator/emulator or device logs, screenshots, manual gap. desktop_local_first Desktop app, filesystem, local DB, indexing or packaging. Map local data and OS assumptions first. Local data risk note, runtime log check, recovery path. Filesystem access, packaging, signing and distribution require approval. App logs, build/run command, privacy and rollback evidence. data_migration Schema, backfill, sensitive data, retention or production data risk. Plan migration and rollback before execution. migration-plan.md, database-dictionary.md, data quality checks. Production DB/data access and migration execution require approval. Dry run, backup, validation, owner review, rollback evidence. security_sensitive_change Authn/authz, payment, billing, secrets, PII, abuse controls or permissions. Threat surface and owner review before build. security-risk-review.md, approval boundary, rollback plan. Security scans or external security mutations only when explicitly requested. Tests, audit logging, rate limit, privacy and owner review evidence. ci_stabilization Failing, flaky or unstable CI. Gather failure evidence before changing code. ci-stabilization-report.md, failing job, local reproduction. Remote CI reruns, settings and branch rules require approval. Logs, deterministic/flaky classification, isolation plan, rerun evidence. release_packaging Package, SDK, plugin, app, mobile, desktop or open-source release. Build release readiness before publish. release-readiness.md, package metadata, changelog, artifacts. Publishing, tagging, release creation, upload or package registry mutation require approval. Build/test/docs evidence, security/license notes, rollback and owner review. docs_only Documentation update without behavior change. Update source-backed docs and run docs checks. Source status, affected docs, registry entry when source-backed claims changed. Hosted docs, CI activation and sharing changes require approval. python tools\check_docs.py, strict MkDocs when nav/build-sensitive. standard_feature Bounded feature work without special scenario risk. Use normal lifecycle route. Requirements, plan, test/eval evidence. Writes follow sandbox and project approval policy. Unit/integration/contract checks, docs impact, review. professional_code_authoring Non-mechanical code work where the smallest safe implementation matters. Check reuse before custom code. Coding-standard checklist, existing-capability scan, one-line/native candidate, dependency and legacy-seam decisions. No hook/runtime/automation activation from route selection. Focused tests/evals/review evidence plus unsupported-claim ledger. maintenance Small upkeep, formatting or status sync. Keep scope mechanical and evidence explicit. RUNLOG note or control-plane sync. No unrelated refactor. Focused command or explicit inspection-only gap.

docs.title: Database & Data Methodology Routing
docs.text: Database/data work keeps data_migration as the route name and adds a dedicated Database & Data methodology packet when schema, migration, ORM, warehouse, data quality, lineage, retention, backup/restore or production-data signals appear. Production data access, DB introspection, migration execution, destructive cleanup, backup restore and retention mutation are approval-required.

docs.title: Backend Methodology Routing
docs.text: Backend methodology routing applies when service behavior, background jobs, queues, auth, error handling, observability, deployment or rollback behavior changes. Minimum staged artifacts include backend-service-overview.md, backend-runtime-behavior.md, runtime/failure evidence, observability evidence, security evidence and rollback evidence.

docs.title: LLM / AI / RAG Methodology Routing
docs.text: AI/RAG work keeps ai_eval_regression as the route name and adds a dedicated LLM / AI / RAG methodology packet when prompts, models, eval configs, structured outputs, tool/function/MCP calls, RAG corpora, retrieval, vector stores, embeddings, grounding, agent traces, guardrails or latency/cost signals appear. Live model calls, external eval services, vector DB access, raw prompts/traces/customer text, tool writes, shell/money/data exposure and irreversible side effects are approval-required.

docs.title: API & Integrations Methodology Routing
docs.text:
API & Integrations methodology routing applies when HTTP APIs, event contracts, webhooks, generated SDKs or external providers change. Minimum staged artifacts include api-inventory.md, api-contract-review.md, api-consumer-map.md, api-contract-test-matrix.md, external-integration-approval.md and compatibility/security/error/event/SDK evidence.

External writes are not automatic actions; they require an explicit approval boundary.

docs.title: Security, Privacy & Compliance Methodology Routing
docs.text:
Security-sensitive work keeps security_sensitive_change as the route name and adds a dedicated Security, Privacy & Compliance methodology packet when authn/authz, permissions, secrets, PII, sensitive data, payment/billing, abuse controls, audit logging, supply chain, SBOM/provenance, CI permissions, AI/tool security, external writes, production data, policy changes or compliance overlays appear.

Approval boundary stays explicit: payment/billing, production data, secret rotation, policy changes, external security-system mutations, external writes, publish actions and Codex Security scans are not automatic actions.

docs.title: Delivery, Release & Operations Methodology Routing
docs.text:
Release packaging keeps release_packaging as the route name and adds a dedicated Delivery, Release & Operations methodology packet when release, deploy, publish, package, versioning, changelog, artifact, rollout, rollback, CI/CD environment, release mode policy, platform distribution evidence, release communication, SLO/observability, runbook, incident, postmortem, release integrity or automation promotion signals appear.

Approval boundary stays explicit: publish, tag, release creation, artifact upload, deploy, package registry mutation, marketplace/store submission, CI/CD environment changes and active automation are not automatic actions.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Run route and fixture checks after scenario behavior changes:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py
python tools\check_docs.py

Run broader checks after lifecycle skills, templates or route logic change:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\validate_codex_compatibility.py
python tools\check_docs.py

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• A route can be plausible but wrong when workspace evidence is stale.
  • Scenario detection can force heavy process onto simple work unless false-positive guards remain active.
  • Generated dashboards and graphs can look authoritative; source-boundary labels must remain visible.
  • Approval for one surface must not imply approval for another.

Next artifact: use Behavioral evals to test route behavior, Development standards to select evidence gates and Professional Code Authoring Standards to inspect code-writing gates.

docs.title: Self-Learning Loop
docs.text:
Source status: official + experiment

Self-Learning Loop is the manual-first Product-Agent OS improvement loop for local evidence, redacted owner feedback, metrics ledgers and review-only candidates. It is not an autonomous learning system. The default path does not call providers or models, create Codex App automations, enable hooks, write to target workspaces or apply candidates automatically.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Create a staged state proposal outside the target workspace:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\init_self_learning_state.py . --stage <stage-dir-outside-workspace> --installed-at 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z

Check due status without writing state:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\check_self_learning_due.py . --dry-run --state-file <stage-dir-outside-workspace>\.codex\product-agent-os\self-learning-state.json

Run the manual loop as staged evidence:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_self_learning_loop.py . --stage <stage-dir-outside-workspace> --state-file <state-file> --metrics-ledger <redacted-metrics.jsonl> --feedback-ledger <redacted-feedback.jsonl>

Export optional Promptfoo and HALO-style review packets without running a provider:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\export_self_learning_promptfoo.py . --stage <stage-dir-outside-workspace>

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["Owner approval for manual pilot"] --> B["init_self_learning_state.py --stage"]
    B --> C["Staged self-learning-state.json proposal"]
    C --> D["check_self_learning_due.py --state-file"]
    D --> E{"Due?"}
    E -->|"due"| F["run_self_learning_loop.py --stage"]
    E -->|"not_due / disabled / invalid"| G["Report blocker, no analysis"]
    F --> H["Scope packet"]
    F --> I["Metrics summary"]
    F --> J["Redacted feedback summary"]
    I --> K["Review-only candidate summary"]
    J --> K
    K --> L["Progress JSON/HTML and run packet"]
    K --> M["Owner review gate"]
    M -->|"separate approval only"| N["Future staged repair or target update"]
    M -->|"default"| O["No auto-apply, no target write"]

docs.title: State And Status
docs.text:
The proposed state path is .codex/product-agent-os/self-learning-state.json, with schema self_learning_state_v1. The initializer stages this file and reports state_written: false; a workspace write remains a separate owner-approved action.

Status Meaning Safe next action state_invalid State is missing, malformed or schema-invalid. Stage a state initializer packet; do not write state without approval. disabled The owner disabled the loop or cadence. Record the blocker; the owner must change state explicitly. not_due State is valid but cadence is not due. Do not apply anything; keep the due packet if useful. due Manual run is available. Run --dry-run or --stage. ready_for_owner_review Evidence packet is generated; candidates remain review-only. Owner review; apply/provider/automation requires new approval.

docs.title: Inputs And Outputs
docs.text:
Allowed inputs are Product-Agent OS scope packets, explicit state files, redacted owner feedback JSONL, metrics JSONL with synthetic or redacted privacy status, checked-in docs, plans, eval summaries and accepted gaps. Raw chat logs, raw transcripts, private payloads, secrets, credentials, unredacted PII, hidden telemetry and provider output without approval are forbidden.

Key staged outputs:

Artifact Role Boundary .codex/product-agent-os/self-learning-state.json Proposed initial state. Stage-only until owner approval. .codex/product-agent-os/self-learning/state-initializer-packet.json Scope, proposed state and validation packet. No schedule, provider or target write. .codex/product-agent-os/self-learning/runs/<run_id>/self-learning-run-packet.json Manual run evidence packet. Candidate-only; no auto-apply. .codex/product-agent-os/self-learning/evals/eval-cases.json Durable eval cases. Synthetic/redacted; no Promptfoo run claim. .codex/product-agent-os/self-learning/evals/failure-taxonomy.json Failure routing taxonomy. Routing evidence, not incident completeness. .codex/product-agent-os/self-learning/evals/promptfooconfig.yaml Optional Promptfoo-compatible config. Provider run requires separate approval. .codex/product-agent-os/self-learning/evals/halo-recommendation-packet.json HALO-style recommendation packet. Local recommendation only; no HALO service call.

docs.title: Eval And Repair Layer
docs.text:
The current failure taxonomy covers state/scope blockers, missing evidence before completion, wrong skill or surface selection, unsafe approval boundary crossing, stale docs or registry, weak evals, raw private context risk, missing rollback and staged repair validation failures.

Promptfoo integration is export-only by default. The adapter writes prompts, tests and assertions but does not execute a provider. HALO-style packets translate eval cases into recommendations with hypothesis, recommended action, learning objective, expected metric delta, guardrails and rollback.

self_learning_repair.py defines a Codex staged repair worker contract without auto-apply. The task contract names candidate id, objective, allowed files, forbidden files, validation commands, rollback target and privacy boundary; the result packet names changed files, validation results, summary and unsupported claims. Validators block absolute paths, private refs, out-of-allowlist changes, auto_apply, provider calls and target workspace writes.

sequenceDiagram
    participant Owner
    participant Loop as Self-Learning Loop
    participant Worker as Codex staged repair worker
    participant Review as Owner review
    Owner->>Loop: approve candidate review
    Loop->>Worker: staged repair task contract
    Worker->>Worker: local allowed-file patch proposal
    Worker->>Review: staged repair result packet
    Review-->>Loop: approve / reject / request changes

docs.title: B44-S7 Evidence
docs.text:
B44-S7-SELF-LEARNING-MANUAL-PILOT-A01 is recorded in docs/superpowers/specs/batch44-self-learning-loop-approved-manual-pilot-summary.json. It shows that the state initializer reached ready_for_owner_review, the runner used state_source: explicit_state_file, one redacted feedback row and one metrics row were consumed, two review-only candidates were produced, the Promptfoo export produced 8 eval cases, the taxonomy has 9 failure classes and the HALO-style packet has 6 local recommendations.

Accepted gaps: this is one manual pilot, not promotion evidence; Promptfoo was exported but not executed; the HALO-style packet was generated locally, without a HALO service call; generated HTML and reports remain review evidence.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Focused checks:

python -m unittest tests.product_agent_os.test_self_learning_extensions -v
python -m unittest tests.product_agent_os.test_self_learning_state -v

Docs/control-plane checks:

python -m unittest tests.product_agent_os.test_product_agent_os_docs -v
python tools\check_docs.py
git diff --check

docs.title: Execution-loop diagnostics
docs.text: The manual loop also measures time to first target diff, agent count, review/repair cycles, unchanged command repeats, control-plane writes before acceptance, target/test churn, compaction, stale lifecycle markers, mixed skill sources and projection conflicts. A budget breach produces intervention_required and a stop-or-narrow recommendation; it never edits prompts, skills, config, hooks or automation automatically. Missing records mean insufficient_evidence, not a successful run.

docs.title: Source, cache and active-session state
docs.text:
Source status: official + project evidence

Sources: Agent Skills, Plugins, Build plugins, Skill exposure and invocation boundary, docs/superpowers/specs/batch42-instruction-tool-use-compliance-matrix.json.

Product-Agent OS separates three similar but different states: source tree, installed cache and active Codex session. Diagnostics often go wrong when a file on disk is treated as runtime exposure.

docs.title: State Model
docs.text: State Example evidence Allowed conclusion Source tree plugins/product-agent-os/skills/*/SKILL.md, scripts, templates, docs. Capability exists in repository source. Packaged plugin .codex-plugin/plugin.json, plugin metadata, bundled skills/apps/MCP/hook config. Capability can be packaged or installed through the plugin route. Installed cache Local installed plugin copy and skill files. Capability may be available to Codex after install/restart, subject to enablement. Active session Current session skill list, plugin/app/tool exposure, loaded instructions. Capability is visible in this session. Route evidence Prompt fixture, transcript eval, current response or runtime route packet. Capability was selected for this prompt class.

docs.title: Read-only Comparison Packet
docs.text:
Before any cache refresh or global config change, create a read-only packet:

Field Meaning source_skill_count Count and names from repository source. cache_skill_count Count and names from installed cache, or not_inspected. active_session_exposure Skills/plugins/tools visible in the current or fresh session. policy_flags allow_implicit_invocation, explicit-only gates and forbidden automatic surfaces. restart_boundary Whether a new thread, app restart or CLI restart is required for proof. unsupported_claims Claims that remain unproved. next_safe_action Smallest non-mutating action or exact approval needed.

Do not store local absolute user paths, raw private prompts, raw logs, secrets, tokens or unredacted sensitive findings in public docs or examples.

docs.title: No Auto-Repair
docs.text:
The comparison packet does not authorize:

  • plugin cache write or refresh;
  • global Codex config write;
  • project .codex/config.toml mutation;
  • hook trust change;
  • MCP/app connector install;
  • active automation creation;
  • fresh-session proof claim without actually starting a fresh session.

If repair is needed, route it as a separate approval with owner, target surface, rollback, verification and no-unapproved-actions proof.

docs.title: Fresh-session Proof
docs.text:
A fresh-session proof should record what changed between old and new context:

  1. Source evidence used.
  2. Cache/install evidence used.
  3. Session start or restart boundary.
  4. Visible skills/plugins/tools.
  5. Prompt used for route smoke.
  6. Resulting route and unsupported claims.
  7. Residual risk if current session remains stale.

Until this exists, use present_unverified, planned-only or approval_required instead of fixed/ready language.

docs.title: Technical features and installation
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: Codex plugins, Build plugins, Agent Skills, Subagents, Codex MCP, Codex hooks, AGENTS.md, Codex with Agents SDK, Product-Agent OS architecture.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Product-Agent OS is a local Codex plugin package. Use it to stage control-plane artifacts, route product-agent workflows, run deterministic validators and package repeatable methods as skills. Installation does not grant permission to start live systems, call providers, mutate target repositories or publish anything.

This quick-start page is not the full command-policy matrix. The broader list of docs-tooling commands, install/runtime variants and approval-state cases belongs to later DOC-M26; final root site freshness belongs to DOC-M25 after G2-G5.

docs.title: Capability status
docs.text:
Capability Status Boundary Plugin manifest Implemented. Declares package capabilities only. Lifecycle skills Implemented. Recommend and stage work; they do not override approvals. Staged infrastructure renderer Implemented. Writes to explicit staging output, not silently into the target workspace. Fixture eval runner Implemented. Local deterministic evidence only. Transcript eval runner Implemented. Uses synthetic/redacted transcripts and privacy checks. Codex compatibility validator Implemented. Checks package shape, not live operational readiness. Graph/cockpit orientation Staged evidence route. Generated views are not source of truth. Live runtime/provider/mutation actions Approval-bound. Disabled until a specific owner-approved packet exists. Professional Code Authoring Source contract. Uses Professional Code Authoring Standards; does not prove real agent behavior or runtime enforcement.

The cockpit surface groups graph data into reader-facing views: Project Map, Code Intelligence, Contracts, Quality & Metrics, Operations & Risk and Proposal Ledger. The recommended path is graph, guided read order, source files, then tests/evidence. The cockpit and query packets do not prove runtime behavior, browser behavior, source freshness, contract correctness, test pass status or release readiness.

docs.title: Operator contract
docs.text:
The operator must keep actions explicit:

  • read source files before claims;
  • stage proposals before target mutation;
  • keep Source status: on non-index docs;
  • run focused verification after meaningful changes;
  • keep live server launch, browser automation, provider/API calls, canonical graph mutation and git actions approval-bound;
  • never store secrets, credentials, customer data or raw private chats in docs, prompts, fixtures or templates.

docs.title: Package layout
docs.text:
The package lives under plugins/product-agent-os/ and includes:

  • .codex-plugin/plugin.json for Codex plugin metadata;
  • skills under skills/;
  • templates and packaged examples under assets/templates/;
  • eval fixtures under assets/eval-fixtures/;
  • scripts for rendering, validation and eval execution;
  • docs under docs/product-agent-os/ and docs/product-agent/;
  • local tests under tests/product_agent_os/.

docs.title: Bundled MCP
docs.text: MCP declarations are integration boundaries, not blanket permission. A declared MCP server or tool must still respect sandbox, approvals, source policy, external-system ownership and current verification evidence.

docs.title: Packaged skills
docs.text: Packaged skills cover requirements authoring, implementation planning, test/eval design, risk review, docs maintenance, release packaging and agent team design. Each skill should name trigger, inputs, outputs, verification, failure modes and stop conditions.

docs.title: Generated infrastructure
docs.text:
Generated infrastructure is staged-first. Use dry run before staging:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\render_infrastructure.py <workspace> --dry-run

Use staging only with an explicit output directory:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\render_infrastructure.py <workspace> --stage <output-dir>

The renderer must preserve user-authored files outside managed sections. Existing unmarked AGENTS.md, .codex/config.toml, hooks, workflows and automation files are user content and should be staged as companion proposals unless an approved merge path exists.

Packaged hooks and automations are examples or candidates. They must not be activated silently.

The generated .codex/config.toml includes a product-agent-os-project permission profile. The profile keeps .codex itself read-only while opening only Product-Agent OS project artifact directories such as .codex/agents, .codex/skills, .codex/workflows, .codex/artifact-templates, .codex/evals, .codex/runlogs, .codex/automation-candidates, .codex/pr, .codex/product-agent-os and .codex/eval-reports. Sensitive control surfaces such as .codex/config.toml, .codex/hooks, .codex/automations and .codex/plugins remain approval-bound.

On Windows, a managed permission profile can still be blocked by inherited filesystem ACL deny entries on .codex. Check the scoped Product-Agent OS paths with:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\prepare_windows_codex_permissions.py <workspace>

Apply the scoped ACL preparation only with explicit owner approval:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\prepare_windows_codex_permissions.py <workspace> --apply

The apply mode creates only the approved Product-Agent OS .codex subdirectories, disables inherited ACLs on those subdirectories and removes inherited deny ACEs from the same subdirectories. It does not open the .codex root, config, hooks, automations or plugin cache by default.

Generated infrastructure also includes the system file hygiene surfaces:

  • .codex/workflows/system-file-hygiene-audit.md;
  • .codex/artifact-templates/system-file-hygiene-report.md;
  • .codex/automation-candidates/system-file-hygiene-audit.md.

Professional Code Authoring infrastructure includes .codex/workflows/coding-standards.md and .codex/artifact-templates/coding-standard-checklist.md. The public map lives in Professional Code Authoring Standards; the artifacts remain source contracts until a later approved runtime or owner-pilot batch supplies stronger evidence.

docs.title: Local commands
docs.text:
Common local checks:

python tools\check_docs.py
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\validate_codex_compatibility.py
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_transcript_eval.py plugins\product-agent-os\assets\eval-fixtures\transcripts\product-agent-os-synthetic-sessions.json

Run the read-only system file hygiene audit:

python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\validate_system_file_hygiene.py <workspace> --trigger soft_size_review

Use the full unit suite when scripts, templates, fixtures or lifecycle behavior change:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v

Use strict MkDocs when navigation, Mermaid, Markdown extensions or generated site behavior changes:

python -m mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Self-verification metrics loop
docs.text: The metrics loop evaluates agents, skills, prompt/policy packs, router/tool policy and harness-version behavior from read-only evidence. It can stage scorecard records, reports and modernization candidates. It must not self-apply updates, create active schedules, leak raw traces or call live providers without explicit approval.

docs.title: System file hygiene audit
docs.text:
Product-Agent OS includes a read-only system_file_hygiene_audit contract for keeping project system files compact and source-owned. The audit uses hybrid triggers: weekly full review, monthly deep ownership review, on-change review after system-file edits, size-threshold review, and release or automation approval review.

Maintained surfaces include root control-plane files, README.md, nested AGENTS.md, .codex/config.toml, MCP config, .codex/agents, .codex/skills, .codex/workflows, .codex/artifact-templates, .codex/automation-candidates, .codex/hooks, .codex/evals, .codex/pr, docs source-control files, .github/workflows, CODEOWNERS, SECURITY.md, and checked-in plugin package control files. The audit reports size limits, duplicate headings, mojibake/BOM markers, secret-like literals, historical ledger leakage and active schedule markers inside automation candidates.

The audit does not compact files by itself and does not create a schedule. It emits JSON plus a staged system-file-hygiene-report.md; any edit, hook activation, GitHub workflow, Codex App automation, MCP change or external write remains a separate owner-approved slice.

The JSON packet contains audit_trigger, finding_type, compaction_decision, approval_boundary, no_secrets_status and active_schedule_markers. The CLI --trigger records the run reason, prints JSON, returns 0 for ok or review_required, and returns 1 only for blocked; the workspace remains read-only.

The status dashboard projection shows file_statuses, mtime_utc, age_days, content_digest and top_finding as generated review evidence. Dates come from filesystem metadata: they are freshness hints for review, not semantic proof that file content is correct or current enough to claim completion.

docs.title: Project code graph and cockpit
docs.text: The project code graph and cockpit provide orientation evidence. They can stage graph JSON/JSONL and offline HTML/JSON review surfaces under .codex/product-agent-os/. They help readers find source files, edges and stale assumptions, but generated views are not source of truth and cannot justify completion claims by themselves.

docs.title: Codex installation boundary
docs.text:
Codex plugin installation makes package capabilities available to Codex surfaces. It does not:

  • publish the plugin;
  • install dependencies;
  • start local servers;
  • activate hooks or automations;
  • call external providers;
  • mutate global config;
  • stage, commit, push or open PRs;
  • approve production data, hosted docs or database access.

docs.title: Guardrails
docs.text:
• Keep official OpenAI/Codex behavior source-backed by official docs.
  • Keep community claims under docs/insights/ with trust and verification labels.
  • Treat generated reports, dashboards, memory and chat recall as non-authoritative.
  • Require explicit owner approval for external writes, live calls, publishing, production data, hosted docs, CI activation, security scans and active automation.
  • Preserve staged-first behavior and rollback/disable paths.

docs.title: Verification commands for this repo
docs.text:
After documentation-only changes, run:

python tools\check_docs.py

After plugin scripts, templates, fixtures or tests change, also run:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py

Strict MkDocs is needed when navigation, Mermaid, Markdown extensions or MkDocs configuration change:

python -m mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• The checked-in Product-Agent OS plugin package and repository docs.
  • Local Python, MkDocs dependencies and current project instructions.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Local validation evidence for docs, plugin compatibility and deterministic tooling.
  • Operator guidance for installation boundaries and generated artifacts.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Plugin installation does not approve publication, live calls or target workspace writes.
  • Generated graph and report output can become stale unless fingerprint and source boundaries are checked.

docs.title: Hallucination Control
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: Structured Outputs, Model optimization, OpenAI Cookbook hallucination guardrails, Agents SDK guardrails.

docs.title: Types of hallucinations
docs.text: Type Example Control Factual Invented API capability Grounding + citations Citation Nonexistent link or source ID Citation validator Format Response does not match the schema Structured Outputs Tool Model claims it called a tool, but did not Tool trace Temporal Outdated price, version, model Fresh source check Scope Model answers outside the provided context Context-only policy

docs.title: Layered controls
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    I["Input"] --> C["Context boundary"]
    C --> S["Structured prompt"]
    S --> O["Structured output"]
    O --> G["Guardrail / verifier"]
    G -->|pass| A["Answer"]
    G -->|fail| R["Retrieve more / clarify / refuse"]

docs.title: Prompt-level controls
docs.text:
Use concrete rules instead of a generic "do not hallucinate":

Use only the provided sources.
Every factual claim must cite a source ID.
If no source supports the claim, put it under `unsupported_claims`.
Do not infer API behavior from names alone.
If current facts are required and no browsing/tool is available, say that verification is required.

docs.title: Structured Outputs limits
docs.text:
Structured Outputs help keep the response shape, but do not guarantee factual correctness. Official documentation warns separately: if user input is incompatible with the task, the model may try to fill the schema.

Add an explicit fallback:

{
  "answer": "",
  "citations": [],
  "missing_context": ["No source describes this API behavior"],
  "unsupported_claims": []
}

docs.title: Verifier agent
docs.text:
For important answers, use a separate verifier:

Role: Verifier
Goal: Check the factuality of the answer against the provided context.

Rules:
- Ignore style.
- Check every factual claim.
- Mark each claim as supported, unsupported, contradicted, or needs_fresh_check.
- Do not repair the answer unless asked.

Output:
- supported_claims
- unsupported_claims
- contradicted_claims
- missing_context
- verdict: pass | fail | needs_more_context

docs.title: Doubt Verification Packet
docs.text:
For Product-Agent OS, a verifier should return a doubt_verification_packet, not free-form advice. The packet contains a claim ledger, requirement ledger, evidence ledger, missing_context, accepted_gap and final verdict.

Claim statuses are supported | unsupported | contradicted | needs_fresh_check. Verifier must not repair before evidence: it first records the gap, source and risk, then the reviser changes only confirmed gaps. If evidence is unavailable, the final answer should name the missing check or approval boundary instead of a completion claim.

docs.title: Hallucination score
docs.text:
The Cookbook approach can be adapted into a simple scale:

Dimension Pass condition Factual accuracy No unsupported factual claims Relevance The answer solves the question, not an adjacent task Policy compliance Source, safety and tool rules are followed Contextual coherence The answer does not contradict session/context

If any dimension fails, the answer is not published without correction or clarification.

docs.title: When it is better to refuse to answer
docs.text:
Refusal or clarification is better than an answer when:

  • the context does not contain the needed facts;
  • the question requires current data and a tool is unavailable;
  • sources contradict each other;
  • the user asks for exact versions, prices, dates or legal/medical/financial advice without fresh verification;
  • schema forcing makes the model choose from false options.

docs.title: Context engineering
docs.text: Source status: official + experiment Sources: Prompting, Model optimization, Codex memories, Agents SDK sessions.

docs.title: Context as a supply chain
docs.text:
Context should be a managed supply chain of facts:

flowchart TD
    U["User question"] --> N["Need analysis"]
    N --> R["Retrieve sources"]
    R --> F["Filter relevance"]
    F --> P["Pack context"]
    P --> A["Answer"]
    A --> C["Cite and verify"]

docs.title: Source hierarchy
docs.text:
For this knowledge base, the trust order is:

  1. Current workspace and checked-in docs.
  2. Official OpenAI docs and OpenAI GitHub repositories.
  3. Context7 retrieval, if the source URL points to an official source.
  4. Community sources as candidate insights.
  5. Memory as a recall layer, but not source of truth.

docs.title: Context packing
docs.text:
A good context block should not only be large. It should be readable and referential:

<context>
  <source id="S1" type="official" url="https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs">
    Structured Outputs constrain response shape through JSON Schema. They can still contain mistakes.
  </source>
  <source id="S2" type="official" url="https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/model-optimization">
    Model quality should be improved through evals, prompting, representative tests, and iteration.
  </source>
</context>

Rules:

  • give each fragment an id;
  • do not mix sources without labels;
  • remove irrelevant chunks;
  • place fresh or priority facts closer to the task;
  • explicitly mark missing context.

docs.title: Doubt Loop Context
docs.text:
doubt_verification_packet is a context artifact, not memory. It keeps the claim ledger, requirement ledger, evidence ledger, missing_context and accepted_gap separate so a later worker can see what was checked, what was unsupported and what still needs owner approval.

When packing context for completion-skeptic, include the artifact under review, source IDs, current command/eval evidence, user requirements and known non-goals. Do not include raw private chat logs, secrets, local absolute paths or community claims without trust level and verification status.

docs.title: What not to put in context
docs.text:
