docs.title: T8-A. Methodology gates
docs.text: ID Methodology Task Plugin artifact Acceptance Eval/check Residual risk T8-A1 Agentic / AI-native development Clarify the task packet: ownership, forbidden files, approvals, run evidence, stop conditions, promotion path. development-standards.md, lifecycle skills. Every agent task packet contains evidence expectations and the promotion rule manual -> skill -> plugin -> automation. Template tests or skill text checks. Do not turn it into bureaucracy for mechanical edits. T8-A2 TDD Add evidence contract for Red-Green-Refactor. RUNLOG.md, TEST.md, build-slice.md. Fields exist: failing test evidence, green evidence, refactor evidence or explicit accepted gap. Template tests for required fields. Not always applicable to docs-only or config-only changes. T8-A3 ATDD Add acceptance-scenarios.md. .codex/artifact-templates/acceptance-scenarios.md. Trace requirement -> scenario -> check -> evidence owner. Registry/template tests, fixture eval. Do not duplicate REQUIREMENTS.md; the template should be a traceability artifact. T8-A4 BDD Add behavior scenario format without dogmatic forcing. acceptance-scenarios.md, development-standards.md. Given/When/Then or equivalent, business rule, edge case, non-goal and evidence exist. Template tests. BDD does not replace unit, integration and contract tests. T8-A5 DDD Introduce a conditional domain modeling gate. domain-modeling.md, project-readiness.json, implementation-planner skill. Complex backend/workflow/data-heavy projects require bounded context, ubiquitous language, invariant or accepted gap. Eval gate + discovery test. Do not force DDD on simple CRUD/MVP work. T8-A6 Bounded Context Add domain_model signal and traceability to architecture boundary. discovery.py, domain-modeling.md, architecture-overview.md, project-readiness.json, implementation-planner, fixture eval. Discovery sees domain docs/glossary/context map; planner links context to boundary or accepted gap. Discovery/template/lifecycle/fixture tests. A domain/ folder by itself does not prove DDD maturity; mapping still needs human architecture/domain review. T8-A7 Ubiquitous Language Strengthen domain template traceability. domain-modeling.md, project-readiness.json, implementation-planner, fixture eval. Term maps to requirement/source, API/event/contract, UI label, code module or owner, or accepted gap. Template/lifecycle/fixture tests. Requires human domain expert review. T8-A8 FSD Add optional fsd_structure signal and FSD boundary prompt. discovery.py, component-card.md, development-standards.md, project-readiness.json, lifecycle skills. Detection understands app/pages/widgets/features/entities/shared; planner requires public API/import boundary for growing UI only when applicable. Focused T8-A8 discovery/template/lifecycle tests. Do not apply to backend/native/simple CRUD/simple MVP work without UI architecture need. T8-A9 Data-informed development Strengthen metric spec. metric-spec.md, release-packet.md, generated control-plane templates, lifecycle skills, fixture eval. metric_hardening_when_product_behavior_changes, North Star or primary value metric, input/counter metrics, guardrails, qualitative review, privacy classification, retention period, data minimization, owner signoff and post-release review evidence exist. Focused T8-A9 template/lifecycle/fixture tests. Metrics can still be wrong; product owner and post-release review are needed. T8-A10 Eval-driven AI development Add AI/RAG eval spec. .codex/artifact-templates/ai-eval-spec.md, EVALS.md, TEST.md. Baseline, fixtures policy, no-secrets rule, task rubric, thresholds, rerun command and regression handling exist. Template tests, fixture eval. Eval quality depends on dataset and judge calibration. T8-A11 Docs-as-code Close inside T8-C: introduce docs impact gate with applicability status. documentation-system.md, docs-tooling-decision.md, project-readiness.json, generated PLAN/TEST/EVALS/RUNLOG, lifecycle skills. Docs impact can be not_applicable, present_unverified, present_verified, proposal_staged, explicit_gap_accepted, or approval_required; status must name evidence owner, commands, accepted gap or approval boundary. Template/readiness/fixture tests inside T8-C. Do not activate CI/CODEOWNERS, hosted docs, external sharing, DB introspection or docs publication without approval. T8-A12 Systematic debugging Strengthen bug rescue through root-cause workflow. bug-rescue.md, bug-rescue-report.md, risk-reviewer skill. Before fixing there is symptom, expected/actual, reproduction evidence, boundary trace, hypotheses, eliminated causes and a stop condition for no-repro. Behavioral eval + template tests for root cause phases. Small bugs can be overloaded; the lightweight path should accept a one-command repro. T8-A13 No-placeholder implementation planning Ban vague implementation steps in plan packets. implementation-planner skill, PLAN.md, build-slice.md. Every slice has exact files, explicit commands, expected result, rollback and evidence owner; no placeholder tokens, repeated-by-reference steps or vague validation. Skill text tests + plan-quality behavioral fixture. An overly detailed plan can slow trivial docs edits; it needs a mechanical_change exception with reason. T8-A14 Two-stage review Split review into spec compliance and quality/risk. review-slice.md, risk-reviewer skill, RUNLOG.md. Review packet first checks acceptance criteria/source constraints, then checks code quality, tests, security, docs and release impact. Template tests check two verdicts. Doubles review overhead; apply to risky/parallel/public changes. T8-A15 Fresh-context subagent handoff Clarify task packet for subagents. agent-team-designer skill, handoff-contract.md, worktree-ownership.md. Every subagent receives complete task context, owned files, forbidden files, expected verification evidence and handoff output schema. Skill text tests + scenario fixture for complex acceleration. Parallel work without ownership remains risky; default should be sequential when conflict exists. T8-A16 Evidence-before-completion Record the final verification gate. release-packet.md, development-standards.md, generated control-plane templates, lifecycle skills, readiness eval, behavioral eval, fixture eval. Release/ready/completed/fixed/works claims are allowed only with current command evidence, current eval evidence, current runtime evidence or explicit inspection-only gap. Focused T8-A16 tests, fixture eval completion_evidence_contract_present. Quick opinions must be marked as inspection-only; evidence sufficiency still needs human review.

docs.title: T8-B. Standards and specifications
docs.text: ID Standard/spec Task Plugin artifact Acceptance Eval/check Residual risk T8-B1 ADR/MADR Add ADR trigger policy. adr.md, documentation-system.md, risk-reviewer skill. ADR required/proposed for architecture boundary, storage, API contract, auth/security, irreversible migration, automation activation. Template/skill text tests. Not every decision needs an ADR; not_applicable is needed. T8-B2 C4 Clarify minimum diagrams by complexity. architecture-overview.md, docs tooling decision. Small: context/container optional Mermaid; larger: context/container expected; component/code only when useful. Template tests. Diagram rendering in the target repo depends on tooling. T8-B3 arc42 Add architecture quality rubric. EVALS.md, architecture-overview.md. Architecture review includes goals, constraints, context, decisions, quality attributes and risks. Eval/template tests. Rubric is subjective; reviewer evidence is needed. T8-B4 OpenAPI Clarify OpenAPI vs Swagger. api-contract-review.md, docs tooling selector. OpenAPI is source of truth; Swagger UI/tooling is optional renderer/editor/lint ecosystem. Template tests. Tool versions differ; no forced install. T8-B5 AsyncAPI Add producer/consumer compatibility fields. api-contract-review.md. Event contract includes channel, message, payload schema, producer, consumer, ordering/idempotency and compatibility check. Template tests. Event semantics are often not fully expressible by schema. T8-B6 SemVer Add version impact gate. release-packet.md, pr-release-operator skill. For plugin/package/API: major/minor/patch/not applicable with rationale. Template tests. SemVer applies only when public API/version contract exists. T8-B7 Keep a Changelog Add human-readable release categories. release-packet.md. Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security are used when relevant. Template tests. Do not turn it into a raw git log. T8-B8 CODEOWNERS Add governance proposal status. documentation-system.md, staged infrastructure notes. CODEOWNERS status can be present_verified, proposal_staged, approval_required, not_applicable. Discovery and template tests. Requiring owners can slow small teams. T8-B9 GitHub Actions Add least-privilege CI proposal fields. CI/governance workflow section, docs tooling selector. Proposed workflow names commands, permissions, triggers, owners, no external activation without approval. Template tests. External system side effects require approval.

docs.title: T8-C. Documentation tooling selector
docs.text:
T8-C includes closure of T8-A11. The slice is not only a tool recommendation matrix; it must make docs-as-code impact evaluable through explicit applicability statuses and evidence. A workspace can select a lightweight/no-portal path when docs tooling is not justified, but the reason, owner and residual gap must be recorded.

Required status vocabulary for docs_as_code_impact: not_applicable, present_unverified, present_verified, proposal_staged, explicit_gap_accepted, approval_required.

ID Tool group Task Plugin artifact Selection rule Check proposal T8-C1 Docs portal Add docs-tooling-decision.md. .codex/artifact-templates/docs-tooling-decision.md. Choose MkDocs, Docusaurus, Sphinx, Antora, Read the Docs, or none based on stack, repo topology, public docs, versioning need. mkdocs build, docusaurus build, sphinx-build, antora, hosted approval note where applicable. T8-C2 MkDocs Keep as simple Markdown default. Docs tooling selector. Small/medium repo, Markdown docs, simple static site, Python-friendly tooling. Strict build if installed. T8-C3 Docusaurus Recommend for React/MDX/product docs. Docs tooling selector. React/MDX-heavy docs, interactive pages, public docs, i18n/versioning needs. Build command only if package script/tool exists. T8-C4 Sphinx Recommend for Python reference docs. Docs tooling selector, code reference docs routing. Python package/library, public Python API, docstrings, API reference. sphinx-build proposal, import-safety warning. T8-C5 Antora Recommend for enterprise/multirepo AsciiDoc. Docs tooling selector. Multirepo/multiversion docs, AsciiDoc governance, larger org. Antora build proposal only if tooling exists or approved. T8-C6 Read the Docs Keep hosted docs as approval-bound option. Docs tooling selector. Public/open docs needing hosted builds/versioning. approval_required for external hosting/sharing. T8-C7 OpenAPI/Swagger Route HTTP API docs. api-contract-review.md, selector. HTTP API or SDK consumers. Swagger is UI/tooling around OpenAPI, not source of truth. OpenAPI lint/build command slot. T8-C8 AsyncAPI Route event/message docs. api-contract-review.md, selector. Queues, event bus, message-driven APIs. AsyncAPI lint/docs build slot. T8-C9 Storybook Route UI component docs. component-card.md, selector, discovery. Reusable UI components, design system, component states. Storybook build, a11y/visual check if present. T8-C10 Mermaid Default text diagrams. architecture-overview.md, selector. Markdown docs, simple diagrams, no heavy architecture-as-code need. Docs build/render check. T8-C11 PlantUML Optional UML/sequence diagrams. Selector. Team already uses PlantUML/UML or needs complex sequence/component diagrams. PlantUML render proposal only if tool exists/approved. T8-C12 Structurizr DSL Optional C4 architecture-as-code. Selector. Larger/multiservice systems needing C4 model, views, ADR/docs as code. Structurizr validate/export proposal. T8-C13 DBML/dbdocs Database docs lightweight path. database-dictionary.md, selector. Relational DB schema docs, readable schema dictionary. DBML validation/docs proposal; no connection strings. T8-C14 SchemaSpy Existing DB introspection path. Selector/database docs workflow. Existing relational DB where introspection is approved. approval_required if DB access needed; no secrets in artifacts. T8-C15 TypeDoc/JSDoc JS/TS reference docs. Selector/code reference docs section. Public TS/JS packages, SDKs, libraries. TypeDoc/JSDoc build proposal if scripts exist. T8-C16 Sphinx/Javadoc/C# XML docs Language-native reference docs. Selector/code reference docs section. Public Python/Java/.NET APIs. Stack-specific docs build proposal. T8-C17 Vale/markdownlint Optional docs quality lint. Selector/docs governance section. Public docs, regulated terminology, existing docs lint culture. Proposal staged; no CI enablement without approval.

docs.title: T8-CY. Codex-only compatibility contract
docs.text:
Track 8 borrows the idea of explicit runtime compatibility checks, but scopes it only to Codex. Product-Agent OS must not add or require Claude, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini, Droid or generic multi-harness adapters.

ID Surface Task Plugin artifact Acceptance Eval/check Residual risk T8-CY1 Codex plugin manifest Harden .codex-plugin/plugin.json checks. .codex-plugin/plugin.json, test_plugin_structure.py. Manifest includes valid name/version/description, skills, optional MCP config, interface metadata and Codex-safe links. Plugin structure tests. Marketplace requirements may evolve; official Codex docs stay source of truth. T8-CY2 Codex App / CLI / IDE extension Document supported Codex surfaces only. plugins/product-agent-os/README.md, docs update. README states Product-Agent OS supports Codex App, CLI and IDE extension workflows; no non-Codex install promises. Docs check + keyword tests. Different Codex surfaces may expose skills/tools differently; behavior must be framed by available capabilities. T8-CY3 Skills routing Validate bundled Product-Agent OS skills. skills/*/SKILL.md, test_lifecycle_skills.py. Skill descriptions, triggers, boundaries, inputs, outputs, verification and failure modes are present. Skill structure tests. Trigger quality still needs behavioral prompt evals, not only text checks. T8-CY4 Context7 MCP Keep Context7 as optional Codex MCP config. .mcp.json, README.md. MCP config remains secret-free and uses project/user configuration for any API key. Plugin structure tests and source-policy validation. Network and package availability vary; plugin cannot assume Context7 startup. T8-CY5 Staged hooks Keep hook templates inactive by default. assets/templates/hooks/*, merge_infrastructure.py. Hooks can be staged and approved, but plugin does not silently activate session-start behavior. Hook activation gate tests. Users may manually activate hooks incorrectly; docs must state approval and rollback path. T8-CY6 Non-Codex adapter exclusion Make absence of non-Codex manifests intentional. test_codex_compatibility.py, README. Tests fail if Track 8 requires .claude-plugin, .cursor-plugin, .opencode, Gemini extension or non-Codex install path. Focused compatibility test. Repo may contain unrelated docs about other ecosystems; test should target Product-Agent OS package only.

docs.title: T8-CX. Usage scenario workflows
docs.text: ID Scenario Task Plugin artifact Acceptance Eval/check Residual risk T8-S1 Bug rescue Add workflow for users who are stuck in bugs after exploratory or vibe-coded work. .codex/workflows/bug-rescue.md, optional .codex/artifact-templates/bug-rescue-report.md. Workflow requires symptom, expected/actual behavior, reproduction command or manual repro, failing evidence, suspect boundary, files in/out of scope, regression test path, rollback notes. Template tests check reproduction/evidence/rollback fields; discovery test can classify bug_rescue from failed tests/logs/user prompt context. If no reproduction exists, plugin must stop at diagnosis packet, not pretend to fix. T8-S2 Greenfield idea Add workflow for empty folder or idea-stage work before scaffold. .codex/workflows/greenfield-idea-to-plan.md, optional .codex/artifact-templates/greenfield-idea-brief.md. Workflow creates staged requirements, options, non-goals, first vertical slice, acceptance scenarios, metric spec, docs/tooling decision and approval gate before any scaffold. Template tests check no-scaffold-before-approval language and first-slice fields. Over-planning can slow small ideas; workflow must support lightweight mode. T8-S3 Complex system acceleration Add workflow for experienced developers scaling web/API/integration-heavy systems. .codex/workflows/complex-system-acceleration.md, .codex/artifact-templates/integration-catalog.md. Workflow maps web/API/integration/DB/docs/eval slices, ownership boundaries, parallelization rules, external system contracts, integration risks and release gates. Template tests check integration catalog, ownership, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI, DB/docs, release gates. Risk of over-parallelization and conflicting file ownership. T8-S4 Usage mode classifier Add explicit route before methodology gates. discovery.py, runner route packet, workspace-discovery-auditor skill. Audit returns usage_mode for base and extended modes, plus route_inputs separating intent hints, workspace signals and control-plane state. Unit tests with synthetic workspaces, prompt-like inputs and fixture eval expectations. Mode can be ambiguous; output must include confidence and fallback path. T8-S5 Scenario handoff packet Standardize what each scenario hands to the next role. lifecycle skills and workflow templates. Handoff includes sources/context, assumptions, files touched/proposed, verification evidence, open risks, recommended next role. Skill text tests or fixture eval checks for handoff contract. Handoff packets can become verbose; keep scenario-specific minimums. T8-S6 PR review Add workflow for reviewing changed files before merge. .codex/workflows/pr-review-readiness.md, optional .codex/artifact-templates/pr-risk-review.md. Workflow maps diff to behavior/API/DB/UI/security/docs/release risks, missing checks and review evidence. Template tests for diff risk map, contract docs, release impact and commands. Requires git/diff context; if absent, route to maintenance or standard feature. T8-S7 Legacy onboarding Add workflow for old or undocumented repos. .codex/workflows/legacy-onboarding.md, .codex/artifact-templates/onboarding-map.md. Workflow creates source map, run commands, architecture/doc gaps and safe first documentation slice without refactor. Template tests check runbook, docs debt map and present_unverified wording. Discovery may infer too much from stale docs; mark unverified until commands run. T8-S8 API migration Add workflow for changing HTTP/event contracts. .codex/workflows/api-migration.md, .codex/artifact-templates/migration-plan.md. Workflow covers OpenAPI/AsyncAPI, consumers, generated clients, backwards compatibility, deprecation, examples, release impact. Template tests for contract/versioning/deprecation fields. Internal APIs may still have external consumers; require owner review. T8-S9 AI eval regression Add workflow for AI/RAG quality regression. .codex/workflows/ai-eval-regression.md, ai-eval-spec.md. Workflow requires baseline, dataset, rubric, thresholds, one-factor-at-a-time change and no-secrets fixtures. Template/eval tests for baseline and dataset policy. Eval judgments can be noisy; record confidence and residual risk. T8-S10 Native mobile feature Add workflow for iOS/Android/native mobile changes. .codex/workflows/native-mobile-feature.md. Workflow covers permissions, offline states, simulator/emulator assumptions, screenshots/logs and platform build commands. Template tests for runtime verification fields. Tooling varies heavily; plugin should propose commands from detected project only. T8-S11 Desktop local-first Add workflow for desktop apps with filesystem/local DB/background work. .codex/workflows/desktop-local-first.md. Workflow covers local data, filesystem permissions, indexing/background jobs, privacy, app logs and recovery path. Template tests for local data/rollback/log fields. Runtime verification is OS-specific; avoid claiming behavior from inspection only. T8-S12 Data migration Add workflow for schema, backfill and retention changes. .codex/workflows/data-migration.md, migration-plan.md, database-dictionary.md. Workflow covers migration, rollback, data quality, PII/sensitive fields, retention and DB docs. Template tests for migration/rollback/privacy fields. Production DB access requires approval and secret-safe handling. T8-S13 Security-sensitive change Add workflow for auth, permissions, payments, secrets or personal data. .codex/workflows/security-sensitive-change.md, .codex/artifact-templates/security-risk-review.md. Workflow covers threat surface, authn/authz, sensitive fields, abuse controls, approval needs and rollback. Template tests for approval and no-secrets wording. May require dedicated security scan outside Track 8 scope. T8-S14 CI stabilization Add workflow for failing or flaky CI. .codex/workflows/ci-stabilization.md, .codex/artifact-templates/ci-stabilization-report.md. Workflow separates deterministic failure from flake, captures job/command/log/environment evidence and proposes smallest isolation. Template tests for flake evidence and no external CI mutation. Remote CI logs may need approval or connector access. T8-S15 Release packaging Add workflow for package, SDK, plugin, app or open-source release readiness. .codex/workflows/release-packaging.md, .codex/artifact-templates/release-readiness.md. Workflow covers public API, SemVer, changelog, docs, examples, package metadata, license/security notes, publish approval and rollback. Template tests for release gates and no-publish-without-approval wording. Publishing/tagging is external/irreversible and must remain approval-bound. T8-S16 First-run route and intake Add first response contract for initial plugin use. project-lifecycle-orchestrator skill, .codex/workflows/first-run-intake.md. First response states detected/assumed usage_mode, confidence, missing context, next smallest artifact and approval boundary instead of dumping all gates. Behavioral prompt evals for empty, broken, existing and complex repos. Too many questions can stall; plugin should ask only when confidence is low or write approval is needed.

docs.title: T8-F. Readiness eval
docs.text: Gate Applies when Pass condition Accepted gap acceptance_scenarios_when_behavior_changes User-facing behavior or business rule changes. Scenario maps to test/eval/manual check. Explicit gap in RUNLOG with owner. domain_model_when_complex_domain Complex backend, workflow, enterprise, data-heavy or multi-context domain. Domain model exists or proposal staged. Complexity judged low or gap accepted. fsd_boundary_when_ui_grows Growing UI with reusable features/components. Feature/slice/layer boundary or stack-appropriate alternative is named. Small MVP or non-UI project. ai_eval_spec_when_ai_behavior_changes Prompt/model/RAG/tool/agent behavior changes. Baseline, dataset, threshold and rerun command exist. Explicit accepted eval gap. docs_tooling_decision New docs system, public docs, generated docs, API/UI/DB/code reference changes. Tooling decision exists with applicability statuses. Not applicable documented. contract_docs_when_api_or_event_changes HTTP/event contract changes. OpenAPI/AsyncAPI updated or proposal/gap recorded. Internal-only prototype with accepted risk. db_docs_when_schema_changes Schema/migration/data model changes. Database dictionary/DBML/schema docs updated or proposal/gap recorded. No persistent schema touched. release_version_impact_when_public_contract_changes Plugin/package/API/SDK release or public contract changes. SemVer/changelog impact named. No public contract. reproduction_evidence_when_bug_rescue Bug rescue mode or user reports broken behavior. Failing command, log excerpt, test, screenshot, manual repro or explicit no-repro stop condition. No reproduction available; stop at diagnosis packet. approval_before_greenfield_scaffold Empty folder or idea-stage project. Selected direction and first slice approved before scaffold/write proposal is applied. User explicitly requests no scaffold and only wants research/spec. integration_catalog_when_external_systems_exist Multiple integrations, webhooks, queues, external APIs or generated clients. Integration catalog exists or proposal/gap recorded with secrets policy. Simple local-only project or no integration touched. ownership_split_when_parallel_agents_used Complex system acceleration or parallel build requested. File/subsystem ownership is explicit and non-overlapping, or work stays sequential. Parallelism not used. pr_risk_review_when_review_mode PR review mode or diff-focused request. Changed areas, risks, missing checks and release/docs impact are named. No diff/change context available. onboarding_map_when_legacy_repo Legacy repo onboarding or undocumented existing project. Entry points, run commands, docs debt and verification status are recorded. User only requested a narrow code change. migration_plan_when_contract_or_data_changes API contract, schema, backfill, retention or breaking change. Migration plan includes compatibility, rollout, validation and rollback. Prototype with no persisted data/public consumers. security_review_when_sensitive_surface Auth, permissions, payments, secrets, personal data or external writes. Security risk review exists and approval needs are explicit. No sensitive surface touched. platform_runtime_check_when_native_or_desktop Mobile/native or desktop/local-first changes. Platform build/run/log/screenshot or simulator/manual check is named. Docs-only or non-runtime change. ci_failure_evidence_when_ci_stabilization CI stabilization mode. Failing job/command/log evidence and deterministic/flaky classification exist. CI context unavailable; stop at local reproduction plan. release_readiness_when_distribution_changes Package, SDK, plugin, public app or open-source release. Release readiness covers SemVer/changelog/docs/build/security/publish approval. Internal-only unreleased work. plugin_success_metric_for_major_workflow New scenario workflow or major Product-Agent OS behavior. Metric exists for time-to-first-useful-artifact, false positive gate rate or scenario success rate. Experimental workflow explicitly marked. root_cause_before_bug_fix Bug rescue mode, repeated failed fixes or user reports unclear failure. Reproduction, trace, hypotheses and eliminated causes exist before broad code edits. One-line typo with obvious failing test can use lightweight path. no_placeholder_plan_when_plan_ready Implementation plan is produced for non-trivial work. Plan has exact files, concrete steps, commands, expected outputs and no placeholder language. Mechanical docs/config edits can record a reduced plan. two_stage_review_when_risky_or_parallel Parallel work, public contract, migration, security-sensitive or release-bound slice. Review includes spec compliance verdict and quality/risk verdict. Narrow low-risk slice can use single reviewer note with reason. fresh_context_handoff_when_subagents_used Any subagent or parallel worker is assigned. Task packet includes full context, owned files, forbidden files, expected evidence and handoff schema. Sequential inline execution can skip subagent packet. behavioral_eval_when_new_route_added New usage_mode, workflow, skill route or first response behavior is added. Prompt/session fixture proves expected route, minimum artifacts and forbidden actions. Experimental workflow can be marked manual_eval_required for one iteration. codex_only_compatibility_when_plugin_packaging_changes Plugin manifest, skills, MCP config, hook templates or README install docs change. Compatibility report covers Codex App, CLI, IDE extension and .codex-plugin; non-Codex adapters remain out of scope. Official Codex platform changes may require follow-up research. finish_options_when_release_ready PR/release packet is produced. User sees options with evidence state: keep branch, create PR packet, approved apply/merge path, rollback, cleanup. External publish/tag/PR still requires explicit approval.

docs.title: T8-G. Lifecycle skill updates
docs.text: Skill Update Acceptance workspace-discovery-auditor Output applicability statuses, richer docs tooling signals, Codex plugin surface and route inputs. Handoff includes signals, statuses, missing gates, approval-required items, prompt intent hints and Codex-only compatibility notes. requirements-author Ask for acceptance scenarios and product metrics when behavior changes. Requirements packet maps goals to scenarios and metrics or records gaps. implementation-planner Route slices through methodology gates conditionally and enforce no-placeholder quality for non-trivial plans. Plan names methodology/tool applicability, exact files, concrete steps, commands, expected outputs, rollback and verification per slice. test-eval-designer Map scenario -> deterministic/manual/eval check and add behavioral prompt/session eval cases for new routes. Every scenario has a check or accepted gap; every new route has expected mode, artifacts and forbidden behavior. risk-reviewer Review standards/tooling applicability, secrets risk, root-cause evidence, two-stage review requirements and approval requirements. Finds over-forcing, missing docs contracts, unsafe DB/docs generation, weak evidence and skipped spec-compliance review. docs-maintainer Use docs tooling selector and source status policy. Docs changes include build/lint/proposal status. pr-release-operator Add changelog, SemVer impact and finish options. Release packet names user-visible changes, version impact, rollback and evidence-backed options; it cannot publish or tag without explicit approval. project-lifecycle-orchestrator Route by usage_mode and first response contract before assigning roles. Bug rescue, greenfield, complex acceleration, docs-only and maintenance paths select different minimum artifacts and avoid dumping all gates on first contact. agent-team-designer Enforce ownership split and fresh-context task packets for complex acceleration. Parallel agents receive non-overlapping files/subsystems, forbidden files, expected evidence and explicit merge/review handoff. reviewer or equivalent review path Support PR review, security-sensitive modes and two-stage review. Review packets lead with findings, include spec-compliance verdict, quality/risk verdict, missing checks, release/security/docs impact and residual risk. release operator path Support release packaging mode and finish menu. Release readiness offers evidence-backed keep/PR/merge/apply/rollback/cleanup options; external actions remain approval-bound. docs.title: T8-GY. Behavioral workflow eval coverage
docs.text:
Structural template tests prove files exist. Behavioral evals prove the plugin acts correctly when a user prompt creates pressure, ambiguity or shortcuts.

Eval Purpose Inputs Expected behavior Forbidden behavior Route selection prompt eval Check first route before work starts. Prompt, optional workspace fixture, control-plane state. Returns usage_mode, confidence, reasons, fallback and next skill. Start editing before route/safety decision. First-run response eval Check first launch UX. Empty, broken, mature and complex repo prompts. Asks at most one necessary question or proposes next smallest staged artifact. Dump full methodology matrix or scaffold without approval. Explicit invocation eval Check direct user requests. Prompt naming a skill/workflow/mode. Honors explicit route when safe and records why. Let prompt override sandbox/source/approval guards. Adversarial shortcut eval Check pressure to skip gates. Prompts like "just fix it", "no tests", "skip docs", "apply now". Keeps minimal required evidence or records accepted gap. Claim readiness or mutate external systems without evidence/approval. Bug rescue behavior eval Check root-cause discipline. Failing tests/logs or user bug narrative. Requires reproduction or stops at diagnosis; after repeated failures escalates to root-cause review. Keep patching without reproduction or hypotheses. Data migration behavior eval Check database migration safety. Schema/backfill/PII/retention prompt or workspace fixture. Produces migration plan, database dictionary, dry-run/backup/rollback/validation gates and owner review before production DB access. Access production data, run migration, expose PII or claim data safety without evidence. Security-sensitive behavior eval Check security-sensitive change safety. Auth/payment/permission/PII prompt or workspace fixture. Produces security risk review with threat surface, authn/authz, payment, secrets, PII, abuse controls, audit logging, tests, rollback, owner review and approval before implementation. Change auth/payment/permission behavior without risk review, store secrets or PII, imply Codex Security scan without explicit request, or claim security safety without evidence. Plan quality eval Check no-placeholder planning. Requirements and workspace audit packet. Plan includes exact files, concrete steps, commands, expected outputs, rollback and evidence owner. Placeholder tokens, vague validation, repeated-by-reference steps, command without expected result. Two-stage review eval Check review order. Slice summary, diff summary, evidence packet. Produces spec-compliance verdict first, then quality/risk verdict. Treat generic code review as enough for risky work. Fresh-context handoff eval Check subagent task packets. Complex/parallel plan. Each worker gets full context, owned files, forbidden files, expected evidence and handoff schema. Shared ownership ambiguity or missing stop conditions. Finish options eval Check release end state. Ready release packet with evidence. Offers keep/PR/apply/rollback/cleanup options and approval requirements. Publish, tag, open PR or activate automation automatically. Codex-only compatibility eval Check packaging scope. Product-Agent OS package. Validates Codex App/CLI/IDE extension docs, .codex-plugin, skills, MCP and staged hooks. Require or generate Claude/Cursor/OpenCode/Gemini adapters. Cost/model budget eval Check agent workflow cost discipline. Agent team packet and risk profile. Records model/reasoning choice, escalation/downgrade rule and budget note. Default every role to maximum reasoning without rationale.

docs.title: T8-I. Verification plan
docs.text: Check When Expected result Focused discovery tests After discovery.py changes. New signals/statuses pass positive and negative tests. Focused infrastructure template tests After template/eval registry changes. New artifacts are registered and expected fields exist. Full unittest After any plugin code/template/test change. python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v returns OK. Fixture eval After renderer/template changes. python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py exits 0, all fixtures ok: true. Docs check After docs changes. python tools\check_docs.py returns OK. Strict MkDocs build After nav/diagram/MkDocs-sensitive docs changes. $env:PYTHONPATH='C:\tmp\codex_docs_mkdocs'; python -m mkdocs build --strict exits 0. Scenario fixture eval After scenario workflow or usage mode changes. Each synthetic scenario fixture returns expected usage mode, staged artifacts and no forbidden external activation. Behavioral route eval After route, first-response, lifecycle skill or scenario behavior changes. Prompt/session fixtures return expected route, confidence, next skill, minimum artifacts and stop condition. Plan quality eval After implementation-planner, PLAN.md, build-slice.md or task packet changes. No-placeholder checks pass and every non-trivial slice has exact files, commands and expected outputs. Two-stage review eval After review workflow or risk-reviewer changes. Review evidence includes spec-compliance verdict before quality/risk verdict. Codex-only compatibility check After plugin manifest, README, skills, MCP or hook templates change. .codex-plugin, Codex skills, MCP and staged hooks validate; no non-Codex adapter is required. Source registry check After adding community or comparative sources. docs/sources/registry.md includes trust level and verification status.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
• Template rollback: remove template file, template registry entry, generated fixture expectation and related tests.
  • Discovery rollback: revert the specific signal/status logic and corresponding unit tests.
  • Eval rollback: remove only new gates from project-readiness.json and tests that assert them.
  • Scenario workflow rollback: remove workflow/template registry entries and scenario-specific tests without removing generic methodology gates.
  • Behavioral eval rollback: remove prompt/session fixtures and expected-route assertions without weakening source, approval, redaction or no-secrets guards.
  • Codex compatibility rollback: revert Codex-only compatibility report/tests while preserving .codex-plugin manifest and existing plugin packaging.
  • Docs rollback: remove Track 8 sections and links without touching source registry entries that remain valid.
  • No rollback path may use destructive git commands; preserve user-authored files and staged proposals.

docs.title: T9-D2 Requirements and Domain Integration
docs.text:
Status: done

Source audited: docs/methodologies/requirements-domain.md

Deep-audit deltas to implement:

  • Extend Track 8 acceptance scenarios, conditional DDD, bounded-context traceability, ubiquitous-language traceability and false-positive protection instead of duplicating them.
  • Represent requirement taxonomy when relevant: functional, non-functional, compliance, operational, AI behavior, data/privacy and release/rollback.
  • Add requirement quality criteria as a first-class gate: atomicity, clarity, testability, feasibility, traceability, source and owner.
  • Require stable requirement IDs for multi-slice, regulatory, risky, long-lived or public-contract work.
  • Add a requirement registry with status, owner, source and linked artifacts.
  • Treat stakeholder/owner mapping as a first-class artifact for source-backed domain meaning and business rules.
  • Preserve story slicing evidence: value slice, risk slice, MVP boundary, deferred slices, non-goals and acceptance scenario links.
  • Record business rules with source, owner, enforcement layer, exceptions, failure mode and tests/evals.
  • Use Example Mapping for unclear, large or disputed stories: story -> rules -> examples -> questions.
  • Require domain discovery workshop evidence for complex workflow, cross-silo process or overloaded domain language.
  • Track constraints across compliance, privacy, security, operational, performance, platform, accessibility, data retention, localization, cost, rollout and rollback.
  • Require declarative acceptance scenarios with no UI selectors, database internals, function names or test harness details.
  • Record invariants and failure modes when domain state transitions matter.
  • Require domain event contract evidence when events cross boundaries: meaning, producer, consumers, schema link, ordering/idempotency and privacy classification.
  • Add API/UI/data traceability distinct from DDD traceability: requirement/domain term -> API/event/schema/UI/data/code/test/eval.
  • Require domain expert or owner review for business-critical, compliance, finance/legal and AI-generated domain claims.
  • Require requirement change impact review after planning changes: tests/evals, API, DB, UI, docs, rollout and rollback.
  • Allow accepted gaps only with owner, reason, scope, review date, downstream risk and follow-up condition.
  • Route docs-maintainer to maintain requirement IDs, source registry, glossary/ubiquitous-language docs and traceability docs after the requirements packet exists.
  • Reject unsupported claims as evidence: BDD replaces testing, Gherkin is mandatory, a user-story template is complete requirements, a glossary is ubiquitous language, and OpenAPI is requirements source of truth.

docs.title: T9-D5 Codex / Agentic Workflow Integration
docs.text:
Status: done

Source audited: docs/methodologies/codex-agentic-workflow.md

Deep-audit deltas implemented:

  • Represented Codex / Agentic Workflow as durable control-plane and capability governance, not chat memory or broad agent orchestration.
  • Used the full gate set: agentic_scope_classified, source_of_truth_present, control_plane_present, read_only_discovery_complete, approval_boundary_present, fresh_context_handoff_present, ownership_split_present, subagent_parallelism_safe, skill_promotion_evidence_present, plugin_boundary_present, mcp_permission_review_present, hook_activation_approval_present, automation_manual_stability_present, model_reasoning_policy_present, memory_policy_present, agent_eval_workflow_present and agentic_evidence_before_completion.
  • Added severity policy so control-plane/source-of-truth gaps, side-effecting MCP, hook activation, external writes, production data, overlapping subagent edits, active automation and completion claims without evidence are blocker or high-risk when applicable, while lightweight docs/local work remains warning or not applicable.
  • Added runtime routing shape for Codex App, IDE extension, CLI, codex exec, GitHub Action, MCP, Agents SDK and automation, with no default escalation to MCP, Agents SDK or automation.
  • Added lifecycle test policy for skills: trigger tests, negative trigger tests, missing-input behavior, verification-failure behavior and failure-log evidence.
  • Set automation promotion threshold to at least two successful manual runs or an explicit owner-approved accepted gap.
  • Distinguished staged hook templates, read-only validation hooks and blocking/side-effecting hooks; hook activation requires trust review, event/matcher/command, failure behavior, disable path and explicit approval.
  • Required MCP review for new MCP config, changed trust boundary, auth/secrets, remote servers, side-effecting tools, production/customer data or external writes; read-only local docs MCP can be lower severity but still records capability/data boundary.
  • Required worktrees or explicit ownership for parallel subagents when edits can overlap, generated files are shared, migrations/contracts/public APIs/schemas are touched, or merge/rollback risk is high; read-only research can use packets without worktrees.
  • Clarified Codex-native subagents vs Agents SDK: Codex-native subagents are default for Codex App/CLI/IDE engineering delegation; Agents SDK is for code-owned agent apps with application-owned orchestration, tools, guardrails, sessions, tracing and evals.
  • Expanded agent eval workflow with baseline, trace-derived dataset, tool-call correctness, handoff correctness, expected/forbidden behavior, grader or deterministic assertion, threshold, rerun command, regression label, latency/cost and privacy/no-secrets handling.

Implemented scope:

  • Added codex_agentic_workflow catalog coverage for control plane, source of truth, read-only discovery, approval boundaries, model/reasoning policy, memory policy, handoffs, ownership split, subagent safety, MCP review, hook governance, plugin boundary, skill promotion, automation stability, agent eval workflow, evidence before completion and unsupported-claim rejection.
  • Added read-only audit recommendations with deterministic gate, priority and artifact mapping for missing control plane, missing source of truth, missing read-only discovery, missing approval boundary, subagent/parallel work without ownership, MCP side effects, hook activation, plugin packaging, repeated workflow promotion, automation schedules, model/reasoning policy gaps, memory-as-source-of-truth claims, agent behavior without eval workflow and completion claims without evidence.

  • Added Codex workflow discovery signals for .codex/, agents, workflows, artifact templates, skills, plugins, subagents, MCP, hooks, automation, task packets, handoff/worktree artifacts, source-of-truth terms, approval-boundary terms and side-effect risks. Detection remains present_unverified.
  • Routed Codex / Agentic Workflow into all 11 lifecycle skills while keeping hooks, MCP, automation, external writes and Agents SDK orchestration approval-bound.
  • Added fixture eval check codex_agentic_workflow_contract_present; renderer file count is now 102 after adding five Codex workflow artifact templates.

Candidate artifact mapping:

  • context-memory-policy.md is covered by AGENTS.md, .codex/config.toml, model-reasoning-policy.md and generated PLAN/EVALS/RUNLOG memory-policy fields until a later slice proves separate ownership.
  • agentic-workflow-readiness.md is covered by project-readiness.json, generated PLAN/TEST/EVALS/RUNLOG and the codex_agentic_workflow_contract_present fixture check.

The existing Track 9 internal source entry was refreshed to mention T9-D5 coverage.

Severity and false-positive resolution:

docs.title: T9-D8 API and Integrations Integration
docs.text:
Status: done

Source audited: docs/methodologies/api-integrations.md

Deep-audit deltas implemented:

  • Treat API methodology as a contract-source discipline, not a rendered-docs discipline: OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL/protobuf/JSON Schema/Pact sources count as evidence, while Swagger UI is not source of truth.
  • Split schema validation from contract testing: contract-test evidence records provider verification, consumer-driven checks, negative cases, compatibility rules and missing-tool gaps.
  • Add explicit consumer and compatibility gates for public and internal APIs; internal APIs can still have consumers and breaking-change risk.
  • Add security and error depth: contract-linked security schemes, scopes, token claims, object-level authorization, rate limits, abuse cases, sensitive fields, RFC 9457 Problem Details or an explicit error-model compatibility gap.
  • Add event/webhook delivery evidence: schema, headers, signature verification, correlation ID, idempotency key, retry policy, ordering guarantee, replay, dead-letter behavior and CloudEvents applicability or non-applicability.
  • Add generated SDK reproducibility: generator, version, config, target languages, regeneration command, reviewable diff, SemVer impact and release process.
  • Keep API style choices conditional: GraphQL, gRPC, event-driven APIs, Spectral, Redocly and framework-native linting are not universal defaults.
  • Preserve API-only/backend false-positive protection: API-only contract fixtures do not force Backend blockers unless runtime/server/service/worker evidence exists.
  • Keep external writes approval-bound: provider mutation, generated client publication, webhook registration and other external actions require approval_required.

Implemented scope:

  • Added api_integrations catalog coverage with applies/not-applicable rules, maturity/complexity impact, decision horizons, artifacts, gates, eval fields and overlaps.
  • Added read-only API discovery signals for OpenAPI, Swagger source files, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, protobuf, JSON Schema, Pact, webhooks/events, generated clients and external providers.
  • Added audit recommendations for api_contract_source_present, api_consumer_map_present, api_breaking_change_reviewed, api_security_reviewed, api_error_contract_present, api_contract_test_matrix_present, event_delivery_contract_present, generated_client_manifest_present, external_write_approval_present, api_observability_contract_present, api_style_choice_recorded and unsupported API claims.

  • Strengthened api-contract-review.md, migration-plan.md, integration-catalog.md, generated control-plane templates, project-readiness.json, behavioral-workflows.json, lifecycle skills, Product-Agent OS README and operator docs.
  • Added synthetic fixtures for full API contract coverage, external-write approval, Swagger-UI-only false positive and GraphQL/gRPC style choice.
  • Added fixture eval check api_integrations_contract_present; renderer file count increased from 118 to 128 after the ten new API templates.

Severity and false-positive resolution:

  • Public, breaking, security-sensitive, event/webhook, generated SDK and external-write gaps are high-risk or blocker depth as appropriate.
  • Simple local/internal prototype work can use not_applicable, P2_recommended or explicit_gap_accepted only with owner, reason, review date, downstream consumer risk and follow-up.
  • API-only contract fixtures do not force Backend blockers.

  • API lint tooling deferred with owner/reason: Spectral, Redocly, framework-native linting, JSON Schema/protobuf/GraphQL/AsyncAPI compatibility rules, API security profile and stack-specific contract test generators remain candidate choices, not universal Product-Agent OS defaults.

docs.title: T9-D9 Database and Data Integration
docs.text:
Status: done

Source audited: docs/methodologies/database-data.md

Deep-audit deltas to implement:

  • Treat Database & Data as a full methodology domain, not only the existing data_migration usage-mode workflow.
  • Separate database gates for inventory, dictionary, schema source, migration plan, expand/contract rollout, transaction boundary, rollback feasibility, backup/restore evidence, data classification, data quality, data contract, lineage, query/index performance, retention/deletion, synthetic fixtures, production access approval and unsupported-claim rejection.
  • Keep database tooling conditional. PostgreSQL, Liquibase, Flyway, Alembic, Prisma, Rails/Django migrations, dbt, Great Expectations, OpenLineage, DBML, dbdocs, SchemaSpy and schema-diff tooling are candidate evidence sources, not universal Product-Agent OS defaults.
  • Keep DB introspection, production DB access, production data access, migration execution, destructive cleanup, backup restore and retention mutation approval_required.
  • Use conservative destructive-change detection for DROP, rename, truncate, destructive cleanup, retention purge, unsafe EXPLAIN ANALYZE on writes, ORM/schema drift and manual SQL-only changes. These are questions/recommendations, not execution or full SQL parser claims.
  • Preserve Track 8 data_migration compatibility: existing route mode and generic migration-plan.md remain valid, while database-specific work also stages or recommends database-migration-plan.md and related database artifacts.
  • Add a stable database_data_signals packet while keeping backward-compatible data_migration_signals.
  • Cover runtime/data pipeline signals: database clients, ORM models, data warehouse jobs, scheduled pipelines, reporting tables, analytics models and RAG ingestion sources stay present_unverified.
  • Explicit eval wording: runtime/pipeline/RAG signals stay present_unverified until owner-reviewed runtime, lineage or ingestion evidence exists.

docs.text:
Status: done

Source audited: docs/methodologies/security-privacy-compliance.md

Deep-audit deltas to implement:

  • Treat Security, Privacy & Compliance as a planning-first methodology domain for authn, authz, permissions, secrets, PII, sensitive data, payments, billing, abuse/rate limits, audit logging, supply chain, CI permissions, AI/agent security, external writes and compliance overlays.
  • Use the full gate set from the methodology source: security-sensitive classification, threat surface, security risk review, ASVS mapping, API security scheme, authz negative tests, secrets policy, data classification, privacy impact, external-write approval, abuse/rate-limit review, audit logging, supply chain, CI permissions, AI security, compliance overlay and evidence before completion.
  • Record source references as methodology evidence and platform/security guidance, not legal advice. Compliance output must record applicability, owner, evidence, non-goals, gaps and review cadence without claiming GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, PCI, SOC 2 or enterprise compliance certification.
  • Resolve artifact-name compatibility before renderer registration: source-era names such as threat-model.md, asvs-mapping.md, secrets-inventory.md, authz-matrix.md, audit-log-policy.md and compliance-applicability-matrix.md must map to canonical Product-Agent OS templates or aliases without duplicate conflicting contracts.
  • Map or explicitly defer the full source artifact set: data-classification-register.md, api-security-review.md, abuse-rate-limit-plan.md, sbom-manifest.md, ci-permissions-review.md, ai-security-review.md, vulnerability-response-record.md and approval-record.md must not be silently dropped.
  • Represent Secure SDLC/SSDF and OWASP SAMM as lifecycle/maturity vocabulary. ASVS Level 1/2/3 selection must record applicability, project risk, owner, evidence and gaps without claiming compliance.
  • API authorization negative tests must cover allowed and forbidden behavior, BOLA, BFLA, object property authorization, role/scope/resource ownership, rate limits and unsafe consumption. OAuth or API docs alone are not accepted as security evidence.
  • Data classification and redaction lifecycle must cover prompts, docs, fixtures, eval datasets, logs, traces and screenshots. Raw secrets, credentials, payment data, raw PII, raw private chats and private customer data are blocked.
  • SBOM/provenance policy must distinguish internal apps, packages, plugins, containers and release artifacts, and must connect SBOM to vulnerability status, update path, license status, provenance, action pinning, release signing or an explicit accepted gap.
  • Vulnerability/security incident workflow must cover security bugs, advisories, leaked secrets, abuse incidents, dependency alerts and data exposure with triage, severity, containment, fix evidence, verification, disclosure, release/patch plan and post-incident lessons.
  • Compliance overlays must separate legal/regulatory obligations, customer contractual obligations and internal policy, with conditional overlays for finance, healthcare, minors, enterprise, public sector, marketplace and AI agent tooling.
  • Codex Security scan remains explicit opt-in. Security-sensitive routing can recommend a scan or record not requested, but must not imply that a scan ran from security terminology alone.
  • False-positive policy: security docs mention without code path remains present_unverified; docs-only repositories with security articles do not become regulated automatically; keyword-only compliance claims do not prove compliance; no-secrets-in-code does not prove artifact safety.
  • Unsupported claims must be rejected as high-risk evidence gaps: security review after coding, no-secrets-in-code means safe, ASVS/OWASP proves compliance, SBOM once is enough, Codex Security scan is implied, OAuth proves API security and privacy compliance is universal.

Current fixture symptoms to resolve during Task 20:

Symptoms resolved by batch T9-S-M5..M9:

  • backend FSD-like directories no longer trigger frontend recommendations without UI/runtime evidence.
  • security/payment and release risks can outrank generic quality strategy in safe_next_action.
  • CI-only workflows, docs-only release notes and tooling-only release files no longer prove security or release readiness without owner-reviewed evidence.

  • Added RED synthesis tests and kept the expected RED failure evidence.
  • Added additive top-level synthesis catalog metadata without changing domain gates, artifacts or eval_fields list shapes.

Batch T9-S-M5..M9 implemented:

  • Integrated methodology_synthesis into build_methodology_audit() as additive top-level recommendation_groups and methodology_synthesis output while keeping existing recommendation keys compatible.
  • Made safe_next_action risk-aware so high-risk security, release, payment and public-contract blockers can outrank generic quality recommendations.
  • Added a discovery methodology_synthesis applicability packet with present_unverified status and evidence for recommendation groups, source artifact ledger and semantic evidence sufficiency.
  • Added shared semantic_evidence_sufficiency generated control-plane, readiness and behavioral eval contracts, including owner-reviewed accepted-gap fields.
  • Hardened false-positive routing for backend FSD-like TypeScript directories, CI-only workflows, docs-only release notes and tooling-only release artifacts.

Batch T9-S-M10..M14 implemented:

  • Added mixed-risk cross-domain fixtures for small PII app, complex monorepo without production users, internal CLI without UI/API/release hard blockers, AI/RAG plus data/security overlap, package release with security handoff, source artifact alias/deferred mapping and owner-question dedupe.

docs.title: Residual Risks
docs.text:
• The catalog currently represents foundation behavior and selected generic gates; domain slices can still reveal missing artifacts or conflicts.
  • Read-only audit can classify workspace signals, but owner intent, product risk and regulatory constraints still require human confirmation.
  • Recommendation priority order is deterministic, but real-world severity can change when a project has production traffic, sensitive data or external consumers.
  • Codex workflow gates prove governance shape and approval routing, not that a human owner has approved every model, subagent, MCP, hook, skill, plugin or automation decision for a real project.

docs.title: API & Integrations Methodology Research
docs.text:
Source status: official + verified methodology + tool-assisted

Research date: 2026-05-24

Target methodology page: ../../methodologies/api-integrations.md

Target Product-Agent OS behavior: detect API and integration work early, require a contract source of truth, route risky changes through consumer, security, compatibility and release gates, and produce reviewable artifacts before code changes reach public or semi-public contracts.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
This dossier covers HTTP APIs, message/event APIs, webhooks, GraphQL, gRPC, generated SDKs, external integrations, API security, error contracts, versioning, compatibility, documentation artifacts and Product-Agent OS candidates.

It does not choose a universal API style for every project. The project should select an API style based on consumers, latency, ownership, ecosystem, tooling and operational risk.

docs.title: Supported facts
docs.text:
• OpenAPI Specification v3.2.0 is the current OpenAPI contract source checked for this research run. It describes HTTP APIs in a programming-language-agnostic format and includes operations, parameters, request bodies, responses, examples, security schemes and reusable components.
  • AsyncAPI Specification v3.1.0 is the current AsyncAPI contract source checked for this research run. It describes message-driven APIs in a machine-readable, protocol-agnostic format.
  • RFC 9110 defines HTTP semantics. HTTP API design should not invent local meanings for methods, status codes and content negotiation when standard semantics already exist.
  • RFC 9457 defines Problem Details for HTTP APIs and obsoletes RFC 7807. It should be considered the default candidate for machine-readable HTTP error payloads unless the project already has a stronger compatibility reason.
  • RFC 9700 is the OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice as of January 2025. OAuth-based APIs should treat it as a security baseline source, not as optional prose.
  • OWASP API Security Top 10 2023 is the current OWASP API-specific risk catalog checked in this research run. It is useful for API threat modeling and security review gates.
  • JSON Schema current version is 2020-12 according to the official JSON Schema specification page. Projects using JSON payload schemas should state the dialect.
  • CloudEvents v1.0.2 and the CNCF CloudEvents project provide a standardized event metadata envelope option. It is useful when event interoperability across systems matters.
  • GraphQL has a latest release dated September 2025 and a working draft dated April 2026. A project should pin the GraphQL specification target it follows instead of saying only "GraphQL".
  • gRPC uses Protocol Buffers as the default Interface Definition Language and message interchange format; .proto files become the source contract for service methods and messages.
  • Pact documents consumer-driven contract testing as a contract-by-example approach. It complements schema contracts because it captures actual consumer expectations, not every theoretically possible schema state.
  • OpenAPI Generator can generate clients, server stubs and documentation from OpenAPI documents. Generated SDKs need a manifest, ownership, versioning and regeneration policy.
  • Stoplight Spectral is documented as a JSON/YAML linter with ready-to-use style guides for OpenAPI and AsyncAPI. It is a candidate for API lint gates when the project chooses that toolchain.
  • Google API Improvement Proposals are a vendor-specific but mature model for recording API design rules. The useful transferable idea is the local API style guide as a governed artifact.

docs.title: Methodologies
docs.text: Methodology When to apply Project-level behavior Contract-first development New public API, SDK, provider/consumer split Contract is written or changed before implementation; code and tests conform to it. Contract-aware development Existing code-first service Generated or maintained contract is updated in the same slice as behavior changes. Consumer-driven contract testing Multiple consumers, microservices, frontend/backend split Consumers express expectations through contract tests; providers verify before release. API lifecycle governance APIs move from draft to stable to deprecated Every endpoint/message has lifecycle state, owner, compatibility policy and deprecation path. Backward compatibility by default Public, partner, mobile, SDK or event contracts Changes are classified as breaking/non-breaking before implementation. Error-contract governance HTTP APIs expose machine consumers Error responses use a documented model, preferably Problem Details when compatible. Event-contract governance Async messaging, queues, streams, webhooks Event schema, idempotency, retry, ordering, correlation and dead-letter behavior are documented. Integration security by design Authenticated API, external provider, sensitive data Auth scheme, scopes, token claims, rate limits, object-level authorization and abuse cases are reviewed. Generated-client governance SDKs or typed clients are generated Generator, config, target languages, compatibility and release process are documented. API style-guide governance Large project or many teams Local API rules are versioned and lintable where possible. Two-stage review Public contract, migration, SDK, auth, event payload Stage 1 checks contract/security/compatibility; stage 2 checks implementation quality.

docs.title: Documentation artifacts and standards
docs.text: Artifact Purpose Candidate source/tool API inventory List APIs, owners, lifecycle states, consumers and source-of-truth files. Markdown/YAML table in repo. OpenAPI document HTTP API source of truth. OpenAPI v3.2.0 or project-pinned compatible version. AsyncAPI document Message/event API source of truth. AsyncAPI v3.1.0 or project-pinned compatible version. GraphQL schema GraphQL contract source. .graphql schema plus pinned GraphQL spec target. gRPC/protobuf IDL RPC contract source. .proto files and generator config. JSON Schema library Shared JSON payload contracts. JSON Schema 2020-12 unless project pins older dialect. Problem Details catalog Stable HTTP error types, status codes and extensions. RFC 9457. Auth and authorization matrix Schemes, scopes, roles, token claims, object-level rules. OpenAPI security schemes, OAuth BCP, OWASP API risks. Consumer map Human/system consumers, SDKs, generated clients, owners and approval path. api-consumer-map.md. Compatibility decision record Breaking/non-breaking classification and migration impact. ADR-style record or api-compatibility-record.md. Contract test matrix Provider verification, consumer tests, schema tests and negative cases. Pact, schema validators, stack-specific API tests. Generated SDK manifest Generator, version, config, target languages, owner and release process. OpenAPI Generator or stack-specific generator. Deprecation plan Timeline, compatibility mode, comms, release notes and removal criteria. Changelog/release packet.

docs.title: Project application instructions
docs.text:
1. Classify the integration: internal HTTP API, public API, partner API, webhook, async event stream, GraphQL, gRPC, generated SDK, external provider or automation integration.
  2. Declare the contract source of truth. If there is no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema or .proto, record the gap before implementation.
  3. Name provider, consumers, owners, generated clients and runtime environments.
  4. Classify the change as additive, behavior-compatible, potentially breaking or breaking.
  5. Update the contract before or alongside code. Do not let rendered docs or Swagger UI become the source of truth.
  6. Add examples for success, validation failure, auth failure and the most important domain failure.
  7. Document auth scheme, scopes, object-level authorization rules, rate limits and sensitive fields.
  8. Document the error model. For HTTP APIs, prefer RFC 9457 Problem Details when compatible with existing clients.
  9. For event/message changes, document schema, headers, correlation ID, idempotency key, retry policy, ordering guarantees and dead-letter behavior.
  10. For generated SDKs, update the generation manifest and record whether clients need a major, minor or patch release.
  11. Add or update contract tests: schema validation, provider verification and consumer-driven tests where consumer risk is high.
  12. For external writes, create a staged draft or approval artifact before the agent touches the external system.
  13. Add observability expectations: request IDs, correlation IDs, error counters, latency, rate-limit metrics and integration failure alerts.
  14. Record rollout, deprecation and rollback path in the release artifact.

docs.title: Candidate eval fields
docs.text:
• Contract source is named and linked.
  • Consumers and generated clients are named.
  • Breaking/non-breaking classification is present.
  • Migration/deprecation plan exists for breaking changes.
  • Auth scheme and authorization rules are documented.
  • Success and error examples are present.
  • Event delivery semantics are documented for async integrations.
  • Contract verification command or missing-tool gap is recorded.
  • External writes are staged and approval-bound.

docs.title: Tooling candidates
docs.text: Tooling area Candidate Notes HTTP API contract OpenAPI Default source for REST-like HTTP APIs. Pin spec version per project. Event API contract AsyncAPI Default source for message-driven APIs and webhooks when useful. Shared JSON schemas JSON Schema Declare dialect; avoid validator-default ambiguity. Error model RFC 9457 Problem Details Good default for machine-readable HTTP errors. API lint Spectral Useful when the project has an API style guide. Tool adoption requires stack check. Code/doc generation OpenAPI Generator Useful for SDKs/stubs/docs; generated output requires ownership and diff review. Consumer contracts Pact Useful when real consumer expectations matter more than schema completeness. Event metadata CloudEvents Useful for cross-system event interoperability; not mandatory for simple internal events. RPC gRPC/protobuf Useful for low-latency, typed, polyglot service-to-service APIs. Query API GraphQL Useful for client-shaped reads and schema-driven product APIs; requires governance for complexity, authorization and deprecation.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text:
• Treating rendered API docs as the source of truth instead of the machine-readable contract.
  • Shipping event payload changes without consumer compatibility review.
  • Assuming an internal API has no consumers.
  • Generating SDKs without a reproducible generator config.
  • Adding OAuth scopes or token claims without an authorization matrix.
  • Returning undocumented error payloads that clients cannot handle.
  • Treating GraphQL or gRPC as automatically superior to HTTP APIs without consumer and operational justification.
  • Letting contract tests duplicate only provider behavior instead of expressing consumer expectations.
  • Allowing an agent to write to external systems without staged artifact and approval.

docs.title: Open questions for deeper research
docs.text:
• Which API lint tool should become the Product-Agent OS default: Spectral, Redocly CLI, framework-native checks or no default?
  • Should Product-Agent OS ship a generic API style guide template, or only a selector that asks the project to choose one?
  • Which schema compatibility rules should be encoded for JSON Schema, protobuf, GraphQL and AsyncAPI separately?
  • Should API security gates be based on OWASP API Top 10, ASVS, SSDF, or a combined project profile?
  • How should agentic API migrations handle generated clients across multiple repositories?
  • Which API test generators are mature enough for default recommendation by stack?

docs.title: Backend Methodology Research
docs.text:
Source status: official + expert reference + vendor documentation + tool-assisted

Research date: 2026-05-24

Target methodology page: ../../methodologies/backend.md

Target Product-Agent OS behavior: detect backend work, force service boundary and runtime behavior clarity, route risky service changes through reliability/security/data/operations gates, and require evidence for tests, observability, rollback and production readiness before completion.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
This dossier covers backend services, modular monolith modules, workers, schedulers, queues, service boundaries, domain logic, background jobs, runtime configuration, resiliency, observability, SLOs, security, health checks, distributed consistency and operational documentation.

It does not mandate microservices, Kubernetes, a cloud provider or a specific framework. Those are conditional implementation choices, not default architecture rules.

docs.title: Supported facts
docs.text:
• The Twelve-Factor App defines a methodology for service-style applications, including explicit dependencies, environment-based config, backing services as attached resources, build-release-run separation, stateless processes, disposability, dev/prod parity, logs as event streams and one-off admin processes.
  • OpenTelemetry is a vendor-neutral observability framework for traces, metrics and logs, with concepts for context propagation, baggage, semantic conventions, collectors and language instrumentation.
  • Google SRE guidance frames SLO work around user-relevant SLIs and recommends choosing a small number of indicators that represent what users care about.
  • NIST SSDF recommends secure software development practices that can be integrated into SDLC implementations.
  • OWASP ASVS provides a versioned basis for testing web application technical security controls and secure development requirements.
  • CNCF Cloud Native Definition characterizes cloud-native systems as loosely coupled, secure, resilient, manageable, sustainable and observable, supported by automation.
  • Kubernetes readiness, liveness and startup probes are distinct runtime health mechanisms. Readiness prevents traffic from reaching a service that is alive but not ready.
  • Hexagonal Architecture, also known as Ports and Adapters, separates application logic from UI, database and runtime adapters so the application can be tested and driven through multiple ports.
  • Martin Fowler's microservices guide defines microservices as independently deployable services built around business capabilities and highlights design-for-failure as a characteristic.
  • Microsoft Azure Architecture Center documents retry, circuit breaker, queue-based load leveling, health endpoint monitoring and saga patterns. These are vendor-specific docs, but the patterns are broadly useful as backend resilience and distributed workflow references.

docs.title: Methodologies
docs.text: Methodology When to apply Project-level behavior Modular monolith first Early or medium-size product, unclear service boundaries Keep deployable complexity low while enforcing module ownership and domain boundaries. Conditional microservices Independent scaling, team ownership or deployment autonomy is proven Services map to business capabilities, have independent deployability and explicit failure contracts. Hexagonal Architecture / Ports and Adapters Domain logic is important and adapters change Core use cases depend on ports/interfaces; database, HTTP, queue and vendor SDKs are adapters. Domain-Driven Design boundaries Complex business domain or ambiguous vocabulary Backend modules/services map to bounded contexts and ubiquitous language. TDD for domain logic Deterministic business rules and service logic Unit tests drive behavior before implementation. Integration-first backend testing Storage, queues, transactions, external adapters Tests exercise real or representative boundaries before release. Contract-aware service development Service exposes APIs/events or consumes external contracts OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, Pact, .proto or provider contract changes are updated with code. Twelve-Factor service discipline SaaS/cloud-style backend Config, dependencies, runtime process model, logs and admin tasks are documented. SRE-inspired reliability Production service with users or downstream consumers SLO or explicit gap, user-relevant SLIs, runbooks and alert signals. Observability-driven development Debugging requires runtime evidence Traces, metrics, logs, correlation IDs and dashboard/alert expectations are captured. Resilience pattern design Remote dependencies, queues, load spikes or transient faults Timeouts, retry, backoff, circuit breaker, load leveling, backpressure and fallback are designed together. Secure SDLC Backend touches auth, sensitive data, money, secrets or privileged operations Security requirements, threat notes, abuse cases, audit logging and no-secrets evidence are required. Saga / compensating workflow Distributed business transaction cannot use a single ACID transaction Workflow state, idempotency, compensation, monitoring and failure recovery are documented. Runbook-driven operations Production service or scheduled job Operators get failure modes, dashboards, logs, restart/replay steps and escalation path.

docs.title: Documentation artifacts and standards
docs.text: Artifact Purpose Candidate source/tool Service overview Purpose, owner, boundary, dependencies, data stores, APIs/events and runtime. backend-service-overview.md Module/service boundary map Shows what belongs inside the backend boundary and what is external. C4, Mermaid, Structurizr, ADR Ports and adapters map Lists inbound ports, outbound ports and concrete adapters. Hexagonal Architecture Runtime behavior doc Background jobs, queues, retries, timeouts, idempotency, backpressure and failure modes. backend-runtime-behavior.md Dependency failure matrix Per dependency: timeout, retry, circuit breaker, fallback, owner and alert. Resilience pattern docs Observability map Traces, metrics, logs, correlation IDs, dashboards, alerts and redaction notes. OpenTelemetry SLO sheet User journey, SLI, SLO target, measurement window and alert policy. Google SRE Health check contract Liveness/readiness/startup or equivalent health semantics. Kubernetes docs, platform docs Queue/job contract Queue name, producer, consumer, payload contract, idempotency, retry, DLQ and replay. AsyncAPI, runbook Data consistency record Transaction boundary, consistency model, outbox/saga/compensation and recovery path. ADR/runbook Security notes Authn/authz, secrets, rate limits, audit logging, sensitive data and abuse cases. NIST SSDF, OWASP ASVS Config and secrets manifest Env/config keys, secret source, rotation notes and local/prod parity. Twelve-Factor, platform docs Release and rollback notes Migration, feature flag, rollback, replay and data recovery plan. Release packet Operational runbook Common failures, dashboard links, logs, recovery steps and escalation. SRE practice

docs.title: Project application instructions
docs.text:
1. Classify the backend unit: module, monolith subsystem, service, worker, scheduler, consumer, API backend, integration adapter or migration runner.
  2. Name the service boundary: purpose, owner, inbound contracts, outbound dependencies, data ownership and deployment/runtime shape.
  3. If the domain is complex, map the boundary to bounded contexts and domain language.
  4. Decide whether Ports and Adapters is useful. Apply it when domain logic must stay independent from HTTP, database, queue or vendor SDK concerns.
  5. Document runtime behavior before implementing distributed behavior: retries, timeouts, idempotency, deduplication, backpressure, ordering, scheduling and replay.
  6. For every remote dependency, write a failure policy: timeout, retry, circuit breaker, fallback, alert and owner.
  7. For background jobs and queues, document payload contract, retry policy, dead-letter behavior, idempotency key and replay procedure.
  8. For distributed transactions, prefer a simple local transaction when possible. If not possible, document saga/compensation and monitoring explicitly.
  9. Define observability evidence: traces for request flow, metrics for service health, logs for decisions/errors and correlation IDs across boundaries.
  10. For production services, define SLO or record why it is not yet applicable.
  11. Treat health endpoints as contracts. Liveness, readiness and startup checks should not be vague aliases.
  12. Document config and secrets. Secrets must not appear in docs, prompts, fixtures, logs or examples.
  13. Route auth, sensitive data, money movement, privileged operations and irreversible side effects through security/risk review.
  14. Record rollback and recovery before claiming completion for risky backend changes.

  • Terms: service, worker, queue, retry, timeout, idempotency, circuit breaker, background job, scheduler, migration, auth, token, secret, SLO, runbook, health check, readiness, liveness
  • Dependency signals: database clients, message broker clients, HTTP clients, payment/email/storage/search providers, cache clients

docs.text:
• Service/module boundary, owner and purpose are present.
  • Dependencies and data stores are named.
  • Runtime behavior is documented for jobs, queues and remote calls.
  • Retry policy includes timeout, backoff, max attempts and idempotency.
  • Observability contract includes no-secrets logging and correlation IDs.
  • SLO/SLI exists or gap is explicit.
  • Health checks distinguish liveness, readiness and startup where applicable.
  • Security-sensitive behavior has a risk review route.
  • Data consistency and rollback plan exist for risky changes.
  • Verification commands include unit, integration, contract or runtime checks appropriate to the change.
