  warnings: []
  next_action: ""

The result schema is the core Track 5 contract. Fixture eval should grade this contract first; Codex execution quality can be judged only after deterministic gates pass.

docs.title: Routing Policy
docs.text:
The runner chooses the next Product-Agent OS action from lifecycle state and current artifacts:

State Default route Write policy uninitialized workspace-discovery-auditor read_only infrastructure_planned requirements-author staged_only requirements_ready implementation-planner staged_only plan_ready agent-team-designer staged_only team_ready test-eval-designer staged_only build_active builder subagent or build slice packet approved_write quality_gate risk-reviewer read_only review_ready pr-release-operator staged_only release_ready learning-loop-maintainer staged_only learning_ready automation-promoter staged_only maintenance project-lifecycle-orchestrator read_only

The runner may recommend a subagent only when ownership boundaries are explicit. It must not spawn subagents itself from deterministic tests; it returns a route packet that Codex can execute in the active session.

docs.title: Guardrails And Validators
docs.text:
Required validators:

  • validate_codex_runner_request - schema, surface, write policy, and approval state.
  • validate_control_plane_context - required Product-Agent OS artifacts and lifecycle consistency.
  • validate_route_packet - recommended skill or subagent is valid for lifecycle state.
  • validate_handoff - reuse and extend Product-Agent OS handoff fields.
  • validate_source_policy - block or mark needs-review before durable source-backed claims.
  • validate_approval_boundary - no workspace writes or hook activation without approval.
  • validate_automation_boundary - active automation creation remains blocked.
  • validate_redaction - no secret-like literals, private customer data markers, raw private chat markers, or absolute user-specific paths in persisted outputs.
  • validate_result_contract - every completion claim has current-run evidence.

docs.title: Fixture Eval Extension
docs.text:
Extend fixture eval with runner fields:

codex_runtime_runner_status: "route_ready | needs_context | needs_approval | blocked | not_applicable"
codex_runtime_runner_checks:
  contract_mode_offline: true
  route_matches_lifecycle_state: true
  approval_required_for_writes: true
  handoff_incomplete_blocked: true
  active_automation_blocked: true
  secret_redaction_enforced: true

New synthetic fixtures:

  • codex-runner-ready - complete control-plane context produces route_ready.
  • codex-runner-missing-context - missing PLAN.md or acceptance criteria produces needs_context.
  • codex-runner-handoff-incomplete - missing constraints or verification_evidence is blocked.
  • codex-runner-approval-required - build/write route without approval produces needs_approval.
  • codex-runner-automation-blocked - active automation request is blocked.
  • codex-runner-secret-redaction - secret-like and absolute-path strings are redacted in result.

All fixtures must use synthetic data only.

docs.title: Security And Approval Model
docs.text:
Default policy:

  • read-only unless the route explicitly says staged_only or approved_write;
  • no network access;
  • no external dependency installation;
  • no direct API calls;
  • no active automation creation;
  • no project write from the runner itself;
  • outputs redacted before persistence;
  • failures return machine-readable status and no traceback in normal CLI output.

Blocked by default:

  • global Codex config mutation;
  • hook activation without Track 4 approval;
  • merge/apply without approval record;
  • active automation creation;
  • external system writes;
  • raw private chat logs;
  • secret-like literals in outputs;
  • absolute user-specific paths in persisted artifacts;
  • claiming implementation success without current-run evidence.

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
Deterministic Track 5 tests remain unittest and standard-library-only.

Required tests:

  • runner contracts validate valid and invalid request/result payloads;
  • package imports with only Python standard library;
  • contract mode runs offline against a fixture workspace;
  • lifecycle state maps to the expected Product-Agent OS skill route;
  • build/write routes require approval;
  • incomplete handoff is rejected;
  • source-policy blocked prevents route readiness;
  • active automation request is blocked;
  • redaction removes secret-like literals and local absolute paths;
  • fixture eval includes codex_runtime_runner_status;
  • plugin structure test proves runner exists but is not default-activated;
  • normal verification commands do not require network, API credentials, or dependency installation.

Required verification after implementation:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py
python tools\check_docs.py
$env:PYTHONPATH='C:\tmp\codex_docs_mkdocs'; python -m mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
Track 5 is complete when:

  • plugins/product-agent-os/scripts/codex_runtime_runner/ exists and imports with standard library only;
  • contract mode returns a valid codex_runner_result;
  • route packets correctly map lifecycle states to Product-Agent OS skills or subagent roles;
  • workspace writes, hook activation, merge/apply, and automation remain approval-gated;
  • runner validators catch incomplete handoffs, blocked source policy, missing approval, active automation requests, and secret retention;
  • fixture eval reports Codex runtime runner status and catches regressions;
  • plugin manifest and lifecycle skills do not make the runner default-active;
  • source registry and docs navigation include this Track 5 spec;
  • full verification pack exits 0.

docs.title: Residual Risks
docs.text:
Even after Track 5, a Codex-only runner cannot prove product correctness for every project. It can prove that lifecycle routing, handoff shape, source policy, approval boundary, redaction, and fixture eval behavior are stable.

The runner intentionally delegates actual model work to Codex. Quality still depends on the active Codex surface, selected model, prompt context, project artifacts, and verification evidence.

docs.title: Implementation Handoff
docs.text:
Implementation should be split into focused tasks:

  1. Codex runner contracts and result schema.
  2. Context loader and lifecycle state detector.
  3. Route planner for skills and subagent role recommendations.
  4. Redaction and deterministic guard validators.
  5. Contract-mode CLI wrapper.
  6. Fixture eval extension and synthetic runner fixtures.
  7. Plugin structure tests proving the runner is present but inactive by default.
  8. Documentation, source registry refresh, navigation, and full verification.

Each task should start with failing tests where practical, preserve Track 4 safety behavior, and avoid unrelated refactors.

docs.title: Spec Self-Review
docs.text:
Coverage:

  • standalone API-backed runner is removed from scope;
  • Codex-only execution boundary is explicit;
  • current Track 1-4 implementation and clean baseline are recorded;
  • route packet, handoff, result, approval, source, automation, and redaction policies are explicit;
  • fixture eval and verification requirements are defined.

Scope check:

  • Track 5 is one coherent Codex plugin orchestration layer, not a deployment platform or external app;
  • no deterministic test requires network, credentials, or third-party dependencies;
  • actual Codex model execution remains in the active Codex session, not in a separate runner process.

Ambiguity check:

  • default Product-Agent OS workflow remains unchanged;
  • no API keys or external credentials are used;
  • the runner may exist in the repo while remaining inactive by default;
  • writes and automations remain approval-gated through existing Product-Agent OS controls.

docs.title: Track 9 Methodology Intelligence Design
docs.text:
Source status: local product design + methodology research synthesis

Sources: Methodologies for Large Projects, Business & Product, Requirements & Domain, Solution Architecture, Frontend, Backend, API & Integrations, Database & Data, LLM / AI / RAG, Quality, Testing & Evals, Security, Privacy & Compliance, Delivery, Release & Operations, Codex / Agentic Workflow, Product-Agent OS plugin docs.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Track 9 turns Product-Agent OS from a scenario workflow plugin into a methodology-aware product engineering system. When connected to a user project, it should first understand the workspace, classify project complexity and delivery maturity, build a project delivery map, then recommend the right methodologies, documentation artifacts, readiness gates, owners, evidence, approvals and next actions.

The product goal is to replace chaotic vibe-coding on real projects with a guided path toward product-ready software: clear intent, scoped architecture, useful artifacts, current evidence, reviewable risks and staged changes that are safe to show to users, teams or stakeholders.

docs.title: Core Product Principle
docs.text:
Track 9 must cover all aspects of development without forcing all methodology on every project.

The operating rule is:

cover every methodology domain
force only what is clearly applicable
record gaps and assumptions honestly
stage artifacts only after approval

docs.title: Existing Foundation
docs.text:
Track 8 already provides scenario routing, conditional readiness statuses, evidence-before-completion, acceptance scenarios, conditional DDD, bounded-context traceability, ubiquitous language traceability, conditional FSD routing, metric hardening, docs tooling selection, standards trigger policy, transcript/session evals and detailed methodology_applicability packets.

Track 9 builds on that foundation instead of replacing it. Scenario routing still answers "what situation is this project or request in?" Methodology intelligence answers "which engineering disciplines, artifacts and evidence are proportionate for this project's complexity, risk and maturity?"

docs.title: High-Level Flow
docs.text:
Track 9 uses a two-step onboarding flow.

User connects Product-Agent OS to workspace
    ↓
Read-only audit
    ↓
Complexity and maturity classification
    ↓
Delivery Map
    ↓
Methodology applicability analysis
    ↓
Human-readable audit report + machine-readable JSON
    ↓
User approval
    ↓
Staged artifacts and control-plane proposals

The first step is read-only. It produces recommendations and questions. The second step stages artifacts only after explicit approval.

docs.title: Classification Model
docs.text:
Track 9 uses two independent axes.

maturity_level describes the delivery and governance level:

Level Meaning baseline MVP, solo owner or low-risk internal work; minimum requirements, plan, checks and runlog. team Multiple engineers, subagents or workstreams; ownership, handoffs, architecture boundary and docs impact matter. production Real users, deployments, data, release process or operations; security, rollback, release readiness and runtime evidence matter. regulated PII, payments, healthcare, finance, minors, enterprise governance, legal/compliance or audit requirements.

complexity_profile describes the system and change complexity:

Profile Meaning simple Small project or narrow change with few dependencies and low blast radius. standard Normal product or service with tests, docs, API/UI/data surfaces or repeatable delivery. complex Multiple subsystems, integrations, teams, domains, workflows, data stores or runtime environments. high_risk Security, privacy, money, production data, irreversible migration, public contract, AI behavior, release or operational risk.

The classifier records:

  • observed_signals: facts discovered in files and workspace structure;
  • intent_signals: user request or prompt intent, never treated as proof by itself;
  • unknowns: facts that cannot be proven from workspace state;
  • questions_for_owner: questions that should be answered by the user or project owner;
  • provisional_assumptions: conservative assumptions used to choose a safe next step;
  • confidence: confidence for each classification and domain recommendation;
  • blocked_until_answered: whether missing answers block staging or implementation;
  • safe_next_action: what Product-Agent OS can do without overclaiming.

docs.title: Delivery Map
docs.text:
The read-only audit produces a Delivery Map rather than a passive repository summary.

The Delivery Map includes:

  • surface map: stack, package managers, entrypoints, test commands, docs, CI, runtime manifests and generated folders;
  • system map: domains, subsystems, UI/API/data/AI surfaces, data stores, external integrations, deploy/runtime surfaces and ownership gaps;
  • lifecycle map: current Product-Agent OS lifecycle state, control-plane status, existing evidence and missing files;
  • methodology map: applicable domains, missing gates, unverified artifacts, accepted gaps and approval-required actions;
  • next-action map: prioritized actions that connect a reason, methodology, artifact, owner, evidence and approval boundary.

docs.title: Audit Outputs
docs.text:
The read-only audit produces two outputs:

  1. methodology-audit-report.md Human-readable report for the user. It explains project classification, Delivery Map, methodology recommendations, questions, assumptions, risks and next actions.

  2. methodology-applicability.json Machine-readable contract for plugin scripts, lifecycle skills, fixture evals and later staged artifact generation.

The JSON output must be stable enough for tests and fixture evals. Markdown is for humans and must not become the source parser for plugin behavior.

docs.title: Recommendation Model
docs.text:
Recommendations are prioritized actions, not a list of documents to generate.

Each recommendation records:

  • priority: P0_blocker, P1_high_risk, P2_recommended, P3_optional_maturity or not_applicable;
  • reason: why this matters for this project;
  • methodology domain;
  • readiness gate;
  • recommended artifact;
  • evidence required;
  • evidence owner;
  • approval boundary;
  • accepted gap option;
  • residual risk;
  • safe next action.

This prevents document spam. An artifact is recommended only when it closes a gate, reduces a risk, supports ownership, records evidence or enables a concrete next action.

docs.title: Methodology Domains
docs.text:
Track 9 includes every methodology file under docs/methodologies.

Slice Source file Product-Agent OS purpose T9-D1 business-product.md Product hypothesis, value, opportunities, metrics, guardrails and measurement. T9-D2 requirements-domain.md Requirements quality, acceptance scenarios, business rules, domain model, traceability and change impact. T9-D3 solution-architecture.md Architecture boundaries, views, ADRs, quality attributes, tradeoffs, ownership and fitness checks. T9-D4 quality-testing-evals.md Risk-based tests, evals, current evidence, runtime/manual/visual evidence and CI quality gates. T9-D5 codex-agentic-workflow.md Control-plane maturity, model/reasoning policy, handoffs, subagents, MCP, hooks, skills, plugins and automation promotion. T9-D6 frontend.md UI behavior, component states, Storybook applicability, visual/a11y evidence, responsive checks, performance and FSD boundaries. T9-D7 backend.md Service boundaries, modular monolith vs microservices, runtime behavior, queues, observability, SLOs and rollback. T9-D8 api-integrations.md OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL/gRPC contracts, consumers, compatibility, errors, generated clients and external writes. T9-D9 database-data.md Database inventory, schema source, migrations, transactions, data quality, classification and production access. T9-D10 llm-ai-rag.md AI behavior spec, eval baseline, prompts, models, tools, RAG sources, grounding, datasets, approvals and cost/latency. T9-D11 security-privacy-compliance.md Threat surface, ASVS/SSDF, authorization tests, secrets, privacy impact, supply chain, audit logging and compliance overlays. T9-D12 delivery-release-operations.md Release readiness, versioning, changelog, artifact manifest, rollout, rollback, CI/CD governance, runbooks and operations.

The order is intentional: product intent, requirements, architecture, quality and Codex workflow come before technical domains. Security/privacy and delivery/operations remain cross-cutting overlays but still receive dedicated domain slices.

docs.title: Domain Slice Contract
docs.text: Each domain slice follows the same implementation contract.

docs.title: Catalog Entries
docs.text:
Each domain adds machine-readable catalog entries:

  • domain id;
  • purpose;
  • applicability triggers;
  • non-applicability triggers;
  • maturity impact;
  • complexity impact;
  • related Track 8 scenarios;
  • related artifacts;
  • readiness gates;
  • eval fields;
  • conflict and overlap notes.

docs.title: Discovery Signals
docs.text:
Each domain defines:

  • file, folder, manifest and config signals;
  • prompt intent hints;
  • signals that only support present_unverified;
  • unknowns that should become questionnaire entries;
  • false-positive risks.

docs.title: Readiness Gates
docs.text:
All gates reuse the existing status vocabulary:

  • not_applicable;
  • applicable_missing;
  • present_unverified;
  • present_verified;
  • proposal_staged;
  • explicit_gap_accepted;
  • approval_required.

Detection alone can only produce present_unverified. present_verified requires current command evidence, owner evidence, artifact evidence or a clearly recorded accepted gap.

docs.title: Artifact Templates
docs.text:
Each domain adds or extends artifact templates only when they are tied to a gate or recommendation. Templates must be synthetic, source-safe and secret-free.

Examples include product briefs, requirement traceability matrices, architecture review records, frontend state matrices, backend runtime behavior docs, API consumer maps, database migration plans, AI eval specs, security risk reviews and release readiness packets.

docs.title: Lifecycle Skill Updates
docs.text:
Each domain updates relevant lifecycle skills:

  • workspace-discovery-auditor observes signals and unknowns;
  • requirements-author captures product, requirement and domain evidence;
  • implementation-planner blocks build work when applicable gates are missing;
  • agent-team-designer maps ownership and handoff boundaries;
  • test-eval-designer selects checks and evals;
  • risk-reviewer reviews missing evidence, accepted gaps, conflicts and risky changes;
  • pr-release-operator includes release, contract, security and operations impact;
  • learning-loop-maintainer records lessons and domain decisions;
  • automation-promoter refuses promotion without maturity evidence and rollback.

docs.title: Tests And Evals
docs.text:
Each domain slice must add:

  • focused unit tests for catalog/discovery/gate behavior;
  • fixture eval coverage;
  • false-positive tests when the domain can be over-applied;
  • docs sync;
  • Product-Agent OS docs updates when user behavior changes;
  • source registry updates when source-backed claims change.

docs.title: Adaptive Deep-Dive Loop
docs.text:
The Track 9 queue is a living backlog. Each methodology file is inspected before implementation and can expand into multiple sub-slices.

T9-Dn-0: domain deep audit
    ↓
T9-Dn-1..N: implementation sub-slices
    ↓
T9-Dn-final: domain verification and docs sync

Each domain deep audit records:

  • concepts already covered by Track 8;
  • new concepts;
  • duplicate or overlapping gates;
  • new artifacts;
  • existing artifacts that need extension;
  • likely false positives;
  • required tests and evals;
  • open questions;
  • items deferred to cross-domain synthesis.

The backlog may change when a deep audit finds hidden sub-tasks, cross-domain overlap, false positives, duplicate artifacts, insufficient tests or a changed product direction. Every change must be recorded in RUNLOG.md or a Track 9 status/backlog document with rationale.

docs.title: Cross-Domain Synthesis
docs.text:
After all 12 domains are integrated, Track 9 runs a synthesis slice.

The synthesis pass must:

  • deduplicate gates;
  • merge overlapping artifacts;
  • identify conflicting recommendations;
  • define priority rules;
  • normalize naming and vocabulary;
  • map mutually exclusive frameworks;
  • add cross-domain false-positive fixtures;
  • verify that recommendations stay proportionate;
  • update docs and final Track 9 baseline.

Known overlap areas:

  • metric hardening appears in product, quality and delivery;
  • security review appears in backend, API, data, AI, delivery and compliance;
  • architecture boundary appears in requirements, architecture, frontend, backend, API and data;
  • evidence-before-completion appears everywhere;
  • release readiness appears in delivery, security, docs, package/plugin and operations contexts;
  • accepted gaps and residual risk appear in every methodology.

docs.title: Safety Rules
docs.text:
Track 9 follows these safety rules:

  1. Read-only first. Workspace onboarding produces audit output only.

  2. Recommendation before generation. Product-Agent OS explains why an artifact or methodology is applicable before staging it.

  3. Explicit approval before staged artifacts. No target workspace writes happen without approval. Staged artifacts remain reviewable proposals.

  4. Conditional methodology. DDD, FSD, security/compliance, release governance and other frameworks are conditional.

  5. No false readiness. Observed files, directories or prompt intent do not prove readiness.

  6. No document spam. Documents exist to close gates, reduce risk, record ownership or enable next action.

  7. No secrets or private data. Reports, fixtures, templates, prompts, memory notes and examples must not contain secrets, private keys, tokens, customer data, raw private chats or absolute user-specific paths.

  8. Evidence before completion. Ready, completed, fixed, works and release claims require current evidence or an explicit inspection-only/test-gap label.

docs.title: Verification Strategy
docs.text:
Every Track 9 implementation slice must run verification proportional to touched files.

For docs-only or design docs:

python tools\check_docs.py

For plugin scripts, templates, fixtures or tests:

python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_fixture_eval.py
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\run_transcript_eval.py plugins\product-agent-os\assets\eval-fixtures\transcripts\product-agent-os-synthetic-sessions.json
python plugins\product-agent-os\scripts\validate_codex_compatibility.py

For navigation, Mermaid, Markdown extensions or MkDocs-sensitive changes:

$env:PYTHONPATH='C:\tmp\codex_docs_mkdocs'; $env:NO_MKDOCS_2_WARNING='1'; python -m mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Definition Of Done For A Domain Slice
docs.text:
A domain slice is done when:

  • its methodology file has been deeply audited;
  • applicable concepts are represented in catalog, discovery, gates, templates, skills or evals;
  • duplicates and overlaps are recorded for synthesis;
  • false-positive risks are covered by tests or explicitly deferred;
  • user-facing docs explain behavior where needed;
  • current verification evidence is recorded;
  • residual risks are explicit.

docs.title: Definition Of Done For Track 9
docs.text:
Track 9 is done when:

  • all 12 methodology files complete the domain integration loop;
  • the plugin has a unified methodology catalog;
  • read-only audit produces methodology-audit-report.md and methodology-applicability.json;
  • recommendations are prioritized and linked to artifacts, gates, owners, evidence and approvals;
  • staged artifacts are generated only after approval;
  • cross-domain synthesis resolves duplicates, conflicts and naming drift;
  • regression fixtures cover high-risk false positives;
  • Product-Agent OS docs explain Track 9 onboarding and methodology selection;
  • full test, fixture eval, transcript eval, compatibility, docs and MkDocs baseline passes.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
Track 9 does not:

  • activate hooks, automations, GitHub Actions, external writes, package publishing or release actions without explicit approval;
  • make every methodology mandatory for every project;
  • replace human product, domain, security, legal or architecture ownership;
  • claim semantic correctness from artifact presence alone;
  • infer production, compliance, privacy or business risk from files without recording uncertainty;
  • use Markdown reports as the parser for plugin behavior;
  • store private customer data, raw private chat logs or secrets in generated artifacts.

docs.title: Initial Risks
docs.text:
• Scope risk: 12 domains create a large implementation surface. Mitigation: domain-by-domain slices and adaptive deep audits.
  • False-positive risk: methodology signals can over-apply gates to simple projects. Mitigation: non-applicability triggers, false-positive fixtures and accepted gaps.
  • Duplication risk: many domains share gates and artifacts. Mitigation: synthesis backlog and final cross-domain synthesis pass.
  • User-experience risk: recommendations can become overwhelming. Mitigation: priority levels, safe next action and staged generation only after approval.
  • Verification risk: deterministic tests can prove contract shape but not methodology quality. Mitigation: owner review fields, residual risks and future semantic evals.
  • Stale-doc risk: methodology docs and plugin catalog can drift. Mitigation: docs sync checks and Track 9 status/backlog evidence.

docs.title: Open Design Decisions For Implementation Planning
docs.text:
These decisions are scoped for implementation planning, not unresolved design gaps:

  • Whether methodology_catalog lives as JSON only or as Python data with generated JSON.
  • Exact file paths for read-only audit outputs and staged artifact output.
  • Whether each domain deep audit gets a dedicated status document or one combined Track 9 backlog.
  • How much of the catalog is generated from docs/methodologies versus hand-authored in plugin assets.
  • Which domain slice receives the first executable implementation after foundation.
